I completed this mod in one sitting.  I give it a 97/100.  Little nitpicks:
Of course those are all very, very minute.  Keep in mind that this mod has been in development for a few years with the help of some very excellent people.  It was constantly being fine-tuned and playtested by some 50 playtesters.  The mod's release date was even delayed so it could be perfected and made to work.  Worst case you'll get a little framerate lag.  Best case you'll be forwarding the cause of Science again.
One small word of caution: this is a mod, not the original game nor a collection of PeTI maps from the workshop.  You'll need to know how to solve tests and how to think your way through Portal 2 in order to finish this mod.  That being said, this mod is a delight for players of
experience level.  If you, a newer Portal player, ever get stuck on a chamber (quite likely to happen later in the game), take a little break, give it a little thought in the background of your mind, and the solution should come to you.  Even better for newer/casual players is the story mode, so now you don't have to suffer as much when solving puzzles.
Bottom line: download it — you won't have any regrets, I promise you, especially since the whole amazing project is

My first A3L experience:
*Le me speeding down the street in my car when suddenly a wild police officer appears from alley*
"10-20 on the 10-72; Kavala Square." He says into his radio, his sirens wailing and lights flickering. I take a sharp turn to the left, making the officer fly 20 feet into the sky, his hatchback giving its final, saddening yell before plummeting to the ground, exploding and killing the officer on impact.
I turn around, a Hunter and two SUVs headed my way: I must escape quickly! I held shift, accelerating my car by 10km/h. I proceeded down the road that I originally aimed for, soon turning into a dark alley to avoid contact with the law-enforcement.
"NEEEEEEOW!"
A series of blue lights and sirens sounded past my location. I was safe; or at least I thought so. Before I could realise, a PD helicopter was patrolling the skies, soon discovering and announcing my location. As its beam of light beaconed at me, I reversed from the tight space, and sped to the town centre - Kavala square.
Disobeying the speeding limit, I held my finger firmly on the shift key, knowing that if I let go I'd be trampled and macerated by the Hunters that persued me. Realising that the whole of Kavala PD was now shadowing me, I lead them to their unexpected deaths: attempting to de-sync ram those like the detective I eliminated before. It wasn't long until they raced down the street - I stuck the front of my vehicle out of the gap, sending the impenetrable Hunter to its destined death.
Untouched, my car remained in pristine condition, however I was still in pursuit. Locked onto me, the chopper hovered above, revealing my position. Intimidated, I abandoned my Offroad and scrapped my clothes, sprinting to the suit-store. I purchased a cheap hobo-outfit and ran back to my car, only to realise it is now under the jurisdiction of the cops as they formed a road-block, defending the crime-scene.
Attempting to explain to the officers that the vehicle belongs to "my friend", they stated that I should leave. In protest, I stole (however I do not think of it as stealing, rather borrowing my own ride) the OffRoad, detonating two police cars and myself during the process.
TLDR: I rammed some cops, abandoned the car, changed clothes, stole the vehicle back and we all exploded.

I'm not one for easy and simple reviews, so if you don't want to read the entire history of me playing this game and just want me to get to the point:
Now then, I started playing Team Fortress 2 in the year 2012 (In the Pyroland update), a friend of mine recommended it to me and told me that it was free-to-play. I was at first hesitant, it was my first ever real shooter, yeah I was rather new to PC gaming back then. But I downloaded it and just started playing with him. I was awful, of course. As a Gibus wearing, Pyroland exploring, free to play I had really no reason to be good. I then heard about one of my favorite youtubers playing the game and I just joined him. I exactly remember how it went, he was still rather small in comparison to now but I just wanted to talk to one of my idols. He accepted my friend request and we started trading and talking.
I am now a admin on his Steam group and a staff member of his Discord. Why do I bring this up? To display the kind of connection I have to the game, it made me meet my idol and befirend him and meet so many more likeminded people who loved the game. I then decided in 2013 to finally buy a Key within the MvM update and I was never so satisfied with a purchase in my life. I met many more people, some I'd today consider to be "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s" and some that I still consider some of my best friends ever. This community and the love that many of it's members have for the game still astounds me. It was like a daily routine, always joining a pub server and having fun with a bunch of people.
Flash forward to 2015 and things don't look as good anymore. I started playing other games and my interest in the game fell. Sure, I'd join into a match or two or open a crate with some rest money I had left from a purchase, but really:
It was not the same anymore.
You'd get one or two updated every few months that added nothing more but cosmetics and maybe a weapon that sucked.
And in 2016 it happened, the "Meet your match" update.
Suddenly all of the interest I had left was gone. The matchmaking, the changes, the interface, it was all just bad and terribly handled. I went on to play more new stuff and TF2 was nothing more but a memory and I seperated myself from all of my friends that I got to know because of TF2.
In late 2016 I got an invite to a discord chat.
It was one of my old friends talking to me about a discord server for the Youtuber at the start. I joined and was instantly greeted with love and surprise, by a community I thought that had forgotten me. A bunch knew me, alot had heard of me, alot got to know me. While I was not completely back into the game, I finally felt welcome in a world that I started to believe was only there to kick me in the stomach. I felt good and even if I fell into depression or tough times, a few were there to help me.
Now back to TF2 (Can't believe I sidetracked so much): A month ago I got a message from a friend telling me about how great the new "Jungle Inferno"-Update was. I reinstalled the game after a month of having it deinstalled and...
I'm in love again.
To be fair the matchmaking is still not good, there is no elo system and especially ranked needs a rework. But by god, it feels like the game is in hands again that actually like this game and want it to succeed, I can finally join a pub again in like 5 seconds and have 4 Snipers and Spies on my team, one of them wearing the Gibus and the other 3 standing in one place. I can finally play a class again that makes me feel ultra powerful while I stomp all the enemies or play Pyro and hate myself.
I can play with my friends again.
I love TF2.
And I thank TF2.

Plants vs. Zombies can be considered a linear tower defense style game. It makes use of resource collection (in this case sunlight) and turret style defense (such as flowers, peas, walnuts and other dangerous veggies) against an onslaught of enemies (zombies) from a preset direction. The story is simple, yet compelling enough, by game play alone to get you through to the end. Though the idea of plants fighting off blood thirsty brain eaters sounds completely outlandish, the game's artwork, characters and the personalities given to each inanimate reanimate, as well as each plant, make this game one of the most ridiculous mashups ever created. However, Plants vs Zombies is also one of the best games I have ever played and I constantly find myself hopping back to it, if only to tend to my Zen Garden...

Saints Row: The Third is a third person shooter taking place in the open world city of Steelport. It's a game that doesn't really take itself too seriously which is either a good or bad thing for some and the graphics are cartoonish to go along with the humor of the game which might fall flat for some people at times.
In Steelport you'll be spending your time either completing the missions, doing activities and finding the collectables, or going around the city causing mayhem. The story itself is based around getting revenge for someone and thats about it, lasting roughly 10+ hours. To make it even worse; Saints Row 4 basically renders every action you did during this game entirely pointless. However the missions themselves are pretty enjoyable, and the interactions between the characters are interesting despite not being too fleshed out.
While the story isn't too particularily compelling and the game's humor and graphics may not appeal to everyone, Saints Row: The Third is solid overall and pretty fun to play by yourself or with a friend. It occassionally goes on sale for $3.74 and it's definitely worth purchasing for that amount.
► Fun single player and co-op gameplay experience
► Lots of customization options for your character, gang members and cars
► Variety of missions
► Interesting characters
► Many Activities to do and secrets to find
► Upgrade system (guns, character, homies)
► The timing for the songs / tracks bring out the feeling of a scene, especially the final mission
► Solid controls
► Linear progression in the plot, where as the first two games would let you choose the order you could take out the gangs
► Story isn't particularily interesting or compelling
► Acheivement hunters won't be able to 100% due to the character gallary being down
► No cutscene replay option as with the first two games
► The city itself is particularily dull and lifeless
► Stuck with any upgrades choices you make, can't switch them on or off
► Humor is a hit or miss for some people
► Few one time only choices that affect bonuses you'll recieve, but otherwise won't affect the storyline
► Upgrading too much may ruin your experience if you want a challenge

It's kind of strange to make an open-world game whose story & missions are shorter and more concise than its predecessor. Isn't an open-world game about having a ton of stuff to explore and do? Which to me is the conundrum of Saints Row: The Third. It's still a fun game, and recommended, but a lack of content volume (not variety) disappoints after the plethora of activities in Saints Row 2.
+ Good gun-play, character upgrade path, weapon upgrade path.
+ Graphics are really good (DX11) if your machine is powerful enough to turn the settings up (a far render distance is pretty taxing).
+ The story is ostentatiously stupid fun - like a fantastic B-movie - if you can enjoy it for what it is, and not expect something more serious like Saints Row 2.
+ Good voice acting from everyone.
+ Some fun new activities, and most of the old activities are back: Escort, Trail-blazing, Mayhem, Hostage, and more, as well as new variants (like Tank Mayhem), or new activities entirely (Guardian Angel, Assassinations).
+ Autos are still customizeable, most of the options staying the same. The vehicles drive better than than the ones in SR2, though there are fewer varieties.
+Tons of personal costume and character customizations.
+ / - Lots of R-rated content. Just saying. I mean, it is a Saints Row game. But when one of the available melee weapons is a giant d**k bat that is called the "Penetrator" - yeah...
- While the activites are fun, and there are a lot of activity icons that appear on the map, there aren't very many of them. In Sants Row 2, each activity had 6 levels to be completed. Here, there is just ONE instance of each activity at a map icon. Early in the game, completing some activities unlocks more of the same activity (at another location) at a higher difficulty, which is fine. But there is a LOT LESS content here. Got the game to 92% completion in 32.3 hours.
- Lots of DLC. With a lot less content already, be sure to get Saints Row: The Third - The Full Package - or don't bother buying the game.
- Crib customization is GONE. This really bummed me. Yes, there are three cribs / strongholds that can be upgraded, but the upgrades are all pre-determined, and don't change look / layout of your crib (upgrading can make the building taller, giving you a higher view, but that's about it).
Temper your content expectations and Saints Row: The Third becomes a gleeful B-movie romp, missing the seriousness of Saints Row 2 and the all-out insanity of Saints Row IV. Recommended at a minimum of 50% off (which happens during most major sales events).

delivers what it promises, the mod have well-detailed environments that realy helps in immersion, and are very nice to look at, there is always something grabbing your attention, be they a poster, model, an architecture detail etc.. the puzzles are indeed logic based, although sometimes appear that they're rly complicated, the solution is almost always something that can come naturally when you stop and take a second look at it, is needed to say there is no re-teaching of the ABC's of Portal so it kinda assumes that you played at least one of the original games, the story is very interesting, it begins in the 50's and takes you back to the glory days of Aperture, you travel thru the place guided by Cave Johnson himself (which obviously isnt voiced by J.K. Simmons, but Harry101uk does a very nice job making him sound believable) to not give too many spoilers.. you are led to a relaxation vault, something goes wrong and you stay there longer than expected, you're woken up by someone and starts the journey to the surface, but that's where the problems start, first of all there is too much dialog, which is very good don't get me wrong, but if you rely on the subtitles, get ready to see some huge blocks of texts that will surely deviate your attention from the awesome scenarios at some points. Your partner most of the time is Virgil, an A.I core who wants to and help you and himself to escape. The actor voicing him is great and always sound very enthusiastic, but he is the one responsible for explaining to you the story... so... prepare your ears, also there is a recurring event in the story that is responsible for giving a sense of urgency to your actions SPOILER
, but unfortunately at least for me this had no effect at all, i never felt the sense of urgency that the event was suposed to pass... this is in no way fault of the developers since the limitations in the engine don't actualy helps them to show it happening everytime that the story adresses it, it doesn't ruins the story for me, but kinda breaks the immersion.
     Overall as I said earlier, Portal Stories: Mel delivers what it promises, awesome visuals, puzzles based on logic and an interesting story, and best of all, it's free .. despite some problems here and there in the story the game still deserves your attention... so what are you waiting for? go play it.. EN:
Rating: 9/10

delivers what it promises, the mod have well-detailed environments that realy helps in immersion, and are very nice to look at, there is always something grabbing your attention, be they a poster, model, an architecture detail etc.. the puzzles are indeed logic based, although sometimes appear that they're rly complicated, the solution is almost always something that can come naturally when you stop and take a second look at it, is needed to say there is no re-teaching of the ABC's of Portal so it kinda assumes that you played at least one of the original games, the story is very interesting, it begins in the 50's and takes you back to the glory days of Aperture, you travel thru the place guided by Cave Johnson himself (which obviously isnt voiced by J.K. Simmons, but Harry101uk does a very nice job making him sound believable) to not give too many spoilers.. you are led to a relaxation vault, something goes wrong and you stay there longer than expected, you're woken up by someone and starts the journey to the surface, but that's where the problems start, first of all there is too much dialog, which is very good don't get me wrong, but if you rely on the subtitles, get ready to see some huge blocks of texts that will surely deviate your attention from the awesome scenarios at some points. Your partner most of the time is Virgil, an A.I core who wants to and help you and himself to escape. The actor voicing him is great and always sound very enthusiastic, but he is the one responsible for explaining to you the story... so... prepare your ears, also there is a recurring event in the story that is responsible for giving a sense of urgency to your actions SPOILER
, but unfortunately at least for me this had no effect at all, i never felt the sense of urgency that the event was suposed to pass... this is in no way fault of the developers since the limitations in the engine don't actualy helps them to show it happening everytime that the story adresses it, it doesn't ruins the story for me, but kinda breaks the immersion.
     Overall as I said earlier, Portal Stories: Mel delivers what it promises, awesome visuals, puzzles based on logic and an interesting story, and best of all, it's free .. despite some problems here and there in the story the game still deserves your attention... so what are you waiting for? go play it.. NOW!!!!

I'm not one for easy and simple reviews, so if you don't want to read the entire history of me playing this game and just want me to get to the point:
Now then, I started playing Team Fortress 2 in the year 2012 (In the Pyroland update), a friend of mine recommended it to me and told me that it was free-to-play. I was at first hesitant, it was my first ever real shooter, yeah I was rather new to PC gaming back then. But I downloaded it and just started playing with him. I was awful, of course. As a Gibus wearing, Pyroland exploring, free to play I had really no reason to be good. I then heard about one of my favorite youtubers playing the game and I just joined him. I exactly remember how it went, he was still rather small in comparison to now but I just wanted to talk to one of my idols. He accepted my friend request and we started trading and talking.
I am now a admin on his Steam group and a staff member of his Discord. Why do I bring this up? To display the kind of connection I have to the game, it made me meet my idol and befirend him and meet so many more likeminded people who loved the game. I then decided in 2013 to finally buy a Key within the MvM update and I was never so satisfied with a purchase in my life. I met many more people, some I'd today consider to be "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s" and some that I still consider some of my best friends ever. This community and the love that many of it's members have for the game still astounds me. It was like a daily routine, always joining a pub server and having fun with a bunch of people.
Flash forward to 2015 and things don't look as good anymore. I started playing other games and my interest in the game fell. Sure, I'd join into a match or two or open a crate with some rest money I had left from a purchase, but really:
It was not the same anymore.
You'd get one or two updated every few months that added nothing more but cosmetics and maybe a weapon that sucked.
And in 2016 it happened, the "Meet your match" update.
Suddenly all of the interest I had left was gone. The matchmaking, the changes, the interface, it was all just bad and terribly handled. I went on to play more new stuff and TF2 was nothing more but a memory and I seperated myself from all of my friends that I got to know because of TF2.
In late 2016 I got an invite to a discord chat.
It was one of my old friends talking to me about a discord server for the Youtuber at the start. I joined and was instantly greeted with love and surprise, by a community I thought that had forgotten me. A bunch knew me, alot had heard of me, alot got to know me. While I was not completely back into the game, I finally felt welcome in a world that I started to believe was only there to kick me in the stomach. I felt good and even if I fell into depression or tough times, a few were there to help me.
Now back to TF2 (Can't believe I sidetracked so much): A month ago I got a message from a friend telling me about how great the new "Jungle Inferno"-Update was. I reinstalled the game after a month of having it deinstalled and...
I'm in love again.
To be fair the matchmaking is still not good, there is no elo system and especially ranked needs a rework. But by god, it feels like the game is in hands again that actually like this game and want it to succeed, I can finally join a pub again in like 5 seconds and have 4 Snipers and Spies on my team, one of them wearing the Gibus and the other 3 standing in one place. I can finally play a class again that makes me feel ultra powerful while I stomp all the enemies or play Pyro and hate myself.
I can play with my friends again.
I love TF2.
And I thank TF2.

Team Fortress 2 has been around for 10 years, and is still being updated. There's a number of reasons it sets apart from other shooters. For one, visualy it's cartoonic instead of the realistic COD or CS:GO. While there's the main goal or objective, it doesn't mean you have to focus completely on that. You can have fun messing around by taunts or tricks only done in TF2, having hilarious moments with not just your team, but even "enemy" players. While it's not perfect, it's still well developed, even while under a 5 man team curently. A big reason for it lasting this long is the comminuty. There's another side with them and what you can do. Another plus about this game, is you can customise some things that only you see, change models and textures, custom animations (if you know how), even hit/kill sounds. Intalling customisations is easy, just look for the "custom" folder in the files. In conclusion, hopefully Team Fortress 2 will stick around for a very long time.

The Arma series redefined war games and Arma 3 is the pinnacle. You will die and it won't be 'fair' but war is never fair. With an entire open world, you must use the terrain, keep you head down and most importantly know when NOT to take that shot. This is a game of survival, what matters most at the end is that you survive and not your position on the scoreboard.
For it's large and fiercely loyal community, nothing else comes even close to Arma - if Call of Duty and Battlefield were Snakes and Ladders, then Arma would be Chess; more complicated but infinitely more rewarding if you have the patience, the temperament to plan every move and most of all to learn from each encounter.
I will always recommend Arma, but it's not for everyone and it's not without it's faults. I would suggest that if you still have doubts about buying the game after reading this review, you watch the 'ShackTack' Arma 3 videos on Youtube which will give you a good idea of the nature of the game.

Chances are, you already know what Saints Row 3 and 4 are like, but if you don't, let me assure you that they are batshit insane. In a good way of course! It's an open world sandbox game crammed full of humor and off-the-wall action. Basically it's sort of like what if you took the premise of another open world sandbox like GTA or Just Cause and then shook it up in a container with all the best gangster/gangsta movies, 80's action movies, saturday morning cartoons, and japanese television you could think of. That's the best analogy I can offer, because this game has so many references and allusions in it that all make the gameworld vibrant. The missions are interesting, the plot is actually decent (minus writing out a fan favorite character), there's variety of weapons and vehicles, and there's enough unlockable cosmetics and mods to find to keep you busy for a long time. The only downside to me is that the combat wasn't very challenging, when it could have been a little tougher. Otherwise though, there's plenty of cool stuff in the fights that keep them entertaining. I heartily recommend this game to anyone looking for something fun that doesn't require too much brainpower or long stretches of time to get into.

I started playing this game a few months before the new map was released and man oh man has it changed. This is the most fun/annoying/exciting/dissapointing/addicting/depressing game I have ever played. If you are naturally competetive this game will frustrate you from the beggining because there is a lot to learn. You will need to learn how to loot quickly, have map awareness, game awareness, be able to make decisions quickly in order to be average at this game. It can be very overwhelming at first but playing a lot and frequently will help you the most.
I think it is important to remember that this game was in a pretty bad place before the release of PUBG. There was no haste to fixing things, the dev team seemed pretty unresponsive and the community managers did not help much. That is not the case now. This company has been extremely transparent in the last 6 months and they seem to be really making an attempt at listening to what the players want. The last 3 updates for this game have been overall very good and I think are indicative of what we will see from here on out. Be careful about listening to people who absolutely crap on this game. Does it have its flaws? Absolutely. Is there stuff that is being updated now that should have been updated two years ago? Yes. Remember that their was a big internal overhaul with the team working on this game. Many people left and many new people replaced them and then some. What is important is that right now they are doing what they should, they cannot go back in time.
If you can handle the very passionate fanbase, the minor but annoying "broken" aspects of the game, the time it takes to learn the game, then I would recommend buying it. It is a fun game, and I find myself playing more and more after each update. Watch many different streamers play first, watch some youtube videos from the dev team, look at the last few patch notes, then make your decision. If you cannot handle the above in any capacity, do not waste your money or time. Go in with an open mind and a non-biased attiude and give it a shot.

Saints Row The Third Review.
After picking up the frainchise on a bundle.  Which gave me the DLC for 2, 3, and 4.  And having Gat of hell gifted to me during the playthrough of the 4th one.  I find myself playing through the 3rd one again, on hardcore mode.
This game is amazingly insane.  While GTA has a very serious look on whats going on with it.  This game takes a more humorous and funny approach to it.  While not loosing itself in the rediculousness.
Most of the game play itself is serious enough.  Angering the police and the gangs kicks up more elevated response from them.  Helicoptors, snipers, odd speicalists (wait till you see the deckers)

Whenever I think of a shooter game, I think of TeamFortress2. This game was and is still one of my all time favourite games. The artwork is ravishing, the characters are enternaing and simplistic, and the game play is hectic and enjoyable. Builds in this game are jam-packed with creativity. I always enjoyed games which have builds, focus trees or anything else. It bring a sense of uniqueness which makes you want to strive to achieve more. Unlike any other standard shooter games, TeamFortress2 is very relaxed and... casual. The casualness of the game brings a fun environment where the player can just mess about, playing it in anyway they want. Their also is a competitive game mode (Which takes 10 years to get in!) for any player who wants to challenge themselves. I have been waffling about how good Teamfortress 2 is, but I haven't mentioned any of its cons.
The two main concerns I have with TF2 is that updates are scarce and it takes ages to join and real server. Updates are a necessity. Games such as rust have updates two times a month. Updates help cleanse bugs and also keep the elements of the game in shape. Unlike rust, TeamFortress2 has a measly one update per YEAR. However, this is due to a small amount of game developers working on the game (This problem is quite complicated, I would suggest you to spend your time on this video
. Due to the latter problem I mentioned, I just go to Community servers. The only problems with that is that you will be limited to maps Turbine and 2Fort. Other dilemmas include hacker and exploitation (Personally, It never affected me).
Indulge yourself with other reviews, then think. Is this game worth it? At the end of the days it's your choice. Whichever choice you make, I will assure you that it will be right. I hope you found this review compelling.

Okay so... as I've played for around 1.3k hours, I guess I am ready for doing a little review. I have been playing this game since 2011, so that's around 6 years. I know I should have more hours for 6 years but at some points I stopped playing it.
Team Fortress 2 is an awesome FPS game and it's also free which makes it the best FREE game ever. Although Valve hasn't always listened to players and has made some mistakes the game is still alive after 10 years and has more players than a game like H1Z1 which is a really famous game. The game has to offer 9 classes which you can choose between. You pick a class you like and play it, play it, play it and play it. You play through maps and once you get to around 1k hours you will start to get better at some certain classes and you feel alot more comfortable just wrecking everyone. Although the game is P2P (Pay to play) you are still able to do the main stuff in this game. And I think that basically 80% of the people have atleast 5 dollars just to put on this game and finally become a "P2P". This game is amazing due to having cosmetics that almost none of the other Free to Play games has. This game has so so so many options. Now they've added contracts which you can spend time on and might even get Unusual Weapons. So I mean this game is awesome and I definetly recommend checking it out.

I like the amount of mods it has and the awesome community I dislike the the company who developed it "bohem interactive" they make over price DLC which can be bypassed using mods. I recommend this game to all team players.

While not the most challenging "Tower Defense"-type game, it's the most complete experience from the genre. What do I mean?
First off, it's charming. Cute, funny, bursting with character: It's just unqiue. Each zombie-type and plant has it's own little encyclopdia entry, often-times filled with the discarded dreams of zombie youth or a taste of plant family-drama.
Second, it keeps your fingers busy even when it's being easy. I don't know about you, but I HATE having down-time in my games. YOU are the one responsible for collecting resources with a clickity-click (along with coins to unlock items) and is a welcome change from the passive reception of wealth in the genre.
Third, there are loads of little fun mini-games and extras that the game encourages you master. Zombie-bowling anyone?
So yeah, buy this game. The learning-curve is gentle (maybe a little bit too gentle!) and is a great starting point for anybody who is wondering what's so fun about Tower Defense games.

Straight Forward Review:
This is the best military shooter I've ever played. The map is incredibly large, as in if you ran from point A to point B sprinting, it would take you hours. The customization system is absolutely fantastic, with a wide variety of options to create your soldiers, weapons and gear. Multiplayer is engaging and fun, where team play and communication are vital to proceed forward in hostile situations, and complete a series of tasks and/or missions. The way you engage missions is unrestrictive in terms of the way you want to proceed, such as in vehicles, on foot or when eliminating targets (this is where communication is a must).
My Thoughts/Opinions:
Personally, if I were to add more things to the game, it would be more vehicle customization options. There's very little you can do in comparison to your character customization. It would be cool if you could attach a GL or MG to a civilian car, and change mounted/attached gun types on tanks and LAVs. Maybe add chassis modification so that we can change a few looks to headlights, bumpers, armour (which could potentially affect speed positively or negatively). More colour schemes would be nice also. With aircraft, it would be more exciting if we could change the gun types in terms of various machine guns and missile launchers, and possibly adjust thruster types? Basically an improved vehicle customization system overall.
With weapon options, you can just go ahead and download mods. There are some really nice mod packs that supply you with a variety of weapons to choose from!
Conclusion:
Overall, Arma 3 is personally my favourite military shooter... ever. Buy it if you're a fan of FPS or third person shooters.
- Also please note this game is highly demanding when it comes to graphics and optimization. You are going to need more than the recommended specs that are listed. My recommendation is a GTX 950 or more (or an 860m if you're a gamer with a gaming laptop), this game has some serious detail. Also make sure you have an i5 or i7 core processor, with an 8gb RAM or more. -
My Verdict - 9/10.

You need to try it to get a feel if you would like Arma, its not like Battlefield or Call Of Duty. I did buy the game before I even had a PC that could run it and that was a bit of a gamble. I do enjoy the game.
I have played both Call Of Duty and Battlefield and this is quite diffrent to both of them. While it is more realistic than both of Call Of Duty and Battlefield there are community based mods that take this further and make the game feel much more realistic (such as ACE).
Since Arma 3 is such a large game (as a community) its best that someone buys the game and trys it out. I made a list of Pros and Cons just so you can get an idea of how the game feels.
Pros:
Wide range of gamemodes and community made content
Great community backing it
DLC is not "forced" appon players (such as Helicopter DLC, players can use the helicopters as long as they are not in the "crew roles"). The main thing being the DLC is not made in a way that you are forced to buy it so you can have a great experience.
The modding community does provide a massive range of content that can be used from maps, to new vehciles, buildins and guns for players to use.
Single player and offline game play runs very well.
Aircraft are easy to fly but they need you to master them. You can learn to fly your self in the editor with helicopters but if you want to get a hand on using them for combat, do the tutorials and then join a mill-sim unit and build your skills from there.
Cons: (this is mainly performance related stuff)
I recomend installing the main game on an SSD to prevent frame drops, mods and other content should be fine on a HDD but if the mod is causing the game to slow down put it on the SSD with Arma 3. I used to have Arma 3 on a HDD and running around 20  frames per second in multiplayer (this is in kavala on altis when playing KOTH), after using Arma 3 on an SSD I was getting about 60-70 frames per second in multiplayer (in kavala on altis playing KOTH). (Since you proberly don't own the game when looking at this review, kavala is a large town/city on a map called altis, altis is a large island and is based on a real world place called "Limnos" near "Greece").
Random memory leaks causing massive frame drops and making the game unplayable for 10-20 minites unless you restart. This can be a problem if your playing gamemodes that are persistant and save data such as KOTH, flying aircraft or you are in some form of combat since you will most likly die.
The frame rate will drop quite randomly when playing multiplayer (single player its fine its quite consistant)
Server sometimes don't always give error messages on missing dependencys (while this won't affect your every day player, if you host servers this can be really hard in helping diagnose problems. I resently have a problem where I was missing a software dependency and the server would crash without an error message. I have not been able to replicate this since the latest update so I think its been fixed).

This game is stupid.
Not in the way you're thinking. Think over-the-top hollywood action sequences, except even crazier and stupider. For example, in the second "mission" of the game (which is literally right after the intro mission and character creation), you'll be jumping out of a plane, shooting other people who jumped out of said plane, shooting an absurd amount of cars that fell out of said plane
, catch someone in midair, then shoot the cockpit window of another plane that
, fall all the way through
plane and out the other side to start the whole thing over again.
It only gets crazier and stupider from there, but that's part of what makes the game so
. Saint's Row the Third is all about doing stupid, crazy, wacky things, and it knows it. It's not just stupidity and wackiness, though. While the game makes fun of a great many practices used by businesses in general these days, overused tropes, and even itself (even hanging a few lampshades here and there), the main story is surprisingly involved (though still crazy and stupid as a whole) and one of the potential endings is actually rather serious (as are a few of the messages hidden in the crazy).
While certain other games (*cough* GTA *cough*) are trying to go more for "realism" and constantly saying "You can't do that", or "You have to do this", Saint's Row the Third shrugs and says "Yeah, sure, you can do that. Why not?" (And Saint's Row IV takes it to the extreme). It's also perfectly willing to say "You don't have to do this". Most of the game is not in the main quest, but in the minigames all around the city, and you don't even have to get very far in the main story to be able to do most of them. In addition, while you have to make a choice at the end of the main quest, you are
locked into that choice, and in fact can play the other choice immediately after completing the one you picked.
While there's not really much replayability (other than starting a new game and/or playing with friends), the game technically doesn't end, and you can continue running around the city doing whatever stupid stuff you want (and if you've been upgrading your character enough, you can even jump from the height limit to the ground without taking damage, and eat bullets for breakfast), or finishing up whatever minigames you didn't complete while doing the main story. The gameplay, while not perfect (and glitchy at times, particularly in multiplayer), is fairly solid. Graphics are perfectly fine.  Sounds are good. Oh, and there's no "cover system". You take cover by, *gasp* hiding or crouching behind cover, and enemies
move around to get a better angle on you (though the AI is still rather stupid and tends to only win by spamming moar dudes at you). Cars will also explode (because it's all about the crazy stupid) after taking enough bullets, so don't hide behind them for too long. You can also grab enemies and use them as human shields, either executing them when you don't need them anymore, or throwing them at their allies. Another nice feature is the ability to keep any vehicle (barring certain mission specific ones) you steal. Not just one or a few at a time like GTA. All of them. Just take it to one of your garages, or soup it up in a Rim Jobs, and it will be available to you from any Rim Jobs or garage for the rest of the game. It's that easy. You can even have one of your "homies" deliver a vehicle you own to you!
There's plenty more fun, crazy, stupid stuff you can do in this game, but you'll have to look at other reviews for those (or even the descriptions for certain DLC (*cough* mind control explosive octopus cannon *cough*). All in all, I consider SRTT a good break from all of the standard tried and true formulas that are just rehashed over and over. A fun game that doesn't take itself seriously, and doesn't expect you to take it seriously either. Worth every penny, IMO.

Plants vs. Zombies is sort of like a tower defense game in that you use an infantry of plants to fend off zombies coming in on the right side of the screen. There are 49 unique plants, 25 different zombies (excluding one), and five different areas to fight on, so there's plenty of strategies you can use (I use the Potato Mine for the first few zombies during the day, for example). Finding the right strategy for you might take a while, as your plant variety grows after each level.
The difficulty increases at a steady rate until you get to the extras, which can be very panic-inducingand add a lot as a post-game. Mini Games put a twist on how you play, Puzzle makes you really think, and Survival (at least the hard ones) can get insane. I'd also like to note that Laura Shigihara did a wonderful job composing the music.
Plants vs. Zombies is up there in my favorite games list. It's a decent length, has plenty of variety, and can be enjoyed by kids and adults alike. If you somehow haven't played it yet, pick it up!

Arma 3 is a (semi) modern/futuristic military simulation taking place generally in the next ten or fifteen years. If you've played and enjoyed the previous tittles, this one is almost certainly somthing you should look into. I have found that this is one of my all time favorite games after it passed up Arma 2, and is nowhere close to dying with the support it has. However, if your looking for a game with "Run and gun" style gameplay, you probably won't apreciate this game fully.
--Pros
1) Pretty long, in depth campaign to get new players into the basics of the Game.
2) Complete open world levels with vehicles from tanks to fighter jets.
3) A mission editor to customize your own content and scenarios.
4) An active modding community pushing everything from character skins to entire islands and new factions.
--Cons
1) If you don't have a tough computer you may not be able to run the larger maps or heavy combat scenarios
2) Key binds. Lots, and lots of keybinds for everything from looking at your watch to swapping grenades.
Also, if you ARE swapping over from Arma 2, "G" is bound to grenade by default in Arma 3. (If you're an Arma 2 fan you'll understand why this can cause problems early on.)

I have not played enough tower defense games to be sick of the genre.  I enjoy card collecting and deck management.  Plants vs. Zombies mixes these attributes with a comedic theme that I found enjoyable.
That said, I would have liked more freedom with the game's "infinite replayability".  It's fine if you're looking for a campaign or you don't mind what you're playing at any moment, but you can't define the permutation for a quick round of entertainment.  Adventure mode must be played from beginning to end with no way to return to prior levels.  Alternate modes must be unlocked.  Eventually, an endless mode will allow players relatively unrestricted access to their collected plants.  However, it suffers from the same linear restrictions as the adventure mode with the added discouragement of losses erasing progress.
This would be a thumbs up if I could get more than 20 fps with a powerful computer.

First off, SR3 is not as good as SR2 or SR4. With that out of the way, it's still a lot of fun. The Saints, after having rebuilt themselves from literally nothing to owning the entire city of Stillwater, are now massive celebrities who own the Ultor Corporation and have enough lawyers to keep them out of Prison no matter what they do. This prompts another major crime org from Steelport to attempt to knock them off their perch, leading to the Saints invading steelport and also picking a fight with the US government.
That the plot. What's more important is, you can steal and go on tank rampages in this game. There's a button that allows you to punch people in the balls. You get access to Attack VTOLS and Helictopters to increase the mayhem and at one point get to sink an Aircraft Carrier(Spoiler Alert).
The game can a bit Wackier then the 2nd game, which doesn't always jive with the Darker themes at time(the Saints commit a number of acts that could be easily defined as terrorism).
OTOH, the DLC is a lot of fun, even if not required. Gangstas in Space invovles the Boss starring in a cheesy Sci-Fi B movie like you'd see in the 1950's(filmed in present day), while The Trouble With Clones is a huge Homage with classic Monster Movies from the same era(and a huge King Kong shout out at the end). Both are fun diversions and set the stage for SR4.
If you like SR, you owe it to yourself to try this. If nothing else, pick it up during a sale with all the DLC discounted.

I've owned this game for 360, but without all the DLC. Now I do. So let me start my review based on what I've experienced.
Saints Row: The Third would've been a great game IF Saints row 2 did not exist. This doesn't mean it's bad. While it does lack a lot that Saints Row 2 has to offer, both story and gameplay wise, Saints Row: The Third still manages to throw hours of gameplay at your face that will keep you entertained for quite a while (Longer if you have a friend to tag along with). Compared to previous games, the story falls short from interesting, but replaces that with humor and comedy (Not something I enjoyed, but doesn't mean you won't) But in the end, the game is still fun and a great time spender. For the price of the full package, it can't be beat. Get it. You won't regret it.
P.S. if you like old Saints Row, well this is as good as it gets considering Saints Row 2 is horribly optimized rendering it nearly unplayable for some.

Saints Row: The Third is an over the top third person, open world sandbox action game. We are given the role of the boss of the third street saints which is a character that is fully customizable to our liking. We are given a huge open world sandbox area to play in, which is filled with collectables, activities, side missions and various shops!
There are also tons of different vehicles ( Air, Land, Sea ) in this game which we can add to our garage for our collection and most of the vehicles are fully customizable, from changing colour palettes to choosing between various hoods and wheels. There are also a decent amount of weapons in this game ranging from a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to a rocket launcher and all of them are upgradable.
The writing in the story is well done in terms of silliness as there are a few moments where it made me laugh! Most of the characters are quite interesting and well written as well, there was not a moment where i thought a character did not belong in this game. Along our journey we would also accumulate "Homies" which are unique characters that joins our gang which we could call on and they would follow us around to help out.
Unlike most other games of similar genre, Saints Row: The Third does not take itself very seriously and we can see that from the story and some of the very fun stuff placed into the game such as the purple♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bat which we can use to club enemies and civilians to death. If I were to give this game a rating, I would give it a 9/10 as it is a very fun game with lovable characters!

I like this game. It has many fun things in it. That's the problem though, it just has a bunch of fun stuff. It doesn't have the wonderful outright commitment to mind melting ball shaking glorious laser alien insanity of Saints Row IV, nor does it have the wonderfully quirky self aware grounded gang warfare of Saints Row 2. It's fun and funny but it's not that replayable and  is generally way too easy. Like, you get complete control over air to surface missiles in the second ♥♥♥♥ing mission and helicopter support not very long after. Not to mention that about halfway through the game you practically have an infinite supply of money and if you spend upgrade points right it just gets even easier. So to return to the first sentence, I like this game but wouldn't purchase it unless it was on sale or part of the franchise pack (or unless yo already have SR2 and 4 and want the set).
It is fun though, just not as good as the games on either side in the series.

You play as some sort of magical wizard gardener or something who uses sentient plants to defend your wizard brains against hordes of the undead who shuffle single-file through your front yard.
The plants and zombies take on many forms, from your standard ambling corpse to pole-vaulting zombies to zombies riding on zombie dolphins in your pool. The plants do everything from produce sunlight (the source of your magic powers) to shoot flaming peas at your decomposing foes.
It's a fun point and clicky game with a very nice difficulty curve. New plants and zombies are introduced on a regular basis to keep things fresh but never in an overwhelming fashion.
It's definitely the best plant-based zombie-defense wizard game I've ever played.

As an analogy, I have always seen the "Saints Row"-series as the younger, funnier and immature brother of the "Grand Theft Auto"-series. This is what the creators of SR probably had in mind when they were making their game. The rate of absurd immaturity isn't necessarily negative, au contraire; it creates that light and amusing atmosphere that I've come to expect of Saints Row.
+ Very amusing
+ Absurd, though great humour
+ Simple & clean upgrade system
+ Great character & vehicle customisation (which personally always makes the game a lot more fun for me)
+ A lot of diversity (more on this in the cons though)
+ Cool NPCs
- Main story arch is too short in my opinion
- Frustrating AI (which is a problem in lots of other games too)
- Although SR likes to mix up the missions and activities, you might actually feel that the everything is quite repetitive
- Even though the NPCs are great, I think that you should be able to spend more time with them and get to know them better, they are after all " your crew"
Saints Row: The Third is a great successor to the previous game and meets my expectations of the game, which doesn't mean there isn't room for improvement. Playing the game was very satsifying though I doubt I will playing more than two playthroughs, except if my OCD were to kick in and make me want to get all the achievements.
My score for SR3 would be 7.5/10

Arma 3 is by far my favorite game to date considering it's Realism, Graphics, Features and of course all the Mods that add on to the nearly endless amount of things you can do with the Base Game's Eden Editor and Zeus mode.
The only thing i can say that "may" frustrate some is the learning curve but with the Virtual Reality Training Simulator it will teach you all you really need to know from Compensating bullet drop to Crash Landing a helicopter if you're Rotor is damaged. (However the Learning Curve is what makes Arma, well Arma)
Aside from that i must say that the game always stays fun and HELLA CHAOTIC (especially in online multiplayer) because this is not just someone shooting at you from a distance or calling in an artillery strike with some binocluars. There is a ♥♥♥♥♥ across the ridge who spotted you and is calling out the compass bearings to reveal your position so his buddies can light your♥♥♥♥♥up, or he is calling out your exact coodinates (or your Grid) so that some ♥♥♥♥♥ in an artillery truck miles away can nail your position exactly. So when♥♥♥♥♥♥goes down in this game♥♥♥♥♥♥GOES DOWN.
The maps on this game by the way are absolutely massive, Atlis clocking in at about 250 sq km, Stratis at 20 sq km, and Tanoa (the new DLC map) 100 sq km. All consisting of different terrain from A large hill country feel in Stratis, more flat land in Atlis but strongly representing a wartorn country, and Tanoa having a very dense Jungle terrain with many islands to be explored and its very own guerilla faction and Nato (Pacific) and CSAT (Pacific).
Vehicles in this game feel VERY real opposed from most other games. Tanks will have a Commander Seat, Driver Seat, Gunner Seat, and Passenger seats (all having their own role) and goes the same for most other vehicles such as a jet fighter or a helicopter where you will most likely have a Co-Pilot or multiple gunners. Controls are a bit more tedious but allow for much more control and flexibility on most vehicles.
All in all Arma 3 is by far my favorite game to date and im sure it will stay that way for a long time, the devs keep up to date with patch updates and bug fixes and the community is always active and consistently putting out new mods. 3 years after Release the graphics still amaze me and the game itself always stays fresh.
10/10 would crash land a helicopter in the jungle to be chased and killed by guerilla fighters again.

I suppose i better get round to writing a review for Arma3. This game has come a long way since its initial release, its the best one in the Arma series and the only downside being lack of official content as far as tanks, planes go. However that being said there is a ton of mod content that has a lot of quality mods along with Workshop being properly integrated into Arma and the game having its own Mod launcher that makes it easy to set em up and load.
The recent (mid-to late 2016) update to the lighting improved visuals a great deal including the water, Arma now is more beautiful to look at than before and of course the Tanoa DLC is a must have also which is their best DLC so far in my opinion. The game has a great mission editor which now is in 3D, in terms of being in the game world and placing objects, vehicles etc, make it easier to make a mission than ever before, but still has a little bit of a learning curve but is powerful enough to make great missions if you put the time into learning how to use the editor.
The game also has a great stance feature, which may seem complicated at first, but becomes second nature, being able to adopt different height in stances which is invaluable to using cover effectively with it.
If you are after a milsim this is a good choice and it doesnt really have any peers at the moment.
The Devs three years on are still adding updates, and new features, eg. being able to fire your weapon from a vehicle as a passenger, weapon resting. They have some more DLC planned for more tanks and aircraft in the near future (at time of this review).

Dai toni meno cupi  ma più satirici\sarcastici,Saints Row 3 cerca di togliersi l'aria da brutta coppia di GTA che la serie si è fatto con i primi due capitoli.Ovviamente in nostri eroi (o anti eroi in base alla nostra  visione della vita) hanno fatti passi da giganti,infatti sono passati da Stilwater a Steelport,una città di ricconi dove sono diventati delle  vere   icone pop.
Il gioco comincia con  Shaundi,Gat,il nostro personaggio che non avrà un volto per il momento e Josh Birk il quale dovrebbe far aumentare la popolarità della gang.La rapina sembrerebbe una cosa da poco visto tutto quello che la gang ha passato nel secondo capitolo,ma molto presto si scopre ad essere un obbiettivi molto arduo mettendoci alle calcagna   tutta Steelport e siamo presi dalla Syndicate,un organizzazione europea  con a capo Phillipe.Da qui comincerà la nostra nuova avventura.Graficamente il gioco è molto cambiato mostrando un look molto più cartoon anche se non usa il cell-shading.Il terzo capitolo è stato pure ottimizzato per bene rispetto al secondo capitolo.Ed è stato anche aggiunto un personaggio che assomiglia e che ha il doppiaggio di Sasha Grey
Pure in questo capitolo  staremmo a combattere contro altre gang,molto più serie e più ricche   rispetto a quelle viste nei primi due capitoli.In Sanits Row 3  sono state aggiunte anche varie possibilità di scelta in  certe missioni,scelte che influenzeranno sulla fine del gioco
oppure saranno scelte che ci permetteranno di fare determinate cose oppure no.
In questo terzo capitolo  incontreremo tantissima nuova gente,formando cosi una gang molto grande,potremmo acquistare lotti ed upgradarli, le auto che ruberemmo si potranno modificare facendole diventare più foti ,perfino indistruttibili (GTA coppia ora?!),potremmo anche potenziare le nostre armi  oppure il nostro personaggio o l'intera gang.Nel gioco non ci è data alcuna possibilità di  trasferire il pg di SR2 nel terzo capitolo.
La modalità co-op funziona più che bene e sono state aggiunte moltissime missioni secondarie molto più divertenti di quelle viste in Saints Row 2.La tracklist è mediocre,proponendoci brani che  dal mio punto di vista fanno ribrezzo,si salvano solo alcuni presenti  nella stazione radio The Mix.
In conclusione con Saints Row 3 abbiamo un cambiamento  molto forte,scelta più che ottima visto che mancano da anni giochi Tripla A che cambiano ad ogni titolo nuovo,ma anche perché cosi hanno il loro stile,il loro marchio di fabbrica.Di certo chi ha preferito il tonno più cupo ed una campagna emotivamente più forte si ritroverà in discordo con questo gioco  ma in prevalenza rimane un ottimo titolo che riesce a superare i suoi predecessori,se vogliamo azzardare  possiamo dire che RockStar con GTA5 ha cercato di prendere un pizzico della follia made in Saints Row.Comunque è  gioco consigliato  che dura al incirca come SR2 ma grazie alle  varie possibilità  che il gioco ci offre  queste ore si allungano molto di più.

If you're not very patient then I'd give it a pass. The game is more about tactics than action, and one hit can be deadly. If you try to play it like Battlefield, you're gonna have a bad time. There are "life" mods too that put a fun spin on the game if you don't want to do combat, and others that are geared toward survival. Arma is built to simulate combat, however, and while it has a pretty wide variety of vehicles (helicopters to pickup trucks) it really focuses on the infantry experience.
Singleplayer is fun - since Arma is really an engine more than a game, even the included campaign is built with the same tools as the modding community, and there are tons of user made missions on the workshop. The mission editor is intuitive as well so its pretty easy to set up your own quick missions. I'm about halfway through the campaign and the missions are fun and interesing so far, the AI is dumber than humans (obviously) but I just installed a mod to make it better.
Multiplayer is where it shines especially with a group of people on voice comms. Servers are available for PvP play as well as 50+ player co-op vs AI. While much of the time you're surrounded by chaos, there's not much that can top the satisfaction of surviving a firefight with your ragtag group of random players after the adrenaline rush from having each other's backs when all hell breaks loose and succeeding against the odds.
Arguably the best part of Arma is the developer support. Bohemia Interactive continues to improve the game at its core, and talented modders take it a step further. Arma 3 will be active for a long time to come.

Arma 3, what you can say, its essentially a master peace in war simulator front. Game mechanics take while to learn, but its worth it in the end when your rolling with full team, do missions, get helo to get you off from area to next. Player base is plentiful and really nice people, who want this to be best experience for them selfs and others, so lots of role playing can be seen. Ou and dont even let me start about mods! How ever Arma 3 is not with out its draw backs... huge range of different keybindings/actions takes time to learn and memorise, there is some bugs still in the game, but nothing game breaking.. even if your car might jump into sky suddenly this usually just causes compulsive lolz and WTF's. Doing missions can become boring for players who are expecting more action.. this is simulation, it means you might stay in that sniper position even a hour and not get any contacts, but you will stay there cause these are the orders you were given by high ups, or risk break down of command structure and immersion. Of course this is rare and depends on mission your doing, but regardless expect lots of running.. and after that even more running. AI in game is ether brain dead or snipe you from miles away.. of course this too can be adjusted and eventually game is best with other human players, where there is plenty of game modes to choose, specially with mods. It's a tower defense game with simple mechanics; it's incredibly easy to learn.  My main gripe is that the game seems to take too long to introduce new mechanics and items, as the games levels tend to be very repetitive.  For a lot of the game you are repeating the EXACT SAME MAP with only slightly different enemies and abilities each time.  Once I found a setup that worked, I found myself recycling the exact same tower layout several times in a row, each time winning the map without losing any towers, which got quite dull.  PvZ does make a good intro for those new to tower defense games, but those seeking a challenge are best off looking elsewhere.  I suppose this is to be expected from PopCap.  I recommend Defense Grid over this, since it has a lot more depth and is still pretty easy to learn even if you've never played a TD game before.

Love the game. Not the new update.
{OKs}
- Shotgun hitreg is worse than before, and the recoil needs reduced some.
- AK is fine. Recoil could be upped some more and spread over time increased.
- New SMG... Glad they majorly upped the recoil, but it's a bit too much. Also needs more damage dropoff.
- AR-15 needs an inbetween of old/new recoil reset. Other wise the new pattern is fine.
- Pistols are good.
- I like that it now shows ranks in lobby.
- I do like the addition of where you are on the map, but the yellow dot that is blimping is kind of childish. The simple red dot from the test server was great.
- Do enjoy being able to NOT use new camera system and reticule.

{NOT SO OKs}
Hmm... Where to begin?
- New running animation reminds me of when you need to take a sh*t but the bathroom is far away. Thus making it look like a lopsided sprint with a slight limp.
- Lighting is very dull, like someone put a pale-grey blanket over the sun.
- The FPS currently... Come on DayBreak. Really? Again? You're killing us. Please fix this!

{OVERALL}
- Again, I do like the game very much. It's very addicting, fast-paced, and has many memorable moments (Thank you DayBreak for the best bugs in video games!), and generally fun.
- Unfortunately, until many things are adjusted, my review will remain negative.

One of the best games I've ever played; an unapologetically absurd open world third person shooter.  In Saint's Row 3 you will:
Create pretty much any character you can think of
Rob a bank while dressed up as yourself
Decide to jump out of planes a few times
Own an apartment with a mounted shark wearing a pimp hat
Drive around in a convertible with a tiger
Protect your cross-dressing friend as he performs on stage
Have some of your fights narrated by Rob Van Dam and Hulk Hogan
Dropkick into vehicles through the front windshield without missing a beat
Sing Sublime's "What I Got" with your homie as your drive to a job
Be a guest on a game show about murdering people dressed as furries and hotdogs
Find a hulked out version of your friend, who you'll then help find love
Get your crew to bring you a helicopter after a quick phone call
Throw yourself in front of traffic for insurance money
Remote control a guy's car to frame him for vehicular homicide before killing him in a gas station explosion
Help your friend in a wrestling match by hitting people with blow up dolls thrown by the crowd
Get turned into a toilet against your will
Purchase the vast majority of an entire city
Beat zombies to death with a phallic bat
Become so well-respected that you can no longer be harmed or run out of ammunition
Get to listen to Bonnie Tyler's "Holding Out for a Hero" during your epic finale
Make a movie to celebrate your crew's exploits
And after it all, the city will love you and hate the task force set up to destroy you.

Pros
-9 Classes that are all distinct.

-Hats
Cons
-The Training Session is out dated
-Some bugs still exist after years. For example the Engineer teleporter trap where you can trap your teammate so they can't move
-Weapons like the Diamondback are OverPowered if in the right hands

Do you like fun?
SR3 is weapons-grade, concentrated fun. It's stupid, and it's offensive, and it's purile, and it's immature, and it's GLORIUS.
There are no tender, deep or meaningful moments to be had here. This game doesn't "make you think." Just to be clear: there's nothing wrong with depth and passion and so forth in games. I love games with strong narrative and plot. But that's not what
set out to do. SR3 was made, expertly, as a sandbox for the player to sow total mayhem and laugh so hard it hurts while doing so, and the only other game I have ever played that managed to accomplish this goal as well or better than this game, was Saints Row 4.
If you haven't bought this game already - it's been out long enough that it may as well be free. Honestly; as far as value is concerned, it's $100 worth of laughs in $5-10 box.
If you're allergic to fun, or get light-headed when someone says a swear, or have tissue-paper thin skin: don't buy this game, it's not for you.
For everyone else that meets the age and system requirements, it's maybe one of the best laughs per dollar values in games to date. Is it as complex/deep/sophisticated as, say, GTA? No, probably not. Is it about 1000x more fun than GTA or almost any other AAA game out there? Yes.

Lets put it this way, Arma 3 has everything you want and more, and if it doesn't you can implement it.. Unfortunately all games have their flaws, Arma 3's flaw is it's optimization. If you want to play this game at it best you need a beefy setup and even then you will still struggle in MP with KOTH or any intensive mod.
I've put about 800hrs (maybe more as i played offline a good bit) in this game so far, i would say half of that time was spent in the editor just messing about. Bare in mind when purchasing this game, this is a simulator and some things don't work correctly (or atleast werent implemented fully).. for instance air combat or sea combat, this is more about boots on the ground, and that is where it excels..
This isn't call of duty and if you are looking for that this isn't your game (Vanilla), however there are mods out there that may cater to that sort of gameplay, and this is the many aspects of this game that i love so much, BI provide the tools for you to create whatever your heart desires.
As i said before there's some things that are annoying or frustration with this game but others that make this game great, for instance the various stances, this has changed how i play fps games for good, I always try to lean or make myself a smaller target and of course they never have anything that is as complex as Arma 3's system.
If you're thinking about purchasing I would say go ahead and be ready to embed yourself in the environment of Arma 3, it's a truly beautiful game when you have the system to show it. And of course there are so many fantastic creators out there with mods that enhance vanilla features or implement new game modes...
See you in Altis or the jungles of Tanoa ;)

Lets put it this way, Arma 3 has everything you want and more, and if it doesn't you can implement it.. Unfortunately all games have their flaws, Arma 3's flaw is it's optimization. If you want to play this game at it best you need a beefy setup and even then you will still struggle in MP with KOTH or any intensive mod.
I've put about 800hrs (maybe more as i played offline a good bit) in this game so far, i would say half of that time was spent in the editor just messing about. Bare in mind when purchasing this game, this is a simulator and some things don't work correctly (or atleast werent implemented fully).. for instance air combat or sea combat, this is more about boots on the ground, and that is where it excels..
This isn't call of duty and if you are looking for that this isn't your game (Vanilla), however there are mods out there that may cater to that sort of gameplay, and this is the many aspects of this game that i love so much, BI provide the tools for you to create whatever your heart desires.
As i said before there's some things that are annoying or frustration with this game but others that make this game great, for instance the various stances, this has changed how i play fps games for good, I always try to lean or make myself a smaller target and of course they never have anything that is as complex as Arma 3's system.
If you're thinking about purchasing I would say go ahead and be ready to embed yourself in the environment of Arma 3, it's a truly beautiful game when you have the system to show it. And of course there are so many fantastic creators out there with mods that enhance vanilla features or implement new game modes...
See you in Altis or the jungles of Tanoa ;)

Originally this game was suppose to be military / army training simulator, but it was turned into a game. Because of the nature of game, it's very realistic and developers have put lot of effort making it as real as possible, however lot of bugs and glitches remain.
In fact 2 developers went as far as going to "spy" on a real military base in Greece and got arrested by the military and their bail was denied, because Greeks accused them in espionage. Google it up if you don't believe me, they were in prison for over 4 months before they finally got out, this is how far they went to get their content right.
Game is very tactical and realistic, it takes only couple of bullets to kill someone, even if they are wearing full armor. Bullets have realistic bullet drop, so weapon scopes must be zeroed to right distance.
I love all the tactical side of the game, but movement and land vehicle controls are bad. Cars flip and slide for no reason, however helicopter and plane controls are quite good.
What i don't like about this game, is those glitches. for example sometimes you stand on top of a rock or something similar and your character just starts sliding down like some matroska and then you fall maybe like 2-3 meters and you die instantly, in real life ... would never happen, unless you trying to kill yourself by falling on your head and breaking your neck, even then it would be hard to kill yourself.
I do recommend this game, but it's way overpriced and those DLCs are too expensive too, even for a youtuber like me .. it's way too much. Spending 100+ eur on a game is ridiculous. However there's workshop, which makes it easy to mod.
In general game is totally worth playing, but could be better.

Pros
-9 Classes that are all distinct.
-At least 100 maps that are all different.
-In new updates there are new weapons added and new cosmetics
-Hats
Cons
-The Training Session is out dated
-Some bugs still exist after years. For example the Engineer teleporter trap where you can trap your teammate so they can't move
-Weapons like the Diamondback are OverPowered if in the right hands
-Some of the hats don't look good.
Anyway, that was my simple review of Team Forteress 2. i recommend that you try this game out. it is overall a great game.

What can I say about this game that hasn't already been said? It's an action/comedy genre that is just completely wacky and throws a lot of random sh*t at you that will make you laugh. It has a lot of charm and you just feel hyped up when you play it, sadly a lot of the missions you get are just side activities and that just get tedious after some time, and they are unskipable, you have to play them to progress through the game, at least they have some funny lines to give when you're doing the missions. The game doesn't take itself too serious which is always a plus in my book, it is on the other hand, nothing like Saint's Row 2 with the gang drama, it has ramped up to be less dramatic and more crazy, it does have some dramatic moments but they are shadowed out by the humor of the game.
The game has really good gameplay on PC, a really good port that works unlike Saint's Row 2 did, it has some really nice character customization, it is not as good as Saint's Row 2 but it's nice, it has a kind of anime style to it which some people will like, some won't. The co-op is really damn fun and you should totally get your friends to play with you, co-op in fact makes the game better. The upgrade mechanic of the game is a bit annoying as you can make yourself invincible by the highest reputation level, and you can't uncheck upgrades to go back to being not OP anymore.
All in all, I'd give this game a 7/10 or 8/10 with co-op.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.
