Are you looking to buy any of Saints games? Here you will get some tips on which one's better. I recommend buying Franchise Pack because all three games are amazing! Review is SPOILERS FREE!
Graphics and Optimization.
Saints Row 2 runs at various framerate with spikes along the way at random moments. Overall it looks ok to me because of great details in cloth, characters models and surroundings.
Saints Row 3 looks like a game I would recommend to a person with the outdoors fear because it looks soo real. Maybe because I launched it right after SR2? The greatest thing is that this game runs much smoother than the previous one.
Saints Row 4 runs even better than SR3 when having the same engine. Amazing job, devs!
Game World
Saints Row 2 has many types of pedestrians scattered around depending on a location you're in. You can find students and goths at University, nurses and doctors at hospitals, bums at local hoods, jugglers on a beach and skaters in mall. Random citizens at diners use laptops, call their friends via phones, eat things and drink popsicles. The best thing about it is that all parts are connected to each other and interacting in different ways. Walking with a straight back katana holder stumbles across a policeman. After yelled curses they start to shoot in each other. Suddenly a driver decides that it's enough red lights on this street so he jammes a gas pedal on the floor and turns on a sidewalk where are the first two men are. On top of that is ability of all characters including the player's to use drinks and food and weed at any time.  All this makes exploration in this game is so amazing. Visiting the same place makes you recall different facts that you discovered. It makes exploration a rewarding system in which you always look up for something amazing around a corner. There are many different buildings you can enter and explore. Some of them are parts of missions and some are not. For me-this game's world is the best of GTA 1-4 and other saints row games because it's living and it's awesome.
Saints Row 3 looks the same at the first sign - the same pedestrians and random folks outside in parks, on piers and in shops. Their look is more casual like what you see in real life. Rarely you come across individuals such as a peeing old man and weird black man with a chicken commercial on a t-shirt underneath weird massive rags. Character's movement is slower and actions they make when something's happening around are slower as well. Overall it feels like the world has less energy in it. The same is about Steelport itself. Everything is sleepy and doesn't catch your eye like in SR2 or GTA Vice City.
Saints Row 4, however, is a different story. Weird virtual effects on buildings, water and citizens are catchy and interesting to explore. Everything implemented connects very well with the whole idea of a matrix world. The more you progress in the game the more weird everything becomes. It's easy to just jump from a roof to roof, then go explore that big glowing alien tower, then suddenly become interested in something red below you and finally find yourself doing that for hours. Since you're acting in Steelport again, it's always cool to find places that you remember and compare them in both games. Until the final mission you're stuck in the night.
Difficulty
Saints Row 2 is the hardest game of three. I can't say how many times I respawned in front of hospital. What makes it so hard? Firstly, there's no upgrades likein  the other two. You simply start and end with the same amount of health + bonuses from side quests. The game itself is much faster and random events occur all the time. It's way harder to fly helicopters. During shooting you want to hide behind something like trashcan. Does it make game more interesting? Yes!  It doesn't look hardcore but provides some challenge which for me is an essential thing for any game.
Saints Row 3 throws at you masses of enemies. A fight may start calmly but be warned! In a few seconds you'll be overwhelmed by enemies. They will send simple cars, then mutants and then brutes and everything times 10! The same thing is going on during missions. Also there are upgrades that help a lot especially when you hit a high level and become unvulnarable to bullets, car explosions and fire. Overall yes it's a hard game at the beginning and then it becomes easy.
Saints Row 4 has spawning aliens and robots and cars with cookies. It has upgrades as well that protect you from certain types of damage and increase health.The main difference from SR3 is an enemy spawnign rate which is much lower. The increased amout of danger levels all the way up to six means that you'll be dealing with various enemies as it grows and at the 6th it'll be a 1v1 fight agains a guard.
Driving, Cars and Driving Cars
Saints Row 2 has the most types of cars I've ever seen: all your normal and fancy defaults as well as busses, bulldozers, weird food vagons, limos, airport baggage carts, trailers, trucks, bikes.
Saints Row 3 appears to have a little bit less amount of 'normal' cars but definately has more weird cars developed mainly for combat and destruction. My favorite feature is drifting. Using cars such as Bootlegger and Churchill allows you to do long around the corners, 180 degrees and spin drifts. Everything about it feels and looks good!
Saints Row 4 is more about super jumps and running so it's not much to say about cars because they're more just of a things somewhere below. You use cars mainly during missions where using of superpowers are limited or disabled. The game still offers you some new fancy crazy vehicles.
Story
Saints Row 2 has three main scenarios each of them is a story of how a gang died. Missions vary in places and objectives and events. For example, sneak into a power plant and steal a radioactive barrel. Escape with it on a heli and mess up with an enemy boss by using it as a ... in a different way. Homie characters are developing during cutscenes.
Saints Row 3 has even more variety and characters and things. It's one big quest about restoring control over Steelport. Missions and sidequests come along.
Saints Row 4 has the most epic story that involves so many crazy and awesome ideas. That's where the creativity flows. Characters development uses connections to the previous games as well as explanations of past events. Although the game features only a couple new characters it keeps it on a high level.
Co-op mode
Saints Row 2 is running without Steam features such as Achievements and Steam Hud menu and Join Game options. If you're not playing with a friend in the same network you'll have to use a third party programm such as Evolve. However, connection is pretty smoove even though between me and my friend are 7.000 miles. The guest has all features that the host has except: no crew and homes costumization, can't buy property and no side quests progress will carry on in singleplayer and games with other folks online. The gameplay is pretty awesome where you drive around together and do missions and even control your roles in side quests.
Saints Row 3 has an easy to connect Steam support to all players - just start a game and right click on your friend and press 'invite'. You can do things together, you explore the city together, you do missions together. Everything is easy and works just fine. The guest cannot costumize crew or houses but is able to purchase property to recieve an hourly income.
Saints Row 4 has the same easy way to connect to each other. Co-op game still exist on missions and on some side quests however is almost dead during free roaming and collecting stuff. Players use super run and super jump but there's just no way to do it together or simultaniously. So the gameplay looks like this. You and your friends are doing things and sometimes start missions and do them together. After the missions they again move in different directions.
Have fun.

Let me start by saying that this game should be free to play at best.
I have never played a more unbalanced or bugged game in my life. I have also never seen a more unrealistic or pathetic attempt at a shot gun. It effectively has less range then a tazer. Honestly the way it is used is like a melee weapon.
The developers keep updating the game apparently based directly on community feedback but with every update there seem to be more and more bugs. For example you can parachute into buildings if you are lucky, obviously giving you a major advantage getting guns and loot when you land right next to them while your opponent has to run up the stairs first.
The loot is not equally distributed at all and the distribution has been getting worse and worse since the developers have started tuning the distribution system. You quite often land next to your opponents and then run into a house in need of a gun but it does not have a single gun in it. Then you sometimes find a house that only has 5 of the same gun in it and nothing else. Today i was looking for a helmet: I ran through 8 unlooted shops without a single helmet in one of them.
The weapons are very unbalanced although surprisingly the developers are trying to make this game competitive in the example of competitive games like CS:GO. But the shot gun should be completely removed in my opinion. The way it behaves is absolutely unpredictable. The AK47 has as much bullet drop as the arrows you shoot with the bow. I actually think crossbow arrows might have less drop than AK47 bullets.
There are so many bugs I don't even want to name them all because it will take such a long time. From people driving in their vehicle which is in perfect condition and the vehicle then just suddenly, randomly exploding and killing them to major desync issues where you become invisible to your partner or you drive arround in an invisble vehicle or landing on top of a shopping cart and getting completely stuck right in front of one of the shopping centers. It goes on and on and on.
It's just a big mess really and the community is extremely toxic. I wouldn't pay a dollar for this game. Fortnite and Last Man Standing are free to play and from what I've heard way better than H1Z1.

If there was ever a place to jump into the Saints Row series, this is probably it.  As of this writing, the first Saints Row was exclusive to the XBox 360, which I don't own so I can't comment on it.
Saints Row 2, while a great game, felt like a Grand Theft Auto clone.
But Saints Row 3, that's where this series finally found its legs.  The over the top gameplay, weapons, and humor work in all the right ways here.  I was kind of bummed to see Johnny Gat taken out of the picture so early on, but the rest of your crew picks up the slack wonderfully.  And Chandi... well don't expect the same Chandi you met in Saints Row 2 if you played it.
When you start playing this game, you may notice that your weapons all just seem a little...weak... when compared to the stopping power of typical games of this genre.  It just took considerably more shots to bring down enemies.  Thankfully, just about all the weapons are upgradable.  With a little investment, you're back up and running and then some.  And the weapon variety in this one is great.
The music selection is quite acceptable.  And a little sing along with Pierce just sets the tone so nicely.
The DLC just ads to the madness.  Starting a gang battle then calling in a truckload of zombies is the kind of thing that GTA never lets you get away with.  I will admit that having so many homies at my beck and call made me feel a little overpowered at times, but it was so much fun.  I've also found a new appreciation for Japanese gameshows thanks to Prof. Genki.
For folks who like their games crude, funny, mature and diverse, I can't recommend this one enough.

Hands down one of the best sandbox games I've ever played. The amount wacky content that Saints Row: The Third throws at you is enough to keep you entertained for hours. There is no gritty realism to the game, because you can see that the series from this point on decided to ditch all that for mindless chaos and fun.
There's a plethora of customization here and keeping with the theme of the game you can customize some crazy saints. For example you have the option of giving your character a zombie voice, which makes the dialogue in the game ridiculous to listen to. Lots of creative abilities to upgrade, although I would highly recommend that you start buying as many properties as possible to increase your income. Then you will have enough money to buy whatever your heart desires in the first hours of the game.
There are lots of side activities that you can unlock if you complete the main missions, gang wars that need your assistance whenever you get a call on your cellphone, among other stuff and you will be rewarded with xp (respect being the term used here) so you can level up your character.
There's nothing more I really need to say about this game that you don't already know, so just take it from me; this is an awesome game that you definitely need to play with a friend for maximum lols. Oh, and any game that has death metal playing on the radio will instantly get a seal of approval from me.

A game that used to be the unquestionably greatest online gaming experience you could have.
Then the game went free to play, and onslaughts of furries and kids overtook the game.
It has been ravaged; very little of what used to be there still remains.
Even so, it's far better than most online FPS games. It feels more focused on being fun, rather than being competitive.
But even so, Valve seems determined to turn TF2 into a competitive game, and have castrated countless weapons for the sake of appeasing the miniscule portion of the community who wants it to be an esport.
That being said, as of now, it's still fun. The inferno update was pitiful for the years it took to complete it, but at the very least, it shows that the TF2 team is willing to put forth a vague effort into doing SOMETHING to make the game better. The game may never reach the amazing peaks it once stood over, but it's still worthy of playing, especially far more so than the rest of the generic, samey schlock that drowns the FPS genre.

This game is fun, right before you get shot by a level 100 seeing around a wall using thirdperson, or maybe getting shot from behind while crossing the street, either, if youre a new player, its not ♥♥♥♥ing welcoming at all,
You'll have more fun hiding like a little ♥♥♥♥♥ in the corner of the map then playing the game, which is ironic considering the fact that it's fround upon by the community, but what are you supposed to do, either die by terrible matchmaking where it doesnt even try to pair you with people at the same skill, or win by doing nothing, the game doesnt have a middle ground,
I'd also like to note the fact that you feel like your guns cant hit anything, I pulled out a shotgun in a small room against someone looking directly at their head and the shots didnt register, people can snipe you while you're wondering why none of your shots are hitting when your aiming directly on the person.
If you have bad spawns, or dont know the game that well, you can sometime be running around in a wide open field hoping to find a car. Sadly enough that bad spawn resulted in me getting 9th place cause no one was around me.
There are a full 2 ARs, 1 Shotgun, 3 pistol?s, Some grenades, 3 Backpacks, 2 Body armors, Melees are ♥♥♥♥ing useless, 2 helmets and etc. What im saying is there is very little variety in each type of item, resulting in the same loadouts each time, every weapon is very common so its not hard to have a full loadout before the next guy flies down, which leads me to my next point.
There is no waiting time for people with slightly slower PCs, the people that have $1000 gaming PC will always get on the ground and get loot first, resulting in the slower one to either die or go to less populated areas with possibly less loot.
If you get shot early on you better hope that when you click the play button that you wont be one of the first people hosting a match, or else youll have to wait 5 minutes to play another round, die, then do it over again
After all that, I still play this game because the gameplay had a good foundation and structure, but matchmaking, bad spawns, and lack of variety make it very annoying. The gun play is OK and it's definetly a better experience with friends, the customization is amazing especially with free crates you can open without money, but those drop every 5 levels, and if youre getting destroyed every game its gonna take forever.
Overall a 5/10, 4/10 if you have a slower PC, and 3/10 if you have no friends to play with, but it still can be fun, sometimes.

Everything feels completely fake in the fourth game and no spirit...just all about tech crisis you're stick in and in which you have to get out of.  Not only does the personification a good thing about The Third, but the action and chaos you can create. Of course having some big fun with cheats and all, I find it exciting to create a  five (badge) wanted level with Steelport officers, SWAT teams, and look-alike national guards chasing you down with an attack Heli swarming missles down at you and dodging each one at a time with explosions in the background and escaping the Squad cars, making it look like a "Fast and Furious" cliche. There's so much to do in the city of Steelport. Altough critics and people say the story writers are getting lazy, I can't agree on that. Mostle everything you have to do is designed as a story. One problem after another and right when you think you're done, another job to finish. Customization is also a good key in the game...unleashing your style of clothing and taste to your character. Cars aswell have good customization options. Pimping out rides as best as you can be pimping. Warning: This game provokes maniacal laughter and silliness.
Saint's Row 3 is an open-world driving and flying spectacular. I could just drive all day and ignore the ridiculous gangsters in this game...if I didn't constantly run people over and get hassled by the cops...and their helicopters ... and tanks. But I have my own tanks and jet fighters, so it's ok.
Oh yes, there is a story and it's a fairly good one, but you can burn hours just laughing and having a good time. I usually take a long time to get to wherever a quest starts because I♥♥♥♥♥♥off everything between me and the location, and have to fight the world. Most of the time when I die it's because I crashed head-on into a semi-truck during a high speed pursuit away from the authorities I had been provoking.
At first I didn't like the idea of playing a game with gangs in it, and I certainly didn't want to be part of one. But with SR3 and even more so in SR4, the entire world is a big joke, a playground for the player, so it's not really a "Thug game" or even a game about gangs; it's a ridiculous fun-house ride that just happens to take place in a city.
The guns are awesome and some can be upgraded.
The cars are not just very cool, they are fully customizable.
The player character can be a man, woman, black, Asian, skinny, muscular, or even fat.
Both SR3 and SR4 are fun games, but I prefer 3 because I like to drive. In 4 you get super powers and cars and planes become obsolete.

Eu nunca tinha dado muita atençãoa franquia de games Saints Row, Nunca havia jogado, apenas visto alguns vídeos, nunca tive muita vontade de joga-lo varias pessoas julgam o game como ''Cópia de GTA com Zoeiras'', nas promoções de final de ano aqui da Steam eu vi esse 3°capitulo da franquia por um preço muito bom e decidi comprá-lo apenas para testar e ver se é mesmo apenas uma ''Cópia de GTA com Zoeiras'':
Enredo: 8.5/10 (No começo achava que seria uma história bem fraquinha, mas felizmente eu estava errado... Dps da criação do seu personagem começa mesmo o game , para começar as opções de costumização são bem variadas com muitas roupas, cabelos e como disse muitos falam que é uma ''Cópia Hu3 BR de GTA'' então não pode faltar as zoeiras , e sim elas estao de monte no game , desde deixar o cabelo do seu personagem colorido até deixalo nu, a história envolve um pouco, nada que te prenda muito, mais sim o jogo da aquela sensação de: Ahhh eu quero jogar Saints).
Gráficos: 5.0/10 (Os Gráficos são meio zuadinhos mesmo para a época de que ele foi lançado (2011), algumas texturas são praticamente pixels, mal focados e lisas, sim texturas lisas, principalmente em prédios e em algumas roupas... mais tmb não posso deixar de dar os parabens para alguns aspectos , fumaça, textura das armas e de alguns objetos de customização do personagens são realmente bem feitos , o modelo dos personagens tmb é bem feito, mais no geral fica em meio termo de bom e mal).
Trilha Sonora: 4.5/10 (Ponto muito fraco no game, as musicas que tocam no game são muito ruins, nem uma vc escuta e fala , pqp preciso ver a trilha sonora dps e escutar mais essa musica , todas as musicas são artificiais demais em todas as radios , sem exceções).
Efeitos Sonoros: 7.0/10 (Os sons das armas são bem feitinhos, nada muito especial, tanto das armas de fogo quanto as granadas, um ponto positivo são as vozes originais dos personagens, vozes muito bem escolhidas :D).
Saints Row: The Third é um game mais ou menos, jogando ele tive vontade de jogar o IV? , a resposta é sim.... mais só comprando por promoções, é sim um bom jogo com uma campanha de tempo moderado, mais nem fudendo é melhor que GTA, é parecido mais precisa evoluir demais para chegar aos pés de GTA, Ele é um bom jogo de mundo aberto assim como Watch_Dogs, mais GTA como Sempre é um LVL a mais :D.
Minha nota final para: Saints Row: The Third: 6.5/10

TF2 is a bad game
It cannot be saved by valve
Let me go into some points
1. Matchmaking: The match maker is incredibly poor. Some games take over 15 minitues to find
2. Party system: The party system just does not work. Im in a party the rest of the party members get into the game but i dont. Then i try to join via a invite my friend sent me and it does not work
3. Contracts: The older contratcs like in gun mettle were okay, not perfect. I managed to complete all of them. In jungle inferno the contratcs are poorly worded. For example a contract called "Offensive Classes" I assumed that it would be for the offesnvie classes only ie. The Scout, Soldier and Pyro but no it was for any class and you had to play on a offense map and be on the offense team. This means that you can only get this contract on 2 game modes and on only 1 of the two teams. You also have to complete the match in order to complete the contract so if you finish the contract you have to wait for the game to finish and some gamemodes such as CTF can take over 30 mins to finish 1 round.

Team Fortress 2 is a FPS with cartoonish graphics and heavy reliance on teamwork. It used to be paid, but it went free to play in 2011.
The graphics, despite being a bit old already, still look good and stylish. The maps are usually well-designed and interesting to look at.
The gameplay stands out from your other FPS games for being very different than conventional shooters out there. You can pick from nine different classes: offensive (Scout, Soldier, Pyro), defensive (Demo, Heavy, Engineer) and support (Medic, Sniper, Spy), each with their own unique tools, style, strengths and weaknesses. This forces you to work with your teammates to cover each other's weakpoints and emerge victorious.
There are two main gamemodes: PvP and MvM. The former has a lot of sub-modes, such as Payload, Control Points, Attack / Defense, King of the Hill, or Capture The Flag. The latter, on the other hand, pits a team of six players in a co-op tower defense mode against hordes of bloodthirsty robots, with the objective of preventing them from delivering a bomb to the end of the map.
There is a lot of unlockable weapons, which allow you to customize and change your gameplay style, as well as a ton (and I mean a ton) of cosmetic items, which serve no purpose besides looking cool.
The music, while it can't be heard outside of main menu or promotional videos, is very good and fun to listen to even outside the game.
Unfortunately, this game also has cons. Due to the amount of hats content, the game is very heavy, so computers that aren't brand-new might experience some performance issues. Also, due to it being free to play, pub servers are often filled with noobs who have no idea what they're doing, which can destroy your gaming experience considering the game is teamwork-reliant. Multiple Snipers and Spies is a common occurence.
The community is also... well, not the worst, but one of the worst. Just a quick glance at the forums reveals a ton of unusual and Australium-toting "git gud" elitists who aren't very pleasant to talk to if you're new... or in general. However, that doesn't mean there aren't any people who are actually helpful towards newcomers.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to everyone. FPS veterans however should be prepared for a drastically different experience.

Best words to describe Saints Row: The Third? Zany, outlandish and loony. Saints Row: The Third, the game that defined the series as what it is today.
Being one of my all-time favorite games, I will always recommend this for its sheer madness - Fall in love with the various personas you will meet throughout this game (or if you already played SR1/SR2, then rekindle your love for them!), all the while you're blowing up parts of the town of Steelport.
And in the midst of fighting the syndicates of Steelport to take control, you can always take a break and do some of the fun activities throughout the city (my favorites will always be the Genki ones, be sure to check the DLC as well).
And if things start seeming slow? Ask a friend to join you and cause havoc together, while dressed up as anything between Steampunk heroes to furries in animal suits to straight up thugs - Your street gang, your rules.

The PC version (namely Co-Op) has a bunch of problems, from idiotic AI to immediate vehicle spawns (on your character) to intermittent disconnects and more. Single player, I'm sure this game is fine, but since a lot of people will probably be looking to buy this to play with a friend, I just can't recommend the game the way it is. It was the 'fun with a few issues' type up until the end when it just got ridiculous with problems and arbitrary frame drops (using a GTX970).
If you're looking for single player only, go for it I suppose. If you want Co Op, I would assume SR4 is where you're going to want to look.

TLDR at the bottom
This is one of the best and most fun open world games that I've played in a while. There's more than enough here to keep you playing for hours on end and a full 100% playthrough will take about 24 hours but with the addition of co-op, there's tons of replay value - it's also moddable. What's not to like. The side activities are a great diversion, they let you: rampage in a tank for points; blow stuff up for points; play a game show for points and more (for points.) It's the kind of stuff that you typically do in an open world game like this but this way it feels less grindy or boring to do like some other games *cough*gta4 bowling*cough* Now for the negatives - It's pretty easy to beat. I finished the main plot and a few side missions withing 12 hours on the hardest difficulty - I have the full package/goty and even then with the "op" dlc weapons, I beat the whole thing with pistols. Also, some of the checkpointing is awful. In some sections where I get cheaply killed to say a tank appearing out of nowhere or a car exploding, it can send you back to the very start of a 5 minute hold out or protection task
Pros:
-Lots to do
-Great fun
-Engaging side quests
-Co-op
-Mods
-Decent story - infact I liked it, as rediculious as it got (you play as a toilet in one mission)
Cons:
-Really easy on hard mode
-Awful Checkpoints
-Useless weapons - use the pistols
TLDR: Great game, lots to do but it's fairly easy and it's badly checkpointed 8/10 Buy it

Team Fortress 2 is a FPS with cartoonish graphics and heavy reliance on teamwork. It used to be paid, but it went free to play in 2011.
The graphics, despite being a bit old already, still look good and stylish. The maps are usually well-designed and interesting to look at.
The gameplay stands out from your other FPS games for being very different than conventional shooters out there. You can pick from nine different classes: offensive (Scout, Soldier, Pyro), defensive (Demo, Heavy, Engineer) and support (Medic, Sniper, Spy), each with their own unique tools, style, strengths and weaknesses. This forces you to work with your teammates to cover each other's weakpoints and emerge victorious.
There are two main gamemodes: PvP and MvM. The former has a lot of sub-modes, such as Payload, Control Points, Attack / Defense, King of the Hill, or Capture The Flag. The latter, on the other hand, pits a team of six players in a co-op tower defense mode against hordes of bloodthirsty robots, with the objective of preventing them from delivering a bomb to the end of the map.
There is a lot of unlockable weapons, which allow you to customize and change your gameplay style, as well as a ton (and I mean a ton) of cosmetic items, which serve no purpose besides looking cool.
The music, while it can't be heard outside of main menu or promotional videos, is very good and fun to listen to even outside the game.
Unfortunately, this game also has cons. Due to the amount of hats content, the game is very heavy, so computers that aren't brand-new might experience some performance issues. Also, due to it being free to play, pub servers are often filled with noobs who have no idea what they're doing, which can destroy your gaming experience considering the game is teamwork-reliant. Multiple Snipers and Spies is a common occurence.
The community is also... well, not the worst, but one of the worst. Just a quick glance at the forums reveals a ton of unusual and Australium-toting "git gud" elitists who aren't very pleasant to talk to if you're new... or in general. However, that doesn't mean there aren't any people who are actually helpful towards newcomers.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to everyone. FPS veterans however should be prepared for a drastically different experience.

If you're stuck between PUBG and KOTK let me just break it down for you.
KOTK PROS -
•	Fast paced
•	Will run much better on most low end computers, don’t try to buy PUBG if you don’t have at least a decent computer
•	Nice art style
•	Consistent updates
•	Simple
•	Very entertaining with friends
•	Spawns are completely random
•	Good time-to-kill ratio with headshots (as in feels correct when shooting, I feel like I'm doing damage)
•	Car mechanics work fluidly in this game
•	Great skins
•	Ranking system is great
KOTK CONS –
•	Hit or miss when it comes to hit registering (better hope you’re lucky)
•	A few very minor bugs
•	A 1 in every 500 chance you run into a hacker of some sorts
•	Game ends in a few set areas so it gets old after a while but a new update will fix that
•	Not many different variants of guns (new one coming soon)*out now the Hellfire
Overall I love KOTK and I personally prefer it, but I’ll still put it to you straight on PUBG.
PUBG PROS - VERY CONSISTENT UPDATES
•	Very realistic looking graphics and weapons
•	Weapons can have attachments
•	Huge map
•	Hiding is pretty good (especially in wheat fields) which may be a con for you
•	Map helps you find your way easily (very noob friendly)
•	Ability to choose where you land to a degree
•	Many different map settings
•	Weather occurs
•	Character movement is absolutely dope in my opinion
•	There’s boats
•	More weapons
PUBG CONS –
•	Misleading weapon mechanics and time to kill
•	Cars are clunky and all around just do not work well
•	The ability to choose spawns makes players spawn in a very linear line which isn’t my favorite honestly (and no you cant reach almost any point when you drop out, you can go pretty far though)
• 100 (from what I've had in games at least) people spawn compared to 174 in H1Z1 which just makes H1Z1 more actioned packed
•	Kick and bullet drop on weapons seems to be not as polished in my opinion then KOTK
•	You have nothing to really play for, there are ranks (stats wise) but H1Z1 has a way of making you feel more rewarded with placements (yes you get points at a end of a game in PUBG so you can get your 6 cent skin)
On the bright side of things, I do believe PUBG has a way higher ceiling then KOTK so it could easily prove me wrong.
So there you have it. I was trying my best to not be biased but overall KOTK is my game. Don’t get me wrong, they are both good games and have their own futures. Should be great to watch them grow. Hope this helped. Later.

Saints Row: The Third is an over the top, open world over the shoulder third person shooter with strong action, good controls and some over sexualized comedy. There are plenty of giant purple bats, leather clad dancers, and awkward situations all done for the sake of comedy. You play as the head of a gang from the start, but really its a group of three tight friends that grows bigger to include a giant powerhouse, an ex FBI tech geek, a pretensions actor, a serious turncoat twin and an auto tuned pimp. These aren't just quest givers, you can call on them to help you on missions. When they're with you, they're smart enough to find cover in gun fights, take hostages and even steal a car to follow you when you drive off without them. When your "homies" fall, you need to pick them back up or lose the mission. There are frequent checkpoints, but with a game so fun, I don't mind if I die.
The franchise really took a step away from being just a lesser version of Grand Theft Auto. They upped the gameplay and the comedy. Where GTA 4 turned gritty and real, Saints Row went the silly fun route. You can take hostages to use them as human shields. Improve your aim by crouching down. Head shot any enemy for an instant kill. Otherwise the enemies will spin around hoping to find cover and forcing your aim to follow them. There are multiple flying take downs and the animation seems outstanding for something that has so many of them.
There is so much customization too. Everything from customizing your own look, to creating how your gang looks. If you want all thugs, go for it. If you want all space men or strippers. That's up to you. Their stats aren't affected. Its all just a look. Having your crew around makes an interesting mission even more fun. The whole thing is streamlined. Go to your PDA that will get a phone call sending you to a location on your GPS to start the mission. You'll find a wide variety in missions, fly to this location, take out a bunch of gang members, hop in a turret, drive through hostile territory, jump out of a plane ..... in a tank and shoot at people and other tanks as you fall. Then hop in a virtual world with a new weapon. Its always interesting and a few missions take place outside of the city in their own unique environments.
Some missions end with a choice that really adds replay value. Do you get a one time sum of cash, or do you want a constantly generating smaller sum of cash. Do you want the aide of someone new or keep someone old? Even down to trivial things like discounts on car upgrades vs discounts on weapon upgrades or who you let live.
The city of Steelport is a bright, beautiful, vibrant and gritty city. It all depends what area you're in. The industrial zone  has no lights, while the tourist part has beautiful neon lights. The city really lights up at night and looks amazing while flying. As the game progresses, the sights change. You'll see a sunken aircraft carrier, a plane tail up and much more to remind you of just how you've affected the city.
Since this is a new city, you'll need to take it over. How do you do that? Participating in side quests like racing cars or a turf war with one of the three rival gangs in the city. You can buy stores that count to the take over percentage. There are even score based games like insurance fraud and mayhem that have you rag dolling into cars or destroying property. When you own a percentage of the city, you'll make money for it every real life hour you play. Outside of controlling the city, you can participate in assassinations, car thefts and hijackings with a passenger, then hold them until you get a ransom.
Money for weapons becomes irrelevant. You'll always have more than enough ammo even if you never visit a gun store. What the money really goes to are upgrades. In the PDA menu you'll upgrade how much ammo you can have, what guns your crew has, your total health, how fast it regenerates, how much stamina you have and so much more. This is the expensive part of the game. Each gun has four levels of upgrade. The fourth level is always something silly like explosive bullets from a pistol.
There are plenty of weapons in six major types, melee, small, sub machine guns, shot guns, assault rifles, misc (rockets), sniper rifles and four types of throwable things like grenades. You can only have one of each weapon type equipped at a time, but that's more than enough. Some missions require you to use a rocket launcher and it won't just give you a launcher, it gives you unlimited rockets. Its one of the joys of this game. High powered weapons with big effects. Once the STAG army shows up, there are some even more creative weapons like a force rifle that when used it pushes away enemies and fully charged obliterates them. There's just so much variety here, even a tactical missile strike, but that's not nearly as fun as everything else.
Bosses are big brutes that can run right through you. They are pretty simple to take down though. Shoot them enough times and a quick button prompt will finish them off. The ones without guns will throw cars and benches around. The ones with guns carry flame throwers or heavy machine guns that thankfully jam. With them gone you can pick up their heavy weapons to use as your own, but the bigger the weapon, the slower you move. These weapons are worth the time for the power and fun they bring, especially the sticky bomb launcher.
On top of that, you can climb into vehicles, cars, motor cycles, trucks, but better than that are tanks, armored SUVs, helicopters and some futuristic hover jets and cycles. The hover jets and cycles have two modes, jet and hover. Its perfect from a gameplay standpoint, go fast or hover so you can easily take out slow moving ground units and land on a dime. The vehicles with weapons are a lot of fun to shoot with unlimited ammo, but there are cool downs. Tanks that pancake cars. Missiles that lock onto things and follow them. Its very enjoyable.
The characters in your crew are excellently voiced and your chemistry together really shines through. Sure they poke fun at one another, but they have some memorably fun times beyond just shooting things. Silly happy moments like singing to Sublime on the radio and Oleg revealing how he has met his intellectual equal while in a firefight. The bosses of the gangs are worthy characters in their own right. They really make cut scenes interesting.
With you playing a criminal and all, there is notoriety in stars. The cops won't just chase after you, but the gangs and STAG army will too. Police will send helicopters with snipers. Enemy gangs will even setup roadblocks to stop you. It gets to a chaotic level sometimes when a gang and an army are after you. All three factions including your own start to fight in giant wars that can have dozens of people. Its amazing to be a part of. The game makes good use of big environments so you can flank your enemies and they can flank you.
Saints Row: The Third is an amazing and fun game with enough DLC to choke Godzilla. Its mostly all just cosmetic stuff. The Complete Pack has been $5, there's no reason not to pick it up, but with its comedy, its just not for kids.

Honestly my favourite of the series so far.
Score breakdown-
Gameplay: 8/10. The sandbox of SR2 has been upgraded, given a new coat of paint, and had a ton of secrets stuck into it. The gunplay is also improved, and the car physics reach the balance point between racing-sim realistic and action-movie stupid. Lack of customisation is disappointing, though.
Graphics and Art Style: 9/10. It takes a lot of effort to make a giant purple rubber wang look like something badass, is all I'm saying.
Writing: 8/10. Even though most dialogue exchanges are serious, there's an overarching sense of self-awareness and humour that makes the game stand out. And when they do make a proper joke, it's generally pretty funny, and some made me have the pause the game, lest my giggles mess up the level.
Music and Sound Design: 8/10. There's lots of liscenced songs to listen to, and the rather infamous parachute penthouse raid scene is made all the more memorable by a rather well-placed Kanye West song.
Stability and Glitch Control: 9/10. Glitches are uncommon, and never game-breaking. The worst that will happen is some teleporting enemies.
Overall score: 8.4/10. It's the standout in a series known for being standout. Plus it's usually cheaper than chips when the summer sales come around.

ONE SENTENCE REVIEW:
Saints Row The Third is a fun open-world third person shooter with a deep character customization and fun co-op modes yet suffers from tedious and repetetive story missions.
LONG REVIEW:
Saints Row The Third is big departure from the [somewhat] serious and mature tone of Saints Row 2 is replaces it with this over the top, comedic storyline that doesn't take it self too seriously. When you first start the game you are met with a deep cuztomization mode for character. Practically everything in a Character Creator is present in the game and more. This makes for either a funny character or a character that may just look like you. What makes this character creator even better is that you can upload your creations for everyone to download. This makes for dozens of interesting character creations.
After the character creation you're brought to the first mission of the game, which is: Robbing a Bank, and then getting in to jail. After this you are now brought up by a generic "I will take back what is rightfully ours" storyline that doesn't do anything new and at times it just feels predictable. What makes this worse is that way the story missions are done. You need to reach a certain point to get to the story missions, so you are FORCED to play all of the side missions before progressing. Now the problem with this is that it feels like it was added for the sake of making the storyline longer. What could've been a 3-5 hour storyline is padded out to around 6-8 hours because of these missions. What's even worse is that these missions get stale really quickly and it doesn't help that most of the jokes in this game are crude and unfunny.
But the game does redeem itself with it's gameplay. Shooting is fun in the game, driving feels smooth, and customizing your car is really cool. Sadly the missions of the game is a double edged sword where as there are missions that are fun (mostly the story related missions) but then there's always the "padding missions" which just feel boring. But I still recommend playing this because of its fun open world gameplay and its Horde mode. Though it does nothing new to introduce to the genre the horde mode is fun mode that can be played with friends. Sadly you cannot use your campaign character to play in this mode.
Overall Saints Row The Third may have its faults but in the end of the day, its still a fun game to play.

I rarely rate a game this high, but this one is a perfect 10/10
for the genre it represents vs. any competitive products out there.
Bar none, the BEST military simulation on the PC that is
available to the public and priced under $10000
Yes there are flight sims that do flight more realistic,
there are tank sims that do tanks more realistic, etc, etc, etc.
However, there are no other games that combine ALL the aspects
of a military simulation in one full package like the Arma series does.
Arma III is the continuation of the Arma series, which started out as
"Operation Flashpoint 1985".
OPF1985 was considered the best of it's time when it was released and the
Arma series has continued that tradition with many of the same developers
that created OPF1985.
With a simple quick mission builder, a full blown complex high-end mission editor,
mods, mods, and even more mods to make Arma III something really special to those
of us who enjoy these type of games.
If you want the same feature set, but more realistic you would have to actually be in the
military and have a security clearance and thousands of dollars.
But you can get close to the same thing that real militaries around the world actually train
with for less than $60 and you don't need to sign-up for service.
If you want to enjoy this, but can't afford it at full price or have an older or slower PC,
then Arma II almost as chock full of features and mods so if you can't get this, get Arma II.

Simply the best Mil Sim out there! The story is very nice and it doesn't try to copy Battlefield or COD, instead it creates a believable story which I really enjoyed. You're not a hero, you can't take 10 bullets in your body and miraculously survive, your health doesn't regenerate, it's a true Mil Sim and this is why it's so enjoyable. You have to think very strategically if you wish to survive. The same goes for the multiplayer, there's a lot of tricky mechanics and you'll have to know them all if you want to become a good rival to a well trained team. I truly love the game but it does have its issues: performance is heavily dependent on CPU (if you have a good PC, you'll suffer), your AI time is hard to direct, often you'll find yourself running in the back and trying to catch back to your team and end up getting killed because the friendly AIs were careless (enemy AIs are some of the best AIs) and some DLCs should be part of the base game, it doesn't make sense having to pay to get some very basic karts in game and some outfits... The pros heavly outweight the cons so I absolutely recommend this game !

This is your poor man's clone of GTA. Like a cheap alcohol, it gets the job done, but not without a lingering after-taste and  inevitable hangover.
The game starts strong to lure you in, with lots of dialogue and flashy moments, but soon degenerates into repetitive grinding through minigames that are all the same, pointless hoarding of money and premises and accessories. I did like the character editor, but everything else has a terrible taste of cheapness.
The shooting is extremely bland, the guns are weak and sound and feel like plastic toys. The enemies are stupid, but so they are in GTA so I don't mind this aspect too much. What's worse is that there is no inspired writing in the game to speak of, if I compare it to diverse and amusing mission and plot twists in GTA San Andreas and Ballad of Gay Tony. The characters are generic stereotypes, forgettable fast cardboard cuts.
The whole game really resembles a cheap proustityute (don't really understand why Steam censors such a neutral word) by character - boasting, garish, with oversaturated colors that hurt the eyes, foreceful attempts at humor that are not really funny (most of the time), and shameless copying of GTA game mechanics. There are a few amusing moments to be fair, but too few and too far in between.
The driving is especially bad, the cars feel like they have no momentum and are cut from cardboard. There are also many wierd bugs in the physics of the game, somewhere you shake off being hit by a falling truck, and sometimes you just touch a standing car and fly off across the street, blood everywhere.
The cheapness permeates mission design too - there are no outros or escapes, the missions are  simply cut off in the middle of a shootout after the objectives are met. The enemies spawn all around you, so the action degrades into a chaotic mess.
All that said, the game is mediocre in my opinion, but in its basic functionality, it just works. I had no technical problems with the game, besides the occassional minor and obvious bugs, I had my basic enjoyment of breaking stuff, killing and explosions, and I was rewardes by a crude pop culture reference here and there, or a teenager-style joke.
Just like bottle of a cheap vodka, it will get you drunk, but won't create any memorable experience.
The DLCs are totally shameless, but that's what gaming marketing devolved into.
5/10 from me, with a hesitant "No" as a recommendation. If you like garish, mindless things, change it to "Yes".

SR3 is a solid third-person action game that doesn't take itself seriously, at all.  There's not a lot to say that hasn't been covered by other reviews.  I've had a ton of fun with this and would recommend it to anyone who enjoys tongue-in-cheek open-world action games.  I'll add a few points that may not be obvious from other reviews: first, the game runs pretty well on lower-end systems.  On my old system (core 2 duo, 2.6Ghz, 4Gb RAM, Nvidia 9600GT w/512MB) it ran well on lower settings and I never had any crashes or freezes, either in single-player or co-op.  The DLC also adds quite a bit of content, especially considering how cheap you can usually find it.  And lastly, the "community" option doesn't currently work for a lot of PC players, and hasn't for quite some time.  This means that if you're planning on getting this game, creating a character, and bringing the same character design into SR4, that probably won't work.  Deep Silver says that it became an issue when a lot of the THQ servers went down, presumably during the bankruptcy, but this feature has been down and unavailable for around 4 months, maybe longer?  Just something to be aware of before you spend the money, since that matters to some players.

Personal Rating: 6 of 10
Saints Row the Third is Open Sandbox game where you can unleash your monstrosity to the public with the selection of arsenal and vehicles of mass destruction and on top of that with a dash of bland tasteless humor. I was looking forward to this game, being played and really enjoyed Saints Row 2, and I must say this game was a big let down.
First off, the story is not that engaging and each mission simply feels like run 'n' gun which is something you can do by provoking the law enforcement or other gang. Only different is the missions puts you in a building (where some mission uses the same building again and again) instead of the street. As the story progresses, the missions feels dull, repetitive and you simply continue play for the sake of progressing. The game designer made a few changes to the game notably the unlockables. You play missions, perform stunts, complete side quests and etc. to gain respects. As the respect levels up, more perks are unlocked and you can purchase them such as more ammo, durable cars and; well the usual stuff. Right from the start, you can literally play god if you kept doing the side quests and challenges and eventually you will gain the amount of money and respect to unlock these perks.
Secondly, the graphics was a nice upgrade from the predecessor but nothing groundbreaking or jaw droppping. The designer decided to add in humor factor and thus you no longer get the realistic gangster feels. Personally, I don't mind breaking off from the conventional sandbox games like Watch_Dogs and GTA but it just feels weird having a gangster theme game with cartoonish and plasticky models. The soundtrack also does not captures you or brings the game out to life; it just doesn't click disregard on what radio channel you listen when playing. The only time which I actually felt hilarious and chivalrous was the last mission with the music being played.
Lastly, bugs. This game is infested with tonnes of them but they have this character respawning system whenever you are stuck which is nice. And there is an achievement in the game that you cannot unlocked because the community feature of this game is broken (rumors saying that THQ shut down the servers after selling off the franchise). The developers/moderators (from official community) claimed there are indeed fixing the issue but it has been around for a year or so. There are graphical, physics, ragdoll glitches but since the game is humor based, I don't if I can classify them as bugs or developer intended (like Goat Simulator).
Overall, if you manage to pick this game up for a couple of bucks its all worth it. Beyond that, even with all the DLCs this game fails to live up its reputation or what the game designer had intended.

Just a disclaimer before you read on that if you want an in-depth review on whether or not to buy this game then this may not be the review for you because I’m going to be mainly focusing on replayability.
In my opinion there are not that many games out there that have as much replay value as Arma 3 (if you know any that are just as or more replayable then please share). For example, there are loads of different server types each giving a fresh experience; be it the jolly cooperation of the Invade and Annex servers, the lone wolf survival of Wasteland servers (you can also be in teams) or roleplaying as whoever you want in an Altis Life server. This is only a handful of the vanilla multiplayer options available. There is also a decent campaign to play in singleplayer and with a few good scenario mods you can have endless mission possibilities. There are, of course, mods for multiplayer which increases the server type variety even more.
The excellent replayability is just one of the many pros of this game so without a doubt I highly recommend picking this game up. You won’t be disappointed!

Saints Row 3 is a really fun game. The map is fun to explore, and the activities are fun and diverse. The one thing that this game does best is the opening. In the first 2ish missions you rob a bank, rob an armory, jump out of a plane, and jump back in a plane only to jump out of it again! It does a good job of making you feel like a bad@$$. The dialouge is hilarious, and there are some really funny running gags (such as the chess one). My one complaint would be that after the second mission Johnny Gat dies. The weapons are really cool like the rc gun where yu can hack into a civilians vehicle and drive around, or the reaper drones where you pretty much can control an air strike. The respect system was greatly improved from saints row 2. In 2 it acted as a system where you could only do a mission if you had one bar, but here it acts as a system where the higher your level, the better the character upgrades you can get. However, I felt a lot less motivated to do the activities now, and I hardly did them at all (not because they weren't fun, but because I didn't need to.) This is one game where I would also recomend getting the dlc for it. You get new activities, smissions, weapons, and vehicles. They are really solid and I had a great time with them. You don't need to play the previous games to understand whats going on, but Saints Row 2 is a great game. There are references to the previous games, but nothing that will ruin it in any way (for example I haven't played the first one, but I still was able to understand 2 and 3) Overall, Saints Row 3 is a great game if you want to shoot a lot of people and have a good laugh (and even if you aren't it is still really good.)

Arma 3 is in one word; Amazing.
There are cons to this game however, nothing is perfect, but I think that the list of pros does make this game great.
I'll start with the cons and pros.
Cons:
-Bad framerates at multiplayer, many players with high powered PC's still experience issues with framerate on large scale servers with many players, though this is only for huge servers.
-Controls are difficult to master and require time and practice since there are much controls that you don't typicaly see in other FPS's
-DLC's and expansions are overpriced, many will argue that this is false so I state that this is my opinion. The DLC's are somewhat not adding enough for the price except for the Marksman's DLC which is a fair deal, and the Apex expansion is very overpriced considering the game is 40$ and the expansion is 35$, You would expect to recieve 80% of content in relation to the game but you only get about 50%. Again, this is my opinion and others will say it's fair.
-Millitary simulation: (This can be a pro to many therefore I shall place it aswell at the pros list) There are many real millitay concepts here, if you're looking for a more casual game, this might not suit you well.
Pros:
-Amazing quality, both in aspects of graphics and features. The game is filled with quality details to the maps and objects and with amounts of content of the base game.
-Replayabilty and scenarios: The campaign is long (in the good way), with a good story, good background and keeps you on the edge of your seat, there are scenarios and showcases that add more things to play and do, along with trainings for new players and veterans looking for improvment of their skills. Many multiplayer modes including the never-the-same Zeus gamemode keep you always entertained at games.
-Mods: The Steam workshop community has so many different addons from new gear and items up to complete campaigns, all easily controlled by the game launcher and have very little chance of causing problems to the original content. Besides the Steam workshop, there are other sources of mods on the internet that have even more content that can be easily installed with the game launcher.
-Editor: The in-game editor lets you create your own missions and publish them on the workshop or save them for yourself to play on your own server. The editor is simple to use, with many tutorials in-game or on the Community guides.
-Helpful community: From guides to friendly teamplayers, the community here is full of people willing to help and work together, I cannot say that is true 100% of the time, there are always some bad eggs yet the admins quickly put them in their place.
-Active developers: BIS is constantly working to fix bugs and bring new content to the game and they do it very quickly too.
-Millitary Simulation: Unlike other titles, this is a less casual one and offers genuine millitary concepts, if you're a millitary enthusiast then this game may suit you well.
Overall:
For the price of 40$ you get a great package of a high quality game with endless content and with high quality players.
It never feels like there's nothing new to do and you can always keep playing more and more. The sandbox features are amazing and keeps all options clear.
I definetly reccomend it.

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

I believe this game has under-sold in what it offers, since it gives us this great amount of content with more to come and more to be made by us.
Cheap DLC, and great expansion(s) are a huge plus that I am willing to purchase.
All my hours are on the multiplayer, and some on the single player/coop aspect. It's just perfect that we can play game modes like Wastelands and many others like KotH without getting bored since It's nearly impossible for us to reach the end of the infinite possibilities that this games offers us.
Three years later, and the graphics still look fresh (with some ups and downs).
NOW, the main negative point is the optimization (or the lack thereof). This game is a MESS when it comes in that department. Nvidia or AMD, this game is VERY CPU bound, and I have an i7 4790k ffs. On normal ops and missions this game runs decently, but those aren’t the reasons I bought and play the Arma series. I play KotH, Wasteland and Altis life. Those game modes aren’t optimized for anybody, ranging from 16 fps on my last AMD CPU build to sometimes 30 (on the start of a server restart). And, 22 fps to sometimes 54 (on the start of a server restart or empty server) on my current i7 build. The Newest Dayz build runs like a Source game compared to this.
Verdict: If you like tactical gunplay, open maps, and low framerate. Buy this game

Let me be straight here. This is a very fun game. However, I don't have the fastest computer. Actually, it's quite a bit on the slow side, and this is the ONLY reason why I can't recommend this game to everyone. If you do have a fast computer, ignore all this, this game is REALLY goddamn fun, go get it.
After a good handful of story missions, about two hours or so into the game, you go storm a big tower that's filled with a bunch of goons. Midway through this mission, you have to fight a big special enemy on top of a falling object, where a cutscene takes place, after which you only have to get the enemy to about a quarter of his health before he falls off and dies. However, if your computer isn't the fastest, like mine is, this cutscene fails to load, and the game thinks he's a normal enemy, that you have to deplete all his health to move on, which is impossible, since you're only given about 3 seconds. As such, you die in one hit when he knocks you off instead, and you have to keep repeating this over and over until you give up.
No method of in-game cheating fixes this, not even pure invincibility or guns that would kill extremely quickly, the only fix I would think of is downloading a save off the internet from someone else. As a result, you're stuck with a game that you can't finish, save for DLC missions, which is extremely disappointing.

What I liked about this game: Just about everything. It's an excellent port of one of the best sandbox/crime games of the last generation.
It's got the absurd fun of the PS2 era GTA games with the graphics and environment almost as good as GTA4 (props to rockstar).
The combat is fun and feels active. The story is humorous. The amazing interactions with your fellow gang-members are brilliant. It's the best Saints Row game, edging out the pretty awesome SR2.
What I don't like: The weapons. I always just end up using the pistols, and rarely the assault rifle. Everything else feels redundant to me. Shotgun has no range, SMG has no accuracy. The specials are fun but not practical for every fight. I feel like they could have done a better job with weapon diversity and balance.
The upgrade system makes you overpowered by the end of the game if you focus on health boosts and damage resistance. By the end of my first playthrough (x360) I was immune to almost all types of damage and had unlimited ammo.
Also: If you buy the complete package, the DLC will auto install and you'll start the game way stronger than you're supposed to be, with more vehicles, weapons, and perks than you should have.
Regardless, game is mad fun.

There isnt a single minute when playing SR3 that you arent aware that its a GTA clone, so its probably only fair that we mention GTAIV in the review of the game. When GTAIV was released, it was a game changing moment for the industry. It was large and pretty and to get there, Rockstar sacrificed a lot of the gameplay from GTA: San Andreas. For the whole, gamers gave their approval and the bar was set - we would now have big, empty games where the need for graphics outweighed the need for gameplay and the rocky road to The Last of Us began.
Saints Row 3 is the antidote to this decision. It allowed Rockstar to keep the dating, the awful minigames and the pointless collecting, providing it could keep all the fun stuff from GTA: San Andreas. In many ways Saints Row 3 is a throwback to Vice City and is the game GTAIV could, and probably, should have been. It has one aim - to provide you with a game that is fun, and it does that in spades. Noticeably, the entire map is unlocked from the start (though not all the sub-missions arent), you are introduced to tanks and missiles by only the third mission amd there are dozens of unlocks to improve your gameplay right from the start and added to continuously during the game.
The game is essentially a sandbox gangster game with a different gang to the GTA universe. The gangs in SR3 are fun and straightforward. You may argue that the general tone is less mature that GTA, but I would completely disagree. The humour may be, at times, peurile - but it doesnt have the massive problems with women that all the GTA games have; nor does it crave attention with its earnest portrayal of violence. Its GTA that lacks maturity.
SR3 does come wrapped up with lots of DLC, none of which is essential. Its a relatively easy game, which gets easier if you level up through the sub-missions. If you have never played a Saints Row game then choose SR4: it is essentially exactly the same game as SR3 but with slightly more content. But as a standalone game, SR3 is excellant and I just wish the games industry made more games like this nowadays.

This game was by far the best First Person Shooter I have ever played in my life, and with the new Jungle Inferno update (aka the Pyro Update), it’s better than ever! With 9 classes to suit your playstyle, several different maps and game modes (including the Mann vs Machine game mode, which is my personal favorite), and MANY customization options, Team Fortress 2 (or TF2 for short) is an amazing game for players who love first person shooters. All 9 characters are a fun challenge (except Pyro) that train the player to think efficiently in order to win. The characters are also very lovable in their own way. Every aspect of the game is amazing, and the best part is that it’s (kinda) FREE! Although you need to pay for some of the bigger things like Competetive, the player has many options to start with for free, not a single penny spent. The only complaints I have right now is that matchmaking is not always the best (although it has gotten better), there are long delays between updates, and the game seems to be a bit unstable for me (maybe it’s because of my computer, I dunno.). Otherwise, if you were to ask me if I recommend this game, I would say HECK YES!

A quick rant: Arma 3 could have surpassed Arma 2 in so many ways, and it has, but my biggest issue lies within the fact that the developers decided to move to a near future setting. That alone makes the game seem like less of a sim to me, and more of a Futuristic FPS with incredibly complex controls. The amount of content at the start was also quite lacking, deciding to use multiple varients of one rifle instead of making seperate platforms, making the game monotonous without mods to add in modern day weaponry.
That being said, if you can get past all of the glitches, poor optimization, obtuse control scheme, and incredibly fragmented comunity, this is by far one of the greatest games ever made. Arma 3 excels in one thing that is only equaled by Garry's Mod: Sandbox gameplay. This is less of a game and more of a set of tools to create and execute scenarios made by the community, whether it is a single player making small scenarios for themselves, or a team of creators making an expansive mission for their unit to play co-op with. This is bolstered by the excellent modding community, which is always active and looking to add more amazing content to this already great game. Arma 3 is what you make of it, so if you are into PVP or PVE, there is something in this game for you.

This game has too many bugs.
I've played this game for over 1600 hours and I kept thinking it would get better but it never did. Daybreak prioritizes new features and DLC (aka skins) over fixing the game.
Here are a few of the literally hundreds of bugs that have piled up in their backlog:
1. When a player exits a vehicle at the exact same instant that another player attempts to enter the vehicle, the person entering the vehicle becomes imprisoned in the vehicle and can't do anything. They must wait for someone to kill them or they must exit out of the match.
2. Dragging and dropping items in your inventory very often doesn't work. Items sometimes won't drag when you click them, items will sometimes get stuck to your cursor, items sometimes won't drop when released, it's very unreliable and it's a big part of the game.
3. Zooming with a sniper rifle or binoculars while behind cover will cause your character's line of sight to tilt upward toward the sky. This makes it impossible to peek around cover with a scoped weapon.
4. Being struck by a moving vehicle will sometimes kill you instantantly. Other times, you take no damage. It's completely random.
5. Landing on a vehicle while parachuting will often deal huge amounts of damage and can often kill you.
6. Cars explode instantly when they hit common obstacles at weird angles.
7. Cars sometimes won't drive when you get into them. They tell you they're out of gas when they clearly are not. You have to press the gas pedal twice in order to get the car to drive.
8. Grenades sometimes won't load. This is not a game mechanic, this is a bug. You have to drop the grenade and pick it up again in order to load it. Nevermind that it makes no sense to "load" a grenade.
Daybreak has known about these bugs for months and never bothered to fix them.
Instead, they pump out map changes and new skins.
I understand that this game is Early Access, but this is the buggiest Early Access game I've ever seen and it does not seem to me that Daybreak is interested in making the game better.

Some sandbox games are well respected for their realism. After all, it takes a lot to create a city, populate it, give players a chance to live in a virtual parody of reality, and at the same time do so in a way that draws players in an makes them feel they truly are in an enclosed living breathing world. Well grounded characters have to blend together with a physics engine that makes sense, because players are always going to be searching for that one thing that feels too inconsistent with what we know about the world today. So it's fairly impressive how well Saints Row: The Third draws in players considering that every ounce of realism is tossed right out the door within the first ten minutes, giving players an amazingly wild ride that features some of the most memorable (and believable) characters you'll ever have the pleasure of playing with in a sandbox game.
Don't get fooled by the fact that this is the third game in the series; even though the plot picks off right where the other games left off players are treated to a nice summary of the Saints' accomplishments prior to this installment. Having reached the height of their fame and popularity the local gang has become a bit full of themselves. They're now robbing banks with masks that look like their faces, cutting movie deals, and just generally getting used to the good life. This complacency eventually gets them into quite a bit of trouble, and soon the Saints find themselves in a new, unfamiliar city having to work their way back from the ground up.
Apart from the main story being a little predictable, it's a fantastic ride through and through. Part of this has to do with how over-the-top the action is in just about every situation. Stealing UAV bombing drones, skydiving from helicopters to crash parties and freefalling from an airplane while shooting through falling debris to kill rival gang members in mid air. These all set the tone at an early point in the game that the action is going to be consistently over the top and the player will get the experience all the best parts of it. With the mind already suspending a lot of belief that any of these things could ever happen it's easy to believe that the storyline is just background fluff for the experience, but the character interactions are so genuine that it's hard not to really feel for the Saints' cause.
There's absolutely no time wasted in any of the dialogue, no fillers with useless information, no string of swearing just for the need to be edgy, and in a world where players can dress up like vampire hookers driving a ice cream truck, while avoiding mutant hulks that throw people at you, being able to be to really connect with these characters so effortlessly is incredibly valuable.
But thankfully the character design isn't the only solid thing in Saints Row: The Third. Combat naturally plays a large role in attempting to carve out a gang empire and that's exactly where the game becomes additively satisfying. Guns are just about everywhere and take up the usual role in any third person shooter. There are sniper rifles, rocket launchers, pistols, machine guns, and all of them are simple as pointing and clicking away. Then, of course, you have weapons like the laser guided precision airstrike gun that summons up sharks, or mind-controlling squid gun (which naturally shoots out a squid which takes over any potentially hostile NPC). The sheer wackiness of some of the weapons that players get access to is both shocking and hilarious, and it's clear that only some sort of genius could ever come up with the vast array of weaponry featured in this game.
Melee weapons offer a little bit more versatility this time around, as some attacks can be used indefinitely, while others have limited use but offer special attacks like an explosive knockback. Melee itself plays another huge role in the game, and is arguably the most defining feature of the franchise.
Fluid, over the top, and a lot of fun, melee moves mix up the typical shooting elements of the game to great effect. Drop kicking one enemy only to run over and take another as a hostage, all without changing weapons or being forced to handle different mechanics, makes tackling a large group of foes very easy. This is good, because players only ever seem to fight a small horde enemies every time.
Naturally with weapons, cars, and gangsters come customization features, of which Saints Row 3 isn't remotely short of. Players are able to level up weapons, increasing both individual features and aesthetic looks over time. Vehicles on the other hand have just as many customization options as the player character does, and all of it is incredibly easy to control. Grabbing a car and tossing on a unique paint job is incredibly easy, and using cash earned in-game you can choose to tweak the frame of individual vehicles with little to no effort. Even those who are typically disinterested in visually tweaking cars should find that the quick and painless options offered make the process fairly fun.
Character customization on the other hand is a completely different beast altogether. Outside of editing a characters general face, height, gender, voice and all the other usual suspects players are allowed to dress their characters to an amazing extent. Visiting clothing stores throughout the city will grant players the option of shopping from that particular style and anything from business attire, street clothing, bondage gear, or just plain strange costumes. The selection is fairly large, made better only by the fact that players will generally find these stores by bumping into them mid-exploration rather than simply searching them out by necessity.
Another fantastic point of customization in Saints Row: The Third is how players are allowed to manage their in-game finances, with an offering of more than just customized weapons and crazy looking hats. Players can also purchase property all over the city that generates revenue every hour, or serves as alternative safe houses where players can store vehicles, weapons, or clothing. It's one of many different rewards for exploration that doesn't come in the form of finding hidden items.
Graphically there's not too much to be dissatisfied with when it comes to Saints Row: The Third, as it's an open world title that does everything it can to absolutely minimize any loading times. Naturally entering a special vehicle segments or a special indoor building will trigger a bit of loading, but for the most part players should find the entire experience relatively seamless. The soundtrack is also well done, being a great blend of scripted talk show radio work, satirical commercials, and real music. Special missions will often come along with a predetermined soundtrack, which sets the tone fairly well as long as you're in the mood to Kanye West or some other rap/rock artist.
Saints Row: The Third is, simply put, absolutely insanity at its best. While some sandbox titles strive for realism, or destructive scale, Saints Row: The Third instead takes a combination of all the features that have defined sandbox games as of late (driving, shooting, wandering large setpiece cities) alongside a blend of everything that defines how memorably wacky a game can be. There's very little in this title that wont satisfy most gamers, and that the entire game can be run through with co-op just adds to the fun. Getting every property, finding each hidden item, wiping out every gang and finishing every mission will naturally take a bit of time but the best part about Saints Row: The Third isn't about the hours you intentionally invest, it's finding out how much time you've lost having fun without ever realizing it.
