Well it's been a few years since I've played and man I'm ashamed to say the same old junk exist. I'll share what's still an issue and where the game has gone from first year to now.
The Bad
1) The "find a group" constantly pairs you with people who are already in a game. I mean WTF????
2) Sometimes jumping into games onto buildings with no exit or other "non-playable" areas causes your person's parachute to hang up for like 30 seconds. Super annoying.
3) OFTEN players are skipping around the screen with mega "lag spikes". I know for SURE it's not my PC or my internet. I'll restart, verify game integrity and ensure I'm within my best "server region". I ask other players if they get it and they say not as often as I;  but sorry, it happens to me too often and only within this game that I can't blame any technicals on my side for the issues.
4) Obviously hackers but not nearly as bad as it once was. However, you only need a small % to ruin it for a lot of people. At least they TRIED to clamp down on it after years of allowing their business model of profiting from hackers repurchasing over and over has probably died down a bit.
5) Player models outside of close range are just black outlines of players. That's so pathetic!
6) Hit registration is not very good but hey, at least it's consistantly inconsistent. But is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥when you wait 5 minutes to get into a game, 5 minutes to loot up only to have some random hit reg cause your death or prevent you from getting a hit you should get. BUT you have to add in the time it takes to get into another game (5 minutes to get in, 5  5 minutes to loot) ...so in actuality, it wouldn't be SO bad if it didn't mean that it would cost you ~20 minutes of your time. I'm sorry, but I value my time a bit more than this.
The Improved
1) Map has "filled in" to make the areas look less bland and plain.
2) City areas you won't have 2FPS with an i7-6700k / 1080GPU like before.
3) # of cars and car physics greatly improved.
Sorry, but after 3+ years to have these "blocker" type bugs still present and/or aren't fixed in a timely manner is simply not an excuse for a title with so many copies sold.
Will they eventually fix them? Probably, but will take another year to do so!
The game style is still fun but you didn't invent the game style. You should get credit for how you execute the game style and you're still slow at creating a bugless interaction that rarely impedes on a players ability to play the game without wasting lots of time suffering through them.
If the game went on sale for $9.99, I would say it's worth it. But for $20, there are other similar titles that I would recommend purchasing first.

TL;DR: Bad optimization, but amazing graphics, Fantastic versatility though lacking in total content, a bit lacking on equipment but overall enjoyable
9/10
Lets start with the infantry combat
9.5/10
I LOVE the infantry combat in A3, it is incredibly immersive, and intense. One of my biggest issues in shooters is movement, it always feels too restrictive, in this case the different ways in which I can move and lean in order to stay in cover or provide a good shooting position are fantastic. The recoil and the fatiuge although irritating are very well done, the infantry wheight system as a whole is enjoyable and just adds to the experience. The only bad thing I have to say about infantry is the weapons, the variety is somewhat lacking. Yes the attatchment system is fantastic and at first it seems like you have alot of guns to choose from but even with apex the majority are just copies of a base gun with different barrell lengths and stocks.
Next, Vehicles.
9/10
Driving in Arma 3 is an enjoyable experience, the helicopter flight models are great as are the vehciles no real complaints here. My problem is with jets. The flight models feel clunky and are overall just not fitting with the rest of the vehicle models. Another problem with the jets is that each faction only has one, NATO: A futuristic A-10, CSAT: An arma version of the Yak - 130 which is a light attack aircraft, and AAF: the Buzzard which we all remember as the Albatross from A2. The problem with this is that all of these are mainly ground attack aircraft, the buzzard is the only one with an AA configuration and it still sucks, you may find yourself wishing for a bit more variety here. Now onto the good things.
Barring jets the vehciles feel solid and are really fun to drive and fly [even the jets with their clunky flight models]. Vehicle mounted guns are just really fun to use, the heavier things like tanks especially so with their auto ranging and lock functions.
Finally the engine and game content
These are really my biggest problems with Arma 3: AI, and Content.
Lets start with content. Take away all the DLC that costs money [everything save for zeus] and you are left with some pretty restrictive choice, there is almost no variety. Even with all the pricey DLC after a while equipment still feels lacking, regardless if its Guns, Cars, Helicopters, or Jets everything is a bit too small of a category.
Next we have AI. The. God. Damn. Proximity. Detection.
This AI detection is some of the most irritating stuff ive ever seen, especially for ZEUS missions. it makes stealth near impossible sometimes.
Finally I want to talk about versatility
This review is recommending you buy Arma 3 I've pointed out the flaws but how I still love most of the systems. Even AI which ive complained about being a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥for ZEUS, im still a Zeus fanatic. The biggest selling point to me for A3 is the sheer versatility of the game. You can do things ranging from the most extreme milsim missions to extreme life roleplay to dicking around with zombies. The game is incredibly versetaile in the different ways you can use it and I love this, and the sheer beauty of the graphics only adds to this. Yes its lacking in content and optimization and even though I want these fixed they dont stop me from enjoying the hell out of this.
Again overall 9/10 I highly reccomend you buy this if you like simulation, regardless if its life, or military. It may have a steep learning curve but its worth the time

Oh Saints Row... where do I begin?
PROS:
~Copious amount of customization. This was probably the biggest selling point for me. The sheer number of hairstyles, outfits, and costumes for characters was really fantastic for anyone who values character creation/customization. Vehicle customization is also incredible and almost every vehicle has many mods that can be applied to it, not to mention the multitude of colors and wheels that can be applied.
~Ridiculous gameplay. Not as "out-there" as SR IV, but it had its silly moments. I never had a boring experience in this game, save for some of the early missions which are based on activities. By the end of the game, you can unlock damage negation to just about everything except for melee weapons (for whatever reason), unlimitied sprint, boost for all cars, all of which make the gameplay more about just having fun.
~Infinite replay value. Like most open world games, it's hard to run out of things to do. In the immediate post-story game you can complete any and all activities that you haven't already, you can purchase all stores for additional income, there are DLCs that can be completed at any time, and there are some optional side missions to keep you entertained. In the long-run, once everything you can possibly do is done, you can still resort to doing whatever the hell you want because it's Saints Row and its just pure fun.
CONS:
~Multiplayer with lesser computers. Saints Row was built for consoles, there's no denying that, and because of that, the way multiplayer syncs up with your partner is through framerate. That means if I'm running it at 60fps, and my friend is running it at 10fps (because their computer is garbage) then your characters are going to warp around because the game can't sync. This was never a problem for me because I never played with that person, but if your computer is low-tier, I would stay away from multiplayer.
~Pierce. Pierce is in this game and I kept waiting for a mission where I could choose whether or not he can continue his existence. There was no mission to kill Pierce. Fortunately, you can *SPOILER* sell-out Birk.
TL;DR:
I don't think I have ever had this much fun with a game. In terms of fun and rewarding gameplay, story missions that didn't get old, and laughs from the excellent writing and zany gameplay, it has not disappointed me.
9.9/10
FINAL THOUGHTS:
Buy this game, I honestly had more fun with it than Saints Row IV because vehicles and weapons still have purpose in this one.

4) Obviously hackers but not nearly as bad as it once was. However, you only need a small % to ruin it for a lot of people. At least they TRIED to clamp down on it after years of allowing their business model of profiting from hackers repurchasing over and over has probably died down a bit.

BUT you have to add in the time it takes to get into another game (5 minutes to get in, 5  5 minutes to loot) ...so in actuality, it wouldn't be SO bad if it didn't mean that it would cost you ~20 minutes of your time. Sorry, but after 3+ years to have these "blocker" type bugs still present and/or aren't fixed in a timely manner is simply not an excuse for a title with so many copies sold.
Will they eventually fix them? Probably, but will take another year to do so!
The game style is still fun but you didn't invent the game style. You should get credit for how you execute the game style and you're still slow at creating a bugless interaction that rarely impedes on a players ability to play the game without wasting lots of time suffering through them.

TL;DR: Bad optimization, but amazing graphics, Fantastic versatility though lacking in total content, a bit lacking on equipment but overall enjoyable
9/10
Lets start with the infantry combat
9.5/10
I LOVE the infantry combat in A3, it is incredibly immersive, and intense. One of my biggest issues in shooters is movement, it always feels too restrictive, in this case the different ways in which I can move and lean in order to stay in cover or provide a good shooting position are fantastic. The recoil and the fatiuge although irritating are very well done, the infantry wheight system as a whole is enjoyable and just adds to the experience. The only bad thing I have to say about infantry is the weapons, the variety is somewhat lacking. Yes the attatchment system is fantastic and at first it seems like you have alot of guns to choose from but even with apex the majority are just copies of a base gun with different barrell lengths and stocks.
Next, Vehicles.
9/10
Driving in Arma 3 is an enjoyable experience, the helicopter flight models are great as are the vehciles no real complaints here. My problem is with jets. The flight models feel clunky and are overall just not fitting with the rest of the vehicle models. Another problem with the jets is that each faction only has one, NATO: A futuristic A-10, CSAT: An arma version of the Yak - 130 which is a light attack aircraft, and AAF: the Buzzard which we all remember as the Albatross from A2. The problem with this is that all of these are mainly ground attack aircraft, the buzzard is the only one with an AA configuration and it still sucks, you may find yourself wishing for a bit more variety here. Now onto the good things.
Barring jets the vehciles feel solid and are really fun to drive and fly [even the jets with their clunky flight models]. Vehicle mounted guns are just really fun to use, the heavier things like tanks especially so with their auto ranging and lock functions.
Finally the engine and game content
These are really my biggest problems with Arma 3: AI, and Content.
Lets start with content. Take away all the DLC that costs money [everything save for zeus] and you are left with some pretty restrictive choice, there is almost no variety. Even with all the pricey DLC after a while equipment still feels lacking, regardless if its Guns, Cars, Helicopters, or Jets everything is a bit too small of a category.
Next we have AI. The. God. Damn. Proximity. Detection.
This AI detection is some of the most irritating stuff ive ever seen, especially for ZEUS missions. it makes stealth near impossible sometimes.
Finally I want to talk about versatility
This review is recommending you buy Arma 3 I've pointed out the flaws but how I still love most of the systems. Even AI which ive complained about being a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥for ZEUS, im still a Zeus fanatic. The biggest selling point to me for A3 is the sheer versatility of the game. You can do things ranging from the most extreme milsim missions to extreme life roleplay to dicking around with zombies. The game is incredibly versetaile in the different ways you can use it and I love this, and the sheer beauty of the graphics only adds to this. Yes its lacking in content and optimization and even though I want these fixed they dont stop me from enjoying the hell out of this.
Again overall 9/10 I highly reccomend you buy this if you like simulation, regardless if its life, or military. It may have a steep learning curve but its worth the time

There's always a little bit of suspension of disbelief in video games. You're supposed to buy into ideas like an inexperienced kid beating up 20 guys, or armor being lighter when you tuck it into your backpack, or NPCs dying in cutscenes when you have the means to ressurrect fallen party members.
Saints Row comes in and says, "Hey, this stuff isn't believable anyways... so let's have fun with it."
It's a game reminiscent of Borderlands where the focus is less on creating a believable world and more on EXPLOSIONS, and man is it gorgeous to experience. The humorous dialogue, the no-holds barred characters, and scenarios so outrageous that even your character will point out how nuts it is. Even the tutorial area begins the game on a high note, from the moment a grandma pulls a gun on you to wrestling matches with crime bosses, the silliness just doesn't stop.
Yet it never ceases to be amusing, and it is constantly being unpredictable. The characters aren't deep, but they're funny and they help make Saints Row 3 a great romp for anyone who wants to kick back and blow stuff up.

I have to say, this game has an... interesting history. Being a game that is 10 years old, and still getting active support it definitely has a longevity that can't be denied.
It's easy to say that 90% of Valve doesn't care about it, and you'd be right, but the remaining 10% are clearly passionate about it. I mean, at the time of writing, it's gotten one of the biggest and best updates it's had in a long time (New weapons!!!), and that alone managed to double the size of it's already sizable playerbase.
The weapon and class balance is out of whack for sure, but that's something that the dev team is currently working on (if they aren't fixing bugs included by the Jungle Inferno update). There IS competitive matchmaking, but it's slow as hell to get to a match, and that's coming from someone who lives in the blessed land of this game's matchmaking (Seattle). You'd be lucky to find a match at all. It's also♥♥♥♥♥♥ so it's not worth trying in the slightest at the moment. There IS some comp fixes in the works, but who knows when it's coming. This is Valve we're talking about.
For a F2P game there are surprisingly fer P2W elements. The most you'll have to spend is $1-2 USD and you're set. More if you want the new cosmetic items, but give it some time, and those will be available for free. The game's item economy is so large, that after some patience and effort, you can actually make money off of these items. A considerable amount, too.
The community can be toxic, but don't expect them every single match. Also, like any large multiplayer game, there are some unwritten rules you should take note of. I recommend you learn what a friendly is at the very least.
The skill required can be daunting, but given time, you can learn everything this game has to offer (Rocket jumping, sticky jumping, surfing, playing spy, etc.)
Conclusion: Good game. Has it's problems, some of them being pretty significant, but it's still fun. The most played game in my library, as a matter of fact.

Some kind of a middle-ground between Microsoft Flight Sim and Call of Duty, Arma 3 aims for realistic military strategy and deployment. Unlike a standard first-person shooter this doesn't manifest as a "gritty" and "hard boiled" experience, more rather it can bring to your attention just how hum-drum and by-the-numbers modern warfare can be waged.
Arma goes for such a hands-on touch that means in order to be effective in practically any deployment you must first familiarize yourself with the standards of calibrating your weapons for the specific range of the enemy you are engaging, and many encounters can be as simple as spotting an enemy combatant and relaying their bearing and distance from your position to an artilleryman.
To many this can be boring, but there is a rare value in such authenticity. That being said the scope of the base game is best left behind in favor of a modded gametype, and indeed the vast majority of working servers do require many mods to play. It can take a fair amount of time to properly set-up and play a modded game of Arma, but it should be known that Arma is workshop compatible and contains incredibly easy-to-use modding tools in it's own launcher.
Between finding players, setting up mods and generally familiarizing yourself with the game, it can take very long to get started, but thankfully the result is fantastic and completely unique, if a little buggy.

Saints Row 3 had a lot of potential to be something great. However, the company ruined this game, dumbed things down, and released just an okay product. Saints Row 2 is head and shoulders above this game, there's no competition.
SR3 lacks the fun factor that SR2 had.
The world in SR3 is boring, dull, and dead.
There's very few things to do in this game and they're all short.
The story is fairly bad, makes little sense, and isn't as funny as it should be.
Customization is lacking A LOT. SR2 not only had a lot better customization, but it just had better looking character models in my opinion. These new characters are just too bulky looking.
The customization colors are lacking. The colors change from clothes to clothes and car to car, they also give you very little range in terms of shade.
The combat is decent but very unpolished. It's just clunky and doesn't work the way it should.
Upgrades are a joke
Low variety of weapons (they feel the same and don't change much, there's just too few of them)
You can't pick up random objects and use them as weapons (like in SR2)
Overall, it's a good game, just doesn't compare to SR2 in terms of quality and quantity. It tried to be over-the-top funny but it just ended up being stupid and boring. I have beat the game almost entirely (just a couple missions left) and so it does have a decent length if you do all of the assassinations, car jacking, challenges, and activities.
If you're looking for a decent game with okay gameplay that will last you a few weeks, this is a possible choice. I highly recommend purchasing Saints Row 2 for the consoles (pc port has issues, but runs good for me). I had high hopes for Saints Row, but sadly they've officially killed the series with SR4 being even worse.

When looking at the Saints Row series, it is important to distinguish the pattern that emerges...
Saints Row: This game opens as a serious role-playing game with an urban setting where you join the Third Street Saints and partake in their endeavors led by their charasmatic leader, Julius. I took it as a well made spin-off of the Grand Theft Auto series with a solid story.
Saints Row II: What occurred to me is that the game developers realized their series would not be able to compete as well as Grand Theft Auto, so they spiced it up a bit. This game begins to introduce the one key element that sets this series apart: "Over the top".
Saints Row: The Third: This game is the one that is known to have "perfected the Saints Row formula". It fully develops the outrageous, hilarious, and "over the top" theme with the plot, action, and characters. Saints Row: The Third
+ Pretty good graphics.
+ Lots of distractions and diversions to take part in and the main storyline has decent length. The game took me about 60 hours to complete.
+ Wide selection of weapons to use in-game, including rifles, explosives, submachineguns, pistols and shotguns.
+ Ability to customise your character with different voices, taunts and appearance prior to game commencement.
- Story is meh, moves away from the traditional gangster theme seen in Saints Row 2. It's a bit whacky in its approach. Saints Row: The Third is not a serious game. Some people will like this, others won't. Personally I didn't like it.
- While there are many optional activities to partake in, most of these are repetitive and are exactly the same as the tasks given in Saints Row 2. No variety here...lazy development. Considering these activities are designed to soak up a core amount of gameplay time, it really does impact on the quality of the title.
Overall Score: 7/10

Saints Row... Most would say it's a copy of GTA. But it's much more... weird. That's why it's so awesome.
In SR:TT our gang robbed a bank. But something went wrong, and they got caught by cops they couldnt bribe. It came out that bank they attempted to rob belonged to The Syndicate. After declining "very good" offer from boos of the organisation, they fight they way out from plane (loosking one of characters), and end up in Steelport, broke because of The Syndicate's hackers. They have to build their empire in this city, and kick Syndicate's ♥♥♥. So thats for the background.
Steelport is a big city, so it offers a lot of fun- starting with missions, to regular fight with police, just for fun. At the beggining of the game we create our own character, and only limitation is our imagination. Macho, typical blonde girl, or Conchita Wurst lookalike - up to you. You can further personalise your character, for example by visiting tatoo shops, clothers shops, or plastic surgeon. Anytime you want.
Important thing in a game is your phone. Here you can see the map, call for help from gang mates, buy upgrades and start missions. It's pretty convenient if you ask me.
Upgrades.. by progress in game and leveling up, you unlock more ways to waste your money. Whoops, sorry - making your character invincible to everything can help. Too bad it's available at the end of the game, but still. Making your character faster, mates more effective and ability to call vechicle anytime? I like that!
And vechicles... in game there are 3 types of vechicles- air, ground and water. Air ones get unlocked mostly by story progress, water by purchasing right building, and ground ones... If you steal any of them and go to your garage, you got it. And you can pay for upgrading it. Want red cop car with spikes on the wheels and booster? Sure, why not? Big pink SWAT car? You got this. All up to you. Just to add, flying is much more enjoyable that in GTA. ANY GTA.
Weapons. You get around 7 slots, eeach for diffrent weapon type. Meele, pistol, SMG, shotgun, AR and special. You can pick a weapon of your choice from available guns for that slot. You want Laser Rifle more than AK made into Machine gun? Okay. Sawed-off instead of Laser Shotgun? Okay. Gigant♥♥♥♥♥♥♥for katana? Sure. Most of them can be upgraded, so Deagle can fire explosive rounds, Sawed-off can set enemy on fire and so on.
Side missions. There are a few types, from driving your mate around and making business, taking part in deadly reality show, to rampage with a tank. Just for fun. They are requied to take over a district, along with purchasing properties. What for? Fun. And achivements.
To sum up, i cant really think about anything against SR3. Total personallistion of... everything? Check.
Interesting mechanics? Check.
Great story (as excuse to destroy everything) and awesome characters? Big F...ing Check!
Oooh, no wait. There are minuses. Motorbikes (i hated them...). DLCs (so much, paid and requied for geting every achivement possible). But anyway, thoose are just a small problems. Game itself? Awesome!

This is one of those rare, beautiful games where you can sink hundreds of hours into, and never even see another player. In the 400ish hours that I've logged in at the time of writing this review, I have spent maybe 9 or 10 hours playing multiplayer. In my opinion, the multiplayer isn't even worth it most of the time. The most popular game-modes are King of the Hill, Wasteland, Exile, and Altis/Stratis Life.
King of the Hill puts Blufor vs Opfor vs Independent against each other, for control of a small area (usually a village with towers). While this game mode can be fun at times, it typically becomes a lag fest, since you're looking at populations of around 150 players. That means you'll see players rubber-banding, appearing to phase through walls, and some shots not registering.
Wasteland does the same team setup, except there are gun shops, random events, and most servers will have you starting off with nothing more than a pistol (although some will spawn you with a rifle). This is a survival game-mode, and the looting system is on par with Day-Z (although no zombies) if you're familiar, which means when you die, it is all gone. This game mode, much like Day-Z, is a constant killfest. If you are Opfor or Blufor, you aren't allowed to kill other team-mates, but the independent team (which is always the predominant team) can kill everybody, including other independents. So either you try to survive with other team-mates, only to be overrun by independents who know each other outside of the game, and team up on everybody, or you get spawn killed 24/7 as an independent.

The real masterpiece in this game, is the Eden editor. You select a map you want, and you are given every human, gun, item, vehicle, etc. in the game, and you can spawn them in as you please. Bottom Line:
Get it on a console system instead of PC!!!  Don't pay much for this game no where you get it.  The PC version is a little bit buggy, though not as bad as Saints Row 2.  It will occasionally crash on you, so SAVE EVERY FIVE MINUTES.  It is more stable than SR2 and the graphics are slightly better.  The price for better stability and graphics is a smaller game world with fewer activities and challenges, fewer player/vehicle customization options, and fewer "cribs" to call home in the game.  And the story is pretty ridiculous.  Still, it can be fun if you get it for really really cheap.
So you play as the leader of the gang "Third Street Saints."  In SR1, you rose through the gang ranks and then got blown up at the end, wound up in a coma.  In SR2, you rebuilt the gang as its leader, since all the old members were dead or gone; you defeated all the rival gangs in the city and took over the biggest corporation around.  Now this game starts up some time after that.  Your gang is now a media empire, with commercials and movie rights and all that.  You start off bringing an actor on a "staged" bank robber (which really isn't so staged) to give him the right experience to play the lead role in the new Saints movie.  Things quickly go wrong and once again the Saints gang is defeated and torn down.  Now you're in a new city, fighting a new group of gangs and the triad.  So basically you have to expand your criminal empire into this new territory.
It's like GTA 3 in a lot of ways.  You can kill people, rob shops, steal cars and helicopters, and do a series of missions to advance the main game story.  You can also do several types of mini-game events all over the city:  drive a hooker and john around town for a good time, drive a flaming ATV around and set things on fire, base-jumping, insurance fraud, etc.  All the old favorites from SR2 are back.  You can also purchase shops and certain other properties in the city.  Each one you buy increases your allowance which you earn every half hour of play time or so.  Money is used to buy ammo, upgrade guns, and buy skills and such for your character and your gang.  You still earn reputation points just like in SR2, but now each reputation level will unlock some new upgrades... but you still have to pay some cash to activate each upgrade.  And there are A LOT more reputation levels in this game.
The city in this game is yet another series of islands and bridges, but it's smaller than SR2's Stilwater.  Also, you don't get calls every so often to go defend a certain territory.  Instead, you might get a call to do a "survival" mission where you just have to survive several waves of enemies each lasting for a set time limit.  Some of them are pretty tough, since the cops will bring in the military with tanks and helicopters in this game once your heat gets bad enough.  That, and there are gang action activities where you find a bunch of rival gang members who all get red icons over their heads when you get close;  kill the ones with the icons to win the event.
Another change since SR2 is now you have fewer options for clothing and vehicle parts and paints.  But in my opinion most of the clothing (particularly the DLC ones) looks better in this game than in the previous one.  You still can change your clothes one piece at a time, but you have fewer pieces in this game.
Anyway, give it a try if you enjoy games like Grand Theft Auto 2 or 3, and if you played and enjoyed Saints Row 2.  You don't need to play SR2 first though.

This is the game I wanted Grand Theft Auto IV to be. A wide-open world, tons of variety, tons of in-game content and tons of ridiculousness without venturing into outright parody.

The story was simple enough to understand my character's motivation, entertaining enough to get me to see what was next and challenging enough that I didn't feel bored or overwhelmed at any point.
Co-op doesn't add anything new to the experience (no new modes or anything), but it does make things go quicker and it's fun to either team up or try and sabotage one another's actions. It's unobtrusive and unnecessary but still viable and enjoyable, which is just how co-op ought to be.
If you're a fan of the 3D-era GTA games or a fan of open-world games in general, you owe it to yourself to play this game. If you've been disappointed by the newer GTA games and you want a return to ridiculousness, you'll find solace and renewed entertainment here.

I have to say, this game has an... interesting history. Being a game that is 10 years old, and still getting active support it definitely has a longevity that can't be denied.
It's easy to say that 90% of Valve doesn't care about it, and you'd be right, but the remaining 10% are clearly passionate about it. I mean, at the time of writing, it's gotten one of the biggest and best updates it's had in a long time (New weapons!!!), and that alone managed to double the size of it's already sizable playerbase.
The weapon and class balance is out of whack for sure, but that's something that the dev team is currently working on (if they aren't fixing bugs included by the Jungle Inferno update). There IS competitive matchmaking, but it's slow as hell to get to a match, and that's coming from someone who lives in the blessed land of this game's matchmaking (Seattle). You'd be lucky to find a match at all. It's also♥♥♥♥♥♥ so it's not worth trying in the slightest at the moment. There IS some comp fixes in the works, but who knows when it's coming. This is Valve we're talking about.
For a F2P game there are surprisingly fer P2W elements. The most you'll have to spend is $1-2 USD and you're set. More if you want the new cosmetic items, but give it some time, and those will be available for free. The game's item economy is so large, that after some patience and effort, you can actually make money off of these items. A considerable amount, too.
The community can be toxic, but don't expect them every single match. Also, like any large multiplayer game, there are some unwritten rules you should take note of. I recommend you learn what a friendly is at the very least.
The skill required can be daunting, but given time, you can learn everything this game has to offer (Rocket jumping, sticky jumping, surfing, playing spy, etc.)
Conclusion: Good game. Has it's problems, some of them being pretty significant, but it's still fun. The most played game in my library, as a matter of fact.

Simulation isn't the defining aspect of Arma. It's scale.
The enormity of the map is the foundation for the experiences that distinguish Bohemia Interactive's flagship franchise. It's what makes radios, topographical maps, binoculars, and compasses practical equipment in an FPS. It's what allows for kilometer-long headshots and coordinated convoy raids. It's what makes using your eyes to spot hints of enemies--muzzle flashes, tracers, gunsmoke--as valuable as being a crack shot.
The scale of Arma 3 dwarfs everything in the genre, including Arma 2. Altis, a keyhole, is a Mediterranean island-nation assembled from ruins, airports, coastal villages, solar power plants, military outposts, salt flats, and tank-friendly scrubland. It's a variegated backyard for you to play war in, but what's more significant is that Arma's landscape finally has the technology it deserves.
Arma 3 represents an aesthetic overhaul of the series. Unbelievable dynamic lighting, a volumetric cloud system, genuine vehicle physics, 3D weapon optics, ragdoll, noticeably improved weapon audio, and other grainy, eye-level details await scrutiny inside Arma 3's macro elegance. The best improvement is the merciful cutting of Arma 2's rigid, Tin-Man-without-oil combat animations, which makes infantry combat more responsive in your hands.

After buying Saints Row: The Third, quite a while back in a weekend sale, I wanted to play it for the longest time, however because my operating system was Windows 8 it didn't want to seem to play nice with my computer and I was unable to run it, after I recently updated my windows operating system from, Windows 8 to Windows 8.1, I can now fully play the game, so I decided that I might as well dive into it and play it, since I payed for it.
Thank god I did, because I have now found one of my favourite games, I love it, for the life of me I could not stop either playing it or thinking about playing it, I got that invested. People always moan about games not having great graphics or being current gen, or being the game that everyone is playing, however I personally play games to have a fun time, and did I have a good time? I can 100% say that this game has been one of the most funnest games I have played in quite a while.
I always hear people say that Saints Row is just a GTA rip off, but I totally disagree with that, GTA is more based around crime and drama, whereas Saints Row is based around its zaniness and how crazy a journey it decides to take you on and this game has it all, from naked levels to skydiving in a tank to zombies. I definitely recommend this game to anyone that likes laughing out loud at some of the most craziest things you will probably ever see in gaming.
Out of 10, I'd give this game an 8, the only slight problem I had with it was the difficulty in some places seemed a bit off, but for the price I payed, I can't really complain.

When I first bought Arma 3, it was nothing more than a clay giant, rough round the edges, very buggy and incomplete.
Multiplayer was a pain, due to the constant lag and server crashes, but this was early 2015, two years after the first release.
Spent almost 700 hours on it, mainly messing around with the editor and playing in a clan.
After a year, I left it to explore other games, as this is my usual behaviour on most titles.
Came back recently after the Laws of War content was released and I found it very changed, for the better. Lag is almost not anymore an issue and tons of details were added. The simulation level is very high during ground fights, but loses points when it comes to fly planes and helis; as I am a Digital Combat Simulator veteran, I am used to master-level flight simulation and I find the air content a bit too easy and incomplete. Multiplayer is more stable and the Apex update shows how hard developers have worked these two years, bringing Arma to its finest moment.
So, do not be affected by recent negative reviews, this game is a masterpiece of this age.
And then there's Arma 2 Operation Arrowhead as well, if you enjoy Middle Eastern conflict more.
PROS:
- Good gameplay mechanics
- Large scale conflict simulation
- Astonishing graphics
- Good dynamic environment
- Some good dlcs to get
- Interesting campaigns
- The Editor gives endless possiblities.
- Tons of mods
CONS:
- Simulation loses ground on choppers and planes, becoming more arcade
- Exploiters and script-kiddies still ravage multiplayer servers from time to time
- High priced dlcs may discourage some people despite their good content
9/10 very very very recommended.

I want to put on record that this game is LOTS of fun.
The one thing I can say about Saints Row the Third (SRTT) is how quickly it makes you forget your expectations and just have FUN.  It wants you to be random and just enjoy the game without consequences; something I suspect Volition went out of their way to ensure. The controls (aside from the still foreign weapon select) are tight and the controller integration is very solid (Thanks Team!) so it made SRTT a very enjoyable/playable experience to me.
The story is just hilarious, the graphics are still holding their own and the driving is just fantastic compared to other titles (I am looking at you GTA). In fact, every game should have a quick steal option for cars modelled after SRTT. This series has always done Character Creation well but this time around it is just MENTAL. There is a slider for EVERYTHING! You can truly make your character your own which is just an awesome finishing touch for this game.
My only two complaints with the game are prehaps the side missions could have had some degree of integration with the main story (aside from just being fun things to do) and that the story missions (whilst being selectable in the phone) didn't have a clear indication of which order you should play them in. I kind of just shotgunned an entire characters worth of story in a single hit and got a bit lost until I realised it tied in with other missions I hadn't played yet. These are just minor gripes however and you might have a completely different outlook on these issues.
So, should you buy it? Yes. It is cheesy, over the top wild action and I had a great time playing it. Well done Volition!

Saints Row the Third is the third title in the Saints Row series. But it's also a lot more different then the previous SR games. In this game the creators took a risky move and made it more like a comedy and not a serious gangster game. And it paid off, although they lost some fans of the series, but gained a lot more and kept the majority of old fans. It's hard to compare SR2 and SR3 because they became very different.OK, so the game starts when you and your gang are robbing a bank, but the robbery fails, and you get arrested. Later The Boss (you), Shaundi and Johny Gat are released to the man who owned the targeted bank, Phillipe Loren. Whos also a leader of the Syndicate. On Phillipe's private jet he offers to let the Saints live if they turn over most of their earnings, but you refuse the offer and break free. While getting out of the jet you and Shaundi jump out while Gat offers to cover you. And you end up in a new city, city of Steelport. Where you need to take down the Syndicate. First off all I want to say that they made a wonderful job with music in the game. It suits it really well, and can give goosbumbs while playing the game. The controls are really comfortable and easy. Visuals, graphics are well made, no more smoggy look like in SR2. Cinematics are very well made. The story is great, fun, it has a lot of jokes which makes it a lot more fun to play. There are a few things that I don't like though. Like no MP mode just coop, and for a lot of people coop lags. And there not as many of side missions as it was in SR2. In overall SR series made me to become their fan, and I highly recommend it for every one.

When I first heard of this game, I was really skeptical about buying it or not. A friend of mine recommended it, but I thought that It was a shallow GTA clone. Eventually, I decided to give the game a try. Games that give you a gender selection and don't "lock" you into playing a male or female, are always on top of my list.
At first, the game DID remind me of the GTA series, but it didn't take long for the story and how your character behaves to prove me wrong. This game has a class of it's own, it's fun, has really ridiculous missions (in a good way, of course), and it's highly addictive. The best part of this game, is that it never ends. Even if you get a 100% completion, you can repeat and re-do almost everything as many times as you wish, or completely ignore the missions, and free roam causing mayhem for no particular reason. There were even times when I found myself walking in the streets of Steelport, just for the heck of it!
Another strong feature of this game, is the character customization. It is very fluid and detailed, allowing you to make your character the way you wish. You can even buy clothes and weird props in order to make him/her look exactly like the character you imagined. The only downside to it, was the limited hair styles. That doesn't mean however that the game lacks a decent selection for the player to use. Best part, is that you can change your character's appearance (even gender, race and voice) whenever you feel like it, so it keeps the whole idea fresh.
Gameplay wise, the game has a "classic 3rd person action game" feel, with easy controls, and many variations, allowing you to shoot, hit, or even engage in "quicktime" events with your enemy. The vehicles you can use also add to the whole feeling, as each type has it's own unique behavior. Heck, you can even ride a tank!
In overall, the game is by itself a unique experience, and I highly recommend it. So if you're a fan of gangster action, comedy, madness and zombies (!), this game's definitely for you.

I'm a big fan of Sandbox games... a BIG fan. I love the GTA series and have played every one of the games. I love Mercenaries and Just Cause for there wacky obsession with dethroning military dictatorships. I love the experimental Sandbox games like Jak 2 and 3, or Sleeping dogs that mix melee combat and puzzle solving into the mix to spice things up.
The Saints Row franchise in particular has always been my favorite Sandbox game franchise of all time. Every game does something new and interesting in the name of fun and FUN alone. While many have complained about the wackier sense of tone and emphasis on over-the-top action, I for one embrassed them, defending the new identity the games EARNED after years of berate and unfair judgment by GTA fans (Which still occurs, sadly). Personally, I didnt much like SR3 when it first came out on the Xbox 360 (My former platform of choice) and found it a bit of a disappointment. Years later I pick this gem up in a sale as the complete version just to give it another chance, and surprisingly, I loved it WAY more than I did before. It baffles me as to why. Is it the additional content which i found fairly enjoyable? is it the significantly improved graphical and performance quality on the p.c using Direct X10-11? Is it the acceptance I felt after playing SR4 about a year prior to this review which I felt concluded the series beautifully? I cannot say. I appreciated the writing more even, which I remember hating but.. dont now? :I
+Great shooting and weapon variety, among the best in any Sandbox game and easily outdoes the GTA games.
+Solid graphics and art design, especially for a game from 2011. Direct X10-11 probably helped, and I'm glad they added it in :)
+Decent writing, but probably isnt for everyone. Still funny enough to me to feel confident as a plus side to the game.
+Lots of content! I remember thinking this game was short and refering to Angry Joe, he claimed the game was only like 15 hours? It sure as heck more than that! With the Full Package Edition upgrade for $5 (Big whoop) it's easily 60 hours for full completion on Normal Mode, in one playthrough... without coop. So if any says its too short, they are lieing!
+CO-OP!!!
+Excellent customization, and again, outdoes GTA.
+Decent soundtrack. Not the best in the series. It isnt as good as SR4's, and pales in comparison to SR2's, but it's got a pretty solid selection.
+FUN! FUN! FUN! FUN! FUN!
Easily worth $20, but I got it on a sale along with the other 2 games on steam with all their dlc for $13.75. ABSOLUTELY worth it regardless.

I knew what to expect going into Arma III from previous experience with Bohemia Interactive games, yet I was still overwhelmed by the amount of features I had to wrap my head around before I could play it with even moderate proficiency. It’s a first-person shooter alright, but it’s not another “left trigger to aim down the sights, right trigger to shoot” kind of game. You’re going to have to use almost every key on your keyboard, memorize specific key combinations and what each does depending on whether you’re on foot, in a tank, a helicopter, etc.
I felt comically inept fumbling through my first few hours. With so many different firing modes, stances, movement speeds, and other options, I had difficulty just walking, drawing my weapon and firing, to say nothing of using my equipment, making sense of the map, and working with my squad. I had to wonder what my AI squadmates thought of me, the clueless rookie, stumbling into the bushes before I accidently pulverized myself with a satchel charge I didn’t even mean to deploy.
To make matters even more difficult, in its current state Arma III doesn’t offer a real tutorial. Its Showcases (playable scenarios showing off its many features) follow a logical progression that introduce you to increasingly complicated mechanics. However, they each do a poor job of explaining how to use them or how they may be useful later on. The only real instruction comes in the form of on-screen hints that tell you which keys do what. It’s an inefficient method to teach you how to fly a helicopter, and practically useless when it comes to explaining the tactical value of more esoteric equipment and features.
In one of the more interesting Showcases you are given access to a non-lethal aerial drone and an armed ground vehicle drone which you can use to eliminate targets in a nearby town. After much experimentation, I devised a tactic of sending my aerial drone ahead to scout and tag targets, which then allowed me to coordinate mortar fire and corner enemies in the town. It was satisfying because it allowed me come up with a strategy which felt entirely my own, and one which nearly no other shooter could accommodate. On the other hand, there was a needless amount of frustration along the way that could have been avoided with clearer UI and better instruction.
ArmA III: Checking Out The New Content - Gamescom 2013
ArmA III: Checking Out The New Content - Gamescom 2013
10:10
As you can imagine, Arma III’s potentially much more enjoyable when you’re playing online with real people – especially those who already know how to play and can teach us its secrets. It doesn’t have a capped player limit, so in theory a server where 100 players are facing another 100 players in a gigantic sandbox where almost everything is possible is one of the best shooters I’ve ever played. But without investing long-term in a clan or other group that will ensure a reliable team of significant size, those are hard to come by. In practice, new players are presented with a list of servers half-full of random people who aren’t communicating, and where everything that can go wrong is going wrong. Since Arma III doesn’t offer obvious incentives for players to cooperate or even funnel them to the same areas of its enormous maps, multiplayer’s mostly uncurated chaos. It’s amusing in its own way, but something I would rather watch in a YouTube video than it play myself.
Counterintuitively, smaller matches are more fun for a new player trying to find his way in this world. In one pick up co-op game, six fellow players and I (and a group of AI bots) were tasked with a simple mission: find a way off the island. We spawned at a random spot along the coast and were given two locations, miles away, where we could find a boat or a helicopter for extraction. We ended up not even making it halfway to either destination, but I enjoyed our journey quite a lot. We heard a gunship in the distance and dashed across a field to take cover in a forest. We stumbled upon and successfully seized an enemy outpost, where we commandeered a truck. We arrogantly tried repeating the same strategy with a larger town on our way to an airfield... and were caught in the open by snipers. This is what developers mean when they talk about emergent gameplay, and it’s where Arma III shines.

After declining "very good" offer from boos of the organisation, they fight they way out from plane (loosking one of characters), and end up in Steelport, broke because of The Syndicate's hackers. They have to build their empire in this city, and kick Syndicate's♥♥♥♥♥ So thats for the background.
Steelport is a big city, so it offers a lot of fun- starting with missions, to regular fight with police, just for fun. At the beggining of the game we create our own character, and only limitation is our imagination. Macho, typical blonde girl, or Conchita Wurst lookalike - up to you. You can further personalise your character, for example by visiting tatoo shops, clothers shops, or plastic surgeon. Anytime you want.
Important thing in a game is your phone. Here you can see the map, call for help from gang mates, buy upgrades and start missions. It's pretty convenient if you ask me.
Upgrades.. by progress in game and leveling up, you unlock more ways to waste your money. Whoops, sorry - making your character  invincible to everything can help. Too bad it's available at the end of the game, but still. Making your character faster, mates more effective and ability to call vechicle anytime? I like that!
And vechicles... in game there are 3 types of vechicles- air, ground and water. Air ones get unlocked mostly by story progress, water by purchasing right building, and ground ones... If you steal any of them and go to your garage, you got it. And you can pay for upgrading it. Want red cop car with spikes on the wheels and booster? Sure, why not? Big pink SWAT car? You got this. All up to you. Just to add, flying is much more enjoyable that in GTA. ANY GTA.
Weapons. You get around 7 slots, eeach for diffrent weapon type. Meele, pistol, SMG, shotgun, AR and special. You can pick a weapon of your choice from available guns for that slot. You want Laser Rifle more than AK made into Machine gun? Okay. Sawed-off instead of Laser Shotgun? Okay. Gigant♥♥♥♥♥♥♥for katana? Sure. Most of them can be upgraded, so Deagle can fire explosive rounds, Sawed-off can set enemy on fire and so on.
Side missions. There are a few types, from driving your mate around and making business, taking part in deadly reality show, to rampage with a tank. Just for fun. They are requied to take over a district, along with purchasing properties. What for? Fun. And achivements.
To sum up, i cant really think about anything against SR3. Total personallistion of... everything? Check.
Interesting mechanics? Check.
Great story (as excuse to destroy everything) and awesome characters? Big F...ing Check!
Oooh, no wait. There are minuses. Motorbikes (i hated them...). DLCs (so much, paid and requied for geting every achivement possible). But anyway, thoose are just a small problems. Game itself? Awesome!

Arma 3 is a very fun game. It is, however, very demanding of computer resources. You'll most likely have to run it on low if you're using a medium to low end PC if you want any kind of framerate. The game itself is much more realistic than other shooter games like Battlefield, Insurgency, and, obviously, Call of Duty. The game takes into account bullet drop, bullet origin, sight zeroing, and much more. There's even an optional advanced flight model for helicopters that makes it much more realistic and difficult. The DLC for this game gives no direct advantages over others due to the nature of the game. There are DLC weapons and vehicles, in which the DLC weapons tend to have some advantages and disadvantages compared to non-DLC weapons and DLC vehicles can only be driven by those with the DLC. The community is not the best, but not the worst either. In order to enjoy the game without trolls, I recommend joining a unit. Most public zeus servers run into trolls after about an hour of activity. Zeus is a gamemode where one or two players take the role of a Game Master and design missions on-the-fly. There is also a large mod community. Many of the mods like RHS and ACE3 are great. Bohemia even put out an official mod that contained the ADR-97. The ADR is very similar to the P90, but because it is a mod, it cannot be used on official servers.
TL;DR: Buy game, join a unit. DLC is good, but not necessary.
Edit: Why I think this game deserves the "Labor of Love" Steam Award: Arma 3 launched on September 12, 2013. Since then, the game has still reveived numerous updates that introduce everything from bug fixes to new DLC. Users without the DLC when it launches still usually get a free platform update which improves the game experience overall, like when active and passive radars were introduced to already existing vehicles when the Jets DLC launched. The game is largely supported by its community, with the developers openly supporting mods. They always push updates to the dev branch first to make sure that the people there can help iron out the bugs before patches go live. Even now, Tac-Ops DLC is around the corner. It isn't promised to do anything special except for introduce a few new playable scenarios, but in a time before the main campaign, which may help give some background to it.

Do not get this game unless you have a group of friends to play it with. Seriously.
The public multiplayer servers are mostly atrocious (King of the Hill is the best you'll get, but even that blows), and MOST of them are just perpetually empty. The single player campaign is laughably bad - from terrible voice acting to bad writing to ludicrously magical super-AI that snipes you through a bush from 1,500m away ... it's just a constant exercise in frustration.
The game is horribly optimized and constantly dropping frames, seemingly irrelevant of what's actually happening on your screen.
Also worth mentioning that, unless you wanna shell out another ~$60 for the DLC, you're not going to be able to use about half of the weapons in the game, or access the superior map. The default maps, Stratis and Altis, are boring islands completely devoid of any real life, aside from a few dozen copy/pasted towns and miles and miles of blank, arid land. The DLC map, Tanoa, looks signifcantly better - but I'm not paying $30 for a good map and around a dozen weapon reskins.
Unless you're a glutton for clunky punishment, this game is not for you.

Team Fortress 2 is an objective-based team shooter. The classes you can choose from are limited but extremely diverse, and vary in functionality and gameplay. With the 9 classes available, you'll never get bored (or at least not in a while) as each class also comprises of numerous sub-classes made by using different weapon loadouts. The game modes that exist are fun and encourage teamwork among players. While most of the community is helpful and respectable, there is however a section of the community that could be considered 'toxic' (ie. hackers, exploiters, griefers, etc.) but they are few and far between. With the latest update released the game has recieved new maps and weapons, thus adding to the diversity. Long story short, this game is fun and entertaing and I highly recommend it, even if you're new to shooters you'll most likely enjoy this game as it is far from 'run of the mill'.

Short review: Bonkers, crazy, fun.
Longer review. Saints Row: The Third (SR3) is the first game in the series that I've played. I've sunk over 40 hours into it and got somewhere around 80% of the way through, according to the game's progression indicator. I've no real compulsion to complete it because it's just fun to steal a car, beat up the odd person in the street, or give the police something else to do besides eating donuts all day.
In SR3 you have the freedom to select your in-game character, choosing voice, body type, clothes, and more. Later on, you can visit the plastic surgeon to modify your look if you fancy a sex change, get some tattoos at the parlour, or simply choose a new outfit to wear. Similarly, you can visit the gun shop to kit yourself out with a wide variety of conventional and much less conventional weapons. Fancy a weapon that fires guts to attract the local sewer shark? That's available as an unlock after completing one of the quests. How about a weapon that fires mind-controlling squids? Yep, that's there too.
In short, SR3 is about unrestricted fun. Health regenerates once you hide in cover, weapons are so freely dropped by opponents that ammo flows like water, and getting around the city is up to your style.
Recommended.

TF2 is the only game that pays you to play it, dropping items that can be refined into metal scraps worth real world money. Whether you want to pour money into it to become the most sharply dressed mercernary on the battlefield or want to use it to siphon money out of to fund your next indie game purchase, TF2's overarching community market and itemfind system makes it a worthwhile venture for anyone.
Much further from dead than most people would tell you. Something about the words "free to play" keeps young children and foreigners with pings of 200+ wandering blindly into the fray for the players of 1000+ hours to kill with little to no resistance and put into their frag videos, and the newest updates are shockingly content-rich and reward players with free cosmetic and item drops.
If you haven't tried it yet, don't let anything stop you. TF2 has a wonderful and natural progression from "oh my gosh I got a kill" to "hell yeah, 35-player killstreak" that keeps you strung along and having fun at any skill level. Definitely worth the asking price of less than nothing!

Having played Team Fortress 2 on PC for almost 2 years now, and having played it on other mediums for far longer, I can say that there are reasons that this game has been alive for 10 years and is still going. The humor, the combat, the graphical style (colors and art style), the myriad of fleshed out characters (playable and Non-playable), the customization system, the economy, the creative community, and even the smaller competitive scene, are all factors that make TF2 as unique a game as it is, and are all parts of why so many people have played it over the years.
TF2 has been called a 'legacy game' meaning it is a game that has existed for a long enough time and has impacted the gaming community in such a way it is almost impossible for it to die, furthermore, the inspirations and concepts that came with TF2 will continue to influence gamers and the ones who make our games for many, many years to come, another fact that can make it worthwhile to at least try it for ones-self.
Finally, did I mention it's Free-To-Play? meaning even those who have not a cent in their steam wallet can pick up this game and play it themselves, a fact that has surely attributed to the giant community and the mess of silliness the game offers up to anyone who is willing to dive in.

There's all these reviews creaming over the giant purple d*ldo bat, but considerably fewer about blowing up luchadors and British-accented Tron-style hackers with a VTOL fighter jet that shoots homing laser missiles. Sure, the novelty of a sex toy as a weapon is amusing, but it doesn't cause nearly as many explosions.

A game that could be amazing, but is completely broken by all the completely illogical bugs.
Let's start with the absolutely horrendous framerate, this is not something based in inadequate hardware. Once you start playing on a server, you may notice 100+ fps, things are moving along nicely. This means you managed to strike gold, and entered a freshly booted server. As soon as you get into a small community, the framerate drops. To insanely low levels. <45 fps is hardly uncommon. This happens on every single server. Once the server is rebooted, your 100< fps is back.
This is of course just the tip of the iceberg. Every single staircase, on all three maps, will ♥♥♥♥ you up. You get stuck in them, you teleport around, you fall through them. Amazing stuff when you're running up a tower while being shot by everyone, including their grandmas.
Once we've started handling this, usually rememdied by running in fully standing position, you're still getting rubber band lag and all kinds of incontrollable spastic movement. Amazing.
But here's the real piece of the pie - the server browser is the worst browser I've EVER had to handle. Not only does it send you flying to another server when you select one, but refreshing the server list, even with decent constraints, it's a major gamble. Will you find ANY server at all? Probably not. Okay, let's restart the server browser then. No. Of course not, you have to restart the whole ♥♥♥♥ing game to even have a chance. But no, usually you still find absolutely nothing, what so ever. Okay, so you give up, and decide that 40 minutes of trying to enter a server is way too much. OH hell, look, ARMA 3 keeps running, even though you closed it 5 minutes ago. And you've suddenly got no internet connection. Supposedly this is due to some overloading of routers, but have fun trying to solve that issue. Nothing helps. You just need to wait it out. Or reset your router. Or restart your computer.. Nothing helps in any consistent manner.

Best ending ever (the "bad" ending) for such a crazy action game. Do yourself a favor and play the ending twice. Save often so you have some choices (upgrades, mission paths, etc.).
There will be an endgame mission where you can save an important supporting ally or not. First, save them, and play through the fun cheesy good happy buddies ending. Okay good, golf clap, here's a trophy.
Then go back to the decision point, _don't_ save that ally, and then play the frakking incredible, over-the-top, cinematic "bad" ending. It is super-badass. Can't believe it hasn't been applauded more in the gaming press.

Arma 3 is a diverse platform for a variety of game modes spanning from casual 'life' based games to hardcore military simulation. Other than the campaign it offers no core gaming experience, but the endless array of high quality polished addons enhances the experience and gives the player various outlets of entertainment, free, within a single game. The mods are mostly available on the steam workshop for easy access and fast downloads accross the world. Other sources include armaholic and
.
Development suport has been relentless and relatively responsive to demand. Bohemia Interactive has made the game much more accessible for the broader public, inviting a wider playerbase to the game keeping servers populated. Population has been increasingly infleunced by entertainers such as FrankieonPC, PsiSyndicate and DevilDogGamer who continue to advertise new mods and gamemodes to the public.
Sometimes I look at my profile and think how I could possibly have sunk that many hours into Arma 3. But Arma 3 is only the host to a wide array of games. That's why I'm proud to call Arma 3 my favourite game.

Saints Row 3 does feature a decent amount of content and a fantastic character editor. Graphically and performance wise, the game looks great most of the time,and performs gret as well. The game features a bright and vibrant art style in most places while having some places looing like copy and pastes of others. While Saints Row 3 fails to please fans of the series, it may still be an appeal to those who are looking for a good time with a nice amount of content to cover, I would recommend this game for when it is on sale.

Arma 3 is a diverse platform for a variety of game modes spanning from casual 'life' based games to hardcore military simulation. Other than the campaign it offers no core gaming experience, but the endless array of high quality polished addons enhances the experience and gives the player various outlets of entertainment, free, within a single game. The mods are mostly available on the steam workshop for easy access and fast downloads accross the world. Other sources include armaholic and
.
Development suport has been relentless and relatively responsive to demand. Bohemia Interactive has made the game much more accessible for the broader public, inviting a wider playerbase to the game keeping servers populated. Population has been increasingly infleunced by entertainers such as FrankieonPC, PsiSyndicate and DevilDogGamer who continue to advertise new mods and gamemodes to the public.
Sometimes I look at my profile and think how I could possibly have sunk that many hours into Arma 3. But Arma 3 is only the host to a wide array of games. That's why I'm proud to call Arma 3 my favourite game.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Bullets, boobs, ten foot phallics for no apparent reason. Sure, if that's your thing.
Saints Row: The Third is a fun little title, both Single and Multiplayer. There's a great deal of map to explore for first timers, and a decent enough design to keep long time players invested in running around the same place. Whether on foot, driving, or even flying, you'll find the city of Steelport to have been designed with large scale police/gang wars to happen, which are at times painfully easy to trigger. However, it becomes apparent in the late game (or the completionist's game) that gangs don't make a return once you've finished them off completely, leaving only the option of restarting your save, or keeping a backup, if you want to get back into fighting eerily similar bad guys.
You'll start off with none of it, but money becomes literally no object after only a few hours, so the feeling of limitation for car mods, weapons, or more phallic whacking objects, quickly goes away.
The number of weapons in the base game doesn't leave a bitter taste in the mouth, but more variety for legitimate weapons would have gone a long way.
Still, if you want a fun distraction before GTAV makes its PC debut, or if you'd rather the silly, over the top nature of Saints Row over the former, it's the best of the series thus far

Arma 3 is unlike any of the other games in the series. Where most of the other Arma games felt sluggish or rough around the edges, Arma 3 smooths them out, eliminates them and massively improves on them. At first I was hesitant to drop $40 on this game since I wasn't too fond of Arma 2 and the uninspiring gameplay that it was to me. However, with Arma 3 it is entirely different! This game brings me closer to my childhood favorite Delta Force franchise by Novalogic. The missions in Arma 3 are incredibly fun, well made and genuinenly interesting. I love that the voice overs in the campaign are so life like including but not limited to actual character personalities, where as Arma 2 felt more like ONLY a simulator. Not only that, but the grachics and sounds are EXTREMELY well done and when using a nice audio setup (or good headphones) there's a real sense of experiencing what it feels like to be in Kerry's (main character) shoes from bullets snapping, crackling and wizzing by, to the deep thump of rounds being shot all the way till you hear the realistical explosion in the distance as your enemy or friendlies get lit up. If you are on the edge on whether or not to buy Arma 3, I would say get it and enjoy!

Considering this is the only installment I've ever played, I must say I'm a bit upset with myself for choosing this game to start with because it's literally the pinnacle of the sandbox ganster genre. There's really no where else to go but down from here regardless of which game I play next in the series.
It's got just about everything you could ask for, great selection of clothing and customization, good variety of weapons, both useful and novelty. It's easy to navigate around the map and the GPS is very well detailed. The map size is also just the right amount of large... it never really seemed overwhelming to me even from the start. Games like GTA and Crackdown just annoyed me with all of their collectables and cluster, this game does it right.
There's plenty of side quests and optional missions to partake in so you'll deinitely be getting your money out of it. The humor is just the right amount of juvenile... you can avoid it completely if you wish to do so. It's over the top and meant to be a parody of sandbox gangster genre games and it definitely delivers. The DLC also adds a lot to the game but can get lost in the mix if you've never played the core game first... I might be basing some of this review on that, so make sure to pick up a complete pack on sale.
The finale is also hilarious with a well known 80's pop song playing while you finish the final mission... One of the more satisfying game endings I've seen.

I honestly feel kind of ashamed that I have played over 1600 hours in this game and have yet to review it. I was a major fan of Arma 2 and while my steam profile doesn't show it, I logged thousands of hours into it and it's expansions. Needless to say when Arma 3 was announced and eventually given an Alpha release I was day one. Even with the performance problems I was experiencing, I was having a blast. Once I upgraded (CPU only) my performance increase by more than I could think to measure. That's not to say everything with the game is perfect.
I'll start with the guns. They're not terrible but I'm not a huge fan of the models (Katiba or the MX). The only one I KINDA liked was the MX SW. The Abr is really nice but I was missing my favorite 5.56 models. Like the M4. Or the 416. However with the recent Apex expansion, they've added weapons in called the Spar-16 which basically looks just like a 416.
Speaking of Apex, I gotta mention that a lot of people have stated they could not play multiplayer with servers running Apex. This is plain false. Bohemia has had a long standing policy of not separating the population with DLC. The only part of Apex that would keep anyone from playing on a server is the map. Considering how many maps exist for Arma 3, you would be hard pressed NOT to find a server running a different map. To an extent you can even use the weapons or attachments from the DLC but this is primarily meant for people to check them out. After a few moments an advert for the DLC  will come across the screen.
Now to performance. People do still suffer with frame rate issues and it can be frustrating, believe me. There are a lot of guides out there on how to increase it. Those guides have helped a lot of people and there still exists a lot of people it does nothing for. Single player generally runs great for people but on multiplayer it rears its ugly head. The problem being here that performance isn't solely placed on your rig. The servers rig needs to be able to push what it's trying to do while Arma juggles all the things that it does on such large maps. Some game modes will be worse than others and this isn't to say the problems with performance rest solely on the server or your PC. But it's something to take into account as well.
From my own personal experience, I was originally running an AMD 8 core processor at like 2.5 ghz I think it was. 8gb of standard ram and a Nvidia 660ti. Regular 3tb hdd. I bought a new motherboard and case with the i7 4770 3.4 ghz. With the AMD I had MAYBE 10-15 fps on Stratis alone or with a handful of people practically doing nothing. The i7 alone, I saw an increased gain. On stratis, full server, at the heart of a battle I was maintaining 30fps on ultra. Lot of people might think that's nothing great but from just upgrading my CPU it was quite an increase. Since then I've moved up to 16gb of Ripjaw (I think that's the name) ram and in November I'm finally upgrading from my 660ti to the 1080. What I currently have I never dip below 30 fps on a full server and often times I see it get up to 40-50.
All that said, everyone is going to have a different experience in this game. It's not easy and there's a good learning curve. Tons of keys to remember. Even coming from Battlefield, it might be hard for new players to understand just how big Altis is. Hell, even Stratis. I've played everything from coop missions on to king of the hill, altis life, wasteland, breaking point, epoch, Exile, and much more. I've spent so much time doing all these different things, I still haven't beaten single player yet.
The last thing I gotta mention is the workshop or even armaholic. At either place you can find missions, new units, weapon packs of all kinds, gear packs, and the list goes on. There is so much here. I wish I could begin to describe just how much is available from people who poured their time and passions into. Even if you don't own the game, you could go look at the workshop just to get an idea of what all is there.
TL;DR This game is fun and frustrating at differing times. If you want something new and challenging, I can't recommend this more.

In all seriousness, though, this game is awesome.  I, being a fan of more serious games like Arma and Half Life(2), was origionally skeptical about this game.  However, watching the (many) videos of Saints Row III I grew to like it.  RPGs were nearly my least favorite genre of games until I played this, in which I have gotten many different RPGs, such as Fallout.  Saints Row III combines Story, Co-Op, and Character Customization in a way that makes it semi-unique.  Don't like the way your character looks?  Don't try to download a mod, just pay a (rather costly) visit to the nearest plastic surgeon to change any features you might've not liked.  The Drop-In, Drop-Out Co-Op also works decently well, with a little lag on either side (sides being the players, of course).  Finally, the thing I like most about Saints Row III? The customization.  No, not Character Customization!  Car Customization.  Car finatics will like this game a lot, with (semi) realistic car handling.  There's even a choice to get cheaper car parts in customiziation in one of the (missions) in the Story.
All in all, a great game.  Don't let the mature-ish humor get in your way of your decision.  This game is worth every second of it, in my opinion.  If I had to, I would give this game a 95/ 100, because of thesomewhat inappropriate humor.

Saints Row: The Third. I thought it was a very good game. The thing that got me the most was the comical humor. The costumes and wardrobes, to the sexual references and balancing dead bodies with exaggerated weapon effects. I found this game to be a LOT beter compared to Saints Row and Saints Row II. If follows the time line, which is always a plus. The amount of things you can do, in my opinion, is much more and better than GTA. GTA is more on a serious note, which is good; Saints Row: The Third has some serious moments, but knows how to offer a laugh and good time with a balance.
The Story Line is pretty simple and basic, but not as generic as you would expect. You have a mixture of things, from saving your Homies, to fighting Gangs, Police, Military, Politicians, Zombies and Aliens. The gangs, especially one in particular are trying to take turf. What kind of gang isn't? The Genki line I found the most fun. It's basically like a game show arena. You fight your wat through enemies as well as the environments. It's definitely rewarding in the end, but not as much as it should be. In the end, you begin to gather forces for a take over. A bloody, deadly and annoying battle takes place.
The Combat System was very fun. Shooting duel pistols at enemies and watching them fly across the street. The Genki Mobile went shoots flames around all sides of the car as you drive, leaving a flaming inferno of destruction in your path. Falling from a disintergrating plane and shooting people as you fall with style. Fighting in wrestling rings with other gang members. Or you can do it with classic style by running them over with your cars and going on a shooting rampage. Some people may frown on it, but it is only a game after all. It could even relieve some frustrations.
Didn't have much of an Online Experience. It's pretty difficult to find others willing to play or willing to stay. So, unless you have a friend to play this with, I would recommend that more. At least if you want the achievements that go with this.
