After successfully taking over the town of Stillwater in the last game, the Saints popularity and brand has exploded. Billboards are everywhere, they have their own energy drink, and people stop them in the street for autographs even in the midst of battle.
But it's not easy being at the top, it just makes you a bigger target. During the first mission, a bank heist goes wrong, and you find yourself fighting rival gangs and a military force in a brand new city - Steelport. This is an industrial city with big skyscrapers, factories... and maniacs with rocket launchers.
When you first bring up that world map, the art design and music instantly makes you think of Grand Theft Auto IV's map. But Saints Row isn't a realistic gritty sandbox where you pay bridge tolls and go bowling... it's more of an absurdest parody of the GTA games.
One of the biggest differences between the two franchises, is that here you get to live out your wildest character customisation dreams - which we'll always appreciate. There's an almost endless supply of facial tweaks, from eyelids to reptilian make-up... there's stacks of gestures and taunts... skinny and fat sliders, skin colours that include metallic yellow and green... and even a 'sex appeal' slider. There are also a stack of voices to choose from for your character. Most of our favourite voices are back from Saints Row 2, with one notable addition - the zombie.
It's quite an achievement that all of these clothes fit so well, with no clipping on all body types I tried. And there's something about seeing these crazy characters in cut scenes that not only makes this a very individual experience - but it just makes the main character seem even more insane then he/she already is. It also surprised me how well made these cut-scenes are, for a game that embraces the silly so much. The whole presentation is well done actually, and the selection of music on the radio stations is great too... but it's the mission music that really compliments the action perfectly.
The intro to this game is so exciting. In the first hour you'll rip a vault out of a bank, get kidnapped, parachute out of a plane, then shoot the window out of one coming towards you, take out everyone in it and then fight goons in mid air until you land in Steelport. They put a lot of work into those first couple of missions... and straight away you realise that everything looks better compared to the last game. There's a floppy, cartoony feel to the world and the character models; which you especially notice riding the sidewalk. All the models look more solid, with better animations in general. The cars look better too, with improved physics which makes for some excellent crashes.
Once you zoom around, you'll notice how smooth the world is. It's not beautiful but there's a lot on screen at once and there's a good draw distance, with a nice amount of detail. One thing that always bugged in me SR2 is the way vehicles would spawn and disappear as you looked left and right, which broke the world a bit for me. I noticed that they've fixed that.
Getting in and out of cars is something that you do a LOT in a game like this, and here in Saints Row 3 you actually have a 'quick hijack' which lets you leap into vehicles instantly; and that sums up the overall concept of this game - which is that it doesn't want to waste your time, and tries to keep things as fun and fast as possible. There's even a 'warp to shore' mechanic so you don't waste time swimming. Developer Volition really does a good job of keeping the gameplay streamlined.
Enemy AI is a bit hit and miss though, sometimes they won't notice you for a while, or they'll just stand out in the open. There's no cover system so their options are a bit limited anyway. And in most of the missions where you're fighting a bunch of goons, there are usually only 2 or 3 character types, which can't help but feel out of place for a game with such great customisation to your own character.
The story missions in Saints Row: The Third are full of variety. The best range from exciting base infiltrations, ambushes, jet missions and some other crazy stuff that I won't spoil for you. There's no longer any multiplayer VS which I don't think will be missed that much to be honest.. But now there is a wave mode.. called '♥♥♥♥♥D MODE' where you'll face off against a variety of foes that grow in size, and shrink... in a bunch of situations. It's horribly unbalanced but undeniably fun.
Now, this is a very crude game, and I have to say I've really wrestled with my morals on this one, and what I consider to be passably appropriate in a game like this. On one hand - I get the same maniacal joy of being an idiot, running people over and enjoying all of that that silly humour the same as anyone else. And I also get that this is a particular genre that is about crossing the line - while not taking itself too seriously... However, I can't help but ask myself what kind of a person is okay with grabbing a woman by the hair and face-slamming them into the pavement. It is pretty full on that you can do these special moves on the civilians - I was okay with doing it to the enemies, they're trying to kill you. There isn't much punishment either for hurting the civilians - cops come but you don't feel much of a penalty.
I felt with GTA IV it was treated as a real crime, and here it's just glorified with those special moves. Should that choice even be there, and does it need to be? Do I really need to wield giant purple♥♥♥♥♥♥♥- why is that in the game?
One bit that took it too far was the human trafficking mission... you open a bunch of crates looking for 'hoes' to which you can then keep as your own hoes for long term income, or sell back for a quick cash reward. On the boat where they're kept, you'll find all sorts of contraptions such as 'fisting machines'... and that crossed the line.
I'm so torn with this one, I almost feel hypocritical because some parts I was absolutely fine with, but other parts I just found abhorrent. I don't want be a prude, but the sexual and degrading elements of the game took it way too far and put a dampener on my experience. I mean, what's next? Violence against children? Would that be okay in a game like this, because it's not meant to be taken seriously so it just gets a free pass?
All in all it's a very good game, good graphics, good story and good missions. This is a game that should definitely be played by adults. If you can look past those few tasteless elements that just go too far, it's still worth an 9/10.

This game was nothing like I expected it to be. When I purchased this game I believed I was getting a military simulator that was nicely polished, contained a good backstory, a good multiplayer, and a nicely explained tutorial considering the price of $69.99 I paid for it. I was completly wrong.
Backstory: One of the most ridiculous things about this game is that it claims to be a military simulator. I can tell you it's not even close. First off it takes place in the future, not a couple years, but far in the future. So far in the future where for some reason todays weapons no longer exsists. Yes, that's right there are no M4's, Scar's, HKs, Ak's, ACR's, etc in this game. Just this shows how this game fails. How can you claim to be a military simulator and not even include weapons that our forces use around the world to not be in this game. And even the weapons that they do include are very limited. I'm talking like maybe 20 weapons. That's just one example. I could go on about how just sticking a needle or wrapping a bandage on your teammate revives them or how the campaign doesn't make any sense, but lets just move on.
Controls: The controls are the most confusing thing I've ever had to use. The placement of them are confusing and hard to remember. I tried changing them, but instead of swapping them it just tells you that the key is already being used so then you have to figure what key is already using that. That wouldn't be so hard if it wasn't for the fact that there are like 100's of different key combinations.
Tutorial: Honestly why is it even here? It is so bad I can't understand it. It does nothing to explain the confusing controls as mentioned above. Instead the majority of it will have you run around to points, yes run around. And I'm not over exaggerating that either. It's like the developers couldn't even start on how to explain everything so they decided to teach you common knowledge that you would already know from any other FPS like how to run, walk, move your screen, etc. Even when it did get into something useful like using the map, it still wasn't even properly explained.
Movement: I figured that movement and aiming would be different from other FPS games. But come on, the movement is so sluggish on this game. Aiming is the same way. Everything feels so cumbersome, especially with the funky key placement. Maybe eventually I would get used to it, but it truely destroys any immersion that game could have.
Graphics/Optimization: First off graphics don't make a game, but they certainly help with immersion. And the graphics were ok at first, but then I realized that it was eating my computer resources that I had to scale everything back. Even at poor graphic setting I still had a low framerate issue. That is truely unbelievable considering the graphics are disgusting at this level yet  at the same time I can manage high-ultra settings on Battlefield 4 at 60 FPS. So the game just fails so hard here and really this shows that no effort was put into optimization. I mean come on Rust has better optimization and that game is indie and still in early access.
Multiplayer: So this is supposed to be Arma's big thing. Yet I hated this more than anything else. I constantly had to look up servers to join. If I found a server it would launch the game, load the server, load everything in, and then tell me that I was kicked and I need to reserve a spot at some stupid website. When I finally get into a server that you don't need to be whitelisted or reserve a spot I still had problems. There're no explainations on what to do and the community just expects you to know everything. I litterally kept getting "hit Alt + F4" or "call an admin" to my questions from other players. When I did figure things out on my own it seems like I can never do anything. On king of the hill gamemode I would have to travel miles to get into the battlefield. Sometimes I was luckily enough to get in a helicopter. Of course as soon as I got out I would get killed instantly by players who have a ton of money and can buy the best weapons. Then I tried alatis life and I would just keep spawning on a stupid small island with no way to get to the mainland with no explaintion on what to do. And Arma life you can't even join without paying a monthly payment. That's where I gave up on multiplayer, litterally a true disappointment, just alot of confusion and time wasted.
Overall from what I learned: It seems that these developers are those type of people that rush a unfinished game with loads of issues and expect the community to mod it to be playable. So if this game was $10 that might be acceptable depending on certain conditions. But I litterally paid $69.99 for this game and expect nothing less the AAA quality. I got none of that. I had to check and see if this game was still in early development, but nope it was released OVER 3 YEARS AGO. Seriously, I can't imagine what it was like when it came out. And I'm not a very critical person, I usually enjoy most video games. And I really wanted to like this game, but from the limited weapons, confusing controls, and a letdown of a multiplayer I just couldn't do it. I gave it two chances, and if I played this game any longer then I couldn't get a refund. And I have NEVER made a refund for any of my games before. But this, this is unacceptable and I am getting a refund for this game right away.
Edit: I forgot to add that the A.I. is incredibly stupid when it comes to custom missions released by the community. Another reason why this game was a big let down. Also if you think any of this review is just me ranting then you can buy the game and see for yourself. As long as you don't go over 2 hours or so of gameplay then you should be able to get a refund.
Edit #2: Don't take my word of the refund though, do it at your own risk because I don't know how steam desides whether or not you're eligible for a refund. In this case I was, may not be the same for you.

Taking place a few years after the events of SR2, in Saints Row the Third the Third Street Saints went from a violent vigilante gang in Stilwater to a large scale corporate entity after teaming up with former rival ultor. However this fame doesn't last long as a failed bank heist and a nearly botched escape results in the Saints once again being viewed as criminals rather than heroes and also pits the Saints up against another corporate faction calling themselves the Syndicate. Not only that, but the Saints forced out of Stilwater and into the city of Steelport. Things get even uglier when an elite spec-ops group known as STAG is called in to take down the two warring factions.
The Good: Gunplay is much smoother now, AI for both enemies and teamates has thankfully been improved, enemy factions can send so called "specialists" (which come in the form of brutes, snipers, riot officers and a few other variants depending on which faction you fight) , runs MUCH smoother than SR2's PC port and has a decent amount of mods which you can get from the Saints Row Modding Forum.
The Meh: Clothing customization has been cut down a bit, if you played SR2 you'll notice that some areas of Steelport look pretty neat while others suffer from Copy\Paste Syndrome, and despite the fact that enemy AI has improved even having the new enemy sub-classes the civilian AI has been dumbed down a bit.
The WTF: If you've ever played SR1 or SR2 than this games heavier emphasis on the insanity might be a turn-off, a fan-favorite character "dies" in the second mission, Even though there's a ton of special weapons you can unlock in the game most of the other weapon categories only have anywhere from 2-3 weapons, some of the weapons from SR2 (more specifically the Minigun, Flamethrower and Sledgehammer) are now "temporary weapons" which means you can't place them in your inventory (although this can be fixed with a mod from the Saints Row Modding Forum).
This used to be a fun game, but, Valve ruined it, its not fun anymore, so to be honest, i just cant recommend it, but, thats my opinion.

A gleefully silly, incredibly fun game.  The game's bizarre amorality really grew on me as time went on.  The open world missions weren't that interesting, but the main story arc was varied, manic, and full of unique and exciting elements.  The use of music was absolutely perfect.  Using "Power" during the raid on the penthouse and "Hero" during the finale were perfect choices.  My only complaint is that I can't add my own mp3 list for the car stereo (which was an option in the first game).
Two pieces of advice.  First, this game is easy.  If you want a challenge, use hardcore mode, which is more like what you'd expect from normal difficulty on an average shooter.  Second, the DLC really imbalances the game, especially the vehicles.  I'd suggest holding off on installing the DLC until you've finished the main story arc.

This game was nothing like I expected it to be. When I purchased this game I believed I was getting a military simulator that was nicely polished, contained a good backstory, a good multiplayer, and a nicely explained tutorial considering the price of $69.99 I paid for it. I was completly wrong.
Backstory: One of the most ridiculous things about this game is that it claims to be a military simulator. I can tell you it's not even close. First off it takes place in the future, not a couple years, but far in the future. So far in the future where for some reason todays weapons no longer exsists. Yes, that's right there are no M4's, Scar's, HKs, Ak's, ACR's, etc in this game. Just this shows how this game fails. How can you claim to be a military simulator and not even include weapons that our forces use around the world to not be in this game. And even the weapons that they do include are very limited. I'm talking like maybe 20 weapons. That's just one example. I could go on about how just sticking a needle or wrapping a bandage on your teammate revives them or how the campaign doesn't make any sense, but lets just move on.
Controls: The controls are the most confusing thing I've ever had to use. The placement of them are confusing and hard to remember. I tried changing them, but instead of swapping them it just tells you that the key is already being used so then you have to figure what key is already using that. That wouldn't be so hard if it wasn't for the fact that there are like 100's of different key combinations.
Tutorial: Honestly why is it even here? It is so bad I can't understand it. It does nothing to explain the confusing controls as mentioned above. Instead the majority of it will have you run around to points, yes run around. And I'm not over exaggerating that either. It's like the developers couldn't even start on how to explain everything so they decided to teach you common knowledge that you would already know from any other FPS like how to run, walk, move your screen, etc. Even when it did get into something useful like using the map, it still wasn't even properly explained.
Movement: I figured that movement and aiming would be different from other FPS games. But come on, the movement is so sluggish on this game. Aiming is the same way. Everything feels so cumbersome, especially with the funky key placement. Maybe eventually I would get used to it, but it truely destroys any immersion that game could have.
Graphics/Optimization: First off graphics don't make a game, but they certainly help with immersion. And the graphics were ok at first, but then I realized that it was eating my computer resources that I had to scale everything back. Even at poor graphic setting I still had a low framerate issue. That is truely unbelievable considering the graphics are disgusting at this level yet  at the same time I can manage high-ultra settings on Battlefield 4 at 60 FPS. So the game just fails so hard here and really this shows that no effort was put into optimization. I mean come on Rust has better optimization and that game is indie and still in early access.
Multiplayer: So this is supposed to be Arma's big thing. Yet I hated this more than anything else. I constantly had to look up servers to join. If I found a server it would launch the game, load the server, load everything in, and then tell me that I was kicked and I need to reserve a spot at some stupid website. When I finally get into a server that you don't need to be whitelisted or reserve a spot I still had problems. There're no explainations on what to do and the community just expects you to know everything. I litterally kept getting "hit Alt + F4" or "call an admin" to my questions from other players. When I did figure things out on my own it seems like I can never do anything. On king of the hill gamemode I would have to travel miles to get into the battlefield. Sometimes I was luckily enough to get in a helicopter. Of course as soon as I got out I would get killed instantly by players who have a ton of money and can buy the best weapons. Then I tried alatis life and I would just keep spawning on a stupid small island with no way to get to the mainland with no explaintion on what to do. And Arma life you can't even join without paying a monthly payment. That's where I gave up on multiplayer, litterally a true disappointment, just alot of confusion and time wasted.
Overall from what I learned: It seems that these developers are those type of people that rush a unfinished game with loads of issues and expect the community to mod it to be playable. So if this game was $10 that might be acceptable depending on certain conditions. But I litterally paid $69.99 for this game and expect nothing less the AAA quality. I got none of that. I had to check and see if this game was still in early development, but nope it was released OVER 3 YEARS AGO. Seriously, I can't imagine what it was like when it came out. And I'm not a very critical person, I usually enjoy most video games. And I really wanted to like this game, but from the limited weapons, confusing controls, and a letdown of a multiplayer I just couldn't do it. I gave it two chances, and if I played this game any longer then I couldn't get a refund. And I have NEVER made a refund for any of my games before. But this, this is unacceptable and I am getting a refund for this game right away.
Edit: I forgot to add that the A.I. is incredibly stupid when it comes to custom missions released by the community. Another reason why this game was a big let down. Also if you think any of this review is just me ranting then you can buy the game and see for yourself. As long as you don't go over 2 hours or so of gameplay then you should be able to get a refund.
Edit #2: Don't take my word of the refund though, do it at your own risk because I don't know how steam desides whether or not you're eligible for a refund. In this case I was, may not be the same for you.

Saints Row: The Third takes place three years after the previous game. You are the gangleader of the Third Street Saints. The Saints are no longer just a brutal and effective criminal operation but now a fully-fledged media empire with their time split equally between doing dirt and setting up legitimate businesses and a popular line of merchandising.
After a bank heist gone wrong, the Saints find themselves in Steelport, butting heads with a local crime group known as the Syndicate. From there it is the classic rise to power story.
The appearance and personality of the Saints' leader is completely up to you, thanks to the character editor. You can make him or her look genuinely cool, or a complete abomination. If you want to change your look, or even your sex, visit a plastic surgeon in the city and change it. If you want a new outfit, there are shops full of every type of fashion imaginable.
Missions place you in increasingly unpredictable situations. It starts out fairly low-key with a raid on a military base to steal weapons for the gang, but it finishes with an explosive finale involving tanks, jets and city-levelling explosions. In between, there is a zombie outbreak, a trip inside a Tron-like computer world and much more, it gets wilder and more varied.
There is also an element of choice to the decisions you make. Certain missions see you choosing between two options that will affect the story, sometimes in quite dramatic ways.
The game has a lot of replay value, after finishing the main story you are able to do a lot of side missions, e.g. car-stealing missions and assassinations.
The best way to play Saints Row: The Third is to play with a friend. The co-op action and the careful attention to detail in the co-op mechanics are masterful. It is easy to drop in and out of a friend’s game and the way progress is tracked is very smart. If you join a game where the other person is further along in the plot than you are, you can still play a plot mission with them.
The dialogue between the characters is consistently hilarious. The game is packed with in-jokes, meta humor and constantly swerves into almost surreal territory.
The graphics may not be mind blowing, instead the game really shines with the sound. Everything sounds great from the gun battles to the snippets of incidental speech that you get when wandering around. The voice acting takes it up a notch though with some truly memorable performances. The best thing is the music selection though. A great selection of dance, hip hop, indie and metal are on offer from the in-game radio stations.
Overall I think the game is fantastic. It just gives you so much to do and a lot of fun if you play with a friend. Saints Row: The Third is worth to buy.

Well, this might be a very important title. Ive been an Arma-fan since I jumped into the DayZ-cestpool, back in Arma 2. Been enjoying the mods immensely, and was looking forward to more of it, in better visuals, animations and stuff. And Arma 3 sort of delivers that. Some would say, to the max. But Ill be a little realistic in this review, to make it honest without bias etc.
First off, the main game itself, is a masterpiece of Armystuff lol. There is no denying it, really. And with the mods and DLCs etc. It becomes a truely huge game, for army-fans. Including the special ops-lovers out there (I know you want it!). THe diversity of tactics, machines, gear and modes of play, is staggering, once you take a look at the whole Arma-world. Ive given up on trying to fathom it all lol. But I love the concept.
Visuals are maybe just below the top-titles, but being improved all the time. Remember, this is a massive multiplayergame sandbox, so it cant compete with linear singleplayer titles ofc. But it really has some satisfying maps and areas, that look absolutely wonderfull. Lighthouses at night, bombardments over the cities, tracerfire throught he forrests and so on. You will see once you enter yourself lol. Its epic.
On the down side, the realism seems a little too hampering, at times. Working with the concept of DayZ and the old Arma-rule: Your equipment has to be cumbersome to work with, so we have to be safe, before emptying our backpacks and so on. However, to this day, I find it too hampering, tbh. The inventory system is and have always been the down side, imo, with this series. Its slow and glitchy. There are mods out there, that makes it better, but in the end, the main version sucks. You kinda get used to it, though, so its not that bad I guess.
The building system has some good idea, but for some reason, the modules are also kinda glitchy and often wont align to ground and such. THe physics are also a bit weird (floating walls etc.) But the ideas are awesome, and hopefully in time, they will iron out the kinks and all.
THe maps are absolutely huge. And sure feels good playing. The ALtis/Startis maps are a little boring, tbh. THe dry Greek-style islands make for a very monotone vista, but the design of them, seems alright. There are other maps, and some are pretty sweet. I havent played the newest one yet (Pangea I think its called?), but I hear good things about it.
If you want a good look at the game, and what to expect, check out Frankie On PC and Sada´s exploration of the newest map. Good fun too :-)

Arma 3 is a game you'll either love or hate and personally, I love it. Sure, the game is a bit confronting at first, as it looks like it has a million controls (pro-tip: If you're mostly sticking to infantry combat, you'll only have a handful more buttons and button combinations to learn than the most shooters E.G. Battlefield) and the game definitely feels clunky when compared to other FPS games out there (though, it's come a long way over the years), but in a way, that adds to part of it's charm once you get past that. Small things such as having multiple shooting stances, meaning if you're near a hole in the wall you can raise or lower your body until you're at a level that allows you to use that hole to engage through, makes a huge difference into how combat plays out in this game compared to others on the market. You'll want a beefy PC, moreso in the CPU department than the GPU, to get the most out of the game and a lower end computer can be a bit of a hinderance in PvP (E.G. you may be unable to see your shots landing at long range), but for PvE this won't be as much of an issue.
The game has a wide range of multiplayer game types and anyone should be able to find something to accomodate them. There's King of the Hill battles akin to Battlefield, Life servers that are sort of a mix between The Sims and GTA Online, Invade and Annex servers (Players fighting AI to take back towns), so on, so forth. There's also a huge community of players who make custom missions, be it a coop adventure or an organised PvP battle, there's more arcade orientated units and groups who focus on making combat as realistic as possible. There's also a huge amount of mods and community addons for the game, from missions, uniforms, vehicles, weapons, realistic functioning radio plugin, so on, so forth. One need only look and you should be able to find something you want, both in terms of content and community.
Arma 3 is definitely a game worth picking up if you like realistic combat, a sense of community and/or a huge range of community added content.

TLDR: 9/10 - Recommended for more tactical and technical minded gamers. The slow pacing of the game in general may turn some people off.
This is the only game I know of where tension of battle gets to you. You play as your typical soldier with a stupidly wide variety of gear, but this isn't a game where you use twitch reflexes to get a 360 no scope headshot 400 meters away.
This is a war simulator. Just like when you play paintball, your pitiful and infantile COD and Quake skills are useless here. Hearing gun fire and bullets whiz past your ears makes your heart race as you scramble for cover only to be shot in the back by a single man flanking you to the right 300 meters away which led him to ultimately tear the rest of your heavily armed squadron apart.
Pros:
- Tense simulation of war. You need to think about your movement, your insertion points, flanking positions, bullet drop, target decisions, fatigue, tactical planning etc.
- Then throw all those plans out the door the moment you hear bullets being fired. Suddenly you're pinned down and need to radio in to Bravo team to take out the machine gunner nest.
- Graphics are great after the recent Apex Expansion.
- Massive map with great attention to detail.
- Stupid amount of user mods that are fun to download and play.
- Multiplayer is a slight hit and miss but overall great fun in good servers. I recommend servers like Wastelands, Annex and Invasion, Altis Life or King of the Hill (My favourite)
- Single player is loads of fun, quite intense as well.
- Heaps of vehicles to play around with. I found myself flying a helo just to explore the expansive map of Altis.
- Can make an endless variety of custom made scenarios with the new Eden editor. Much better than the previous iteration IMO.
Cons:
- You need a beefy machine! This game is a bit of beast to tame. I currently run max settings (1080p), 60% distance render at around 60fps with my laptop. I have a 980m nVidia. Game can still struggle in some multiplayer servers like Wastelands. Other game types seem to be okay but there is a slight performance hit (40fps - 50fps).
- SLI won't help much! The engine isn't designed in that fashion so please don't purchase a second video card thinking you'll get a 100% increase in FPS. This game needs your CPU more than your VC.
- Because it's a war simulator focused on realism, the game is generally slow in pace. If you want a quick in and out game, play COD. Games typically last between 30 mins to a few hours. But just to emphasize, this is more of a simulator.
- Models are generally simplistic but this is not much of an issue given the scale of the game itself.
- Steep learning curve. If you want to get good at this game, you need to invest quite a bit of time memorizing the crazy number of controls and features inside of Arma 3. Having said that, it's a lot of fun learning new things about the military.

So being someone with over 2k hours in ArmA 3, i think it is time to write an updated review of what i think overall of this game. This isn't going to be a extremely long detailed professional review, just a decent overview of what i think and some pros and cons that i have found over the time playing.
So for those of you that don't know what ArmA 3 is, it is a military style simulation game that lets you simulate many types of different gamemodes/situations. This ranges from things like Exile, RP (Cops vs Robbers etc), Mil Sim, Wasteland (TDM open world), advanced flying, etc.
If you would like to do any of those things i listed in that short laundry list of gamemodes, you will most likely like this game. You can do/simulate almost everything you can imagine with just the vanilla game or mods.
If you like games like Call of Duty, Battlefield, or any other FPS game, great! But ArmA is like an open world simulator with a huge learning curve. You cannot simply sit down after downloading this game and just be a ♥♥♥♥ing beast. You need to learn many keybinds, mechanics, and learn how to get more than 30fps. This is not an optimized game so don't expect to get over 60fps most of the time. If you sit down and learn all of these things you will love this game.

Well, this might be a very important title. Ive been an Arma-fan since I jumped into the DayZ-cestpool, back in Arma 2. Been enjoying the mods immensely, and was looking forward to more of it, in better visuals, animations and stuff. And Arma 3 sort of delivers that. Some would say, to the max. But Ill be a little realistic in this review, to make it honest without bias etc.
First off, the main game itself, is a masterpiece of Armystuff lol. There is no denying it, really. And with the mods and DLCs etc. It becomes a truely huge game, for army-fans. Including the special ops-lovers out there (I know you want it!). THe diversity of tactics, machines, gear and modes of play, is staggering, once you take a look at the whole Arma-world. Ive given up on trying to fathom it all lol. But I love the concept.
Visuals are maybe just below the top-titles, but being improved all the time. Remember, this is a massive multiplayergame sandbox, so it cant compete with linear singleplayer titles ofc. But it really has some satisfying maps and areas, that look absolutely wonderfull. Lighthouses at night, bombardments over the cities, tracerfire throught he forrests and so on. You will see once you enter yourself lol. Its epic.
On the down side, the realism seems a little too hampering, at times. Working with the concept of DayZ and the old Arma-rule: Your equipment has to be cumbersome to work with, so we have to be safe, before emptying our backpacks and so on. However, to this day, I find it too hampering, tbh. The inventory system is and have always been the down side, imo, with this series. Its slow and glitchy. There are mods out there, that makes it better, but in the end, the main version sucks. You kinda get used to it, though, so its not that bad I guess.
The building system has some good idea, but for some reason, the modules are also kinda glitchy and often wont align to ground and such. THe physics are also a bit weird (floating walls etc.) But the ideas are awesome, and hopefully in time, they will iron out the kinks and all.
THe maps are absolutely huge. And sure feels good playing. The ALtis/Startis maps are a little boring, tbh. THe dry Greek-style islands make for a very monotone vista, but the design of them, seems alright. There are other maps, and some are pretty sweet. I havent played the newest one yet (Pangea I think its called?), but I hear good things about it.
If you want a good look at the game, and what to expect, check out Frankie On PC and Sada´s exploration of the newest map. Good fun too :-)

Arma 3 is a game you'll either love or hate and personally, I love it. Sure, the game is a bit confronting at first, as it looks like it has a million controls (pro-tip: If you're mostly sticking to infantry combat, you'll only have a handful more buttons and button combinations to learn than the most shooters E.G. Battlefield) and the game definitely feels clunky when compared to other FPS games out there (though, it's come a long way over the years), but in a way, that adds to part of it's charm once you get past that. Small things such as having multiple shooting stances, meaning if you're near a hole in the wall you can raise or lower your body until you're at a level that allows you to use that hole to engage through, makes a huge difference into how combat plays out in this game compared to others on the market. You'll want a beefy PC, moreso in the CPU department than the GPU, to get the most out of the game and a lower end computer can be a bit of a hinderance in PvP (E.G. you may be unable to see your shots landing at long range), but for PvE this won't be as much of an issue.
The game has a wide range of multiplayer game types and anyone should be able to find something to accomodate them. There's King of the Hill battles akin to Battlefield, Life servers that are sort of a mix between The Sims and GTA Online, Invade and Annex servers (Players fighting AI to take back towns), so on, so forth. There's also a huge community of players who make custom missions, be it a coop adventure or an organised PvP battle, there's more arcade orientated units and groups who focus on making combat as realistic as possible. There's also a huge amount of mods and community addons for the game, from missions, uniforms, vehicles, weapons, realistic functioning radio plugin, so on, so forth. One need only look and you should be able to find something you want, both in terms of content and community.
Arma 3 is definitely a game worth picking up if you like realistic combat, a sense of community and/or a huge range of community added content.

TLDR: 9/10 - Recommended for more tactical and technical minded gamers. The slow pacing of the game in general may turn some people off.
This is the only game I know of where tension of battle gets to you. You play as your typical soldier with a stupidly wide variety of gear, but this isn't a game where you use twitch reflexes to get a 360 no scope headshot 400 meters away.
This is a war simulator. Just like when you play paintball, your pitiful and infantile COD and Quake skills are useless here. Hearing gun fire and bullets whiz past your ears makes your heart race as you scramble for cover only to be shot in the back by a single man flanking you to the right 300 meters away which led him to ultimately tear the rest of your heavily armed squadron apart.
Pros:
- Tense simulation of war. You need to think about your movement, your insertion points, flanking positions, bullet drop, target decisions, fatigue, tactical planning etc.
- Then throw all those plans out the door the moment you hear bullets being fired. Suddenly you're pinned down and need to radio in to Bravo team to take out the machine gunner nest.
- Graphics are great after the recent Apex Expansion.
- Massive map with great attention to detail.
- Stupid amount of user mods that are fun to download and play.
- Multiplayer is a slight hit and miss but overall great fun in good servers. I recommend servers like Wastelands, Annex and Invasion, Altis Life or King of the Hill (My favourite)
- Single player is loads of fun, quite intense as well.
- Heaps of vehicles to play around with. I found myself flying a helo just to explore the expansive map of Altis.
- Can make an endless variety of custom made scenarios with the new Eden editor. Much better than the previous iteration IMO.
Cons:
- You need a beefy machine! This game is a bit of beast to tame. I currently run max settings (1080p), 60% distance render at around 60fps with my laptop. I have a 980m nVidia. Game can still struggle in some multiplayer servers like Wastelands. Other game types seem to be okay but there is a slight performance hit (40fps - 50fps).
- SLI won't help much! The engine isn't designed in that fashion so please don't purchase a second video card thinking you'll get a 100% increase in FPS. This game needs your CPU more than your VC.
- Because it's a war simulator focused on realism, the game is generally slow in pace. If you want a quick in and out game, play COD. Games typically last between 30 mins to a few hours. But just to emphasize, this is more of a simulator.
- Models are generally simplistic but this is not much of an issue given the scale of the game itself.
- Steep learning curve. If you want to get good at this game, you need to invest quite a bit of time memorizing the crazy number of controls and features inside of Arma 3. Having said that, it's a lot of fun learning new things about the military.

I would have not bought this game if not for the DayZ mod for Arma 2. I didn't really like Arma 2 all that much, but Arma 3 was much better in terms of gameplay and mechanics.
That said, this is the anti call of duty, anti battlefield, anti arcade fps. This is a very difficult game. It's hard to shoot things from more than 200-300 meters, you'll not be on full auto ever (maybe room clearing with a heavy machine gun haha bratatatatatatatatatatatat). This is basically single well placed shots. If you've ever fired a firearm, pistol, rifle of any sort and tried to hit something at 100m out in a standing position you'll know what I mean. Even on a knee it's hard. Prone is by far the easiest as there is far less sway in your aim, and of course breathing. Anyway, alot of that carries over to Arma 3. 50m targets are fairly easy, 100m + targets start to become troublesome but not too bad once you get used to leading the target just a bit if they are moving or running. We're talking bullet drop, velocity and all those factors. A stiff breeze will throw off your shot (more so for sniping) so it's a good idea to watch the trees for the breeze. Seriously, it's more for sniping but long guns still get affected at larger distances (100m+, but really affects 1000m or more).
I love Arma 3 - for ravage, exile, and all the dayz type of mods. Arma 3 itself? It's cool I guess. Campaign is fun, hard as hell. That's not where this game shines.
This game shines because of the mods, if it wasn't for that this game would be DEAD DEAD DEAD. Hell, I don't even think Arma 3 would be out if it wasn't for Arma 2 and it's DayZ mod. That alone sky rocketed sales for the Arma series and brought to light the game.
If you are looking for a single player version of DayZ - then you should pick up the ravage mod. It is fantastic. There is also Exile which is online multiplayer, very similar to DayZ as well.
Plus there are just a ton of Scenarios to play in Arma 3 itself, things like assasinations, ambush convoys, helicopter attacks, tanks......it's endless.
This game has endless replay value after you finish the campaign (or just ignore the campaign, but I think going through the campaign really teaches you the mechanics of the game and makes playing the mods easier).

The third installment of the Saints Row series is very familiar to the others, yet very different.
The game follows the same basic principals as the last two, rival gangs rise up and take control of the Saints turf and it’s up to you do take it back.  In the first game it was because well, the Saints didn’t exist.  In the second it was because you were in a comma for a very long time and everyone must have said ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥on it” and let all these new gangs take over.  In the Third, well, the Saints are now a global mega brand and have gone soft.  If you’ve played the first two that is hard to imagine for the Saints.
The game opens with one of the best cinematically fun sequences I’ve ever seen in a game.  It both looks good, introduces some of the characters, and sets the tone for what is the somewhat ridiculous game play that is signature in the franchise.
It would seem most everyone, save Gat, has sold out.  Peirce is slinging♥♥♥♥♥tasting energy drinks.  Shandi is no longer the lovable crusty stoner, but a high profile catty brunette touch ♥♥♥♥♥ Jersey Shore wannabe.  You are some kind of high profile celebrity.  Gat is, well, he’s Gat.
This game introduces a few new main characters to the gang as well, each with their own weird backstory.  I didn’t really feel myself connecting with the new characters as much as the old ones.  Oleg is a loaf that cheats at chess.  Angel is whiney ex-luchadore.  Kinzie is a whiney ♥♥♥♥♥ that I much more liked in Saints Row 4.  Zimos is a huge pimp and honestly maybe the most likeable. To each their own.
I hope you like ♥♥♥♥♥♥, because there are a lot of them in the game.
The game is extremely good looking on a PC, it is vastly superior to Saints Row 2 in every conceivable way.  Nice reflections, weather effects, textures and so forth really make me feel like I’m moving around a big city.  Vehicle and character models are well done.  The voice acting is great and the cinematics are top notch.
The game has really taken what was good in the first games and made it better and fixed most of the things I thought were wrong with Saints Row 2.
The number of vehicles in the game has vastly grown.  The car physics are drastically different and diverse from the first game.  Flying vehicles are more or less the same in terms of how to fly them.  There is a new GPS system that directs you where to go by showing you arrows on the street, it is much more convenient than looking at the mini map all the time.
The AI is vastly improved as well.  When you call homies they are no longer simply cannon fodder.  The same is true for the enemies whom tend to swarm you without hesitation and can lead to some very hectic battles.  They no longer hesitate to shoot you.  It does not feel like a console port!
The number of weapons has grown a lot as well.  There are many more weapons and all weapons have upgrade paths, which actually makes you focus on kind of creating a character weapon build.  You probably won’t be able to upgrade everything throughout the story without serious grinding so it’s important to pick and chose what you do upgrade.
The story is merely tolerable, but is unique in it’s own Saints Row kind of way.  The story also allows you to make choices.  Most choices don’t have a very serious impact except for the last one.  Some parts of the story seem very random and ill put together.   Examples include things such as why do I always have to go back to the Penthouse if it was blown up and we aren’t staying there anymore?  Why is Gat even in the game?  Can Shandi stop her QQ and do more pew pew?  Can Angel just die already?
Thankfully you no longer do you have to earn “respect” by doing side activities to play the main story missions, which is a welcome change.
My playthrough consisted of using all the DLC on medium difficulty.  I finished the main storyline in ~14 hours.  The DLC actually makes the game quite easy as it gives you money and xp bonus.  You also start with many good vehicles and military grade weapons which almost give you an unfair early advantage.  At no time did I really feel like I had to do any side activities for extra money which means there’s actually a lot of stuff to do that I didn’t do.  I was able to just pretty much run though the story as fast as I could.
The DLC missions are actually quite good and add a little extra something to the game and was actually some of the best content in the game.
TLDR;  Game is good. Game is Saints Row. Game is sexy and many ♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Play it.

I would have not bought this game if not for the DayZ mod for Arma 2. I didn't really like Arma 2 all that much, but Arma 3 was much better in terms of gameplay and mechanics.
That said, this is the anti call of duty, anti battlefield, anti arcade fps. This is a very difficult game. It's hard to shoot things from more than 200-300 meters, you'll not be on full auto ever (maybe room clearing with a heavy machine gun haha bratatatatatatatatatatatat). This is basically single well placed shots. If you've ever fired a firearm, pistol, rifle of any sort and tried to hit something at 100m out in a standing position you'll know what I mean. Even on a knee it's hard. Prone is by far the easiest as there is far less sway in your aim, and of course breathing. Anyway, alot of that carries over to Arma 3. 50m targets are fairly easy, 100m + targets start to become troublesome but not too bad once you get used to leading the target just a bit if they are moving or running. We're talking bullet drop, velocity and all those factors. A stiff breeze will throw off your shot (more so for sniping) so it's a good idea to watch the trees for the breeze. Seriously, it's more for sniping but long guns still get affected at larger distances (100m+, but really affects 1000m or more).
I love Arma 3 - for ravage, exile, and all the dayz type of mods. Arma 3 itself? It's cool I guess. Campaign is fun, hard as hell. That's not where this game shines.
This game shines because of the mods, if it wasn't for that this game would be DEAD DEAD DEAD. Hell, I don't even think Arma 3 would be out if it wasn't for Arma 2 and it's DayZ mod. That alone sky rocketed sales for the Arma series and brought to light the game.
If you are looking for a single player version of DayZ - then you should pick up the ravage mod. It is fantastic. There is also Exile which is online multiplayer, very similar to DayZ as well.
Plus there are just a ton of Scenarios to play in Arma 3 itself, things like assasinations, ambush convoys, helicopter attacks, tanks......it's endless.
This game has endless replay value after you finish the campaign (or just ignore the campaign, but I think going through the campaign really teaches you the mechanics of the game and makes playing the mods easier).
tl;dr

This is by far, the best game I have ever played. You will find breathtaking graphics, immersive gameplay, and plenty of walking.

It's a far better and more stable *port* than the second game got, and the levels of personal customization are still staggering, but some elements of it feel a bit more... insulting, I guess. For one, It's really damn hard to enjoy gunning down gang members when the brutes can roll up after a few minutes and shut down your fun just by shoving you to death. Story progression isn't so much hand-holding as it is leash-pulling; you're limited from the start to engaging only one gang at a time (mission-wise at least), and even though all the fun sidejobs and goofball challenges are still there (and still fun!), instead of unlocking upgrades and bonus items with them, you just earn cash... so you can buy the upgrades. There's a few things that smack of "broader audience appeal," like nixing all the alcohol and drug use present in earlier titles, but they kept all the absurd violence and prostitution, so it just kinda sends the same idiotic "say no to drugs, but killing♥♥♥♥♥♥is cool!" message I got tired of even as a kid.

As a player, who usually appreciates more linear storytelling, Saints Row: The Third was one of my first ventures into the realm of sandbox-games. And while at times the game feels a bit like a minigame-collection, given all the various activities you are able to engage in, the abundance of optional material is actually one of the games strength. The only real problem I had with the game, was the sometimes frustrating AI of your companion characters, which will lead you to yell "Get in the f***ing car!" maybe a bit to often.
The games strength really lies in the insanity of its content. From the continually ridiculous main story, to totally optional abilities like car-surfing or base-jumping, from causing havoc operating a tank to deliberately letting yourself be run over by cars, the game really understands, what it means to be a sandbox-game. The abundance of character customization options and available vehicles only adds the the feeling, that you can do whatever you want.
Saints Row: The Third is a game, that is designed to be fun, and as along as you aproach it as such, it definetly delivers.

Hmm, where do I begin with this review?
Well, first of all, I am a veteran to this series and I have been playing ArmA for the past 6 years. This is a game that will always keep you interested with the powerful Eden Editor, Zeus, various multiplayer gamemodes and the brilliant singleplayer campaigns.
For the beginners, this is a game that you need to keep on playing to develop your skills, you will not start off as a hero or have the ability to 'run and gun.' This is a military combat simulator sandbox and if you get shot, chances are you will die but if you don't, your abilities will be hindered and become combat ineffective. Best way to learn how to play the game is to go into the editor and make your own little scenario to practise or use one of the many scenarios made by the developers. For multiplayer, there are many different types of gamemodes and missions available across hundreds if not thousands of servers around the globe but if you want a true immersive experience, you would need to join a unit or community that plays with operations, teamwork, coordination and more, including mods to get the best experience.
Mods; man, that's a huge part of the ArmA community. There is a massive community on the BiForums and Steam Workshop dedicated to modifications to enhance your ArmA experience. Some of the big ones like Community Upgrade Project (CUP) has a variety of weapons, vehicles and terrains ported from previous games to ArmA 3. Red Hammer Studios (RHS) has United States Armed Forces (USAF) which includes a large array of US units, weapons, ground vehicles and aircraft. There are so many mods that this game has that I could write a paper to list not even half of them.
The official DLC's for this game are quality content, the Marksman DLC and the Helicopter DLC are a little on the expensive side of things for the amount of content you get but APEX is the best DLC for this game, an entirely new map, lots of new weapons, vehicles, units and more. However I would still suggest you wait until this game and its DLC's go on sale before purchasing it, better 'bang for your buck.'

"But I am a method actor!" exclaims Josh and then he leaves. Leaves everybody. In a bank. Where his pals are about to complete a bank robbery. It is hilarious! Hilarious how stupid some of these characters are and the one-liners in Saints Row The 3rd almost equal to the ones in our favourite American films from the '80s or '90s.
Volition made a replica of GTA IV but made a much better version of it. This is a properly optimised game that looks good and runs well on our PCs. And if you thought the script of GTA included a lot of conversations with dozens of jokes you'll immediately forget that game once you get to know the members of the Saints.
The story revolves around the Saints, an always purple-clad gang who has just taken over Steelport (the fake city where the story takes place) but is thriving to achieve more. To further extend their control over the city they must annihilate the mysterious Syndicate who commands the 3 gangs of Steelport. But then again the government does not like the too much bang-bang in the city so a special anti-gang unit is introduced and you will also have to face its leader, a ruthless general.
Gameplay is exactly the same as what you get used to in GTA IV. There are missions initiated by beacons once approached but the main story missions are launched by calling your buddies on your cellphone. Otherwise, you go wherever you want and do whatever you want in the city. Really. I like how the game rewards me if I hit civilians or when driving for a long time on the oncoming lane or when drifting for a long time.
Remember when Niko hits a car at high speed and flies out of the windshield in GTA IV? Were you laughing hard when that happened just as I did? Well, in Saints Row you have a side mission called "insurance fraud" which means you need to let yourself hit by a car and the more hits you receive the easier it is to fly high (?) and instead of hitting the ground you need to try to hit the hood of another car and so on and so on...the multiplication and the amount of score you receive is enormous! So, you have to be prepared for doing a lot of stupid things with the Saints. This is a must and if you are not up for that you had better quit while you can!
You have collectibles, of course, for the sake of achievements and longevity: you collect cash, sex dolls and drugs. And you can steal vehicles and assassinate people. And you can level-up and spend your hard-earned cash on upgrades. And if you have DLCs you have weapons such as the shark gun that pours blood on people who are then attacked by a shark (yes, the appear from below the asphalt). Stupid fun! Hilarious how stupid some of these characters are and the one-liners in Saints Row The 3rd almost equal to the ones in our favourite American films from the '80s or '90s.
Volition made a replica of GTA IV but made a much better version of it. This is a properly optimised game that looks good and runs well on our PCs. And if you thought the script of GTA included a lot of conversations with dozens of jokes you'll immediately forget that game once you get to know the members of the Saints.
The story revolves around the Saints, an always purple-clad gang who has just taken over Steelport (the fake city where the story takes place) but is thriving to achieve more. To further extend their control over the city they must annihilate the mysterious Syndicate who commands the 3 gangs of Steelport. But then again the government does not like the too much bang-bang in the city so a special anti-gang unit is introduced and you will also have to face its leader, a ruthless general.
Gameplay is exactly the same as what you get used to in GTA IV. There are missions initiated by beacons once approached but the main story missions are launched by calling your buddies on your cellphone. Otherwise, you go wherever you want and do whatever you want in the city. Really. I like how the game rewards me if I hit civilians or when driving for a long time on the oncoming lane or when drifting for a long time.
Remember when Niko hits a car at high speed and flies out of the windshield in GTA IV? Were you laughing hard when that happened just as I did? Well, in Saints Row you have a side mission called "insurance fraud" which means you need to let yourself hit by a car and the more hits you receive the easier it is to fly high (?) and instead of hitting the ground you need to try to hit the hood of another car and so on and so on...the multiplication and the amount of score you receive is enormous! So, you have to be prepared for doing a lot of stupid things with the Saints. This is a must and if you are not up for that you had better quit while you can!
You have collectibles, of course, for the sake of achievements and longevity: you collect cash, sex dolls and drugs. And you can steal vehicles and assassinate people. And you can level-up and spend your hard-earned cash on upgrades. And if you have DLCs you have weapons such as the shark gun that pours blood on people who are then attacked by a shark (yes, the appear from below the asphalt). Stupid fun! You can also have a lot of properties in the city just so you can actually feel like being someone controlling a huge area!

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Saints Row: The Third is a open world action-adventure video game developed by Volition and published by THQ. It is the third title in the Saints Row series. As in the previous games, your-character leads the Third Streets Saints gang in a turf war against three rival gangs using a variety of weapons and vehicles in single-player and cooperative play. Similar to the premise of the previous Saints Row games, your goal is to lead the Third Street Saints gang to overtake its rival gangs in the city turf war.
The game introduces a new setting, the city of Steelport, with its new gangs: the Morningstar, Luchadores, and Deckers, now together known as the Syndicate. Saints Row: The Third introduces experience levels and weapon upgrades to the series. Most actions in the game come with incentives in the form of money and respect (reputation). Money buys land, weapons, and other upgrades, and respect is a kind of experience point that can unlock player abilities like "no damage from falling" or "infinite sprint", as well as upgrades to the player's computer-controlled gang member support.
In turn, players receive further incentive to nearly miss car collisions, streak naked through the streets, shoot others in the groin, blow up Smart cars, and kill mascots in ambient challenges to earn more respect. Lack of respect does not hinder story progress, as it has in previous games.
Player progress and unlocks are managed by an in-game cell phone menu that also lets the player call for vehicle deliveries and non-player character backup.
In combat, you can select weapons from a weapon selection wheel, including regular pistols, submachine guns, shotguns, and rocket launchers alongside special weapons such as UAV drones and a fart-in-a-jar stun grenade.
Overall I think Saints Row The Third is by far the best Saints Row game I've played. If you love the Grand Theft Auto series this is the game for you. I'm sure you'll enjoy it as much as GTA. If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Saints preserve us, this game is insane!
SAINTS ROW THE THIRD is the most unpretentious game I’ve played to date. It aims to be a gloriously over the top thrill ride and it succeeds with great aplomb. From start to finish it’s all-out mayhem. Nowhere else do you get the opportunity to batter someone with a huge adult toy or drive around town with an angry tiger in the passenger seat. Few games have actually made me laugh out loud but SRTT did. There are some truly hilarious moments and plenty of dry dialogue. The one-liners are delivered with perfection by the voice actors (I chose the English voice for the playable character – voiced by Robin Atkin Downes, I believe – and it fitted seamlessly). There have been criticisms that story missions feel more like side missions and I can understand this concern. But story is not really what this game is about. There has to be a narrative of sorts but it’s the freewheeling craziness of the gameplay that makes this game a joy. Graphically the game is pretty good without being notable. Steelport is nicely realised but some of the character models are less impressive. The soundtrack is worth a note as it includes some fantastic music from just about every genre imaginable. It may not be to everyone’s taste but if you fancy 15+ hours of riotous pandemonium (plus however many hours of coop, although I suspect it might get old quite quickly once you’ve finished the campaign and experienced all the hilarity and craziness) then you can’t go far wrong with this game. 4/5

Arma is a great game in a few ways and a terrible game in a lot of ways. If you're looking for something realistic this is it, well kind of. It's very deep and goes a long way to try and be realistic. In most ways it succeeds. In a few though it doesn't, the biggest example of this being the inclusion of 3rd person. 3rd person ruins it for me because players can peak around corners and over ledges with no penalty or chance of being seen while doing so.
There's a ton of content, a large community (most of which are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s but that's usual and shouldn't matter in a review imo), and a lot of thought still goes into this game. The bulk of your experience will be online multiplayer most likely. Possibly just messing around in the 3d editor though. The controls are vast and take a lot of getting used to. The movement is clunky as hell, the environments are ugly as hell (the jungle looks nice in trailers but there's only like 4 different tree assets that just repeat all over the place so after a few minutes you've seen it all) and that's extra $$$$.
If you're going to get this because of FrankyPC's vids - don't. Those are scripted and this game is 80% running / driving and then some really clunky fights.
I still recommend this game with those downfalls because it's still a ton of fun if you give it time to grow on you.

The highly anticipated review for me, because The Saints are special to me, unique as a part. Game, which was theoretically last chance, and last hope for THQ, was the biggest money injection they got, and they still wasn't able to stock up money, to cover up the bancrupt. THQ was with us since 1989, and it's hard to believe, that they're just gone ... Their message was sent through their games. Lots of their projects has been sold to those, who aren't capable of putting it to top level (I won't mention no one, because I have always respected work of the developers).
Saints Row: The Third as a game, and THQ as a dev has point from me, because they were in need of money, but they still wanted to be themselves, and didn't caught up with standard game bussiness model (using same old tactics, to be successful on the market).
SR3 is attacking sandbox genre with its uniqueness, and it's conquering with Grand Theft Auto series way more smart. GTA always trying to be realistic with a bit of "american dream" .. SR3 doing opposite - total rampage, crazyness without limits, absolute unrealistic b-sh*t, octopuses on our heads, dancing pandas, fetish pedestrians, Safeword crib, big dild*s, robotic pu*sy penetrators.
Story is about the rise, about motivation and work to be, what you want to be. The Saints came to Steelport with 0 on bank account, without weapons, without connexions, but with DETERMINATION to conquere whole Steelport and they did it. (Of course I'm not taking it serious) Cutscenes are done pretty well, dialougues are well-written, brilliant, and epic funny. Characters was picked up correctly, almost every one from The Saints are unforgetable - Zimos, Shaundi, Pierce, Oleg, Kinzie and Angel of course.
Story-line is written like you finally think it's over, but it's not even in halfway. Like 3 times I thought it's over, but it wasn't, and I was glad, that story of killing anyone who came to our way continues. Behind story missions there are plenty of "activities" and activities to be done. Like 36 assasinations, 30 car hijacks, 41 challenges, and around 40 activities to be needed done, for taking over Steelport.
Buying shops, and drug labs :X Upgrading mansions and cribs improving your control of the streets, money income and respect. You can tune up almost every car in-game, or find armored street-cleaner car and run over Zombies. Steal a jet, and♥♥♥♥♥up day of police officers, or just grab a tank, and roll through the streets, and running over cars. In CO-OP even better.
Soundtrack is great, playlist on the radios are solid .. Most significant is track POWER from Kanye West from My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy album. This track in original describes power of Kanye, but it's almost accurate, to describe power of The Saints.
In the whole game, there's only 1 thing I actually don't like, and it is level-design. Artificially increased effort, of making game harder, just ain't worked, it was still so easy, but it just look stupid. I will name some situations .. For example, you had to steal military boat. It was just chilling on the water, behind the military camp. When you sneaked from back-side, and tried to stole the boat, it was just still marked on the map, but you couldn't deliver it, because you had to enter the military base, to earn 4 wanted stars, and then you was able to deliver it... Really stupid, and this happening almost every-time in the game, but it doesn't matter that much, because this game is untouchable!

This game is basically mindless violence fun interjected by story and some deep moments.
The game is basically a giant chaotic murderbrawl of chaos. You have to reclaim your empire with military grade weapons and by killing every person in the game that challanges you. The gameplay is good and fast pased with lots of shooting and explosions and the pacing is kept high in most of the missions. The shooting is basically like any other shooting game it has almost a cartoonish feel to it at times.
The story is a mess with the villians jumping from person to person without much connection. There are options in the game which let you get certain upgrades which are basically useless except for the last mission which branches into two for all the villians (however, the missions are very... anticlimatic). There are a few bugs here and there for which I had to just deal and the bikes are almost undrivable.
That being said, the game is fun. Its often called a GTA copy but the point it emphasizes is that its supposed to be wacky and fun. You can dress like a bondage slave and destroy tanks with a remote control. It's not realisitc (you jump into cars like a cartoon) but thats the point. Its fun, comedic, and at times even gets sentimental.
Overall, a definate buy

Team Fortress 2 used to be a great game. A game with a very wide variety of playstyles, player customization, what used to be a very much alive community, a self contained economy, ever challenging gameplay and an ever evolving, ever far reaching high skill ceilling. All of this contained in a stylized, fun theme.
So, why did this game fall down from grace?
Team Fortress 2 has many problems and flaws which make it pretty much worthless to play with. I shall try to go into details as to what these are, why, and what could be done.
1) Competitive.
I'm a competitive person. I like playing against humans - it's never the same experience, it's difficult, challenging and rewarding. CS:GO's competitve was really well made. TF2 used to have a genuine, living and interesting competitive scene. So what happened there?
Valve happened, ever clueless. They essentially forcefully rammed a disfunctional competitive system onto players who never wanted this. Now, whether you're a casual or competitive player, it doesn't matter. You can't just get into a random game which will be fun anymore, and all of this due to the ELO which was enforced.
The competitive for TF2 was very poorly executed. Making it a bit more difficult to get into community servers (less intuitively), limiting the actual fun experience players received by dictating who they'd run into, altering what was a perfect player interface and all of that with no returns. Because the problem isn't just that they broke a lot of things putting these updates, but they did so to put up things which were broken as well. Competitive mode for TF2 does NOT work.
The best option here would be to return to when TF2 didn't have enforced Competitive, and instead make it stand alone, very much like CS:GO's. One of the appeal which TF2 had to players was how quick and easy it was for them to get into fun. This needs to come back.
2) Hat simulator 2k18.
This is actually something I believe is disgraceful. The actual download and storage size is essentially what, 70% texture and model size for hats and skins? This is disgraceful because the only updates which seem to grace TF2 is the one which adds to it's economy - in this case hats. The <ACTUAL> updates (actual content, maps, weapons, game modes, features, events) have been remarkably lackluster as of late, and this simply pushes people away. Worse however is again, how the main updates are all seemingly about new skins most of the time. Updates are very rarely made for the players, but for their wallets.
New hats are cool and all, but they should not be the main call of the game. Bringi ng serious updating and content back to TF2 would breath serious life in again, if it was taken seriously. I am aware there has been a few propper updates, but come on - they are simply too far apart.
3) The last update to TF2's interesting and entertaining comic based story was from the 10th January 2017. That's 10 months and 15 days back. Comparing this to the updates which are gracing the actual fans, there are clearly some problems which need to be adressed. Lots of people are very interested in TF2's lore and story. Many people are interested in the characters. Many people still make SFM stuff of the game. The community still has life - why isn't it treated as such?
I personally see the agressive hat and economy based item updates are extremely short sighted. With gambling down in TF2, the economy took a fairly heavy strike. With people leaving due to the sad disrepair of the game, many people left again. This in turn means a lot less trader as a whole, which means the TF2 economy and value of items, while still "alive", is just short sighted. Generating new hats and injecting new content into the economy isn't going to save the game, it's going to keep it stagnant. Bringing more players and life back will make people more inclined to pay more.
Team Fortress 2 is a game which is undeniably a victim of it's own success. Team Fortress 2 started as a humble game with loads of hickups. It became something great. And then was treated as nothing more than a vulgar cash cow.
Team Fortress 2 still has a lot of potential. It is still visually up to date, fun and with varied game play. In hindsight, games like Overwatch don't have that much when compared to TF2 - the only reason such games managed to take such a hold was due to the greed run disrepair of the state of TF2. Games like OW pulled interest in a way similar to what was keeping TF2's hype and interest alive (that being the character videos and video contents), and simply grew from Team Fortress 2's disrepair. Had the game had good, functional and realistic management, odds are Team Fortress 2 would never even have dipped.
Add to this another few set of problems which are again relative to updates - lack of "♥♥♥♥s" given about the game means that the Windows 10/8 compatibility issues aren't tackled. I could seriously go on like this.
In short?
Team Fortress 2 used to be a great game. It still somewhat is, but it's flaws and idiocincracies do not condone to actually download it and play it. Without change of management, Team Fortress 2 is not going to get better, just worse.
Unless you hear or see some serious, actual change, don't bother sinking time and ressource into a dying venture. Just join the OverWatch bandwaggon (which has a significantly lower skill ceilling), CS:GO (significantly higher but more about the challenge), Paladins and the likes.
There are other games for you to play and have fun. Don't waste your time here. I wasted mine writing this so you wouldn't have to.

* Following story took place on a Arma 3 Wasteland Mod*
So there I was just riding in the back of a truck with my squad when I spotted her. She was so beautiful that I had to do a quick double take. I just couldn't stop staring at her nice curves and soft gleam. I quickly told the driver to pull over, and I hopped out of the truck and ran up to her not fully processing her beauty. For some odd reason I felt like I already knew her name, and without thinking blurted out "Betty its you!". She just stared calmly back at me from the water line, not making asound. By this time, the rest of the squad is making their way over to me asking what was so important. But all talked died away after they caught a glimpse of her. My commander whispered in awe "This can't be real!". She WAS real and sitting right in front of us.
She was the most beautiful submarine that I ever saw! From the dark grey complextion all the way to the thin periscope, Betty was a beautiful specimen.
Then, out of nowhere, we began taking incoming fire from the village behind us. "Fan out!" was shouted by our commander and we began to return fire. I was about ready to join in the fight, but I couldn't just leave Betty. I whispered quietly to myself "I'm sorry fellas but Betty's the only girl for me.". I quickly climbed down the ladder and closed the hatch behind me and started Betty up.
I began backing her up in the search for deeper water, and everything inside me was telling me to go help my friends. But I pushed those feelings behind and turned Betty towards the wide open ocean. I eased the throttle forward, and me and Betty were on our way. I heard the explosion of a couple gernades, and slowly the snapping of bullets died down. The last sight that could be seen through Betty's windshield were the tears streaming down my face, before the dark blue water encased the entire sub.
10/10 would leave teammates for Betty again
