ARMA 3 is a love hate relationship: best mil-sim ever and one of the worst engines ever brought into creation.
ARMA 3 is the most versatile military simulation available and the multiplayer modes are endless. This is the true PC experience when it comes to sheer scope and magnitude. I have put the most hours into this game when it comes to FPS games in the last decade and will continue to play it until the next ARMA comes out.
On the other side of the matter, ARMA is the WORST optimized game I have ever played. It barely makes use of more than one core which effectively makes all GPUs moot and runs at a terrible framerate for everyone. It is beyond ridiculous that any developer would be ok with the absolutely horrible optimization that this engine has. It is really so bad I am having a hard time putting it into words. ARMA has bad optimization for the days of dual cores never mind for today's standards. It is completely embarrassing for the developers to have this shoddy excuse for an engine in 2016. With that being said I love this game and I hate the engine with a burning passion.

After buying and downloading, I couldn't find a single compatible server through the quick match feature. I had to look through servers to find one that didn't mention any mods, to which i was kicked after a few seconds from joining. I learned that your really need the A3 launcher to make this game functional.
It seems that MOST servers are running the exile mod with zombies, which basically just turns this into your standard survival game, where you forage for food bits and water and med kits and run away from zombies, blah blah blah....
I thought this was a tactical large-mapped fps, but wtf do I know?
The only maps i've been able to find that play a normal game style, have snipers that pick me off within 50ft of my spawn. Where I have zero clue where they're coming from.

* Following story took place on a Arma 3 Wasteland Mod*
So there I was just riding in the back of a truck with my squad when I spotted her. She was so beautiful that I had to do a quick double take. I just couldn't stop staring at her nice curves and soft gleam. I quickly told the driver to pull over, and I hopped out of the truck and ran up to her not fully processing her beauty. For some odd reason I felt like I already knew her name, and without thinking blurted out "Betty its you!". She just stared calmly back at me from the water line, not making asound. By this time, the rest of the squad is making their way over to me asking what was so important. But all talked died away after they caught a glimpse of her. My commander whispered in awe "This can't be real!". She WAS real and sitting right in front of us.
She was the most beautiful submarine that I ever saw! From the dark grey complextion all the way to the thin periscope, Betty was a beautiful specimen.
Then, out of nowhere, we began taking incoming fire from the village behind us. "Fan out!" was shouted by our commander and we began to return fire. I was about ready to join in the fight, but I couldn't just leave Betty. I whispered quietly to myself "I'm sorry fellas but Betty's the only girl for me.". I quickly climbed down the ladder and closed the hatch behind me and started Betty up.
I began backing her up in the search for deeper water, and everything inside me was telling me to go help my friends. But I pushed those feelings behind and turned Betty towards the wide open ocean. I eased the throttle forward, and me and Betty were on our way. I heard the explosion of a couple gernades, and slowly the snapping of bullets died down. The last sight that could be seen through Betty's windshield were the tears streaming down my face, before the dark blue water encased the entire sub.
10/10 would leave teammates for Betty again

ARMA 3 is a love hate relationship: best mil-sim ever and one of the worst engines ever brought into creation.
ARMA 3 is the most versatile military simulation available and the multiplayer modes are endless. This is the true PC experience when it comes to sheer scope and magnitude. I have put the most hours into this game when it comes to FPS games in the last decade and will continue to play it until the next ARMA comes out.
On the other side of the matter, ARMA is the WORST optimized game I have ever played. It barely makes use of more than one core which effectively makes all GPUs moot and runs at a terrible framerate for everyone. It is beyond ridiculous that any developer would be ok with the absolutely horrible optimization that this engine has. It is really so bad I am having a hard time putting it into words. ARMA has bad optimization for the days of dual cores never mind for today's standards. It is completely embarrassing for the developers to have this shoddy excuse for an engine in 2016. With that being said I love this game and I hate the engine with a burning passion.

Team Fortress 2 used to be a great game. A game with a very wide variety of playstyles, player customization, what used to be a very much alive community, a self contained economy, ever challenging gameplay and an ever evolving, ever far reaching high skill ceilling. All of this contained in a stylized, fun theme.
So, why did this game fall down from grace?
Team Fortress 2 has many problems and flaws which make it pretty much worthless to play with. I shall try to go into details as to what these are, why, and what could be done.
1) Competitive.
I'm a competitive person. I like playing against humans - it's never the same experience, it's difficult, challenging and rewarding. CS:GO's competitve was really well made. TF2 used to have a genuine, living and interesting competitive scene. So what happened there?
Valve happened, ever clueless. They essentially forcefully rammed a disfunctional competitive system onto players who never wanted this. Now, whether you're a casual or competitive player, it doesn't matter. You can't just get into a random game which will be fun anymore, and all of this due to the ELO which was enforced.
The competitive for TF2 was very poorly executed. Making it a bit more difficult to get into community servers (less intuitively), limiting the actual fun experience players received by dictating who they'd run into, altering what was a perfect player interface and all of that with no returns. Because the problem isn't just that they broke a lot of things putting these updates, but they did so to put up things which were broken as well. Competitive mode for TF2 does NOT work.
The best option here would be to return to when TF2 didn't have enforced Competitive, and instead make it stand alone, very much like CS:GO's. One of the appeal which TF2 had to players was how quick and easy it was for them to get into fun. This needs to come back.
2) Hat simulator 2k18.
This is actually something I believe is disgraceful. The actual download and storage size is essentially what, 70% texture and model size for hats and skins? This is disgraceful because the only updates which seem to grace TF2 is the one which adds to it's economy - in this case hats. The <ACTUAL> updates (actual content, maps, weapons, game modes, features, events) have been remarkably lackluster as of late, and this simply pushes people away. Worse however is again, how the main updates are all seemingly about new skins most of the time. Updates are very rarely made for the players, but for their wallets.
New hats are cool and all, but they should not be the main call of the game. Bringi ng serious updating and content back to TF2 would breath serious life in again, if it was taken seriously. I am aware there has been a few propper updates, but come on - they are simply too far apart.
3) The last update to TF2's interesting and entertaining comic based story was from the 10th January 2017. That's 10 months and 15 days back. Comparing this to the updates which are gracing the actual fans, there are clearly some problems which need to be adressed. Lots of people are very interested in TF2's lore and story. Many people are interested in the characters. Many people still make SFM stuff of the game. The community still has life - why isn't it treated as such?
I personally see the agressive hat and economy based item updates are extremely short sighted. With gambling down in TF2, the economy took a fairly heavy strike. With people leaving due to the sad disrepair of the game, many people left again. This in turn means a lot less trader as a whole, which means the TF2 economy and value of items, while still "alive", is just short sighted. Generating new hats and injecting new content into the economy isn't going to save the game, it's going to keep it stagnant. Bringing more players and life back will make people more inclined to pay more.
Team Fortress 2 is a game which is undeniably a victim of it's own success. Team Fortress 2 started as a humble game with loads of hickups. It became something great. And then was treated as nothing more than a vulgar cash cow.
Team Fortress 2 still has a lot of potential. It is still visually up to date, fun and with varied game play. In hindsight, games like Overwatch don't have that much when compared to TF2 - the only reason such games managed to take such a hold was due to the greed run disrepair of the state of TF2. Games like OW pulled interest in a way similar to what was keeping TF2's hype and interest alive (that being the character videos and video contents), and simply grew from Team Fortress 2's disrepair. Had the game had good, functional and realistic management, odds are Team Fortress 2 would never even have dipped.
Add to this another few set of problems which are again relative to updates - lack of "♥♥♥♥s" given about the game means that the Windows 10/8 compatibility issues aren't tackled. I could seriously go on like this.
In short?
Team Fortress 2 used to be a great game. It still somewhat is, but it's flaws and idiocincracies do not condone to actually download it and play it. Without change of management, Team Fortress 2 is not going to get better, just worse.
Unless you hear or see some serious, actual change, don't bother sinking time and ressource into a dying venture. Just join the OverWatch bandwaggon (which has a significantly lower skill ceilling), CS:GO (significantly higher but more about the challenge), Paladins and the likes.
There are other games for you to play and have fun. Don't waste your time here. I wasted mine writing this so you wouldn't have to.

For every phenomenal atmospheric time you spend, something silly will happen that takes you right out of the moment, but there is nothing, not one single thing that will suck you in and put you right there in the time and place as Arma.
As far as realistic shooters go, this is it. Maybe not in it`s base guise. Default, it is a semi-futuristic shooter, with an awful campaign. Arma never was about the default content though, and the modding community is beyond extensive - it is what Arma is.
Cold war, zombie shooter, pure survival, WW1/2, vietnam, sci-fi, roleplay, hardcore realism - Pretty much anything you could think of is possible in the A3 engine. Modders make the game into what people want from it.
This definitely is not CoD. It`s as far from it as you could get. If you want an arcadey shooter, go there. If you want realism, if you want a massive amount of content, always increasing in so many unexpected ways, get this.
Be aware it is not something that will work on basic hardware. It is not a generic shooter, made for horribly underpowered consoles and ported over to PC. If you have a decent PC though, and are looking for something far more serious than the CoD triple headshot super bonus crap, this is it.

No hope to get a better game than this, just forget Arma, or wait until some better missions will be made and hosted properly in decent servers (I don't know how).
And, I was forgetting, there are still lot of bugs to fix since release years ago.
No words about "Kart" expansion... About price... About other useless DLCs release... Or about Tanoa which make impossible to play now for everyone does not own it.
No words for all of this smoke, not a game indeed, just smoke.

This game is a dream come true for me! This is probably the most realistic combat simulator I have ever played! Being able to play on real, photo accurate locations is really fun, and awesome, especially when you take the vast size of the maps into consideration! My favorite part of this game are the 2D and 3D editor tools that are provided with the game, it allows you to create just about any scenario you can think of! Have you ever wanted to experience a stealth night operation as a scuba diver, and wipe out patrols? Or have you ever wanted to experience a full on war with combined operations, such as hundreds of ground units, armored vehicles, and aircraft? OR have you ever wanted to design a fortress that you and your AI team has to defend from hundreds of invading enemies? Well, all of this and much MUCH more is possible with the easy to use editor tools!
Also, I have come to the conclusion that Arma 3's AI is the most advanced, versitile, and smartest AI than any other game has to offer, I was extremely surprised when I hand-placed a bunch of jets in an airbase, to see the AI know how to actually taxi the jets to the runway strip, and take off in an orderly fashion without running into each other or other obstacles during the whole process!! Also, I didn't even place any waypoints or create any scripts for them, it was all the AI!!! The AI can adapt to pretty much any situation, and will follow orders from you if you are the leader of the group. Plus, it is really fun to watch independent AI squads battle it out without your interactions, the AI squad leaders will actually command their units (even you if you are part of their squad!) in any situation!
The multiplayer is very fun, you can play in a variety of servers that could involve capturing territories, fighting AI, role playing, combined operations with over a hundreds of players, or all of the above combined!!
Lastly, this is more of a thank you towards Bohemia Interactive:
As someone who strongly supports the United States Military, and has 3 brothers in the Army, I thank you for your bold, brave, and admirable move, to not include female soldiers in this game, I understand that society is trying to move in that "accepting", "politically correct", and "equality" direction, but this whole movement is proving to be VERY troublesome and problematic for the United States Military. Ask any American male soldier who has actually fought in combat overseas, what they think of allowing female soldiers fight by their sides, they will ALL say that it is not good, and that they rather keep females off the battlefields. Unfortunately, American society doesn't understand the fact that females naturally do not have the capability of controlling their emotions under stressful and dangerous situations as well as males can. There have been MANY recorded events that involve female soldiers putting their battle partners in grave danger during combat situations due to letting their emotions control them. I understand that this is just a video game, but it still does matter A LOT what developers do with their games, because you would be really surprised how many young men and women go to enlist for the military just because of movies or video games, honestly, it is really quite sad.
So thank you Bohemia Interactive, for making such a good game, you guys are making excellent bold moves, which I believe sets a great example of how other developers should operate, and not fall into the common traps set by society. Thank you!

It was a hot day on the arid island of Altis. My AI companions and I daydreamed of pizza all throughout our patrol. As such, I signaled one of the boys to place an order. We were notified the pizza was on the way to our position, and waited hungrily in one of the various abandoned houses on the outskirts of Altis. However, all was not well. After twenty minutes had passed, a voice on the other end of the radio sprang to life, informing my four man squad of a complete travesty; our pizza had been stolen by CSAT forces.
I sprang into action immediately, retrieving the nearest Lynx and jumping into the nearest vehicle, said vehicle being a sedan. I yelled for my men to get in, but the poor boys couldn't move from their sheer hunger. I bid them farewell and went on my way; this had become a one man mission. And it was personal.
I sped over the terrain, quickly meeting up with the team that spotted the damned pizza bandits. The aroma of pizza was wafting up the nearby hill, overwhelming my fellow soldiers. I threw myself back into the sedan, stopping just on top of the hill. It was time.
I set up my trusty Lynx, and set my sights on the CSAT officer. Around him were three to four other men, all prepared to consume my delicious pizza sent from the heavens. Without a moment's notice, I fired. Down went the officer, sending his men into a panic. I swifty ended their existences one by one. With the area clear, I ran into the previously occupied house to the unwelcome smell of something burning. I looked to the oven with a look of dread plastering itself over my face.
The pizza was burnt. While I was exacting my revenge, the very objective had been left to heat up for too long.
I sprinted from the house and back into the sedan. I launched over the terrain of Altis at full speed; I had to get another pizza, no matter what. But disaster struck. In my haste to drive the four klicks to the nearest Dominos, I sped up a hill and became airborne. I braced myself for the result of my folly. The car flipped over and began rolling once it hit the ground.
Broken glass slashed across my face, and the whiplash was making me sick. The car finally stopped rolling, and remained on it's side. I crawled out of the car via the broken windshield and cried out with pain. My leg was done for, my ribs ached, and blood spurted from the long gashes I'd received.
I laid upon the ground, defeated. I gazed up at the sky, my vision beginning to blur. A light was coming closer, on it's way to envelop me. But something deep within me rejected that light. The sheer desire for a damn good pizza burned within me. I can't give up here.
I managed to sit up, and began performing first aid on myself. I pulled glass shards out of places I didn't even know the human body had, bandaged gashes that would turn into magnificent scars, and snapped my leg back into place. I got up and began moving towards the objective on foot. Two and a half klicks to go.
I had only moved half a klick however, when the radio sprang to life once more. My squad had been discovered by an enemy MRAP. Horror filled my mind as I listened to the sounds of good men being shot like starving dogs. And all I could do was move forward. And then it was silent. I frantically called out over the radio, but no one responded. My men were gone.
I walked on in silence, until finally, there it was. Tears streamed down my face as I stood in front of the Dominos. I ate pizza like no man had ever eaten pizza before.

Team Fortress 2 is a class-based shooter with countless ways to play the game and unlimited  skill ceiling; there are always new things to try and you can always improve at the game.
The latest update "Jungle inferno" is a fantastic display of the hard work and love the developers put into the game. All the new weapons pyro weapons are well thought-out and unique additions to the class (except the hot hand, which is fine). They create new playstyles which are viable without being overpowered. For example the new flamethrower trades airblast-spam (airblast also reworked, no longer an annoying stunlock!) and afterburn for a powerful aim-centric play that keeps itself from being overpowered by punishing the player for missing by significantly reducing the rate of fire and damage.
One thing that was missing from the update was the promised competitive mode changes. Currently the official competitive mode lacks skill balance, the games are balanced by averaging ranks that you gain by grinding the mode (no placement matches). But the delay of competitive changes is only because the developers want to nail the mode this time, instead of rushing it out, like they did for the current iteration. Direct quote from one of the developers: "We didn't feel what was ready was enough to be a worthy refresh of the mode yet."
I thoroughly recommend this game for anyone looking for a skill-based, well balanced, class-based shooter.

I’ve been wanting to play TF2 since I was 9. It seemed amazing. This game really is a great Free to Play first person co-op game. You push a payload cart with your friends while defending. Here are the pros I find about this game:
Pros
- Wide selection of hats, shirts, etc.
- Weapons get balanced
- Gameplay is overall blood pumping
- Events turn out huge and you feel the happiness of the community.
- There are many professional players to help you play better
- (sometimes) matched with people with equal skill level
Cons
- Weapons nerfed until almost forgotten about.
- 32% of the people I find in games are toxic, rude, or flat out racist.
- The hit registration is very poor, especially with low ping. You may hurt someone from far away but up close nothing.
- Some people with low ping are matched with people with high ping, bringing unfair gameplay.
- Speaking of matchmaking, it takes almost 10-20 Minutes to find a server
- Many areas in maps that you can walk through/ aren’t modeled so people can hide there and kill people.
- Balance is bad, for example 6 v 12
- Matched with players with a difference in skill level, *see last Pro*
Sadly there are more cons than pros. But overall this game is truly a game where every day you wake up and think: “Wow, I can’t wait to start up my PC and play TF2!” It gets people wanting more and more, so keep up the good work. I definitely recommend this game to all people!

I’ve been wanting to play TF2 since I was 9. It seemed amazing. This game really is a great Free to Play first person co-op game. You push a payload cart with your friends while defending. Here are the pros I find about this game:
Pros
- Wide selection of hats, shirts, etc.
- Weapons get balanced
- Gameplay is overall blood pumping
- Events turn out huge and you feel the happiness of the community.
- There are many professional players to help you play better
- (sometimes) matched with people with equal skill level
Cons
- Weapons nerfed until almost forgotten about.
- 32% of the people I find in games are toxic, rude, or flat out racist.
- The hit registration is very poor, especially with low ping. You may hurt someone from far away but up close nothing.
- Some people with low ping are matched with people with high ping, bringing unfair gameplay.
- Speaking of matchmaking, it takes almost 10-20 Minutes to find a server
- Many areas in maps that you can walk through/ aren’t modeled so people can hide there and kill people.
- Balance is bad, for example 6 v 12
- Matched with players with a difference in skill level, *see last Pro*
Sadly there are more cons than pros. But overall this game is truly a game where every day you wake up and think: “Wow, I can’t wait to start up my PC and play TF2!” It gets people wanting more and more, so keep up the good work. I definitely recommend this game to all people!

Not just a FPS game but a full on Combat Simulator, Arma3 brings a level of realism to the gaming world that many wargame players may not be ready for. The complexity dwarfs that of COD, GR, and MOH. Small unit tactics and well laid plans are the only way to stay alive in a session of Arma3, going in guns blazing is nothing more than suicide.
This is not a quick twitch FPS, your skills in Borderlands will not avail you here. But that is part of what makes the Arma series so amazing, the ability to bide your time and follow a plan will take you far further than good mouse skills. Looking for a mature game to play with your friends after the kids are in bed? Arma3 fits the bill for the mature gamers out there looking for an intellectual challenge as well a as a fun time.
There is also an amazing online community who supports Arma3, there are more user made mods out there than you could ever possibly use in one lifetime. Want to fight Zombies? There are probably near 100 fully developed zombie mods. Want even more realism? WWI? WWI? WWIII? IV? Vietnam? The mods are out there waiting for you. Arma is an amazing framework for some amazing mods.
On the down side the learning curve is VERY steep. You will spend a lot of time pushing up daisies before you get a handle on the complexities of Arma3. I strongly recommend finding a group you can play and learn with.
If you want a FPS challenge this is your game.

I expected this game to be something like Grand Theft Auto (which I played for all of 30 minutes once).  It vaguely is like GTA...vaguely.  There's car stealing and hookers and killing and mayhem, but in some other dimension where all that stuff ends up funny as hell.  There is a 'bizarre' factor to the game that takes away any qualms or social-consciousness some of us have and lets you become a psychopathic gang leader pretty much guilt free.
I have never laughed so hard at a game in my life and this game is a comedy as much as anything.  The 'Insurance Fraud' mini games especially left me with my sides aching and tears streaming down my face...I'm not into slapstick, but somehow it is beyond hysterical to try to get cars to run you over and they refuse to, while everyone is running in circles screaming right into the path of cars you were trying in vain to get to hit you, and then when you finally do manage to jump in front of a car -- your hope is to be dragged or bounced along as far as possible, hopefully into the front of another car that has no ability to avoid you.  That sounds awful, but in the dimension Saints Row is a part of, the absurdity of the effort will leave you in stitches...your character ends up without a scratch.
I couldn't finish the game because of another mini-game called 'Escort' that I never figured out how to accomplish, but I managed to complete everything else and it was a wild and wonderful ride.  I will definitely play it again, even knowing I still can't do 'Escort'.  It was immersive, funny, intense, crazy, odd...and you get to dress up as a bobblehead.

Some of my favorite things to do in-game are Rocket and Sticky Jumping (even though I'm terrible at it), playing Demoknight, being a friendly, and a bunch of the other fun, stupid, and probably unintended things. GTA and it's clones usually have a lot of humor and jokes in between the realistic and serious plot. Saints Row 3 doesn't give a damn about the realism or the seriousness...
Unlike GTA, Saints Row 3 doesn't take anything seriously. Everything from melee attacks to weapons and characters is a joke, which makes this game a lot more enjoyable than other games in the genre that usually take themselves too seriously. The gameplay is the series' usual stuff, except crazier. In the beginning, weapons and combat are quite normal but, as the game progresses, you get laser weapons, tanks, hoverbikes and even zombies show up. That's all pretty good, graphics are nice, the game lasts for a nice amount of time because of all the cool side-activities you can do and all the time you spend customizing your character and your vehicles, unlocking weapons, upgrading your crib and just messing around in the city...There's also some very fun co-op stuff and a great survival mode.
The only weak part of the game is the fact that the story is sometimes a bit to crazy and "whatever, let's just blow stuff up". Saints Row 2 was a very fun and crazy game but it still managed to have some drama and serious stuff in the story. In Saints Row 3, *SPOILERS* major characters die *SPOILERS* and 5 minutes later no one seems to care. The ending is very fun and it's a nice conclusion but there doesn't seem to be a huge escalation of events up to that point, the game is crazy and chaotic all the way through. Overall, the story is good for some laughs but it's definitely not Shawshank Redemption.
But it's ok! Saints Row 3 is not something you play for the plot. You play it for the open-world fun, the awesome customization and great side-activities. You can also play as a toilet with a mega buster.
Score: 5/5

I recommend Team Fortress 2.
Team Fortress 2 is a first person shooter that combines silly cartoon-like things to a true blood-bath brawl.
A few things that may be considered good is the large ammount of custimization you have over characters and the various play styles that are enabled due to the character's weapons having some customibiility. The pay-to-win system is less on win and more on pay-to-look-awesome, allowing newer players to still have the same normal weapons as those who have paid, maybe not looking quite as Mannly. (Heh, get it? Mann... ly...)
The pay-to-look-awesome system has only one downfall, and that's being called a "F2P" (Free-To-Play) if you havn't paid. Otherwise, it is enjoyable for all. The game offers many useful things to help you get a good start, and again something can be found for everyone.

Having spent about 1,000 hours on Arma2/OA (between D2D/Disk Version/Steam) and 70 hours in Arma 3, it's no contest in anything but graphics. Arma2/OA is much better in terms of realism. The bullet sponge AI in Arma3 (sorry body armor doesn't let you just keep trucking like it was a bee sting) just kill any immersion whatsoever along with the ridiculous fantasy Iranian units. Also simple things like the "flying" drop down when placing units are gone in the new editor for no apparent reason.
Overall Arma 3 does look a lot better, but still runs pretty poorly regardless of high end hardware (i7 960@4.1Ghz+STRIX R9 390X/ 3930K@4.2Ghz+STRIX GTX 1060/ i7 4770K@4.3Ghz+780Ti MATRIX SLI (previously 290X MATRIX CF and 390X STRIX CF) / i7 6700@stock+GTX 1070FE / i7 5930K@4.5Ghz+STRIX 980Ti SLI (previously 780Ti MATRIX SLI).
Rather than wasting time on a dubious futuristic setting it would have been far better for the developers to focus on quashing performance issues and providing a believable simulation with realistic damage based on impact point+round+angle. Also AI is still very dumb and STILL unable to haul @$$ with a sense of urgency.
I see Arma 3 as a downhill slide for the series, being far more casual than previous iterations in terms of attempted realism compounded by unwillingness to expand the core mechanics for realism that had been laid down since OPFP. In a way it's more like the Battlefield version of the series.
Also on the campaigns; they are straight up trash. Resistance and Red Hammer have not been bested to date, although the Arma 2 campaign was pretty fun. Arma 3 is just a slog of monotony; APEX is a waste of money.

Arma 3 is a tactical military shooter, it has an unique spot in having the biggest maps with most players combined. Imagine yourself 120+ players in 2 or 3 teams fighting it out incl vehicle warfare... Tanks planes helis even boats included in that list, described at the shop description arma really sends you to war. The bad side is that this comes at a cost of at least a good pc to even being able to play it to full potential. And even then you limited by what the servers can pull off, eventually you will enjoy the game a lot more in smaller groups.
But arma 3 is not all about war, with steam work shop full of content or not to say the least about "armaholic"...  Arma 3 has so many possibilities that you won't run out of content to play quickly. With arma life which pretends to be a GTA with real players as cops medics and military. Included with gangs and your own choice to be the bad or the good guy and fight it out in the wild wild west. Or mods based on the older arma 2 mod DAYZ still to this day better than the standalone... But also with more known game styles like KOTH which is more a team death match with a level and money systeem.
What the best side and also directly the worst side of arma 3 is that everyone can hire a server. Games can never really die in this way, look at how many still play arma 2 daily... When a game dies mostly seen in EA games shutting down their servers, arma on the other hand will never really close down. Aslong everyone can hire a server whenever they feel like it... Great community can grown upon this but also people can abuse it, with scripts with saved slots as example. Pay the server owner €10.- a month and you can always play (join the server because only vips(donator) can join the last 20/30 slots). While every server has to pay hes server rent, servers with scripts like this or those that show xx amount of players always on the server is a big issue. (mostly combined to too double the effect ofc...) It is funny because i've been admins on several servers, have seen how it has been run from several different points of view. And none of these server owners have ever used or felt forced to use any of these scandals so yes i'm surprised... While most just hire the server as a kind of donation to the game or those who get real donations from community members help the game thrive.
Arma 3 also has a great single player game the voice overs are sometimes weak to say the least but it goes... I won't really call it a story, although a story is being told, just see it like a training course for the multiplayer. ;) Arma 3 also gives you a very strong but still simple 3D game editor whereby making missions is as ease that everyone can do it. Or also known zeus which makes you being able to play as a game master, you can make missions or sent waves while you friends are playing. It gives you an eagles eye of view of the battlefield and gives you the tools to spawn and do almost anything you can Imagine. Arma 3 is one of those uncut gems and well worth every penny you put into it.

Alrighty, to make this sort of brief, which I will most likely fail to do, I will give you some qualities of this game and how they fit in to the game itself. Some of the game's mechanics were unnecessary and a little flawed. First of all, the game is really really easy. The game is not difficult in any way, which is bad for a player like me, who loves a challenge. The character customization is incredibly good and satisfying, as you can even change your skin color to something unnatural and many other cool things. You can make something incredibly beautiful or something that looks incredibly stupid! Good mechanic. Especially after using GTA V's horrible charactter customization. Another mechanic you will probably try out once and then move on, is crouching. If you're using the keyboard and mouse you will be using control for it, and I must say it is incredibly useless. You may find a use for it, but none the less basically useless. Saints Row IV by the way has the same exact map, increased graphics, but not majorly enhanced, and the city's entirely dark all the time, but hey it has super powers. So if you're looking to be more of a gangster get Saints Row the Third. Saints Row The Third had way more "badass moments," that we crave in most video games. The graphics in the game are average if not above average. If you're looking to be more superhero with much more outfit customization then get Saints Row IV. Lots of gamers who played this game, were disappointed to find that the game strayed too far from the original game's gangster feel and leaned more towards a lot of silliness and weirdness, and that was even more advanced in Saints Row IV with you guessed it, Aliens, although they're not really in the game much. The game makes you really want to use every gun and you can go on and argue about whether Grand Theft Auto has better free roam then this game. Personally the car customization is different from Grand Theft Auto V but certainly not better. I haven't played the game in a while, so I don't know if they put a useless speedometer on the HUD while driving. The driving in this game is much easier and in my opinion is much better than Grand Theft Auto V. While GTA V's driving is much more realistic, Saints Row The Third has better driving considering the game isn't centered around driving, yet Grand Theft Auto obviously is centered around....cars. So driving is a great thing in SR3 but toally useless and unchanged in Saints Row IV. Much more weapons in SR3 and way better. The weapons are pretty much the only thing they didn't carry over to SR4. I really enjoyed this game and it continues to be my #1 most played game on my steam game list. I highly recommend this game, but not to hardcore fans of the first two SR games. 9/10 overall.

There is a huge debate about whether to get H1Z1 or Playeruknown's Battleground (PUBG. Both games are where 100-174 people are dropped into a large map to fight to the death as some sort of threat (toxic gas in h1z1 or a blue border that you take damage from in PUBG) is pushing players closer together to a certain point where they are guaranteed to see each other.
H1Z1 pros:
Sound is good
Wild masks and clothes that make it fun
A fun lobby while waiting for game to start
Rounds are quick and fast paced
The parachutes go down faster than PUBG
H1Z1 cons:
Crashes every time I play it.
Not many vehicles
Not a huge variety of weapons.
You can't add scopes to guns (you can in PUBG)
Navigation in game is hard. It doesn't tell you your specific location which makes it hard to avoid toxic gas
Not many updates to fix harmful glitches
You'll run into a hacker every few rounds
Bad community
You can't decide where you start in a parachute (you can in PUBG)
This game is more luck than strategy
Not the most interesting map (no rivers, it's just gas stations and trailers scattered around a few cities)
PUBG pros:
Large variety of weapons and weapon modifications (scopes, clips, suppressors, etc.)
Large variety of vehicles (including boats)
Almost no glitches
Very good at catching hackers
Better community (gives you tips if you are playing squad/duo with people online)
Shows you your specific location on map
Better for sniping people
Better hiding spots
Have a better chance of winning
Better GUI
Better graphics
The developers are much quicker to update glitches
More interesting map that consists of rivers and hills
PUBG cons:
Harder to tell where you are being shot from
The sounds aren't the best (can't tell where gunshots/footsteps are)
Slightly more CPU/GPU intensive (if you turn down the graphics and go into windowed mode, even if you have lower specs, it should be playable)
Overall I would definitely spend the extra 10 dollars on PUBG. I got H1Z1 before PUBG and regretted buying it
Every moment feels real. Performance issues aside, this is a msterpiece.

Imagine this, your walking down a road going on a patrol with your friends and all the sudden a single shot rings out and your squad lead gets hit. Naturally you all run to cover but two more get hit before you can go prone, so you call out to the remaining squad members about how they are doing but you come under fire from the left flank killing everyone they took cover on the left side. So its just you and one friend left, against 5 possible contacts and a sniper. Seems like impossable odds? Well you are in the middle of a town and the cover you went into is a house in which your partner is in the other house so what you do is use hit and run tatics slowly killing them off until you get lucky and wipe off the flanking squad. Now all thats left is the sniper in which you know where he is because you saw his muzzle flash on his first shot. So you and your partner slowly move towards his position out side of town and you take aim, the first shot misses. Now he is alerted to your position and fires a single shot before you could kill him. He misses you, but hits your friend. Arma is a game where a single mistake, a mistake that can change you from the hunter to the prey. It could be even as small as forgetting to bring extra ammo to as major as not following a patrol pattern. Situational awarness is probally the best skill you can have in arma, of course being able to hit things is as well. The only reason why this game is still 40 bucks is not because of the dlc's and the vanilla content (Don't get me wrong i've spent 90 hours on vanilla but thats about it) but mainly because of the amazing modding community.

Arma 3 is a tactical military shooter, it has an unique spot in having the biggest maps with most players combined. Imagine yourself 120+ players in 2 or 3 teams fighting it out incl vehicle warfare... Tanks planes helis even boats included in that list, described at the shop description arma really sends you to war. The bad side is that this comes at a cost of at least a good pc to even being able to play it to full potential. And even then you limited by what the servers can pull off, eventually you will enjoy the game a lot more in smaller groups.
But arma 3 is not all about war, with steam work shop full of content or not to say the least about "armaholic"...  Arma 3 has so many possibilities that you won't run out of content to play quickly. With arma life which pretends to be a GTA with real players as cops medics and military. Included with gangs and your own choice to be the bad or the good guy and fight it out in the wild wild west. Or mods based on the older arma 2 mod DAYZ still to this day better than the standalone... But also with more known game styles like KOTH which is more a team death match with a level and money systeem.
What the best side and also directly the worst side of arma 3 is that everyone can hire a server. Games can never really die in this way, look at how many still play arma 2 daily... When a game dies mostly seen in EA games shutting down their servers, arma on the other hand will never really close down. Aslong everyone can hire a server whenever they feel like it... Great community can grown upon this but also people can abuse it, with scripts with saved slots as example. Pay the server owner €10.- a month and you can always play (join the server because only vips(donator) can join the last 20/30 slots). While every server has to pay hes server rent, servers with scripts like this or those that show xx amount of players always on the server is a big issue. (mostly combined to too double the effect ofc...) It is funny because i've been admins on several servers, have seen how it has been run from several different points of view. And none of these server owners have ever used or felt forced to use any of these scandals so yes i'm surprised... While most just hire the server as a kind of donation to the game or those who get real donations from community members help the game thrive.
Arma 3 also has a great single player game the voice overs are sometimes weak to say the least but it goes... I won't really call it a story, although a story is being told, just see it like a training course for the multiplayer. ;) Arma 3 also gives you a very strong but still simple 3D game editor whereby making missions is as ease that everyone can do it. Or also known zeus which makes you being able to play as a game master, you can make missions or sent waves while you friends are playing. It gives you an eagles eye of view of the battlefield and gives you the tools to spawn and do almost anything you can Imagine. Arma 3 is one of those uncut gems and well worth every penny you put into it.

Imagine this, your walking down a road going on a patrol with your friends and all the sudden a single shot rings out and your squad lead gets hit. Naturally you all run to cover but two more get hit before you can go prone, so you call out to the remaining squad members about how they are doing but you come under fire from the left flank killing everyone they took cover on the left side. So its just you and one friend left, against 5 possible contacts and a sniper. Seems like impossable odds? Well you are in the middle of a town and the cover you went into is a house in which your partner is in the other house so what you do is use hit and run tatics slowly killing them off until you get lucky and wipe off the flanking squad. Now all thats left is the sniper in which you know where he is because you saw his muzzle flash on his first shot. So you and your partner slowly move towards his position out side of town and you take aim, the first shot misses. Now he is alerted to your position and fires a single shot before you could kill him. He misses you, but hits your friend. Arma is a game where a single mistake, a mistake that can change you from the hunter to the prey. It could be even as small as forgetting to bring extra ammo to as major as not following a patrol pattern. Situational awarness is probally the best skill you can have in arma, of course being able to hit things is as well. The only reason why this game is still 40 bucks is not because of the dlc's and the vanilla content (Don't get me wrong i've spent 90 hours on vanilla but thats about it) but mainly because of the amazing modding community.

H1Z1, in short, is a game where at the beginning all the players are dropped from the sky on parachutes, when they land on the ground, they try to collect all kinds of items that may help them survive the game. To help the players find each other, the playground area shrinks every now and then by releasing a toxic gas. The game ends when all the players are dead except the last survivor.
The game is very casual, for example weapons have a goofy recoil, for instance, an AR jumps left and right as you shoot it. You can jump off a car at its full speed and you will be fine. You can use a key from one car for every car. Some people like it, but personally, I'm not a fan of it.
The game has some significant pros like a good optimisation and as it's casual, it's also easy to understand for new players. Ranking system which works quite well and the ability to play with friends on duos and fives.
First and probably the biggest flaw of the game is that it has been in early access for over 2 years now. During this time the game hasn't changed that much aside from some bug fixes, adding skins and UI improvements. I think that the developers have had enough time to release the game, but it seems like the biggest things that they have done are adding a bunch of skins and splitting the game into H1Z1 JS and H1Z1 KOTK so that now instead of one game for 20 euros, there are two for 20 each.
Another thing is a lack of weapons. The game has only one kind of shotgun, two assault rifles AK and AR, bow, crossbow, some pistols and one sniper rifle which is only available in supply drops. I think that the devs should add at least one more shotgun and assault rifle instead of plenty of skins to them.
I'd also want to see some more maps, as there is only one.
H1Z1 is not a bad game. I didn't really know if I should mark the review as positive or not. I'd mark it as a neutral one if I could, but because I can't, I'm forced to mark it as a negative review. So overall, if you like the casual mechanics of the game, don't mind the lack of variety in weapons and only one map. Then the game might be for you. Otherwise, I'd rather spend money on PUBG.

Gonna be a bit confusing, but need to write a english essay for school. Its about if the death penalty should be abloished in America. please leave any advice or suggestions you have if you have the time to look through it. many great thanks-Liam
One thousand four hundred and forty five, that’s how many lives the death penalty has consumed in America alone. The first recorded execution in America was in 1608 when Captain George Kendall was executed for being a Spanish spy. Was it just? Is it right to put someone's life in another’s hands? It's a fiery debate across the whole of America with many powerful arguments on each side. This barbaric form of punishment is harsh and brutal, but also very intriguing. It captivates people like flies swarming to rotten carcass. My view on the death penalty is that it should be eradicated and punishment for capital crime should be remodeled into a more humane alternative.
I believe in my stance on this issue because it's been proven that the death penalty does not deter crime. In fact the death penalty sometimes does the opposite of what it is intended to do. An example of this, is when comparing America and its neighbouring country, Canada. Canada has a much lower murder rate; less than half of that  .Canada's murder rate per 100,000 people in 2015 was 1.68, whilst America’s was 4.88. This example clearly shows that in fact the death penalty does not deter crime and that countries without it may be better off than countries with it.
Another argument against the death penalty is that there is always a likelihood that the convicted criminal is in fact innocent. Since 1973 it's been found that 130 people have innocently been executed. In 1991 Cameron Todd Willingham was sentenced to death for the murder of his three young daughters. He allegedly set his house on fire to cover up his maltreatment of them. He died on the 7th of February 2002. However, on the 13th of March 2015 the state of Texas ordered a unexpected re-examination of the case. It was found that he was unjustifiably convicted, an innocent man had been excised from this world.
Another strong reason to oppose the death penalty, is that it is morally wrong to put the life of someone into another's’ hands. A retired executioner, from the state of  Oregon, declared that after dealing with only two executions in the last fifty-four years he has made it his mission to persuade anyone he can the death penalty is a “failed policy”. He thinks that regardless of their crimes no person should have to go through what he saw. He thinks this because of his personal involvement in the executions, this forced him to have a deeper reckoning with his feelings about capital punishment. As well as this on average the death row inmates spend 15 years on death row. I think this is unacceptable as these prisoners spend more than 20 hours in isolation every day. I think that Americans should no longer accept the myth that capital punishment has a constructive role in the justice system.
My final reason for abolishing the death penalty is that it costs the American government millions of dollars every year. This is mainly due to the state having to provide services such as lawyers, judges, jury and accommodation for the accused. In 2003 a legislative audit in Kansas found the average cost of one death penalty in $1.26million whereabouts a non capital case only costs $740,000. The money that is squandered on these things could be used to great benefit in others areas to improve Americans lives.
However, one point in favour of the death penalty is that the convicted receives a fair punishment as the jury decides what will happen to the criminal. The jury is made up of a group of people with different beliefs, cultures and morals. This allows for a fair trial and a fitting punishment in their eyes. Although this is a firm argument it only highlights how shortsighted the death penalty truly is. The fault is not with the jury and people who decide what punishment is handed out, but rather with the legal system. The death penalty should not be a feasible form of punishment at all and should never have been introduced in the first place.
In conclusion, I don’t think the death penalty is a valid form of punishment. I believe this because of many different reasons such as the morality of taking another's life, the cost of having to sentence a person to death and the underlying prospect of the prosecuted being innocent. I don't think it's justifiable to have someone decide who lives and who dies like an almighty god. Nobody should have the power to end someone's life as if it was flicking a switch.

H1Z1, in short, is a game where at the beginning all the players are dropped from the sky on parachutes, when they land on the ground, they try to collect all kinds of items that may help them survive the game. To help the players find each other, the playground area shrinks every now and then by releasing a toxic gas. The game ends when all the players are dead except the last survivor.
The game is very casual, for example weapons have a goofy recoil, for instance, an AR jumps left and right as you shoot it. You can jump off a car at its full speed and you will be fine. You can use a key from one car for every car. Some people like it, but personally, I'm not a fan of it.
The game has some significant pros like a good optimisation and as it's casual, it's also easy to understand for new players. Ranking system which works quite well and the ability to play with friends on duos and fives.
First and probably the biggest flaw of the game is that it has been in early access for over 2 years now. During this time the game hasn't changed that much aside from some bug fixes, adding skins and UI improvements. I think that the developers have had enough time to release the game, but it seems like the biggest things that they have done are adding a bunch of skins and splitting the game into H1Z1 JS and H1Z1 KOTK so that now instead of one game for 20 euros, there are two for 20 each.
Another thing is a lack of weapons. The game has only one kind of shotgun, two assault rifles AK and AR, bow, crossbow, some pistols and one sniper rifle which is only available in supply drops. I think that the devs should add at least one more shotgun and assault rifle instead of plenty of skins to them.
I'd also want to see some more maps, as there is only one.
H1Z1 is not a bad game. I didn't really know if I should mark the review as positive or not. I'd mark it as a neutral one if I could, but because I can't, I'm forced to mark it as a negative review. So overall, if you like the casual mechanics of the game, don't mind the lack of variety in weapons and only one map. Then the game might be for you. Otherwise, I'd rather spend money on PUBG.

Gonna be a bit confusing, but need to write a english essay for school. Its about if the death penalty should be abloished in America. please leave any advice or suggestions you have if you have the time to look through it. many great thanks-Liam
One thousand four hundred and forty five, that’s how many lives the death penalty has consumed in America alone. The first recorded execution in America was in 1608 when Captain George Kendall was executed for being a Spanish spy. Was it just? Is it right to put someone's life in another’s hands? It's a fiery debate across the whole of America with many powerful arguments on each side. This barbaric form of punishment is harsh and brutal, but also very intriguing. It captivates people like flies swarming to rotten carcass. My view on the death penalty is that it should be eradicated and punishment for capital crime should be remodeled into a more humane alternative.
I believe in my stance on this issue because it's been proven that the death penalty does not deter crime. In fact the death penalty sometimes does the opposite of what it is intended to do. An example of this, is when comparing America and its neighbouring country, Canada. Canada has a much lower murder rate; less than half of that  .Canada's murder rate per 100,000 people in 2015 was 1.68, whilst America’s was 4.88. This example clearly shows that in fact the death penalty does not deter crime and that countries without it may be better off than countries with it.
Another argument against the death penalty is that there is always a likelihood that the convicted criminal is in fact innocent. Since 1973 it's been found that 130 people have innocently been executed. In 1991 Cameron Todd Willingham was sentenced to death for the murder of his three young daughters. He allegedly set his house on fire to cover up his maltreatment of them. He died on the 7th of February 2002. However, on the 13th of March 2015 the state of Texas ordered a unexpected re-examination of the case. It was found that he was unjustifiably convicted, an innocent man had been excised from this world.
Another strong reason to oppose the death penalty, is that it is morally wrong to put the life of someone into another's’ hands. A retired executioner, from the state of  Oregon, declared that after dealing with only two executions in the last fifty-four years he has made it his mission to persuade anyone he can the death penalty is a “failed policy”. He thinks that regardless of their crimes no person should have to go through what he saw. He thinks this because of his personal involvement in the executions, this forced him to have a deeper reckoning with his feelings about capital punishment. As well as this on average the death row inmates spend 15 years on death row. I think this is unacceptable as these prisoners spend more than 20 hours in isolation every day. I think that Americans should no longer accept the myth that capital punishment has a constructive role in the justice system.
My final reason for abolishing the death penalty is that it costs the American government millions of dollars every year. This is mainly due to the state having to provide services such as lawyers, judges, jury and accommodation for the accused. In 2003 a legislative audit in Kansas found the average cost of one death penalty in $1.26million whereabouts a non capital case only costs $740,000. The money that is squandered on these things could be used to great benefit in others areas to improve Americans lives.
However, one point in favour of the death penalty is that the convicted receives a fair punishment as the jury decides what will happen to the criminal. The jury is made up of a group of people with different beliefs, cultures and morals. This allows for a fair trial and a fitting punishment in their eyes. Although this is a firm argument it only highlights how shortsighted the death penalty truly is. The fault is not with the jury and people who decide what punishment is handed out, but rather with the legal system. The death penalty should not be a feasible form of punishment at all and should never have been introduced in the first place.
In conclusion, I don’t think the death penalty is a valid form of punishment. I believe this because of many different reasons such as the morality of taking another's life, the cost of having to sentence a person to death and the underlying prospect of the prosecuted being innocent. I don't think it's justifiable to have someone decide who lives and who dies like an almighty god. Nobody should have the power to end someone's life as if it was flicking a switch.

Longevity is tough for competitive shooters. Hardly a month goes by without new virtual arenas cropping up and enticing you into some fresh conflict, and only a few popular games manage to sustain active player bases even a year after their initial release. And then there's Team Fortress 2. Released in 2007, this class-based classic is still going strong well into its seventh year, thanks largely to its lively and creative community. Since GameSpot's original TF2 review, the game has benefited from numerous updates and made the jump to a free-to-play business model. So how well is Team Fortress 2 faring in 2014 among the current crop of competitors for your time and money?
The short answer is, it's holding up very well. The core action pits two teams of players against each other in a battle to capture points, move a cart, or steal a briefcase. The objective is always very straightforward; it's the interplay between the nine playable classes that makes things so varied and interesting. The speedy scout, the militant heavy, the diligent engineer, the conniving medic, the pesky sniper, the sneaky spy, the feisty pyro, the explosive soldier, and the even-more-explosive demoman all have unique weapons, attributes, and abilities that complement each other and clash in myriad ways. Encounters can vary widely depending on the match type and the makeup of each team, and this unpredictability is crucial to TF2's long-standing appeal.

You know how when you were playing GTA, you would between missions just go nuts driving around the city, running over pedestrians, shooting everything with that rocket launcher, and then trying to escape police? Well this is the game that's ALL about those moments. The game doesn't take itself too seriously, and it wears that fact with pride.
The game knows the crazy things you'll be doing for fun and encourages them, often with a minigame. Did you jump on the roof of a car, which then started driving? Press a button to start the car-surfing minigame where you try to stay on the roof for as long as you can! Did you steal a car that had other passengers in? Press a button to kidnap them and demand ransom. The list of mini games goes on and on.
I wasn't a big fan of the system in Saints Row 2, which required you to complete a certain  number of minigames / activities before you were allowed to continue in the main plot. This system is gone here. You are still encouraged to do side missions to earn respect, which here acts as experience points, unlocking various upgrades (faster health regeneration, more ammo for guns, ability to lead larger groups of gang members). However if you feel like doing just missions for a while, you can.
The main missions themselves are crazy and fun, full of original ideas and jokes. You'll have plenty of lolwut moments.
One thing I spent A LOT of time on is the character customization. I love the idea of being able to customize every detail of character's appearance. The game also offers a large number of clothing to choose from, to get your character to look just the way you want - ranging from serious regular clothes, to super-hero costumes. Or you can just wear nothing at all. I think this whole game mechanic is well balanced - allowing those who care to spend hours finding matching clothes they want, and those who don't really care can quickly purchase one of many pre-made outfits. The same goes for the modification of the actual character.
With GTA taking the more serious path to sandbox city action, it's great to have a game that's all about just having fun. It basically comes down to this - if you enjoyed the random rampages in GTA, perhaps even more than the actual plot, then this is the game for you. If you missed the ability to customize your GTA character, then again, this is the game for you.

While Arma 3 may be more hardcore than battlefield 4 (or call of duty, but everyone knows battlefield is where it's at not counting zombies), the amount of depth is crazy and once you begin to really sink some time into it, truly outshines other shooters. I came to the Arma series with the second installment and was instantly put off by the performance, rarely playing it if at all, therefore I came to Arma 3 fairly late in its development. Like Apex time... The amount of depth is crazy and many features you'll miss in regular shooters (that double ADS and separate head cam especially). While it's fun to drop into a more fast paced shooter, Arma 3 satisfies far more once you become accustomed to the controls and systems. The apex campaign is, in my opinion, a great way to bridge the gap between the Arma universe and traditional shooters, despite the short length, it adds a fairly fast paced, guns blazing campaign all set on an amazing map.
Arma 3 is truly more of a platform than a game and shines when you play the online modes or vast collection of Workshop content, some of the primary game modes are Invade and Annex, which is a massive dynamic war, on whichever island you choose. Altis life which is an Rpg, an Rpg where it is very poor taste to spawn in and shoot people for no reason your first time playing (ah unexpected temp ban never again), or wasteland, a dayz esque hunt for guns and ammo while attempting to control towns and villages for money, but without the zombies. This is just some of the big online modes.
This review may ramble but essentially I am telling you that you are looking at getting a slower paced but far more rewarding shooter that demands tactical team play with an amazing feature set. If you're cool you can even navigate using the stars... Watch the 33 Things About Arma video and when finished click buy. Recommend Apex Edition for extra guns, vehicles, and my favorite map, the jungle of Tanoa. Sales are good considering its been out for a bit and they're common but $75 is still well spent on this. Too bad I'm currently so addicted to Witcher 3 and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by ASU to play... But soon...
EDIT: Since there's so many workshop options I decided just to add a couple of my favorites for newcomers.
1) Resist is a quality campaign following alongside the main storyline of East Wind and was winner of the Make Arma Not War contest.
2) Navy Seals Blood Brothers is another campaign and features 30 missions, also very high quality.
3) Anything dynamic really,  DUWS started my addiction although Dynamic Combat (or Recon) Ops is more up to date and similar. Antastasi is a dynamic mod were you start as a weak guerilla fighter attempting to win the hearts of the people of Altis (or Tanoa, which is better equipment and terrain wise but called Warlords of the Pacific) and take over the island. Finally WLA Amalgamation is another great dynamic war mod with base construction,although the author stopped New content as he was mad BI didn't give him Make Arma Not War win.
4) If you're more daring than me you can use MCC4 to construct quick missions with drag and drop options and custom (improved AI) or Alive for more in depth missions that also features custom AI. Or jsut the built in editor as well.
I also recommend all the RHS stuff as a lot of scenarios will use that and allows a more modern day as opposed to futuristic weapon set. JSRS or Dynasound 2/Enhanced Soundscape plus Blastcore are a must for enhancing sounds and explosions. Rain Textures, ASR AI, Specialist Military Arms, and Aegis are all also must haves in my opinion.

H1Z1: Kotk is one of the most casual as a competitive game. Usually when people say that this game is salty and too competitive, I can say that its true depending on what kind of games you like to play. This game features next things:
-Only few weapons. AK, AR16 (Its M4), Sniper rifle, Shotgun, 4 different pistols, Bow, Crossbow, and few different meele weapons, plus few different grenades.
-Large map, which is sometimes big problem, because spawning too far away from soon revealed "Safe zone" is really critical to motivation.
-Many different vehicles. Quad, Jeep, Police car, etc. Some vehicles are faster than others. Some can take more damage than others and still be functional.
-Explosives. Very, very much explosives. You can find Grenades around the world and dont be surprised about amounts of explosive barrels around the map. Theyre literally EVERYWHERE. Learn to USE them properly because most of the time, if player is near barrel, and barrel explodes, he is dead. So freaking dead..
-Talking about grenades a bit more. Useful throwable items: Grenade, Molotov, smoke grenade. Unuseful throwables: Stun- and gas grenades. They are nice idea, but they do not function properly. You can throw them yes. But player can just run away from gas, and stun doesnt stun anything.
-Freaking annoying micro-transaction. You earn these... CASES, from games you play. Its much like CS:GO. With $5 you can open only 2 of those cases, and most of the time, youll get nothing but $0.1 worth of items.
-5-level crates. Unlike those crates you must pay to open, these cases you get every 5 levels, are free to open. But dont expect anything too nice. Its crap most of the times.
-Scrapyard: You scrap things you have bought on OPSKINS, or things you have gotten from crates, when you have 100 of those scrap units, you can create another $0.1 worth item. Its nice. Trust me. Doesnt hurt at all.
-Parachutes: You only use them when game begins. Everyone glides to ground and starts looting.
Gamemodes:
-Solo: You vs about 150-170 players.
-Duo: You AND your friend vs 150-170 players.
-Fives: You and your 1-4 friends vs 150-170 players.
-Training: You spawn, you die, you respawn, you die..
-Skirmish: Like normal. Just faster, smaller, and on night. ONLY ON WEEKENDS.
Good? Yes.
Bad?No.
Bugs? YES.
Good gameplay? Yes.
Salty? Sometimes.
Would I recommend it? Probably. They are not releasing so much stuff anymore, and latest update was almost only bug fixes and country hoodies.
Wait for sales. Its not worth $20. But its DEFINETLY worth $10.

The best military simulation I've ever played. This could easily be my most favorite game of all time. Those two hundred hours went by like they were a weekend. This is why:
-Realistic sounds and military communication
-Expansive maps without borders that tempt you to see what's on the other side
-Beautiful graphics that immerse you into the military setting
-Authentic physics that mirror true ballistics
-Dedicated and passionate modding community with hundreds of mods that tweak the game in every imaginable way
-Faithful developers that continue to improve and put out new content for the game that they don't charge for!
-Large multiplayer fan base
-YouTube tutorials and general bad assery...
Some Neg:
-Single thread CPU dependant (4790K or 6700K prefered). Will not multithread, which leads to some laggy performance even in single player. Some of this is due to how immense the world is that is being rendered. Apart from that, it's just the way the game was coded and it's not changing.
-Cheezy voice acting and silly repetitive character movements (small nitpick).
Overall, I LOVE this game. Buy it at full price because that is what it deserves!

People spend too much time comparing KoTK to PUBG.  While they sit in the same genre, it seems only fair to compare them alone.  We could go on and on about Daybreak vs Bluehole, but again, totaly differnt companies.
So instead i'm going to focus on what makes H1Z1 KotK UNIQUE.  NOTE HOW I DIDN'T SAY BETTER.  It is this uniqueness that keeps me coming back.
1) Gameplay - Face paced, ~175 people, lots of loot.  A recipie for chaos and fun.  While it may seem disheartening to die so fast, this game provides with a quick blast that is easy to recover from if you lose.  I like this becasue you don't have to spend 30 minutes looting just to get sniped by someone who was in the right place at the right(wrong) time. AGAIN, i'm not referencing PUBG here.
2) Art style - KoTK gets a bad rap sometimes for being too "arcade-like" in it's style.  Well poo poo to that.  That is what makes this game UNIQUE.
3) Gun play - Here I WILL be referencing PUBG.  In PUBG i was able to pick up an assault rifle, and get 7 kills easy on my first game.  In KoTK, it takes much more time and practice to get 1 or 2 kills.  The gunplay while differnt, is handicapped by its lack of scopes and attachments, but at the same time I enjoy the minimalistic gameplay.  While this harder gameplay could be chalked up to bad hitboxes, lag, or what have you, most times I find that when I shoot the gun right, I hit them.  Bullet drop, leading, pre-fire, and recoil are all things that need to be second nature in KoTK.  While again, this could just be becasue the community is older and therefore, more experinced; I don't think that would affect how hard the game is on a newcommer perspective as much.
4) Community - Avoid it
5) Developer - eh.  At least they have to update the game now because of PUBG.  I guess in a way PUBG saved KoTK
Conclusion - 7/10

This game appeals to those individuals looking for a shooter that feels a little more.. serious. Verdun, Squad, and even the previous Arma games try their best to be as complex and realistic as possible, but none of them quite hit the mark.
Arma 3 is a game developed by people who understand that there is more to realism than bullet drop and balistics. They've taken it so much further, and if you're willing to put in the time and effort into investing in the steep learning curve, then you'll find it'll pay you back ten-fold. Nothing is more fun than fully immersing yourself into a dynamic, realistic, and unforgiving open world.
Give the game a shot, it's worth so much more than the listed price. The engine isn't flawless, but it's about the closest to realism you'll get out of gaming for at least the next few years... and that's only because they'll have released Arma IV by that point.

This game started rough in the alpha, but since then I've come to consider this as the greatest shooter of all time. I could gush about it for hours, but I'll keep it to pros and cons.
-Easily the most realistic shooter ever made
-Beautiful graphics
-Great dev who embraces the community and mods
-Least asinine DLC scheme I've seen
-Regular updates that greatly improve the game
-Mods. If you dream it, there's a mod for it
-Best soundscape of any game I've played
-Nails the feel of shooting and moving with firearms better than any other game
-Almost all flaws from previous games have been improved
-Large mutliplayer community
-Difficulty, interface, every control, visuals, and AI are fully configurable to your taste. AI too accurate? You can change that
-Gigantic maps that 400 hours later I still haven't even covered half of
-Unique moments and battles that can't take place in other scripted shooters
-Mission editor allowing for literally any kind of gameplay
-There's not enough time in a life to explore all official and user missions and mods
-Extremely hardware demanding. Get yourself a good processor
--Core i5 4690k @ 4 ghz / GTX 970 OC'd gets 40 FPS on average, but regularly dips to 20
--You'll also want an SSD. Standard hard drives will give you occasional 1-2 second freezes
-You will run into bugs, mostly with how missions play out
-Commanding friendly AI is extremely clunky. Improvements have been made but total overhaul is needed. C2 Command mod mostly alleviates this
-AI is difficult to implement when creating missions
-Mission scripting is difficult and confusing. There is a full wiki and forum dedicated to it but they don't help much
-While the devs are wonderful, the community is elitist and less than helpful
Pick this game up. Seriously. It's worth every single penny.

I am very, very conflicted while writing this review. I really loved playing Arma 3. I've had some good times and made some good memmories. And I still havn't even fully explored all the mods that are available! But like I said, I'm conflicted. And here's why.
If you plan on playing alone, prepare to not have fun. Unless you're a gaming golden god with the reaction speed of a gerbil on speed, and the skills of a pro, you're going to be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off a lot. Especially in specific mods that pit you against other players (Wasteland etc.), you will get angry. Playing mods like this you really shouldn't be someone who gets attached to anything, and is basically entertained by anything that goes beyond finding things go "boom" interresting. If you want to spend quality time, find a MilSim group. But you'll have to spend a good amount of time on ArmA 3 figuring things out, and also trying to actually get INTO a MilSim group.
While I found it fairly entertaining, certain points get tedious and annoying. Especially since the AI have special eyes that can see you from 2KM away as if you were 2M away. But all in all; it's a decent campaign to go through once. (quite lengthy too with about 5 or 6 hours on average.)
I don't know if it can be counted as SP, but the Eden editor can be really fun to play around in! Getting actual things done, and making a working MP map is a huge challenge though. It will take many, many hours to get a MP map working and onto the steam workshop!
Ehm, how do I put this... The community is... different. While it has the internet classics such as rage kids and memelords, it contains a more rare breed of internet personality; the elitist. Don't be fooled by people saying that the community is mature, because of it's learning curve and MilSim niche-ness. Personally, I find the elitism to be the most annoying part about Arma 3. The players who find the need to rub in their kills. The players who have the humility of a peacock. Which also brings me to the last group of people I'll talk about; the die-hards. We all know them. People who have 2000 hours logged in Arma 3 and eat, breathe and probably excrete Arma. While I don't really have anything against them (They're better then me. Oh well.) but it does get frustrating when you have people that are making their tea and at the same time headshot you from 3KM distance.
+ Delivers a MilSim game
+ A decent amount of equipment variety.
+ Loads and loads of good mods.
+ Group fun! ;)
+ The game is pretty stable in my experience. (Bug wise)
+/- Community can sometimes be frustrating.
+/- The game itself can get quite frustrating. (unless like I mentioned, you're MLG pro JesusFPS.)
+/- Steep learning curve to not-scrubness.
- Requires a lot of time to actually get into the more MilSim multiplayer parts.

This game started rough in the alpha, but since then I've come to consider this as the greatest shooter of all time. I could gush about it for hours, but I'll keep it to pros and cons.
-Easily the most realistic shooter ever made
-Beautiful graphics
-Great dev who embraces the community and mods
-Least asinine DLC scheme I've seen
-Regular updates that greatly improve the game
-Mods. If you dream it, there's a mod for it
-Best soundscape of any game I've played
-Nails the feel of shooting and moving with firearms better than any other game
-Almost all flaws from previous games have been improved
-Large mutliplayer community
-Difficulty, interface, every control, visuals, and AI are fully configurable to your taste. AI too accurate? You can change that
-Gigantic maps that 400 hours later I still haven't even covered half of
-Unique moments and battles that can't take place in other scripted shooters
-Mission editor allowing for literally any kind of gameplay
-There's not enough time in a life to explore all official and user missions and mods
-Extremely hardware demanding. Get yourself a good processor
--Core i5 4690k @ 4 ghz / GTX 970 OC'd gets 40 FPS on average, but regularly dips to 20
--You'll also want an SSD. Standard hard drives will give you occasional 1-2 second freezes
-You will run into bugs, mostly with how missions play out
-Commanding friendly AI is extremely clunky. Improvements have been made but total overhaul is needed. C2 Command mod mostly alleviates this
-AI is difficult to implement when creating missions
-Mission scripting is difficult and confusing. There is a full wiki and forum dedicated to it but they don't help much
-While the devs are wonderful, the community is elitist and less than helpful
