Saints Row is like a GTA but in funnier, crazier and a more arcade way.
Steal tanks in midair, surf on car, get naked and run like crazy monkey in the streets, defend yourself with a purple huge dìldo, etc.
Compared to a classic GTA, Saints Row might look easier: your health regenerates (CoD like), you start with lotsa ammo and guns, once you grab a new gun it's added to your crib cache and you don't have to buy it again and so on.
However the game itself is actually much more difficult. You will have to fight both gangs and cops. The city sometimes becomes a real war zone with SWAT team rushing into an interesction full speed with their armored truck, cops choppers firing on hostiles, you defending your crib that has been attacked by a gang, the laters bringing their homies with them. Being in middle of all this mess is eerie. You won't survive with another game mechanisms. So, grab your smartphone and call your crib, your favorites homies and increase the chaos in that intersection even more. Can't seem to protect your crib? Too many people running around and shooting everywhere? Okay, call for an airstrike. Missiles will rain down that poor intersection anihilating everything.
It's a lotta fun, really. You will always find something to do in that city. There are many side missions that get unlocked when progressing into the main story. Doing those mission will increase your influence aera and spawn homies in the street that you can call in case of emergency. Also, your hourly money benefits will increase the more area you got and the more businesses and houses you buy.
And best of all, you can play the whole game in coop with a friend. How awesome is that uh?
HOW AWESOME IS THAT? While you drive, your homie is mowing down he street; while you take cover he throws nades on hostiles; while you run naked in them streets your bro is covering your tight äss  with a molusk launcher. Yeah you heard me. A MOLUSK LAUNCHER THAT CAN MIND CONTROL PEOPLE!!
Now you oughta get it: Saints Row is uber fun and crazy. Even the cutscenes sometimes go like: "Isn't there an easier way to get into that plane?" she asks. You just raise your brows and say "Without a doubt honey.".
There are many more features this game provides, so many I just can't enumerate them here in this review. Now I'm trying to find the negative points of Saints Row... and can hardly find any. Uhhh yes, you cannot import your own music to play it within the game... well, that's it. :D
So what are you waiting for?
Don't wanna waste zombies using a huge dìldo while being naked?
Eheh, well... you don't know what you are missing. :)

This is the second best game in the series. If you are unwilling to suffer the terrible port of SR2 and are not a Crackdown fan (SR4), then SR3 is the sandbox rags to riches game for you. It is an action comedy parody on sandbox action games with great action, cameos, fun writing, loads of toilet humor and breast physics, jetbikes, furry hate, and everything but a Godzilla sized soda can.
It does not have the customization or the story depth of the 2nd game (although it wasn’t Shakespeare either), but the weapons, vehicle handling, graphics and sound are all far superior. I really liked the art direction they took in stylizing the game, but they did not breathe as much life into the city itself. There are only a few basic sets of pedestrians, not a lot of lovingly designed locales, and well some of the systems are just a little too “streamlined”, i.e. they didn’t bother to put a lot of great stuff from the previous game into this one. Why? Probably budget and time, of course. Is it still a great game? Hell yea! You make your own character, suit them up how you like, trick out your weapons and cars, you have more freedom in designing your gang (a little more) and there is a lot more dialogue between the characters (witty banter) on the side missions. Everything flows very well in the game. It’s got great replay value.
Even after tweaking and unparking cores, trying to make the game run, I still get around 30 fps on LOW. When my PC is way above recommended requirements.

The best GTA competitor out there (with Watch_Dogs now close), the Saints Row series have always been less serious, and more about the mindless fun. This game lacks motivation and I'm sure it was rushed towards the end. I seem to find tons of bugs and I'm not even a tester. Was this actually properly tested? I think not. I cannot even believe this has been released at a AAA game price, Saints Row: The Third is a game worth checking out, but you better buy it when it's on a (big) sale. The Third in the saga has interesting features though. It has nice customization regarding the vehicles, characters and clothing.  Although pretty simple on the vehicle side, I find it fun to change some vehicles then drive around with them. There's a lot of clothes in the game, and I can stay about 20 minutes in one shop (or even more!) deciding what to put on my character.
The game looks good. But I've seen games that came out earlier that look way better. The city feels too gray and lacks colours, pretty much how I felt about GTAIV. I really like how the cars handle the lightning and how they look when you slam them into a wall at full speed. The driving is good and bad, depending at what type of vehicle we're looking at. Cars are good, Bikes are kind of bad because the handling is either dreadful or impressively easy, Planes and Helicopters are bad. I don't feel like the planes are going fast and that's a problem. The helicopters do not feel realistic, as they're too easy to fly (but that's just me being picky), planes and helicopters should be smoother with their movements. It's kind of hard to explain, but I dislike how they work on this game, but it's still decent, I'm just picky in what comes to air vehicles!
Story wise, really forgettable. I wasn't slightly interested, I didn't feel bad for one death, I even forgot most of the characters towards the end. If this game had no story at all, I wouldn't mind, because most of it just looked like those boring RPG quests, some even had cutscenes but I wasn't interested anymore... The last mission is nice, but rather boring in the beggining. Despite 4-5 missions, most are an introduction to activities and the rest felt tedious. The activities are a classic in Saints Row, and most of them are really fun! Surely better than the story mode... This is a saga that focuses itself on humor. It may just be me but I think they've failed with this one. I am a guy who loves sexual and dirty jokes, believe me, but I wasn't giggling while playing this. YEAH LOOK, A♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Am I supposed to go HUEHEUHEUEH with this? This game had way too much sexual references and sexual humor for me. These are nice, but they're not nice when they're being said and happening all the time.
There's a good amount of weapons, about 20 total (DLC not included). They're satisfying to use and some have a cool piece of creativity, mostly the airstrikes and reaper drones, those are nice. It's sad than you can't keep some of the wepoans like an electrified Scythe, a frenzy Grenade Launcher or a Riot Shield because they're special weapons. When a weapon is upgraded to the final level, it will shoot shock bullets too, giving increased damage!
Regarding side-missions or phone tasks, there are two: Assassinations and Vehicle Thefts. Vehicle Thefts are probably the worst and dumbest thing in this game. It's the damn reason I'm writing this negative review. Okay so I'm asked to get a Street Cleaner just as an example. By pure luck I find one on the streets, lucky! I get in the vehicle and activate the vehicle theft mission, the waypoint gives me some directions, awesome! But! It takes me to the place where I can get a Street Cleaner and ONLY AFTER THIS, IT SHOWS THE WAY TO THE MECHANIC OR WHATEVER. Seriously? SERIOUSLY? WHY?? It pisses me off so much, couldn't you just develop a system where I can get a damn vehicle and drive to the damn location? Why, because you need to put cops in the scene and make it way more difficult? Cheap tricks for ♥♥♥♥'s sake, if I have the vehicle I have all the right to deliver it. Assassinations on the other hand are way better, and are much more fun to do. Really nice to do them and probably one of the best features in Saints Row: The Third.
I'm still waiting to try this out in Co-op, I believe it will be much better because I'm playing with someone else, but all these flaws are still there in what seems to me to be a rushed game towards the end. On the final mission, I slammed a dude's head into the air for like 10 times, and it was a story-line QTE. I tried to access my garage once and my game crashed. Now I can't access that garage anymore because the game screws it all up being the only way to exit the game and start again. While this is a great, realistic combat military simulator, the multiplayer aspect of the game uses mods for almost every server you connect to.  The process of getting these mods installed is very difficult and in many cases results in days of frustration trying to get it running.  The architecture should be set up to analyze what files are on the servers that are not present on the PC it is run on and download these directly instead of using 3rd party programs to validate mods, which is usually only partially successful.
Check out the original Unreal Tournament for how this could be improved.  That worked flawlessly!
Overall, Arma 3 is a great game and I spend many hours playing it, at least when I'm not trying to fix my mods on my local PC.

I've played 500+ hours on this game and I'm still not bored of it. The game throws you into the battlefield with no help at all, in fact it can be a little confusing at your first minutes of play. But once you dedicate yourself and learn the Art of War, you will soon be talking, what almost seems alien language, to others in your house.
From your usual mainstream happy-go-lucky Call of Duty or Battlefield, Arma 3 teaches you the realism of war by simulating... WAR. It will be frustrating, it will be dirty and it will rewarding!
You can either get into multiplayer (strategic and friendly for the best part), single player (which has a good campaign at the same time introducing you to what you will be heading into for the rest of the game) and editor (a huge sandbox where you can do anything and make anything such as missions, mods, and just mess around to get used to the gameplay and physics).
Absolutely love this game and totally recommend it for veterans and people who are interested in the whole military theme.

Now logging over 700 hours I feel very comfortable saying that it is a great game. The game can be a bit buggy while looking at things from extreme distances or very close but overall with its massive scale it is pretty solid. The controls are a bit difficult to learn because almost every key on your mouse and keyboard are mapped to something and gets worse when adding mods into the equation, but they did a very good job managing it offering multiple pre set button layouts and allowing you to customize them to your liking. On the more positive side the game offers a wide verity of weapons and gear you can chose from allowing you to run a different load out every time you play. Its realistic bullet physics offer entertaining firefights in which you need to dial in the range. The semi realistic medical system is very nice to giving a purpose to having a medic, and opens the door to a list of different jobs (MOS). Because there is a weight system in place it means you can take limited amounts of gear forcing you to chose a specific role like a autoriflemen or grenadier. This forces you to move as a squad if you want to be effective on the battlefield. This has lead to lots of communities being created around this game, for example my current unit the 34th Infantry Division which focuses on realistic warfare. There are also more casual communities like Ahoy Worlds that does not use mods and allows for you to hop in and play with ought having to download mods. Another great thing about the game is it's mods. Unlike many other games the developers fully support mods and allow you to install them off of the steam workshop. Here you will find a surplus of easy to install mods, and if what you are looking for is not on there then I would recommend armaholic which is a great place to find mods. In conclusion I would like to say that Arma 3 is a great game that has some flaws but can be easily looked past because of all the positives.

I will flat out admit that I had never even really heard of Saints Row before downloading this game. I wanted a game that had characters you could customize and that you could explore and play at your own pace. Saints Row: The Third was highly recommended everywhere I looked so I decided to take a chance on it.
And I am really glad that I did. I have never enjoyed a game so much. The storyline was just engaging. I did not expect it to be as crazy as it was but I have to say, I liked it. Going from jumping out of planes  to running naked and drugged through a BDSM club was more entertaining than I could have ever imagined. I found myself actually wanting to play the storyline instead of doing all the side quests first. I wanted to know what happened.
The characters themselves had great voice actors and the dialogue was spot on. It's hard not to get attached to them and actually want to protect them (even when they're being annoying little jerks and dying all the time). You can pick a voice for your character and though much of the dialogue stays the same no matter which voice you picks, each one still manages to have its own personality seperate from the others. The voice I picked, clearly had a thing for Pierce and alluded to it several times in the story. Little things like that are what make this game great.
It is a little bit laggy at times and there is one challenge at the end of the first chapter that is completely screwed up on a lot of computers due to a missing cut scene but I managed to get around that by putting my resolution on low and it worked fine. I didn't think the controls for the keyboard or mouse were particularly tricky and I'm someone with terrible hand-eye coordination so free cameras usually mess me up.
All in all, I loved it and am planning on playing it again.

I've played 500+ hours on this game and I'm still not bored of it. The game throws you into the battlefield with no help at all, in fact it can be a little confusing at your first minutes of play. But once you dedicate yourself and learn the Art of War, you will soon be talking, what almost seems alien language, to others in your house.
From your usual mainstream happy-go-lucky Call of Duty or Battlefield, Arma 3 teaches you the realism of war by simulating... WAR. It will be frustrating, it will be dirty and it will rewarding!
You can either get into multiplayer (strategic and friendly for the best part), single player (which has a good campaign at the same time introducing you to what you will be heading into for the rest of the game) and editor (a huge sandbox where you can do anything and make anything such as missions, mods, and just mess around to get used to the gameplay and physics).
Absolutely love this game and totally recommend it for veterans and people who are interested in the whole military theme.

What is there to say about team fortress 2 that hasn't already been said? It won't die anytime soon, and it certainly has a very vibrant community. The cartoony artstyle and the individual personalities of each class provides a fun experience. These 9 classes have origins and aren't just some mute generic soldiers that you play as in many other FPS games. And even though we only get updates every year or so, that just adds hype to the game when the update is released. Every update of TF2 that I've been around to experience has always had a huge wave of new players coming in to enjoy this new update that everyone is talking about. If more devs were hired for TF2 and we got more consistent updates, then it becomes stale. The rate of updates and the uniqueness of the overall game provides a very pleasant experience. You don't have to own cosmetics to play the game, and more importantly, you don't have to pay to play it anymore. Team Fortress 2 has chisled their name in stone as one of the greatest FPS games of all time, and one of the longest lasting ones. Sure, the game might be dead in the next couple decades or so, but as of now we are still able to play and enjoy the game. I definitely suggust you download this game. You would have a hell of a fun time. And if you get bored of capturing points, stealing intel, and killing virtually anything that wears blue or red, then hop on a community server, they always have something for you to do.

I think Its time for me to type up a review for this game and all I can really that this is the best fu*king game by far that I've ever played ''Yet''

:
Saints Row: The Third takes place in a city called Steel Port in which it's ruled by three gangs, the Morning Star, the Deckers and the Luchadores. The enemies you fight throughout the game consist of the same 4 NPC models for each gang. They've created an excuse for themselves by claiming that they're all a product of cloning.
:
This game is optimized for AMD video cards. If you're using a Nvida card you're going to be experiencing significantly lower frame rate and random frame drops.
:
Money in Saints Row The Third practically flows like water. You recieve money for killing enemies, completing missions, completing challenges, barnstorming and through a multitude of glitches to reach to the money limit of $20,000,000. There's one barn storming location in particular that gives you $12,333 if you fly through it sideways.
:
There's no arrest system, no sneak system, you cannot bribe the police or outrun your nortirety. No matter what you do whether it be as small as punching a civilian or as extreme as slaughtering hundreds of innocent people, the police will attempt to kill you. The
way to lose your notority is to walk into a store or safehouse owned by the Saints or attempt to wait until your notority fades. However, you're likely to commit even more crimes when you're running for your life from machine guns, snipers, attack choppers and tanks.
:
Within the Saints Book there's 34 vehicle thefts needed to be completed to get the 100%. Volition made it to where you get a higher notority level as you progress in the vehicle thefts, just to frustrate the player I assume. Unfortunately, there is no way of outrunning the norority so this side activity is practically
. While driving, enemies will constantly spawn within feet ahead of you, almost guranteeing a crash. I will provide a demonstrition video at the bottom of this review.
:
There's 36 assassination missions needed to be completed for the 100%. These are fairly easy usually consisting of doing a particular thing to lure out the target. However, some require for you to gain gang nortority in certain areas of the map and if you've already taken over that part of the map, you're going to need to complete it on an earlier save or in a friend's game. Towards the end of the assassination missions
will ask you to kill a particular person. This person is the Concerned Citizen you've been doing assassinations for up until that point,
. Killing him before will make the 100% unobtainable. Sadly, nobody warned
ahead of time.
:
Character customization is one of the few things that other games need to take a page from when it comes to Saints Row The Third. Though lacking a skin tone slider, the game allows you to select from a variety of skin tones and options. Unfortunately, there's always an insanely repetitive tune playing in all of the Image as Designed stores while customizing your character.
:
Unlike the Saints Row franchise's previous title Saints Row 2, you can no longer listen to the song playing on the radio while editing your vehicle, you must listen to the same repetitive tune. You also no longer get a view of what your vehicle looks like while you're inside Rim Jobs, instead you'll be viewing your vehicle infront of a black background with tire skids moving left and right.
:
Co-op is a buggy though humorous experience. Some activities will randomly teleport you out of your vehicle that you're otherwise not supposed to exit, causing you to fail missions. Co-op partners and most NPCs will sometimes get stuck in buildings, vehicles, and other clutter within the game, almost ensuring death.
:
Other than completing assassination missions, vehicle thefts, challenges, purhcasing all upgrades, finding all collectables and completing all of the missions, there really isn't much else to do. Just run and gun until your map is fully purple.

If you're looking for an FPS like Battlefield or Call of Duty, beware, this is a military simulator, and you will need more than reflexes and gamersense to master it.
Honestly Though:
This game is spot on with the training and atmosphere the military provides. This game is difficult with all of it's features and I love it. It is NOT easy to hit a target with a rifle from 300 yards in real life, and this game matches that same difficulty. Fatigue is a real thing and it seriously hinders your accuracy in real life; Arma 3 makes you stop and catch your breath if you run too far or carry too much gear, otherwise you will have a hard time hitting your target. The AI in this game is sharp and they have great vision. They will punish you for making silly mistakes. The AI is more advanced than most average fools in other games. For someone who is military, or interested in military combat, this is your best choice for simulation, modding, and enjoyment.

Saint's Row: The Third is by far one of my favorite open world games ever. The story of the game was amazing and kept me and my friend wanting to just skip everything and go throught the story just to see what happens. This is how good the story is. Here are some of the best features of the game:
- The game never really forces you to do any missions. You can explore the world and do crazy stuff before beginning a mission.
- Lots of activities and fun things that you can do. You will play a lot before getting bored.
- Money isn't just for buying weapons and ammo. Money can be used to upgrade skills, vehicles, buy and upgrade weapons, purchase buildings to increase the cash you get per hour.
- INSANE ammount of customization. You can customize everything. EVERYTHING. From choosing how big you want your weiner to be, to even upgrading your crib.
- Creating gangs. You can make and customize your gang. You can make ninjas with shotguns roam around the city. Come on, this is ♥♥♥♥ing amazing.
Single-player itself is fun, but if you have one single friend YOU MUST play the Co-op. The game is even more amazing and ridiculously fun.
Just a few and minor glitches such as sometimes getting into the car you dont want or when pressing "E" to enter a car, your character walks really slowly to the car (which might result in death, as you might be in a hurry to escape the police).
Dispite all these minor bugs, this game is one of my favorite games ever.
Final Rating: FULL 10 / 10
The price tag is worth it for what you are going to get out of this game. About 16-20 hours of the main storyline and double or even triple more for exploring and doing other fun activities.

THIS IS A VERY COMPLICATED GAME. If you're looking for an easy game where you can kick back and relax, this is not the game. It's not really easy to learn, so take yourtime reading guides or watching videos. It's worth it. The player community is really great, except for the few weirdos that you might run into if you go on the Altis Life servers. The vanilla game is very fun and has a lot of content, but the mods make it even better.
PROS
Lots of mods
Great community
Different from other games in this genre
Sandbox mode to play around with stuff
Infantry + Vehicle combat
Just really fun overall
CONS
You can get lots of lag when playing on large player count servers, even on high end PC's
The game feels a little sluggish. Movement and actions just don't feel right.
Unfortunately, like many other games, there are bugs. Arma 3 bugs are pretty bad though. They can often take away from the realism that this game was supposed to provide.
CONCLUSION
I think this is a great game for people who are fans of military genres. The high learning curve is what makes almost every session that you play this game, a lesson. I still have A LOT of things that I have yet to learn about in this game.
OH YEAH I FORGOT TO TALK ABOUT DLCS

THIS IS A VERY COMPLICATED GAME. If you're looking for an easy game where you can kick back and relax, this is not the game. It's not really easy to learn, so take yourtime reading guides or watching videos. It's worth it. The player community is really great, except for the few weirdos that you might run into if you go on the Altis Life servers. The vanilla game is very fun and has a lot of content, but the mods make it even better.
PROS
Lots of mods
Great community
Different from other games in this genre
Sandbox mode to play around with stuff
Infantry + Vehicle combat
Just really fun overall
CONS
You can get lots of lag when playing on large player count servers, even on high end PC's
The game feels a little sluggish. Movement and actions just don't feel right.
Unfortunately, like many other games, there are bugs. Arma 3 bugs are pretty bad though. They can often take away from the realism that this game was supposed to provide.
CONCLUSION
I think this is a great game for people who are fans of military genres. The high learning curve is what makes almost every session that you play this game, a lesson. I still have A LOT of things that I have yet to learn about in this game.
OH YEAH I FORGOT TO TALK ABOUT DLCS
So the DLCs for this game aren't really that good, especially when you can just download mods for free. You can play the game without them, and you can even use dlc content in the Sandbox mod as long as you spawn with the weapon, or spawn inside the vehicle.

With over 600 hours on Arma 3, I feel like I am in a position to review the game in detail, Arma 3 is a military tactical shooter developed and published by Bohemia Interactive with over 20 vehicles to drive, pilot, sail and over 40 weapons to fight with (not including DLC and mods). Now is this game worth the £29.99/$39.99/€34.99 of your money? The short answer is yes, however, the long answer is what follows:
Arma 3 is developed by a wonderful development team that provides consistent updates to an almost 4-year-old game, alongside Downloadable content (DLC). Alongside Bohemia Interactive's support, there is also a wide range of modifications (mods) for Arma 3 that vary from a simple plane to an aircraft carrier to an entire mod for the the United States Armed Forces. Arma 3 has a unique amount of gamemodes and servers some official and some unofficial. Arma 3 also has 2 different islands, one small and one large both with insane attention to detail and after a total of 300 hours of playing on Altis (the biggest map) I still find places I've never seen before and boy don't get my started on the graphics this game has.
While Arma 3 is a very good game, there is a huge learning curve and if you have never played an Arma game before you may be put off and it is extremely daunting with all the buttons and commands and different servers and rules. Any returning fans of the franchise won't be surprised to hear that Arma 3 still suffers from an insane amount of bugs and glitches, and while they can be funny at sometimes, at other times you wish Bohemia would just fix those ♥♥♥♥ing things for once, also if you are just scraping by on the Specs required for Arma 3 I would suggest an upgrade or not buying the game at all. When there are 40 men running around a 270km Island with multiple vehicles and explosions and firefights happening at the same time you might also expect a big FPS drop.
Arma 3 is a massive open world FPS military simulation with thousands and I mean thousands of mods to play from, and an ever growing community with a Development team that is eager to push the boundaries of the Arma franchise, with more DLC, community support, and other things yet to be revealed! I highly suggest you pick this game up (preferably with a friend or two, or maybe even three) and enjoy assaulting a position with Close Air Support from an A-10 while three M1 Abrams flank round the right and a team of machine gunners provide covering fire while you cross an open field eager to engage some opfor scum!

I've logged a few hours on this game so i think i can say a thing or two.
First off Arma 3 isn't your normal First person shooter, This game takes skill, it isn't like Call of duty or Battlefield, ther isn't a rank system and there isn't an XP system. This is 100% millsim, You will throw out into a map that is massive beyhond any map you've ever seen. The combat is random at times and intense with no limit on "fair gun play" Depending on what mode you play you and with who- you won't be shooting your gun a lot. this game takes a lot of time. The story mode is fun and gets you into some good basic combat along with a fair story line.
MP is full of mods and game modes set for almost everyone looking for either laid back game modes that you can hang out and play with your friends, or 100% tactical millsims that rage on for hours with strict Millitary commands and stratagys.
the editer is another great tool in this game, if you wanna try your skills in editing a mission or just playing down soilder to fight it out you can! The editer puts you in the driver seat for what you want to create!
Now lets talk about what you're gonna need for PC specs; first off forget the reccomended specs it's 100% BS
you're gonna wanna an Intel I5 or I7 first off, this game doesn't like AMD regadlesss of cores.
8GB of ram at the least! 12-16gb is best. And a GPU that can hold up to Armas insane looking graphics ( did i mention this game looks amazing?)
Sadly lagg and FPS drops are all to common in this game, even with my PC specs i get 15 20 frames in towns when small battles are going on.
BI never really optamized this game very well and it's really hurting us players who don't have enough money to dump on a new PC (i've been trying since this game came out toget it to run great, still trying)

Pretty awesome style last man standing gametype. Centred around fast furious combat despite huge open spaces...
H1Z1 plays out roughly as a 3 part battle. To do well you must recognise your status and play a style that suits.
Part 1 is intense and sometimes chaotic early game. It begins with a strategic choice where to land when spawned, and strategic choices unfold as you near the ground - and see others going for that car, for example, or that you have the advantage and focus on equipping quickly to go on the attack in the Early Game portion. Likewise, you may simply be in survival mode, avoiding equipped players, crafting armour and doing it tough.
Part 2 is ensuring survival in wherever you stand on the pecking order of the world. If you got the dominant start and killed some people, you basically choose to stay agro or settle down, picking your battles. If you are working your way up and still need equipment, nothing changes just keeping picking your battles and have been running to the zone centre for most of the game. Routes that don't get you spotted easily become natural as you are always thinking forward and planning for being ambushed. By now all players are either heavy on gear from their kills or dead from those battles.
Part 3 is the thinning down to two or three players. Annoying as it is, the best players use positioning and strong damage from range to herd survivors / skirt the battlefield so the opponents inevitably come into contact at closer range than the range fighting player.. resulting in prime position no matter what. It could become a battle of patience if a head to head is fair, a lot of players play positioning and swoop in when one or both of the last players are crippled. In a fair battle of course the patient approach can help.
General thoughts on the gameplay.
- Get good at the early game ASAP nothing else matters as much.
- To learn good spots, look for others landing. More than 1 landing might mean a car, watch and learn
- Have the plan to 100% agro to get experience in many situations and various battle. Die and come back
- Any time you find someone, expect to be attacked by 100% agro players, learn to be alert always act fast don't think
There is a decent level of tactical essense to this game, but it is far more important being able to position and shoot fast, jump around and navigate the environment precisely and fluidly combined with fast aiming and reflexes. When I died to someone jumping around a corner and through a doorway, I could only admire the precision input that resulted in him shotgunning me in the face mid air instantly.. as I barely realise I'm under attack from a footstep - firing off two AR15 bullets in prayer.. this is not a game of Army tactics and superior intellect. H1Z1 KotK is... SAVAGE !
Not much more to say really.. depth is in replayability and team modes along with skirmish which is cool, and events. Note the screenshots are from the very earliest builds which are no indication of the gameplay or pacing. The videos will be the same, personally I would remove most/all of the video and screenshots and make new media ;) get to it devs.

This game is one of the best military simulation games out there, no matter if you like to take things slow or fast, there will be a gamemode that will suit your own playstyle. With recent DLCs such as Apex and the Marksmen update, it adds even more content to the base game. The base game however isn't where this game shines however. It is the community. The community makes a ton of mods for this game to a incredible and realisic standard. Complete with vehicles, aircraft, skins and sound packs, you can customise Arma 3 to your liking. With mods, you can join other players on modded servers for gamemodes such as Altis Life and hardcore Military Simulation or MilSim for short, which is my personal favourite among the gamemodes. The damage system is realistic, having you severely wounded or killed within the first shot, and with good body armour, that number would slowly increase, but first shot kill capabilities with a 7.62 AK-12 or 6.5 MX still remains quite high. Wearing body armour alos means you are trading of speed and stamina for protection. Tank protection or APCs are also reasonable, with MBTs(Main battle tanks) knocked out with a single RPG shot to the rear engine compartment and one shot from anywhere for an APC(Armoured Personnel Carrier) or IFV(Infantry Fighting Vehicle). Combined arms and teamwork in this game is highly valued, as you will most definetly lose if you lone wolf. This game is generally fun and challenging and I would definetely recommend this game.

Arma 3 offers one of the most unique experiences in the First Person Shooter Genre.
At times when Call of Duty and Battlefiled brag about realism, Arma just sits there and laughs.
I bought the base game, no expansions, and it is a very fun experience IF you like it. Rather than running around in an arena and shooting people, Arma offers a vastly more tactial approach. You can be laying in the (virtual) dust for half an hour, slowly crawling along as you make your way towards the enemy in the midst of night - which, by the way, is actually dark, and not just a darker version of day, without NVGs (Night Vision Goggles) you are ♥♥♥♥ed - to get into the AO (Area of Operations) just to die moments later.
And while this certainly is frustrating it also is an important part of the "Arma experience". There are many gamemodes, pretty much everyone will find a gamemode that fits his or her playstyle.
Most Gamemodes on public servers are casual, gamemodes you can play for fun for maybe an hour or two before moving on.
The Groups that take the game more seriously are usually closed off, although reddit can help with finding a unit. Those operations are a lot more tactial, coordination and communication is highly valued and teamplay a must.
The controls of Arma are a topic on its own - many keys, if not all of them, are bound to two or three functions. Left ALT detaches your view from the gun. Right Control + M opens the GPS, K the compass, O the watch (yes, there is a watch in Arma). Double tap K or O and the things stay in place. N for Night Vision, Picture Up and Down for Nulling. The list goes on...
Because there was apparantly no place left on the keyboard Arma uses a context menu, opened by scrolling. In there are many options that usually would be bound to a key (E for enter for example, but that is "Lean right" arleady) so you will have to get used to that.
The movement itself is kind of clunky, however does not really impact the gameplay a lot.
As a word of warning: Arma relys on single core performance of your CPU which means that the game can run hidiously, the engine is not very well optimized.
Overall this game gets a massive ThumbsUp from me.

Dear Arma,
It's not you... It's me.
A popular positive review by [Fog]Snow elequiently said, "Kids play Call Of Duty, Boys play Battlefield, Men play Arma."
I am a man all day, doing manly things at my manly job, and when I come home I just want to be a boy.
I have no problem getting killed with a single bullet, dealing with bullet drop, limited amo, or stamina effects on aiming. I love all of those things, and those are the  reasons I started this relationship. But you're high maintinance, I can't give you the time you require, and I don't have a big enough friend group for you to like me.
Yesterday:
4hrs - Play singleplayer to learn controls, loving the game so far.
0.5hrs - Jump into "Quick Play" try to go into normal FPS game modes like catpure the flag. All but two game modes either told me it couldn't find a server, or that I didn't have the DLC. Seems odd to me.
0.5hrs - Playing "Caputre the Island" spawned in the middle of the ocean. WTF!!? Some guy on mic says you need to install something which will make a carrier ship appear, so if you don't have that you just fall into the ocean and can't get to the helicopters. Hmm okay.
1hrs - Same game, spawning at the points that are on land. Me and about 15 people are all waiting on a heli to pick us up. Sigh... Bored... Oh look a heli, yay!
0.05hrs - Heli gets shot down in route to town, I bail the heli like a Jason Bourne bad @ss and go to deploy my parachute to fly in like a tiger ninja raining down bullet hell that could make a grown man cry... but I don't have a parachute. Splat!
0.5hrs - Profanity, inanimate objects accelerating accross the room at forces greater than or equal to gravity, anger at game, dissapointment in purchase, hope of reimbursement, worry about game time spent in single player, sadness at time lost, look at clock and it is past bed time, tired, work tomorrow.
I am a software engineer by day and spend a lot of time figuring out computer related things. Like a TV show watcher, I too like to unwind at the end of the day, but for me I get that in gaming.
No I'm not 60, I am in my 20's.
WORKING FOR FUN IS NOT FUN WHEN YOU JUST GOT DONE WORKING FOR 8 HOURS.
In conclusion, Arma I'm sure there is someone perfect out there for you...but it's not me. I really wanted us to work out, I truly did, but it wasn't meant to be. I hope we can still be friends....
ps. yes I tried other game modes as you can see from my play time, but I didn't have much success. One game I got in and 2 mins later got kicked, I wasn't using a mic, I was playing the objective so not sure what I did.
yes I know this is a strategic sim, not a fly out of a heli 007 game, I was really mad that I had to A) spawn and wait close to an hour for another heli, or B) quit, download software for the carrier and join back in
In that timespan I could have played 2 BF4 games and had loads of fun. I wish Battlefied was more tacticle, but I'll take it over Arma because I have more fun overall.

Then there are those quiet sneaky moments when you are slowly edging up on your prey, using night-vision or thermal imaging system and picking them off at a distance with a high caliber sniper rifle. Don't even know what hit them. The vehicles, aircraft, demolitions, squad weapons, etc.. really round out the game. With such a broad array of weaponry you can do almost anything you can imagine. Huge community, lots of ready-made scenarios, easy to use editors to create your own missions.

Arma 3 is an engaging, thoughtful, first or third person military simulator. It thrusts you into the near future with a variety of next generation weapons and current ones and having you fight with generalized (factions essentially being generalizations of regional areas (middle east, nato, etc etc)) factions. This game will reward you for taking the time to learn its complexities, and for you to engage and interact with the community. while the single player is fun and well done, it is well surpassed by the dynamic content and communities of players you can find online, granted this does require your effort into finding such communities and actively engaging in them.
Overall I would recommend Arma 3 to anyone looking for a military sim that does a good hybrid between realism and game-play, and has a community that supports engrossing, organized multiplayer game-play.

A noose can be used as a scary yard decoration during Halloween or to improve your fishing or boating experience. If you're using the noose for decoration, know the law before proceeding—some states consider displaying a noose to be threatening and have made it illegal.  If you want to know how to make a noose, follow these steps.
Place the rope on a flat surface in the shape of the letter "C." Find a durable rope that is at least three feet long.
Form an "S" shape with the rope. Leave the lead of the rope (the bottom part of the "S") long so that you can tie it to something when you've made the noose.
Compress the "S" shape. Compress the "S" shape until all three rows of rope are nearly on top of each other, with only a few inches in between them.
Pinch the three lines of rope together in the middle. Pinch them tightly until the ends fan out to create a bow-tie effect.
Take the top of the original "C" and wrap it around the pinched space. Wrap it from the right side to the left, leaving about three to four inches of the rope unwrapped. You should be left with a loop and a string on the left end, and just a loop on the right end of the "bow tie."
Poke the end of the rope through the top of the loop left by the "S".
Pinch the coiled part of the rope. Use your thumb to hold down the short piece of rope that you just worked through the loop on the left-hand side so it bends over the loop.
Pull the loop on the right-hand side of the bow until it closes the loop on the left. If this part of the loop begins to pull on the free rope instead of the loop, pull on the other side of the bow.
Adjust the noose. Adjust the noose until the coils look nice and tight and the loop is the size you wanted.

Obligatory header to the review: I focus on four primary areas whenever I review a game: gameplay, story, graphics, and sound/audio/general things that go into your earholes. Gameplay and Story get a rating scale from 1 to 10, and the AV stuff gets a rating from 1 to 5. My philosophy on this is that there are some instances in which a game may not necessarily have that much in the way of gameplay (take Amnesia for example), but the story/atmosphere/whatever it may be is reason enough to pick it up. Also, take the cumulative score with a grain of salt; it's just a numerical feeling about the game as a whole. That's part of why I do these subscores. Also, keep in mind that I'm not going off of school grade based rankings. A 5/10 denotes what I feel to be an average game. Likewise, 7/10 is a game that I think is pretty cool, and something that gets a 2/10 is near-abomination level. Pinning scores to an even further obfuscated rating scale is kinda senseless, but for the sake of my backloggery, I'll repeat again that 1.0-2.7 is a one-star game, 3.0-4.7 is a two-star game, 5.0-6.7, 7.0-8.7, and 9.0-10 are three, four, and five stars, respectively.
Gameplay: So far, I've played the Saints Row games in order, and I can say without a shadow of a doubt that this is the best one I've played. Missions are better as a whole (and they've got checkpoints, so if the AI derps, you don't have to start the mission over again), and you don't need to grind Activities for them, which was my main sore spot from the prior games. I never felt that you should have to grind in a sandbox game just to be able to progress, and finally Volition agreed. Activities themselves have been revamped in a better way as well. Rather than having about ten levels, each getting progressively harder, they keep it to three levels: Easy, Medium, and Hard. The game is a good length, too; completing the main missions took me about 13 hours (Saints Row 2 took me 12, and that was including grinding/restarting because AI was poop).
Of course, the main game is just the beginning for a sandbox game. Unlocking everything and just generally farting around with it is always the best part. I haven't been able to do much of that, since my Steam backlog has grown to the point that I believe it may be sentient, and I also haven't delved into mods, but I can imagine that for the person who only has 20-30 games in their library, they'll be able to clock about ten times the time that I have clocked so far. Overall, I really don't have many problems at all with this game; at least none significant, that is. That's why I'm giving this game a solid 10 for gameplay.
Story: As Yahtzee mentioned in his review of this game, this is the game that jumps the shark whenever it comes to the story. I don't think that's so bad, however; the Saints Row games are at their best whenever they're the least attached to any sense of reality. I did miss out on a lot of potential jokes, since I picked the Zombie voice for my character (I couldn't resist), but whatever came through definitely got a lot of laughs out of me. Also, trust me; hearing the Zombie voice singing What I Got is possibly the best thing ever. Again, this plot may not be the most well-structured plot of all time, but it certainly delivered on entertainment, earning it an 8/10.
Graphics: I don't know if the game really was as demanding as it seemed, but I noticed my GPU (a GTX 760) having to work pretty hard to keep a solid 60FPS at 1080p max settings. I don't have any other GPUs (or the care, honestly) to see if the game is possibly underoptimized or if it, like GTA4, just needed that much power to run at its maximum. Despite this, the game does look pretty good, even if there are some pretty ugly low-res textures here and there (there may be an HD mod out there; again, I haven't delved into modding my game). Graphics aren't everything, of course, but for having a few questionable details here and there, I'll give this game a 4/5 for graphics.
Sound: They put Strapping Young Lad on the soundtrack. 5/5
No, but seriously, I think this is the best they've done on the setlists for the radio stations. I mean, the first game had Husker Du and the Bad Brains, but come on, Strapping Young Lad. The original songs that they did for the game are quite good as well, I must say. Apart from that, the voice acting is fine, even if the Zombie voice forgot to be a zombie at times. I'm still giving this game a 5/5 for the audio, though.
Overall, the score is 10/8/4/5 for an 9.0/10. It's definitely one of the most fun sandbox games I've played in a long time, and I will definitely put some more hours into it once I fell the savage beast that is my Steam backlog. Also, pick up The Complete Package; the DLC missions are some of the best the game has to offer.

Pros'n'Cons Reviews
+ Super crazy game design, where you can do what-the-hell-ever you want to.
+ Great variety in vehicles. This doesn't apply to cars, which are dull and generic, but holy crap, the other stuff. You want to hijack a jet and bomb the city? Go. Do some rampage with a pixelated tank? Go, go, go. Drive an armed helicopter? Sure. And all those crazy vehicles.
+ Customization. You can literally do everything with your character. Build her/him up from the ground. Buy the craziest clothes or well...you can just run around butt naked. Upgrade the gang or tune your car. The variety is wide here, but in character customization is almost limitless.
+ Mini-games, mini-games everywhere! There are some activities that you won't see anywhere else. Ride along with a tiger, do some drug trafficking, jump under cars to earn money with your insurance, racing with the unimaginable vehicles (yes, Tron mini-game, we are talking about you), destroy cars and citizens while driving a quad set on fire (!!!) or just blow up the city as such. Whoa, even typing those makes us excited.
+ The co-op campaign is a great addition to the game. Yes, it's not very polished, and there are missions where the second player feels like a third wheel, but even then, playing with a buddy is always fun.
+ The game isn't the most beautiful, but still holds up and the characters designs support the crazy game design very well.
~ Steelport is great, but it's very under utilized. By the time we've finished the campaign we didn't know the locations of the most important places. Simply the game doesn't teach you the city. There's always the GPS, so don't even look at the road while driving.
~ The characters in the game fit into the Saints world. They would be ridiculous and bad in any other game, but this is different. Luckily the more annoying characters get fewer "screen time".
~ Open world sand box games tend to have long single player modes. Not Saints Row the Third. The campaign can be finished in about 10-12 hours. It could be a negative point, but the activities and other mini-games will keep you in the game for a good number of hours.
- The story starts off interestingly, but soon falls becomes generic with frustrating and pointless missions that doesn't add anything to the experience (expect the progress in the story, of course).
- The AI is really atrocious. Your companions get stuck often and the enemies just stand there to get shot without any resistance. Strategy is non-existent, when they see you, they try shoot and kill you, mostly without success. And if we are at enemies...
- ... they're bulletsponges. A simple footsoldier takes a clip from your handgun before he dies. You can help this with upgrading your weapons, but event then, the enemies will get stronger as you progress. On a side note, your character also takes a dozen clip to die. Jumping into a room and executing a massacre just stops being fun after a couple of hours.
- The new city is big and open but you can never say that it's living. You get the feeling that there are random stuff happening all the time but without rules or consequences. Steelport definitely isn't a city where you just want to wander around and spend time. Simply there's too much silliness happening around you to feel "home".
Time to beat: 11 hours.
In one word: Crazy
On P'n'C scale: Fun Time

how to make carrot cake:
INGREDIENTS
300g carrots, peeled and grated on a box grater
250g walnuts, roughly chopped
2 free range eggs
1 cup raw sugar
3/4 cup canola oil
1 teaspoon vanilla essence
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 cup plain flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
ICING
1 cup icing sugar
100g cream cheese, softened
45g unsalted butter, softened
1 teaspoon lemon juice
1 lemon, zest, finely grated
METHOD
Step 1
Preheat oven to 180⁰C and line a 24x12cm loaf tin with baking paper.
Step 2
Combine eggs, sugar, oil, and vanilla in a large mixing bowl and whisk to blend.
Step 3
Mix cinnamon, salt, flour and baking powder in a separate large mixing bowl, then sift the dry ingredients into the egg mixture and mix to blend.
Step 4
Add the carrots and walnuts and mix until just combined.
Step 5
Pour the batter into the prepared loaf tin and bake for 1 1/4 hours or until a skewer inserted into the loaf comes out clean.
Step 6
Remove the cake from the oven and cool on a wire rack.
Step 7
While the cake is cooling, place all ingredients for the icing into a food processor or a medium mixing bowl and mix well until the icing is creamy, reserve.
Step 8
Once the carrot cake has cooled completely, carefully remove from the loaf tin and peel away the baking paper.
Step 9
Spread the icing generously over the top of the carrot cake, slice and serve.

I was gonna make a joke but I decided I would actually review the game
PROS
+ Has wide range of weapons to choose
+ Has wide range of maps and gamemodes
+ Has wide range of hats
+ Gets updated semi-frequently (only reason it wouldn't is because of huge changes cough jungle cough inferno cough)
+ Every class is useful in one way or another (While a pyro may not be as useful as say a medic it is still good for many purposes)
+ Has a good amount of classes, not small enough to the point where it is boring and you have no options but no big enough to the point that it is overwatch)
+ Very, very well built trading, workshop, pub/casual, comp etc. community
+ Has been able to compete with new games on the market despite its old age
+ Has good humor
+ Has good, original artstyle, or at least did, which leads me to the...
CONS
- Original artsyle has been ruined by ugly hats and paints that are used frequently ( EX Banana hat, Max's, Lime paint, pink paint etc.)
- Small development team
- Troubles becoming an esport
- Slow development ( in the end worth it, but still slow...)
- People getting tired of waiting for updates and turning to OW, paladins, or any other game unrelated to the class based shooter genre)
- Semi-Toxic, Edgey, and bad parts of the community
- Some classes getting played way more then others
- Used to (not really anymore) be part of the reason some CERTAIN SEQUELS will never come out....
There's obviously some stuff I didn't put in, but I hope this give a general outlook on things on the game. I definitaly feel that this is one of if not my favorite game I've played, and I will stick with it for many, many updates (most being localazation files) and hats, to come. Thanks, and have fun.

The DLCs.

Call me cheap, but as a person with a fairly big collection of games on Steam, I feel like the DLCs for this game are too expensive.
A free worthy game.

Saints Row: The Third is, aptly, the third iteration in the Saints Row series. While I have played the others, The Third was my introduction into the series and remains my favourite out of them all.
In Saints Row: The Third, you play as the leader of the Third Street Saints (confusing much?) as they venture into new territory. Thanks to some aggression from the Syndicate, an international crime organisation, the Third Street Saints find themselves in the city of Steelport with no friends, no money, and no where to turn.
Throughout the game, you complete mini-missions to take control of the city, and main missions to progress in the story. You meet colourful, entertaining characters and build a strong bond with everyone around you. There are a few choices to make, though until the final choice they affect little but the mission rewards.
The graphics in this game are decent, though they are clearly designed to be comical and there are some notable flaws. The cars look realistic, and even accumulate dirt over time, yet the crash mechanics leave much to be desired. Also, when driving using cruise control (very handy for drive-by shooting), the camera stutters.
Characters walking down the street can also look ridiculous. You’ll see an old lady wearing sweats and a hoody next to a young man in nothing but bondage gear. The draw distance is rather limited, unfortunately. I found myself on top of my skyscraper hoping to snipe people down below, but zooming in only left me with a ghost town.
Creating the character is remarkably in depth. You choose your physical appearance with sliders, your skin tone, hair colour and style, eye colour, makeup, and much more. You also select a voice and your taunts, which seem to be more relevant in multiplayer.
Dressing your character up is also extensive. There are four different clothing shops in the game, each with their own sets of apparel options. Changing your clothing often is recommended, as it earns you Respect (the game’s equivalent of experience points).
All the mini-games. I gave up on trying to complete them all because I found it quickly transitioned from “fun” to “mind-numbing tedium”. I stuck to the main missions for most of my game time.
It’s offensive, and funny, and if you like GTA you will like this as well.

Let's see where I can go with this review.
My overall rating: 8.0
Individual ratings:
Gameplay: 7.0
Graphics: 9.5
Single player: 7.0
Multiplayer: 8.5
Okay, so let's start with gameplay.
The gameplay of this game is great. Although the game could use more vehicles, the game itself feels modern, realistic and immersive. You can have a handful of scenarios to test your skills in, or you can jump into user made missions. Both which do the job well. Although the former is limited, the latter is not and there can be a large number of missions available on the workshop for you to enjoy.
The weapons and vehicles feel great to handle when using peripherals such as wheels or flight sticks, and the HUD is easy on the eyes. It looks very neat, so information is organized nicely. You can adjust this to your liking too. No HUD? No problem.
"So, why did you rate this 7.0 if you liked it so much?"
One thing spoils this game - frame rate issues. No matter how I play the game, the frame rate drops frequently and can be very annoying. I've tried everything to get it to work, but nothing changes. Once this is fixed, this will jump up to 8.5. Only other suggestions are minor improvements such as a larger variety of controls for vehicles and fixing the free camera.
Graphics are next and when I maxed out the settings, the game looked beautiful. The models were smooth, the textures were sharp. There wasn't many graphics glitches and you could control the graphics in a variety of ways. I like this a lot. I think the planes should have a larger variety of camouflages, but that's about it. I already mentioned how the HUD looks clean, so I won't mention that again. The environmental effects look nice too, such as rain and night. This is my favourite part about Arma games; although the gameplay is nice, the graphics draw me in more. It's a cool touch.
Single player: A lot of workshop mods as well as a good variety of base missions. Nothing to dislike. However, campaigns shouldn't be dependant on DLC. I don't know about you, but I think the Apex DLC is overpriced. That's my opinion though. VR, or Virtual Reality (a mode in Arma where you can test out weapons and vehicles) is cool too, good for comparing weapons.
Multiplayer: if you don't find yourself in a game full of trolls and team killers, the game can be very co operative. Domination servers are my favourite because it's good to have to adapt to different scenarios. For example, taking out AA, CAS comes in, enemy reinforcements come in so you need to hit a radio tower to stop reinforcements. Things like that. Great with friends too. However, I've had some bad experiences with some ARMA admins (I got banned permanently because I was apparently cheating, all I did was run from a truck to the BLUFOR base) but this shouldn't put you off the other servers where admins are decent.

I was gonna make a joke but I decided I would actually review the game
PROS
+ Has wide range of weapons to choose
+ Has wide range of maps and gamemodes
+ Has wide range of hats
+ Gets updated semi-frequently (only reason it wouldn't is because of huge changes cough jungle cough inferno cough)
+ Every class is useful in one way or another (While a pyro may not be as useful as say a medic it is still good for many purposes)
+ Has a good amount of classes, not small enough to the point where it is boring and you have no options but no big enough to the point that it is overwatch)
+ Very, very well built trading, workshop, pub/casual, comp etc. community
+ Has been able to compete with new games on the market despite its old age
+ Has good humor
+ Has good, original artstyle, or at least did, which leads me to the...
CONS
- Original artsyle has been ruined by ugly hats and paints that are used frequently ( EX Banana hat, Max's, Lime paint, pink paint etc.)
- Small development team
- Troubles becoming an esport
- Slow development ( in the end worth it, but still slow...)
- People getting tired of waiting for updates and turning to OW, paladins, or any other game unrelated to the class based shooter genre)
- Semi-Toxic, Edgey, and bad parts of the community
- Some classes getting played way more then others
- Used to (not really anymore) be part of the reason some CERTAIN SEQUELS will never come out....
There's obviously some stuff I didn't put in, but I hope this give a general outlook on things on the game. I definitaly feel that this is one of if not my favorite game I've played, and I will stick with it for many, many updates (most being localazation files) and hats, to come. Thanks, and have fun.

So I was always sceptical to play the saints row franchise, so very enamoured and snooty with pretty much everything Rockstar has done with GTA. I thought to myself, 'A ridiculous, tongue-in-cheek slapstick take on sandbox criminal gaming? Pshaw, not for me, good sir.’ And then I would doff my invisible top hat and saunter out of the room like a royal prick.
Anyway I’ve played through Saints Row 2 and 3 now and god damn I couldn’t have been more wrong. I made the mistake of assuming that slapstick and ridiculous were synonymous with lazy and cheap. On the contrary, what I’ve been playing is a very polished product, with a dedication to freshness and humour. Not the kind of humour Rockstar is throttling, but instead something that is unashamed to be silly, but in a super sleek, sexy kind of way. It owns it, and just because it dares to be silly doesn’t mean that it doesn’t care to do it classily.
I recommend SR2 for the remarkable grit in its story, and 3 for how smooth and polished (and funny) it is. Give it a shot. Then track down your friend and play it again co-op. The third installment of the Saints Row frachise, this game takes you to Stealport, a booming island metropolis, as the leader of the Third Street Saints. The Saints have become international superstars between the second, and third game. Lost in this new city, you are forced to fight your way through the Syndicate gangs to avenge the death of one of the series most beloved characters (No Spoilers) before you can head back home.
Although the total story only comes to around 12 hours of gameplay, you will find yourself spending many more in this open world searching for Gang Operations, new activities, rare cars, and collectables. Although the game falls short of the second in several areas of customization, you will find most base customization mechanics are pretty much the same. It does not have secret littered about like the Saints Row 2 did, meaning there will be no hidden interiors, no secret islands, no hidden sea monsters, and no hidden CD's. Another area I feel it fell short was the overall depth and beleveability of the map. The interior count was reduced, there were no customizable cribs, several shops, and key features that made the second one unique were all missing. I still enjoyed the story, and the game still was the fun, goofy (Much more out there than the second) and unique experience we all come to expect from the franchise.

Saints Row: The Third is a lot of fun. As the leader of the criminal gang The Saints you will steel cars, take people hostage, blow stuff up, pick fights with random passerby’s  and in general cause mayhem and destruction.
You will kill members of other gangs to gain control over their neighborhood and you will be asked to participate in rather random acts of violence. Almost every act of crime and destruction is rewarded with cash and respect. Both can be used (in different ways) to improve your characters abilities.
The smart thing about the game is that it doesn’t take itself seriously. At all. The knowing wink that states ‘we know this is just a game’ and the low-brow humor could have been annoying.
The fact that you will meet the same NPC’s over and over again and that few of your actions have permanent consequences  could have been a major disappointment.
But when a game is this amoral (or even immoral), it helps that there is no illusion of a real world filled with real people.
--- --- ---
Steelport, the city where the Saints roam, seems to exist in its own reality. And of course it does. Murder, theft and all kinds of depravity don’t have real consequences. It’s difficult to mourn the death of an NPC you just shot to steel his car. You know you will meet the exact same NPC again and again.
You can destroy a large part of the town, only to discover that 10 minutes later the city has been rebuild.
You can shoot a police officer for no reason, use your in game smartphone to call one of your fellow gang members to ask for ‘police forgiveness’ and watch other police officers just walk away.
You see, normally I try to do ‘the right thing’ in games. But Saints Row: The Third makes it possible to enjoy being a criminal by taking away the guilt.
But I must admit that at some point something strange happened. I started to like these characters. Early on in the game your character starts singing along with an NPC and that felt good. When near the end of the game I raced through town to save one of my friends and Bonnie Tyler started to sing “I Need a Hero” I felt heroic.
It helped that I made the protagonist female. Voiced by the excellent Laura Bailey (Female Voice 1) she became somebody that I liked and I could accept her violent side.
I even indulged in some character building. I made the character overweight since I figured she wouldn’t have much self-constraint. I gave her practical clothes since she is a person of action. I made her look like somebody in her mid-thirties because that made sense for a ‘boss’.
And this is the sign of a good game: despite the occasional flawed gameplay and design, despite the fact that the game glorifies crime and violence, I finished the game not just for me, but also for her.

Saints Row: The Third is a game that just makes you feel good and understands how to be plain fun. There are some flaws (such as pretty braindead AI, etc.), but the pure joy the game brings far outweighs them.
I've never had so much fun with customizing a character, and I've never felt as attached to a character I created in any other game. The story and dialogue are very funny, and the game features a full cast of lovable, memorable characters. It's got a very diverse, high quality, and even humorous soundtrack. The actual gameplay and mechanics are not perfect, but, as mentioned previously, it is far more fun than frustrating. The ridiculous carnage you can cause is so ENDEARING, and it's REALLY easy to "make your own fun," as they say. I would be on the way to a mission and just stop and cause mischief on the streets because I felt the impulse to do so. I'd get so wrapped up in my SHENANIGANS that I would completely forget what I was doing in the first place after messing around for 10 (or sometimes more) minutes.
Although I haven't delved into it yet, it appears as though the modding community is rather active and has done some really cool stuff (especially the Gentlemen of Steelport series of mods, which is even supposed to address common complaints that players have had with the game). Regardless, the game itself is DEFINITELY worth the price of admission in my opinion.

The game has good optimization for coop gameplay and all the missions work for coop.

The open world is what makes this game, well, Saints Row.
You can run, drive, sail or even fly around the world for hours, killing people, tanks and making combos and calling down air strikes.
The character (11/10):
So. Much. Customization.
You can customize everything! Your voice, your hair, your sex appeal, your muscles, fat and everything in between.
Final score (9/10).
Would buy again.

Better than GTA
No, I'm not kidding. This is more clever, more creative, more insane, and yet more restrained than GTA. Somehow you end up with a game you don't feel like an idiot for having played DESPITE all that it has in it.
A huge difference is that you don't have to wade through a company/writer's misgivings about EVERYTHING!
Really, I can't be the only one that noticed that 98% of the jokes in post San Andreas GTA games were really ♥♥♥♥♥ing in the form of weak "jokes." ♥♥♥♥♥ing about the government, ♥♥♥♥♥ing about hollywood, ♥♥♥♥♥ing about their fans, ♥♥♥♥♥ing about other fans, ♥♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥ing and whinging their whole budget on stupid♥♥♥♥♥♥and not FUN.
On the flipside, this game delivers a lot of fun and interesting gameplay. Not as much as the game before it, but enough for what I paid for it and DLC. It's also fun to be able to put a little of your own attitude in the game without it being thrown back in your face, and design your own character.
I suppose the simplest way for me to continue this review and keep it fairly short would be to say that in the first impressions war, this wins over GTA V most of the time. Not graphically, but you don't exactly get a gat-mobile, or tanks, or VTOL aircraft in GTA without police slaughtering you, sometimes from when you bumped into or looked at one funny twenty minutes ago.
I've also noticed this game is easier to get a hang of, has better flying, and a better set of radio stations on average than any newer GTA game.
Though to do GTA at least some amount of good, I should bring up that GTA V does have one thing that this doesn't. (that's worth a♥♥♥♥♥♥
The middle finger. That's it. Aside from that, I'd happily leave behind the dour attitude, shallow summation of humanity, and deplorable characters to well, you know, have fun. Which is what video games are for.
Anyway, if you like over the top action, and games that take themselves seriously when they need to but never when they don't, consider this one.

Arma 3 is probably the closest to a military game I've wanted. It has some futuristic themes without going outrageous, yet has the simulation to make it more challenging. I played and greatly enjoyed the Operation Flashpoint games Dragon Rising and Red River, but felt they had too much of a mainstream Call of Duty-esque to them. Especially Red River. While Arma 3 has a decent storyline, the character development isn't there. The main character has little to grow on and other characters while ok, could use some more backstory. Probably the most interesting is SSG Adams.
Weapon usage, ballistics, and sounds have improved since first released. And it's all welcomed to me. Originally broken up into 3 parts, the latest patch makes it all one long story. I love the first and second parts, "Survive" and "Win" respectively. Though they are shorter than "Adapt." Win being the shortest with fewer "cut scenes" than the others. But with the extensive open world, multitude of showcases, and huge multiplayer (which I have not experienced), it has more content than most games come with in an entire DLC season pass. BI has done an awesome job and didn't just give up on it. I highly recommend this came to anyone!

As you first enter the world of Steelport you quickly realize that the game is made to shock the player with various weapons like a giant purple phallus and random sex toys sprawled throughout a majority of the missions. Unfortunately the repetativeness of constantly running and gunning though the huge swarms of baddies, or sitting on a heli/in a car shooting rockets after your persuers quickly made me lose interest quickly.  I often found myself just sprinting past all of the enemies just to get to the next checkpoint, only killing an enemy if i absolutely have to.  Usually the only thing that would respark my interest would be a quick quib my character would say about the situation, or a often funny or awkward cutscene.  A quick example of this would be a mission where a pimp ends up drugging you and then selling you as a sex slave.  When the cutscene ends you are nude
and drugged, and you have to melee your way out of the building.  According to my save I spent roughly 18 hours completeing the game, but it felt much longer than that and not in a good way.  I loved the music score, there are countless times when the music lands spot on with popular choices, like when you end up fighting one of the bosses in a wrestling match the song "You're the Best Around" begins playing.  Another instance when you have to save a teammember from their immiment demise "I Need a Hero" plays.  Both of these choices I felt like were hilarious and very fitting to the situation.  Overall I would reccomend this game to anyone looking to play something absurd, but only at a discounted price.

The fans understand this stuff; they have the intellectual capacity to truly appreciate the depths of these jokes, to realise that they're not just funny- they say something deep about HATS. As a consequence people who dislike Team Fortress 2 truly ARE idiots- of course they wouldn't appreciate, for instance, the humour in Spy's existential catchphrase "Hon hon hon!" which itself is a cryptic reference to Sun Tzu's Art of War. I'm smirking right now just imagining one of those addlepated simpletons scratching their heads in confusion as Robin Walker and John Cook's geniuses wit unfold themselves on their television screens. Weaker than SR2, yet still plenty good on its own, SR3 takes the absurd to a higher level and brings you to a new city. That city however, Steelport, just isn't as interesting as Stillwater was, and the locations are much more forgettable. But it's a sandbox and there is plenty of opportunity to do sandbox stuff here. So ultimately, it is alright.
The story is more whacky than SR2's half-whacky half-dark plotline, but it works ok. Realism is thrown out the window in favor of the "cool" and "fun", but fun is perfectly fine. Just that for those expecting something like SR2's excellent storylines will be in for a little disappointment.
Gameplay-wise, there is plenty to do. The usual blend of missions, activities, places to explore, and an absurd number of people to kill. There are also, of course, plenty of new weapons that allow you to brutally end people in a wide variety of ways. If there is a problem, its that the game is too easy. By the time I hit the level cap, I was basically invulnerable to everything except melee hits, and I had unlimited ammo for all my weapons. With bonuses like that, you don't even need cheats to feel like you are playing with them.
Anyway. Sandbox crime. Bwee. Drive cars. Shoot people. Be insane. That's what this game is about. Have fun. :P

Saints Row: The Third is dumb fun. It's a Openworld style RPG played in a 3rd person perspective where you take the role of the leader of the Saints. You play the boss man/woman him/herself as you lead your saints to dominance over the city. You can play through the story campaign or side missions at your own pace and explore all of the city from the get go.The story is fantastic and missions involve, driving, shooting, falling, blowing up, chasing after, escaping from, flying, jumping, dodging and much more. It's varied and very very fun to play.
This is another game I played with my wife. We really really enjoyed it for what it was. The game activities themselves are fun, the scenarios it puts you in are hilarious. The characters are memorable and enjoyable. We both had a lot of fun playing this.
Co-op was very fluid and smooth - with both of us seeing cutscenes as if we were the boss. We were always together and never got lost. Driving around the city was a blast. We would alternate between one of us driving and the other navigating/shooting. Character customization was a particular favorite part of hers, I really enjoyed the feel of combat/movement.
The worst part was when the story had finished. We didnt really feel the need to continue... but there is always the DLC!
This is definitely one of our favorite co-op experiences. I highly recommend it for co-op. Just don't take it too seriously!

What is Arma: Arma is a lot of things to many people. For some it is just another FPS to purchase play for a few hours, get frustrated at and never play again. For other's it's an immersive experience that can provide intense and realistic situations that are only limited by the mind of the (player) creator.
How do I play Arma: I play Arma with a Relaxed Milsim group. We get together usually once a week to run operations that will last on average about two hours. Occasionally I'll hop in the editor and mess around, but usually it's the once a week event.
How should you play Arma: Play it however you like. If you like the Life multiplayer gamemode then play that. If you're looking for a realistic military game then join a unit and start playing with them. It may take a few tries for you to find the right group but once you do you'll have endless fun.
How steep is the learning curve: when you first boot up Arma and take a look at the controls you'll find that most buttons on your keyboard have a function, and some even have different functions when pressed with another button. The first thing you should do is not panic. Remember this is a FPS, and play it as such. Don't worry about how to deploy countermeasures, or how to lower your weapon, all of that you'll learn as you play. For now just remember your basic FPS controls and start from there.
Where's the fun: In Arma you have to make your own fun. I've played entire missions with my group where I didn't fire a single bullet, I instead sat behnd the wheel of a semi. I've also played missions where we fired so many bullets, that we had to get more air dropped in so that we could keep firing bullets. Don't go into this game expecting some action packed, jaw dropping experience. While those moments will come, they don't happen all the time. This is a team game, and if you enjoy working with any sort of team you will find enjoyment in Arma.
