The choices, and things that go on at times were pretty gross in my opinion, especially when given any deal of thought.  Part of the problem is, I suppose that I started taking it seriously, and then it would go ahead and do something beyond where I would want it to go, and I'd get upset.
That said, it is a high functioning open world game, akin to Grand Theft Auto, with character customization, gang cuztomization, everything customization (To a point) with an interesting cast of characters, and a decent sort of story that  treds along over the top, and then tip toes to seriousness.
I appreciate the little things it does, like letting you choose your own character, even though they fully expect you to play a male character, as you despite whatever is happening are refered to as a guy more than a few times.  There are glitches in the game, and very many annoying things, but the game eventually lets you make the choice to become some, extremely overpowerful thing - so that you can enjoy it (Except, when it takes away your hard earned upgrades because it feels like it I guess) So in, that alone gives it the recommendation for me.
The laughs for the most part didn't reach me, I'm not particularly interested in the bulk of the humour, but I know more than a few people might find it right up their allies.  To me, it stands shoulder to shoulder with the Grand Theft series (Of the ones I've played) As it both does things that are better, and falls behind in other regards.

If you're stuck between PUBG and KOTK let me just break it down for you.
KOTK PROS -
•	Fast paced
•	Better audio all the way around (in my case at least)
•	Will run much better on most low end computers, don’t try to buy PUBG if you don’t have at least a decent computer
•	Nice art style
•	Consistent updates
•	Simple
•	Very entertaining with friends
•	Spawns are completely random
•	Good time-to-kill ratio with headshots (as in feels correct when shooting, I feel like I'm doing damage)
•	Car mechanics work fluidly in this game
•	Great skins
•	Ranking system is great
KOTK CONS –
•	Hit or miss when it comes to hit registering (better hope you’re lucky)
•	Shotgun is kind of broken and in an awkward slightly OP stage
•	A few very minor bugs
•	A 1 in every 500 chance you run into a hacker of some sorts, most are killable but some are top notch
•	Game ends in a few set areas so it gets old after a while but a new update will fix that
•	Not many different variants of guns (new one coming soon)
Overall I love KOTK and I personally prefer it, but I’ll still put it to you straight on PUBG.
PUBG PROS -
•	Very realistic looking graphics and weapons
•	Weapons can have attachments
•	Huge map
•	Hiding is pretty good (especially in wheat fields) which may be a con for you
•	Map helps you find your way easily (very noob friendly)
•	Ability to choose where you land to a degree
•	Many different map settings
•	Weather occurs
•	Character movement is absolutely dope in my opinion
•	There’s boats
•	More weapons
PUBG CONS –
•	Misleading weapon mechanics and time to kill
•	Cars are clunky and all around just do not work well
•	The ability to choose spawns makes players spawn in a very linear line which isn’t my favorite honestly (and no you cant reach almost any point when you drop out, you can go pretty far though)
• 100 (from what I've had in games at least) people spawn compared to 174 in H1Z1 which just makes H1Z1 more actioned packed
•	Sounds are terrible, and I mean terrible, if you’re like me and rely on sound a lot in games this game will upset you highly as in you can't normally tell where shots are coming from if you hear them (I have Razer Kracken Chroma's 7.1 in perfect working order and audio settings are perfect, that being said gunshots and things of that nature are very hard to pinpoint which i don't like)
•	Kick and bullet drop on weapons seems to be not as polished in my opinion then KOTK
•	You have nothing to really play for, there are ranks (stats wise) but H1Z1 has a way of making you feel more rewarded with placements (yes you get points at a end of a game in PUBG so you can get your 6 cent skin)
On the bright side of things, I do believe PUBG has a way higher ceiling then KOTK so it could easily prove me wrong.
So there you have it. I was trying my best to not be biased, but overall KOTK is my game. Don’t get me wrong, they are both good games and have their own futures. Should be great to watch them grow.

What is Arma: Arma is a lot of things to many people. For some it is just another FPS to purchase play for a few hours, get frustrated at and never play again. For other's it's an immersive experience that can provide intense and realistic situations that are only limited by the mind of the (player) creator.
How do I play Arma: I play Arma with a Relaxed Milsim group. We get together usually once a week to run operations that will last on average about two hours. Occasionally I'll hop in the editor and mess around, but usually it's the once a week event.
How should you play Arma: Play it however you like. If you like the Life multiplayer gamemode then play that. If you're looking for a realistic military game then join a unit and start playing with them. It may take a few tries for you to find the right group but once you do you'll have endless fun.
How steep is the learning curve: when you first boot up Arma and take a look at the controls you'll find that most buttons on your keyboard have a function, and some even have different functions when pressed with another button. The first thing you should do is not panic. Remember this is a FPS, and play it as such. Don't worry about how to deploy countermeasures, or how to lower your weapon, all of that you'll learn as you play. For now just remember your basic FPS controls and start from there.
Where's the fun: In Arma you have to make your own fun. I've played entire missions with my group where I didn't fire a single bullet, I instead sat behnd the wheel of a semi. I've also played missions where we fired so many bullets, that we had to get more air dropped in so that we could keep firing bullets. Don't go into this game expecting some action packed, jaw dropping experience. While those moments will come, they don't happen all the time. This is a team game, and if you enjoy working with any sort of team you will find enjoyment in Arma.

Saints Row: The Third is an action-adventure game and the third entry in the Saints Row series. The game is mission based and can be played as a single-player or multiplayer.
Story missions also put you in touch with Saints Row’s surprisingly funny cast of characters. Some are just jerks. Fine, they’re all jerks – but you’ll separate the ones you can’t stand and the ones you’ll choose to drive around with you based on how much of their schtick you can handle. The pimp who speaks entirely in autotune is amusing for the first two missions, then I endeavoured never to meet him again. On a more socially acceptable level, the vengeful Shaundi makes a welcome return from the second game, and the seven foot tall, turtle neck wearing Oleg is a lovable addition.
The humour blends a shock and awe assault of nudity and narcotics jokes with some knowing, clever oneliners: “When will the rescue chopper arrive?” “Oh, in about two waves of SWAT guys”. I teetered on the brink of genuine offence throughout, but stayed on the happy side of disgusted. True, it’s a game that lets you hit an innocent pedestrian fatally in the face with a huge purple dong, but you can’t hire a hooker, drive her into the middle of nowhere and shoot her. And there are no women-slapping quick time events, or any of the other moments of nastiness that GTA slips under the radar in the name of parody.
Often amusing and always insane, Saints Row: The Third proves that it’s fine for games to just get wild and have stupid fun.

Arma is a game for pure badasses.
Aside from all of the big attractions like Life mods and Epoch, this game is a hardcore military sandbox. It's the only game where you can fly a jet, carpet bomb a city, parachute out into water, swim to shore, take out baddies on a boat, proceed to steal the boat, use the machine gun on the boat to blow up the enemies cars, then jump off the boat fly a helicopter 10 meters above the ground under power lines with your buddies shooting from the side of it. Pros:
- There's almost nothing you can't do in the game
- It's insanely good
- Makes ya feel like a badass if you're good
- Everything is so much fun
- Great graphics
- Sounds and animations are fantastic
Cons:
- Some performace issues (Arma 3 is heavily CPU based)
- Buggy (The doors still haunt me to this day)
I personally have an i7-4790k so running Arma isn't an issue at all, but if you've got an i3 or a lower-end model i5 good luck. Just make sure you have a good processor. But even if you can't run it on ultra it's so fun the graphics don't even matter. Would 100% recommend buying it.

Saints Row: The Third is an action-adventure game and the third entry in the Saints Row series. The game is mission based and can be played as a single-player or multiplayer.
Story missions also put you in touch with Saints Row’s surprisingly funny cast of characters. Some are just jerks. Fine, they’re all jerks – but you’ll separate the ones you can’t stand and the ones you’ll choose to drive around with you based on how much of their schtick you can handle. The pimp who speaks entirely in autotune is amusing for the first two missions, then I endeavoured never to meet him again. On a more socially acceptable level, the vengeful Shaundi makes a welcome return from the second game, and the seven foot tall, turtle neck wearing Oleg is a lovable addition.
The humour blends a shock and awe assault of nudity and narcotics jokes with some knowing, clever oneliners: “When will the rescue chopper arrive?” “Oh, in about two waves of SWAT guys”. I teetered on the brink of genuine offence throughout, but stayed on the happy side of disgusted. True, it’s a game that lets you hit an innocent pedestrian fatally in the face with a huge purple dong, but you can’t hire a hooker, drive her into the middle of nowhere and shoot her. And there are no women-slapping quick time events, or any of the other moments of nastiness that GTA slips under the radar in the name of parody.
Often amusing and always insane, Saints Row: The Third proves that it’s fine for games to just get wild and have stupid fun.

Team Fortress 2 is a brilliant game with a brilliant community and exceptional support from Valve. It is easy to pick up, the classes all pander to different playstyles (not necessarily a bad choice) and it isn't a pay-to-win system like other F2P games . Being someone who has played this game without dropping a cent on it, I would say that it is still fun to play without buying anything. The community for the game isn't as toxic as you might expect and are often genuine people that want to have fun in a shooter game. Valve is always updating and fixing the game and has almost entirely removed cheaters (if you find any just leave your match because they are horrible to play with or against). I have a few issues with the game however. The inventory space in the game is limited - so items are constantly having to be removed so that other better items can take their place; however, this problem goes away with microtransactions. I know that it's an F2P and Valve needs to make some money, but it is an annoyance sometimes. My only other problem is that games either last too long (namely capture the flag) or are too short (payload). This doesn't sound too bad; however, it makes you burnout really quickly as the games that are too short often put you off another and games that are too long make you want to commit suicide after they are over because you just wasted 3 hours on 2Fort. I highly recommend this game and you should defintely pick it up

Where to begin..
If I had to pick one word to describe Saints Row: The Third, I would choose the word "bouncy". The game just felt very bouncy. You would be speeding down the highway in a Hummer and a bike would hit you and you'd spin out and fly in the air. I'd crash into the wall of a building and get flung around all willy nilly. There were times during my playthrough where I'd get glitched in a car after doing a Bo-Duke-En. The car would be stuck bouncing up and down really fast, and I'd lose health and die.
The game does have its fair share of glitches, bugs and errors. I'm not using fair share lightly either. I encountered lots during my playthrough which honestly really kicked down my rating for this game. A lot of what I encountered just made the game very frustrating very quick. The very first mission in the game, for example,  where you robbed the bank glitched for me. One of the Saints will come and kick down the door in the mission to proceed to the next room. It didn't happen because he got glitched into a desk. I had to restart. However, even when the game throws as much crap as it did at you, it still is fun to play.
The story was good. It was entertaining and funny. The gameplay was okay, despite the bouncy behaviours I encountered. The DLC's in the game did add entertaining things to do after the main story is completed. I did enjoy all the DLC mission packs. They were short though. Really.. really short. I believe each mission DLC pack have 3 missions. Still a lot of fun. Made me laugh a lot since I never played the DLC's before.
In short, I will recommend this game, however, I don't think it's worth whatever the current full price is for the game. If you don't have the game and it's on sale, definitely buy it. If you want the game but it's not on sale.. just keep an eye out for when it goes on sale.

As far as true to life military simulations. I have been playing the arma series since operation flash point. There's nothing bar none, hands-down.
If you are looking for a fast paced shoot em up , hundred Bad guys flash in front of your eyes in 15 minutes to beat a level then this is not for you.
If however, you are looking for a game where you can make yourself a rank of a colonel, on a battlefield with 2000 individual units on both sides, in a wide-open destructive environment 100km wide. When you will have small individual command of your own 15 man platoon, but you will also  have high command of 12 other infantry companies with two hundred units in each company, as well as aircraft and armored vehicles at the company and battalion level at your disposal in order to advance and find, capture. Or kill the enemy.
It can be a very slow paced game making strategic level decisions as a colonel or switching your player  right down to the grunt level as sergeant in the field on the front lines advancing the main attack. It is slow-paced at times, fast-paced at times, and if you get hit one time by a sniper round, you are dead.  This is not a call of duty get shot 50 times and stay alive, Kill 50 thousand bad guys in a 10 minute period while drinking your 7-Eleven Slurpee with your Logitech gaming headset on. The mod community is so huge, that this game is just about as realistic as it gets. For a military sandbox simulator . And if you have a chance to use VR, I don't think you would ever want to leave this virtual world.
I know that review was all over the place. But I have a lot of hours in this game and Fell in love with it years ago. So if you like more realism vs fast paced and less realism, this is the game for you. Imagine sitting back on a mountainside, controlling six infantry companies of 200 men in each company, using high command system to order each company into a village to attack 1000 insurgents. Using a binocular's as a general to Call in airstrikes, supply drops, heli transports , literally F-15 fighter jets to drop huge JDAM bombs on the village destroying the entire destructive environment, and let's say you get sick and tired of using the high command system as a general and commander of the battalion, you can do a team switch and jump right into any unit that you make playable in the 3D editor, down on the front lines at enemy troops. This is ARMA3.

I personally don't really like the direction the game seems to be taking lately, with the competitive scene and avalanches of cosmetics and whatnot, and I haven't played it at all in months. But 1,947 hours is a big number. If a match averages fifteen minutes, that's almost 7,800 games. If you play three hours a day, every day, that's over 20 months of daily gaming euphoria. That is a lot of kick for a game that's completely free.
Admittedly, I recently tallied up how much all my TF2 microtransactions cost, and it came to somewhere in the realm of three hundred dollars. I was age twelve when most of this happened, by the way. But this game won my money. Between the colourful art style, lovable characters, absolute mountain of different weapons and cosmetics, and unprecedented replayability, this game isn't bad for a F2P.
Maybe you won't get as much out of it as I did back in The Good Old Days (Like, five years ago). Maybe you'll only play 1000 hours before you get bored. But for all the scout-shooting, spy-checking, dispenser-putting, payload-pushing, point-defending, trap-laying, rocket-jumping, ally-healing, hat-hoarding and minigun-spamming, that's a lot of bang for your buck, especially when your buck is LITERALLY NOTHING.

As far as true to life military simulations. I have been playing the arma series since operation flash point. There's nothing bar none, hands-down.
If you are looking for a fast paced shoot em up , hundred Bad guys flash in front of your eyes in 15 minutes to beat a level then this is not for you.
If however, you are looking for a game where you can make yourself a rank of a colonel, on a battlefield with 2000 individual units on both sides, in a wide-open destructive environment 100km wide. When you will have small individual command of your own 15 man platoon, but you will also  have high command of 12 other infantry companies with two hundred units in each company, as well as aircraft and armored vehicles at the company and battalion level at your disposal in order to advance and find, capture. Or kill the enemy.
It can be a very slow paced game making strategic level decisions as a colonel or switching your player  right down to the grunt level as sergeant in the field on the front lines advancing the main attack. It is slow-paced at times, fast-paced at times, and if you get hit one time by a sniper round, you are dead.  This is not a call of duty get shot 50 times and stay alive, Kill 50 thousand bad guys in a 10 minute period while drinking your 7-Eleven Slurpee with your Logitech gaming headset on. The mod community is so huge, that this game is just about as realistic as it gets. For a military sandbox simulator . And if you have a chance to use VR, I don't think you would ever want to leave this virtual world.

I came into this game after having finished Saints Row 4 and 2 first, in that order. The difference between 2 and 4 is drastic, so I was interested to see where The Third would be in relation to those two. As one might assume it’s somewhere in the middle. The second game had missions with only light scripting and a big dose of unpredictable chaos at the hand of the AI and world simulation, while the fourth game was more directed and scripted with a big emphasis on comedy. It can be hard to describe just how different the two feel when actually playing. The closest thing I’ve experienced in other games to the feeling of out of control madness in Saints Row 2 is in the Stalker games. The fourth might at first glance appear even crazier than the second game, but it’s a chaos that feels highly predictable and in control of the creators. The Third tries to do both things, and doesn’t do it as well as either 2 or 4 did. It is without a doubt the worst Saints Row game I’ve played yet.
For the most part Saints Row The Third is perfectly fine. Visually it’s a huge improvement over the second game, and in general the level of polish is on another level. The problem though is that many of the changes make the game more conventional, and as a result a bit boring. For example the weapons and enemy types have changed quite a bit from the second game. Almost all the weapons in Saints Row 2 felt powerful, and in The Third the majority of the guns suck. They aren’t loud enough, and they don’t do enough damage which creates a frustrating bullet sponge feel, even when fighting the weakest enemies. This made many weapons unusable, like all the shotguns and all the submachine guns.
The biggest issue though I had with The Third is the story. In both 2 and 4 it was excellent! Great antagonists and a good sense of progression and character development with proper last acts that resolved everything going on in the games. Real solid work, unlike The Third where it’s more of a mess that doesn’t go anywhere. As far as games go The Third is still alright, and it has several high points, especially in the second half of the game. But it wasn’t nearly as good as the other two, and it felt unfinished. In about a third of the missions there were abrupt cuts where it seemed like there should have been a cutscene, but there was nothing. It also ended a couple hours before I expected it to. Several things are left unresolved, which added to the feeling that they were forced to cut things from the game. Everything that’s in the game is very well polished, but there are gaps, like the ending.
Because the game mechanics are more polished than the second game this feels like an easier game to recommend on one level. But on the other hand I just didn’t enjoy it as much because of that. The second game was on the surface a shoddier game, but while I was playing it there’s no question I was enjoying it more. The fourth game blows The Third out of the water in terms of story, humor, character and just about everything. Even the use of music in the fourth game is a notch above The Third. This is still a good game, but play the other two first.

This game was a gift from a friend, and in the beginning I played it here and there. About 8 hours of not really doing anything and just screwing around in the city while completing some missions, I found myself lost within the wonder of the city. As I bought new games I let this one sit for a while, and I start to play it again a few months later, I start doing some more of the missions and this game pulls me back into the city, pulls me back into the wonder of Saints Row: The Third. The thing I can say whole-heartedly about this game is that it has an over the top unique style to it unmatched by other sandbox games and that's what really drew me into the world.
This game gives you a sense of freedom and the ability to be who you want to be and do what you want to do. That's a hard thing to come by with games sometimes, and for SR3 to nail it perfectly can't be ignored.
There's so many high points to this game, the missions are always fun, the gameplay is awesome, the controls are tight. The story is well rounded, over the top, and full of what the f*ck moments that leave you scratching your head. My favorite moment being the Tron world fighting the leader of the Deckers, Matt Miller. I don't want to spoil too much because what I'm obviously saying is, "Play this game, oh my god, you need to play this game."
Now there are some gripes I do want to point out, now towards the end of the game, there's a mission involving zombies where you have to dispose of containers. This mission to me was a pain in the a**... You have to run container to container trying to avoid the zombies, and there's hoards coming at you from every which way. So it did get annoying trying to finish that mission. My other complaint is the ending mission, going to the three locations to fight off everything thrown at you. It was a bit much even being the final mission to the game.
I honestly the low points in Three Way can easily be overlooked by the next part in the mission which brings the great story to a close. This game should not be overlooked, it's funny, over the top, amazing and unique. If you have the extra spending money or if you're thinking about getting it during a sale, what are you waiting for? Buy this game!

Team Fortress 2 is a multiplayer FPS developed by Valve that's over 10 years old! There's been a relaxed community within the game with items such as cosmetics, unusuals, weapons etc. The game was released in 2007 and went free to play in June 2011.
There are a variety of gamemodes you can play. Ones like capture the flag and control point are the most basic but some like payload and payload race are a original to the game. In 2012, Mann vs Machine was added as a co-op gamemode where you face against robots who are carrying a bomb. There are also custom gamemodes and maps by the community that you can play on. There are nine classes. Some require more skill (
) than others. Each have their own strength and weaknesses. There are also specifc weapons and reskins that are for situational uses in game. Cosmetics are also there, but they don't break the gameplay whatsoever. There's somewhat of a storyline to TF2's history but it's not really relevant to the game itself. The game has a casual and competitive gamemodes for official maps although there are some people who rage quit in casual. Major updates have a pretty decent hiatus between each other, so you might find the content a bit boring once you get used to everything.
The graphics are cartoonish but don't let that fool you. There are some moments where blood is present (
) and body parts explode. Even for a 10 year old game, it holds up quite well!
The music is really good. Unfortunately, it's mainly used in the main menu, winning or losing etc. Surprisingly, when you disconnect from a server, you don't hear any music in the main menu, only when you boot up the game.
TF2 is a great game to enjoy both casually and competitively, with balanced gameplay, fancy cosmetics and nice music, you'll have a great time with the community playing as the RED or BLU teams.

+Nice classes
+Balanced weapons
+Dedicated community
+Fancy cosmetics

-Music not used a lot (especially in the main menu)
-Finding a server in casual and competitive may take a while

I absolutely adore this game. This is the first game I ever bothered to get 100% completion on and that was on an Xbox 360. When the studio started bankruptcy proceedings I wanted to support them, so I bought it again here on Steam when it went on sale and bought it yet again with the Deep Silver Humble Bundle. Saints Row 3 is as close to "perfect" as I've seen in a long time. There are precious few technical issues (bugs, crashes, etc.) and there really isn't ever a moment in the game when it feels like a chore. In other words, everything you do gets you _something_ be it cash, XP, laughs, or all three. And honestly, if you've been looking at Saints Row 4, don't bother. A conservative estimate would be 65% of Saints Row 4 is imported directly from this game -- this stems from the fact that SR4 was actually supposed to be an expansion for SR3 but the studio tanked and the people that bought them decided to stretch the expansion into an entire game. You'll see this is true if you find some commentary on the SR4 DLC. It's about 15 minutes long, is really just one long fight with some voice over work and _says plainly and explicitly_ that SR4 is actually just an expansion pack.
So, yeah. Buy this. This is awesome. Don't buy SR4. ♥♥♥♥ Deep Silver. Philosophically they've gone the EA/Activision route.

I picked this up very cheap during a Steam Sale and couldn’t believe how much fun it was. Following my bitter disappointment with the pile of f garbage that is GTA4, I figured this genre was dead, but SR3 has found a way to breathe new life into it. The GTA series is still following the exact same cookie-cutter format from GTA3 way back on the PS2, but Saints Row has found a way to rebrand itself into something fresh.
While GTA is still making you comb the city for one car you might like to hang on to and can only save it by precariously parking it in parallel spaces outside your apartment, Saints Row lets you fully customize just about any car you can find with colors, wheel spikes, nitro, etc, and can also have it delivered to you in the middle of the street with a simple cell phone call. Yes, this is a feature whose time has come since now you can actually use vehicles you like on missions instead of being scared to death your tank or FBI car will get blown up or fall off a bridge if you ever take it out for a ride.
VTOL aircraft? Jet bike? With lasers? Yep, those are there, too. Controls are very tight, even for the aircraft, the on-foot combat is far superior to what is still, over a decade later, a clunky & broken system in GTA, and the PC version has full controller support.
An actual reason to explore the city and complete side missions & challenges? Yes, the wealth of unlockable options available, from health upgrades to infinite ammo, to extra costumes for you & your followers, there are tons.
It’s also refreshing that Saints Row refuses to take itself too seriously. Half of a GTA game nowadays is listening to endless dialogue & cutscenes, usually with some political bunk the devs think is very profound. But I’d rather have fun and play a game instead of get propagandized to when I’m paying for the experience. Maybe that’s just me.
If you felt the same way about GTA4 that I did but still enjoy these types of games, SR3 won’t steer you wrong. Go for it. If you’re one of the GTA zombie fanboys slavishly giving that tripe 10 out 10 reviews, then don’t worry, GTAV will be out soon enough to give you more of the same.

This game is over-the-top, cheesy as hell, and incredibly silly. It is also amazingly fun, in the purest sense of the word. I'd even argue it's too weird to start with, but if you aren't completely put off by the opening mission there is a ton of fun to be had.
A representative sample of the game's sense of humour (and general sensibility) is the "Stay Classy, Steelport" achievements, which require you to kill a number of enemies with the Fart-in-a-Jar and the Penetrator, which is a giant pink♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ The game is undoubtedly silly and wish-fulfilling, but it's so unapologetic about it that it's actually quite charming. You'll be laughing at the game, until you suddenly realize you're unironically having a blast.
That's also because underneath all that silliness, it's actually a pretty good open-world game. I never felt bored or that I ran out of things to do in Steelport, the cars handle great, and the radio stations have introduced me to so, so many good songs.
I bought the complete pack, and my personal opinion about the DLCs are that they are unnecessary at best and actively annoying at worst: some saddle you with a bunch of ugly costumes that you can never discard from your wardrobe, others give you versions of vehicles (which likewise can't be removed from your garage) you'll get anyway during the course of the game. Even the 'story' DLCs are pretty insubstantial for the most part. I would get the "Gangstas in Space", "Nyte Blade", "Money Shot" and "Explosive Combat" DLCs and give the rest a pass.

I just played through the game for the second time and it took me a while to decide whether or not I was going to recommend it.  The game has huge highs but also has its share of lows that really detract from some of the things the game does well.  Ultimately, however, I think it's totally worth sale price if you can pick it up when it's cheap.  For that amount of money you still get a very good number of gameplay hours from the campaign and sheer amount of customization Saints Row 3 gives.
I'll start with the big positive - customization.  From clothing to automobiles, you can spend plenty of hours just getting your character to look the way you want.  The character builder itself is very well made and lets you make your character look exactly the way you want it to be.  After that, I have to admit I spent plenty of time going from store to store trying to find the perfect outfit to make my character look as awful as possible.  Once my character's physique and outfit were complete, I spent a while stealing cars and trying to paint them to my liking.  The game's customization options are great for anyone who likes a game where you can spend hours customizing your character.
The multiplayer is also a big plus.  There's nothing better than driving around in a stolen cop car as a buff man literally made of gold with your friend riding shotgun as a cowboy (with a real shotgun in his hand for fending off the angry cops and rival gang members).  Co-op was lots of fun and added a couple hours to the game.
The campaign for the most part was fun.  There were a couple missions here and there that were fairly boring or killed the pacing of the game, but most were forgivable and didn't really take away from the game.
Then we get to the negatives.  The game is extremely buggy at points to the point of making the campaign extremely annoying to continue.  In one mission, you find yourself running away from zombies who will randomly light you on fire for no given reason and without any warning.  After getting fairly annoyed at the game for making me flail around on fire out of the blue several times, I looked online and found this was a visual glitch where certain zombies that were lit on fire from the environment would not appear on fire themselves but still be able to ignite players.  I was still able to complete the misson alright, as the mission isn't really that difficult, but the whole mission was still a nuisance.
Perhaps the most annoying thing about the game was the horrendous companion AI.  Yes, plenty of games have horrible companion AI that ruins escort and escort-like missions, but in Saints Row 3 every time you have an AI follower you have to keep looking over your shoulder to make sure they aren't getting themselves killed.  And if they do die, good luck reviving them, as they'll likely be surrounded by 10-20 angry enemies armed to the teeth.  In the final mission alone I had to revive Pierce over 5 times.  He seemed to enjoy running straight up to the tanks and trying to gun them down with a puny assault rifle as they slowly burned his flesh with their firebeams.  Reviving him was difficult, as he would just lie there in front of the tank that could easily take 2/3 of my health on the run over to his body.  Keep in mind I was doing this mission with multiple levels of upgraded ally health too; without the upgraded ally health he would have downed much more often.  Though this happened in multiple missions with different followers, the only time it was ever this much of a hassle was in the final mission.
Another annoying feature of the companion AI is their apparent fixation on clearing out areas before moving forward or escaping.  Plenty of times you'll be surrounded by too many enemies to kill and have to flee quickly with a vehicle or on foot.  However, the AI doesn't seem to recognize this and will stay in the area while still getting massacred.  It takes an extremely long time to get followers into a vehicle when fleeing, and you have to move very far away from an area to get the AI to recognize you want to move on.  Both make come of the campaign missions a bit more difficult than they have to be.
I would still recommend this game for anyone who can get it on sale.  If you like customizing your characters and running around in a fairly open world blowing things up with friends, this game is totally for you.  Just be aware that it is far from perfect and will lead to big amounts of frustration at some points.

So here is the thing about H1Z1, and why it is such a complicated game to recommend or not. I have played this game since before King of the Kill even existed. Back when it was first released as purely a survival game. This game has gone through a huge evolution from where it began. Many in the community who played this game religously (including me at the time) were demanding that the game established a true identity. Back in the day Survival, and Battle Royale were all two moded within one game. While many only played the game for BR, there were still a small diehard group of survival players. So what did Daybreak do? They split the game into two, Just Sruvive, and King of the Kill. The best thing that could have happend for BR. For survival? Not so much. Just survive has been left behind quite a bit in comparison to King of the Kill. In seeing the split, you will notice that most people only played for BR. So is this game good? Well, if you like fast paced, open world, first/third person shooter games then yes. This game is what one would call arcadey. Not quite as tactical as PUBG. More fast paced, and simpler, however. Daybreak has gained a rather negative reputation amongst the community of this game, as not fixing the issues that have plagued this game. Such as, wonky hitreg, creating more bugs when releasing patches that are supposed to fix bugs, Players playing on regions that they shouldn't be playing on due to high ping having negative impacts on gameplay. There is a multitude of things wrong with this game. However, as someone who has dumped hours upon hours into KOTK and pre split H1Z1, I have to say that ultimately this game fun, and deserves the success that is has been getting. Can Daybreak improve the way they do thing in terms of bug fixes and balancing the game? Yes, without a doubt. With that being said though, this game will become addicting real fast if you are into games like this. It will also eat you up and spit you out, and give you the middle finger, because of the issues that still have plagued the game since the beginning, but it will make you a stronger and more resilient because of it. The highs are extremely high, and the lows are extremely low in this game. When you perform well and win fights and games, you will feel on top of the world. When you aren't, you will want to break your keyboard. This game is an experience, either way. For me personally, at the end of it all, recommend this game. For better or worse, it will create memories.

I parachute into a hot zone. I hear the distant crackle of small arms fire. Kind of like fireworks. 4th of July... I snap out of it as the ground suddenly rushes up and meets  me. I roll onto my stomach and crawl into a nearby bush. I jumped with 3 squad mates. Where are they? I glance around. One comes drifting down dead in his harness. The other is nowhere to be found. Tension builds in my belly as the chatter of nearby automatic weapons fire starts back up again. I gaze cautiously out into the outcropping of squat buildings ahead.
Is that where the fire is coming from? I can't tell. Can't be sure.
I am frozen.
There is a house across the street. The street is narrow. I could dash for it. But it might blow my cover. 50 meters never looked so far in my life. I get into a crouch. Glance around again. Suddenly I see smoke rising from a dusting of rocks to my left. I immidiately drop down and toss a grenade. It works, the enemy tango dashes from the rocks. A few swift pops and he's down. Was he alone?
There was no way to know for sure.

Saints Row: The Third is what I would call the "Anti-GTA". Where the GTA series maintained a mostly serious take on the crime underworld sandbox genre, the Saints Row series has slowly become more and more a parody of the genre than a member of it. Saints Row was orginally just a GTA clone, the Saints Row 2 started taking itself less serious by making everything just massively over the top and Saints Row: The Third just fires any remaining realism and seriousness right into space.
Pros: The game is a time-sink 40+ hour game which will have you laughing and incredibly entertained from start to finish. The physics are completely out of control and you'll have mountains of fun just killing people in ridiculous ways. Addiontionally, the game does a tremendous job of providing options for customizing and making your character your own, through incredible depth in facial features, clothing choices, voice options, ability upgrades, vehicles, etc. The mini-games are incredibly fun and the missions are a roit. The game has great characters and voice acting. It's one of those games you keep permanently installed on your hard drive so that once you beat it, every once in a while you can pick it back up to go on a murder spree just for the hell of it.
Cons: The game can be a little glitchy at times and while some are hilarious when they work in your favor, they can be incredibly frustrating when they work against you. Furthermore, the difficulty curve of the game is bell-shaped. Once you start hitting your high level upgrades, you can actually become permanently immune to damage, which more or less takes the any challenge out of the missions. Finally, there's no "game plus" mode, replay old missions, or a way to restart with your current character so once you beat the main storyline, there isn't anything to do with your character except replay the minigame challenges you've already beaten or track down the collectibles for 100% completition.
Verdict: Overall, Saints Row: The Third is a great game which continues right where the previous game left off, further distancing it from GTA and putting it in a class of its own. Highly Reccommended, along with Saints Row 2, if you haven't played that one either.

Is that where the fire is coming from? I can't tell. Can't be sure.
I am frozen.
There is a house across the street. The street is narrow. I could dash for it. But it might blow my cover. 50 meters never looked so far in my life. I get into a crouch. Glance around again. Suddenly I see smoke rising from a dusting of rocks to my left. I immidiately drop down and toss a grenade. It works, the enemy tango dashes from the rocks. A few swift pops and he's down. Was he alone?
There was no way to know for sure.

Having played a lot of Arma 2, I had trouble making my inevitable move to Arma 3. With the tide of players moving to BI's newest version of my favorite game, I couldn't hold out for too long. Perhaps it was the many, many memories I have playing Arma 2 with friends that held me back. I wondered if Arma 3 would provide the same experience.
This review is meant to offer some insight to players still waiting to make the move from A2 to A3. I won't cover much about graphics as the difference is obvious there. Clearly, A3 looks better.
GUNPLAY
This was one of my most important factors in deciding whether or not I would like A3. At first, I hated the gun sway and the seemingly complex stance system and figured it would simply detract from all the fun I could have in PVP. Eventually, like all things, you get used to it and I noticed that I seem to escape more shots from other players and players miss more of their first shots than they did in A2. Is this a new population getting used to the game? Maybe, but it seems like ranging is more important in A3 than it was in Arma 2. I can't be sure but it seems like the distance in A3 is less....forgiving. Once you master it though, firing Arma 3's weapons is more gratifying than in A2. The weapons sound amazing. Fire off an M320 at someone from 1000+ meters and enjoy the feeling that only Arma seems to give.
VEHICLES/AIRCRAFT
One of the first things you'll notice is that ground vehicles don't excatly handle like they did in A2. Be prepared to slow down! Driving some of the vehicles at high speed is akin to steering a cinder block on ice. I still am not a fan of the vehicle handling, but I do like the physics of the cars' shock absorption when getting air or going over bumps. Cars seem to flip more easily than in A2.
One of my favorite things about A3 is the option to turn on advanced flying. This allows you to operate an aircraft more realistically. With this option turned on (game settings I think) you'll get to regulate the power output of your heli, for example. No longer can you descend so fast without concern and then slam on the power at the last second. You'll have to regulate it downward. But, again, this is optional. Again, the sounds are amazing here as well.
LIGHTING
Wow, the lighting is the first thing I knew I loved about A3. The new Tanoa map, being released any minute now through the Apex DLC shows off the lighting really well. A lone lamp post in the jungle that you can actually see from far distances makes A3 maps feel real and alive. The sky lighting can seem a bit bright at first I think, but with some adjustment, it's amazing. Vehicle headlights also look incredible at night and flashlight attachments on your weapons work well to enhance that "oh man, who's watching me right now" feeling.
MAPS
This is where I'm not a fan of A3. I understand the arid setting and what it offers to large scale battles, but it's hard on the eyes. Luckily, modders have brought beloved maps like Chernarus, Lingor, Namalsk, Panthera, and Napf to A3. Today, as previously mentioned, the new Tanoa map drops in the Apex DLC and it's an incredible map. Probably the best map BI has ever released. I fully expect it to become the most popular map for mods like Exile and Epoch. Attention to detail is everywhere. Get lost in the jungles or island hop. I expect gun boats to finally get some love from players on this map.
AI
Ai is much better in my opinion. It's an impossible line to tiptoe, the balance between being a challenge but not too much of a challenge as to be insurmountable. AI in A3 feels like it walks that line much better than A2. Of course, this will probably vary from server to server too much to really say the AI is well-balanced.
BUILDINGS
For those Exile, Epoch, and DayZ-clone mods, you'll be happy to know that A3 maps like Altis have many, many buildings to enter. Nearly all of the buildings in the game are enterable. Loot yourself silly.
SUMMARY
If you look at the server count, the Arma community has clearly moved to A3. And I think this game has earned the bulk of the community. If you played a lot of A2 you might have some difficulty with gunplay at first, but give it time and learn to go prone and deploy your bipod and wait for the right shot. You can deploy your bipod on most surfaces that are at chest level whether standing or kneeling. Get used to using it, it will make all the difference. With Tanoa coming out today, I definitely recommend popping the cash for it and Arma 3.

During the summer of 1983, in a quiet town near Minneapolis, Minnesota, the charred body of a woman was found inside the kitchen stove of a small farmhouse. A video camera was also found in the kitchen, standing on a tripod and pointing at the oven. No tape was found inside the camera at the time.
Although the scene was originally labeled as a homicide by police, an unmarked VHS tape was later discovered at the bottom of the farm's well (which had apparently dried up earlier that year).
Despite its worn condition, and the fact that it contained no audio, police were still able to view the contents of the tape. It depicted a woman recording herself in front of a video camera (seemingly using the same camera the police found in the kitchen). After positioning the camera to include both her and her kitchen stove in the image, the tape then showed her turning on the oven, opening the door, crawling inside, and then closing the door behind her. Eight minutes into the video, the oven could be seen shaking violently, after which point thick black smoke could be seen emanating from it. For the remaining 45 minutes of video, until the batteries in the camera died, it remained in its stationary position.
To avoid disturbing the local community, police never released any information about the tape, or even the fact that it was found. Police were also not able to determine who put the tape in the well, or why the height and stature of the woman in the video didn't come close to matching the body they'd found in the oven.

Having played a lot of Arma 2, I had trouble making my inevitable move to Arma 3. With the tide of players moving to BI's newest version of my favorite game, I couldn't hold out for too long. Perhaps it was the many, many memories I have playing Arma 2 with friends that held me back. I wondered if Arma 3 would provide the same experience.
This review is meant to offer some insight to players still waiting to make the move from A2 to A3. I won't cover much about graphics as the difference is obvious there. Clearly, A3 looks better.
GUNPLAY
This was one of my most important factors in deciding whether or not I would like A3. At first, I hated the gun sway and the seemingly complex stance system and figured it would simply detract from all the fun I could have in PVP. Eventually, like all things, you get used to it and I noticed that I seem to escape more shots from other players and players miss more of their first shots than they did in A2. Is this a new population getting used to the game? Maybe, but it seems like ranging is more important in A3 than it was in Arma 2. I can't be sure but it seems like the distance in A3 is less....forgiving. Once you master it though, firing Arma 3's weapons is more gratifying than in A2. The weapons sound amazing. Fire off an M320 at someone from 1000+ meters and enjoy the feeling that only Arma seems to give.
VEHICLES/AIRCRAFT
One of the first things you'll notice is that ground vehicles don't excatly handle like they did in A2. Be prepared to slow down! Driving some of the vehicles at high speed is akin to steering a cinder block on ice. I still am not a fan of the vehicle handling, but I do like the physics of the cars' shock absorption when getting air or going over bumps. Cars seem to flip more easily than in A2.
One of my favorite things about A3 is the option to turn on advanced flying. This allows you to operate an aircraft more realistically. With this option turned on (game settings I think) you'll get to regulate the power output of your heli, for example. No longer can you descend so fast without concern and then slam on the power at the last second. You'll have to regulate it downward. But, again, this is optional. Again, the sounds are amazing here as well.
LIGHTING
Wow, the lighting is the first thing I knew I loved about A3. The new Tanoa map, being released any minute now through the Apex DLC shows off the lighting really well. A lone lamp post in the jungle that you can actually see from far distances makes A3 maps feel real and alive. The sky lighting can seem a bit bright at first I think, but with some adjustment, it's amazing. Vehicle headlights also look incredible at night and flashlight attachments on your weapons work well to enhance that "oh man, who's watching me right now" feeling.
MAPS
This is where I'm not a fan of A3. I understand the arid setting and what it offers to large scale battles, but it's hard on the eyes. Luckily, modders have brought beloved maps like Chernarus, Lingor, Namalsk, Panthera, and Napf to A3. Today, as previously mentioned, the new Tanoa map drops in the Apex DLC and it's an incredible map. Probably the best map BI has ever released. I fully expect it to become the most popular map for mods like Exile and Epoch. Attention to detail is everywhere. Get lost in the jungles or island hop. I expect gun boats to finally get some love from players on this map.
AI
Ai is much better in my opinion. It's an impossible line to tiptoe, the balance between being a challenge but not too much of a challenge as to be insurmountable. AI in A3 feels like it walks that line much better than A2. Of course, this will probably vary from server to server too much to really say the AI is well-balanced.
BUILDINGS
For those Exile, Epoch, and DayZ-clone mods, you'll be happy to know that A3 maps like Altis have many, many buildings to enter. Nearly all of the buildings in the game are enterable. Loot yourself silly.
SUMMARY
If you look at the server count, the Arma community has clearly moved to A3. And I think this game has earned the bulk of the community. If you played a lot of A2 you might have some difficulty with gunplay at first, but give it time and learn to go prone and deploy your bipod and wait for the right shot. You can deploy your bipod on most surfaces that are at chest level whether standing or kneeling. Get used to using it, it will make all the difference. With Tanoa coming out today, I definitely recommend popping the cash for it and Arma 3.

Bohemia Interactive Fans have been waiting 4 years for the next instalment of their most favourite PC open world military tactical Shooter franchise, Arma 3. Tacking place on the Aegean islands of Altis and Stratis of Greece with both Islands featuring the largess terrain of 290 km2 for any Arma game, Arma has never been so open world before. The islands features over 50 renamed villages with buildings that are both penetrable and destructible. The islands also include all sorts of kinds of wild life ranging from goats to grass snakes, bunnies to butterflies and even sharks and sea turtles in the surrounding waters. The republic of Altis and Stratis is populated by 5 unique factions that includes NATO and CSAT alongside the local AAF, FAIA gorillas and the civilian population. Each faction has their own motives, characteristics, vehicles and weapons.
Arma 3 contains over 20 Vehicles including tanks, cars, helicopters, aircraft and quads that can be driven by players in the game. Plus, there is a selection of over 40 weapons to choose from that can be customised with their own types of scopes and other various types of attachments. Each type of weapons has its own handling, sway and recoil meaning that a Sub Machine gun is much easy to handle at close range then a sniper rifle. Arma 3 is so tactical, it features 15 types of stances that can be very useful in exposing the least amount of your body to the enemy. Although, Arma 3 has realistic ballistic penetration physics depending on weapon type, attachments, material, calibre and distance meaning that hiding behind a wooden fence or plaster wall may not really be a suitable type of cover. In Arma 3 you will have to be careful about how much weight you’re caring which can have effect on stamina. Arma 3 features a realistic night sky which can be useful when you are lost on Altis without a compass as the stars can be used to navigate. There is reasons why so many military veterans are into the Arma franchise.
If you’re a new player to Arma 3 and are intimidated by the large amount of complexity to such a realistic open world military tactical Shooter then you can start off with boot camp. Recently introduced in a free update it offers up a single payer tutorial campaign and virtual reality training topics.
Arma 3's multiplayer is where the game really shines. Servers can have up to 100 players in all out warfare. Other than the vanilla game modes there is a bunch of community made game modes including the very popular DayZ zombie survival game mode. Arma 3 comes with a free DLC called Zeus which can be used create multiplayer scenarios from a birds eye view perspective. Arma 3 content creators also can easily create and save multilayer scenarios by using the in game scenario editor in a matter of minutes. Arma 3 content can be shared and downloaded over the steam workshop with over 10,000 scenarios and addons that have been published and is growing each day. There have been Arma 3 content creation contests with prizes veering from €20,000 to €200,000.
Arma 3's new graphic engine unleashes the full potential of PC gaming. Fans will notice that the new real virtuality 4 engine Is great improvement over Arma 2's engine implementing all sorts of new changes with significant improvements to animations and sounds, combined with the introduction of Microsoft directx 11 and Nvdia physX™, the battlefields of Arma have never felt more real. However Despite being the 4th version of the real virtuality engine it’s still heavily based on the decade old Bohemia Interactive real virtuality game engine that is known for its poor optimisation leading to poor performance making it very demanding on PC hardware, epically when there are allot of AI’s.
Arma 3 Averages reviews of 9/10 (55,000 being positive and only 6,000 negative) on steam. You can download the game now at a standard selling price of $39.99 USD off steam. Although, a steam sale would put a huge discount on the standard sale price if you choose to wait for one. I would recommend getting the Apex Edition as it’s come with all the DLC’s and the just recently released Apex expansion which is currently 20% of. With the game being constantly updated and having constant flow of community made content, the game is a must buy for any PC gamer. As expected for any Arma game it requires a very beathy gaming PC with both a powerful Graphics Card and processor so we recommend that you make sure that your system is well over the games system requirements before you make your purchase. A PC with an Intel core i7 processor and a strong graphic card along the lines of an Nvdia GTX 970 or AMD r9 390 would be an ideal system for Arma 3. Installing Arma 3 on an SSD would also lead to much faster loading times.

The crazy world and mayhem you can deliver onto the world isnt hugely different, but the way it is presented is.

Even though I'm dying to say "I HATE THIS GAME!" I can't.
I like sandbox 3rd person games like this. But let me tell you right now, right off the bat, if you get any kind of special edition that includes DLC, it's going to throw EVERYTHING about the campaign TOTALLY out of whack to the point that just to go to the corner store to buy your first pair of shoes and a pack of gum you're going to need airstrikes, a tank platoon, body armor, health upgrades, and whatever other ridiculousness the DLCs add to the game IMMEDIATELY and without option.
So, the DLCs are for people with no attention span, or who have finished the game already and want some extra playtime out of their purchase. That's fine by me, but I totally screwed myself over when I tried to get a "good deal" and get the DLC bundled when I bought SR3. Huge mistake.
So, the DLC FUBAR situation aside. The graphics, music, storyline, gameplay (with a few pitfalls), and world are all pretty good in SR3. And for its time, I would've said incredibly good!
I can probably sum up the entire rest of my review by explaining one thing... This game is totally up my 13 year old sons alley.
Cheats galore way too early in the game (or forced upon dlc owners from the beginning), so many things easily unlocked that you can practically be a one-man-army whenever you want, no real effort required to see the "end-game" content. It's kind of like...gary's mod met creative mode, met GTA4. *sigh* And twenty minutes later my son would lose interest because he had by then seen all of the unlocks and would forever only play the game when he was bored and wanted to mindlessly destroy things or play in traffic (one of the mini-games believe it or not.)
I tried removing / unequipping all the stuff that was ruining the difficulty and actual progression of the game. But it was such a huge pain and a frustration beyond words. If you're a mature gamer, you're much better off with a GTA title. If you just want something to fumble around with when you're bored, okay, I guess you could do worse than SR3.
But, I tried to warn you.

One of the most enjoyable games I have played, keeps you in for many hours of fun. This game is action packed with a mixture of crude humor and pure random fun. The storyline gets you hooked on and at many points keeps you on your toes. I really liked how at some main points of the story during the missions, they would have you choose an option that changes the result of the mission. The only downside to this, though, is that you aren't able to go back and replay the mission to choose the other option to see what happens (that is without downloading a mod for replays). What made the game really enjoyable is that it is so random with people in mascot suits, ridiculous weapons (e.g. some are from DLC: octopi-mind-controlling gun, spontaneous-shark-devouring gun, giant-purple-man-part bat, and that's only to name a few!), lots of customization for your character or car, and of course, gun upgrades. Who does not like gun upgrades?? There is plenty to do in-game and playing co-op with another friend makes the experience even more amusing. This game will last you quite a while before you really feel finished with it. The graphics to the game are great, the characters are slightly on the cartoony side than realistic which matches great with the not so serious atmosphere of the game. Overall, this game is worth the purchase (especially during Steam sales, you get more than what you pay for!), it has an all around good feel to it, jam packed with things to do/customization, I almost forgot to mention the great music (really good music), is very humorous that will keep you laughing through the story, and just downright fun. Volition did a great job on this game.

The game sports a lot of replayability.
While it's singleplayer can feel somewhat lacking, where it shines is in the multiplayer. There are a wide variety of servers, all with different rules (specifically like gamemode, loadouts, and such) and a wide variety of players to play with. The official servers appear to be held in a place that has extremely high ping, whereas I live in California and the West Coast server still sports the same ping as the European one, the ping does not actually affect the gameplay much if at all. While the AI will shoot you through grass that it should reasonably not have been able to see you through, and such, the players are a massively different story, and are where the game shines. You will find beginners and masters, with players hotdropping in and out of the modes, you in theory have a near limitless pool of players to enjoy the game with.
The game is challenging, and does require a bit of time to learn how to play. But, once you get it down you can easily begin mastering certain mechanics. Your decision making, as well as your ability to properly aim, will improve the more you play. This game rewards smart decision making over definitive skill. For example, picking to be camoed as the grass, and wearing grass on your body (via some equipment options) you can hide in the brush where you won't be seen, and smartly ambush your opponents. Using smoke grenades, or explosive ones, to distract or destroy your opponents, and choosing to reveal yourself at the last minute.
While this may not be Call of Duty or Battlefield, it still sports impressive vehicle controls, that appear to be mainly defined by realistic physics, and the infantry controls, while taking time to learn, allow you to accurately play at the most optimal level if you know how to. Knowing which cover to take, how to take cover, which stance to take for that scenario, and what kind of gun you should bring is something you learn to use over time. You need to smartly learn how to use lean to quickly poke out to take down a target, before withdrawing back behind cover, or risk an enemy sharpshooter taking you out. One player can decide the fate of the entire match by going rambo, knowing where and when to ambush, where to set up explosive anti-vehicle mines, and setting up the perfect chokepoints.
I would suggest most players that are new to the game start with the veteran mode on the official server, while it may be harder than the other modes, the fact of the matter is that it will teach you to become better much faster than you would otherwise. Learning to rely on first person mode, not having the benefits of third person mode that is, will make you much smarter about movement, and allow you to be more conscious of the environment. The veteran mode will also be far more challenging than the regular modes, limiting your hud, requiring you to both visually and mentally time your decisions so that your shooting is always optimal (fatigue, which happens when you carry a lot, run a lot, don't rest, or get shot reduces your aim because your character begins breathing hard/panicking). While this may not seem like fun at first, the first 10 hours are the roughest.
And lastly, while also being most important, make sure to play with friends. This will greatly enhance your experience, and you can teach eachother things you learned, possibly halving your required learning time. All in all, the game sports a lot of replayability due to the wide variety of servers, the variety in game modes and maps (sections of the main map cut into smaller pieces, to not be completley insane), and the wide variety of equipment, ranging from weapons, vehicles, explosives, and aircraft, will leave you with a lot to do, and a lot of fun to be had!

TL;DR - PlayerUnknown's BattleGrounds is a much better game. The game is not refined and has a lot of BS which I personally do not like. Weak 2/10.
At the time of release, H1Z1 was a good game, and appeared to be gaining popularity dangerously fast. The game is still in early access 2.5ish years after it's release. Why? As the WarOwl said, Early Access is a way for companies to get your money without delivering an optimised and refined game - this is what H1 has done.
H1Z1 has many things I don't like about it:
1) The parachute mechanics are beyond f_ucking stupid in the game - if you hit A or D, you will fly at a rapid velocity off to that side. I'm no expert, but this is not how parachutes work.
2) The fact you can bleed. This is a horrible decision for many reasons. Now you can tell me it was for realism all day however see the thing above and try tell me this again. If you land on the floor after dropping, you get hit by a pistol, you can win the fight and subsequently bleed out - this is not fun.
3) The way you drop in. H1Z1 randomly spawns you somewhere on the map. Your spawn can f_uck you over and depending on where you start off, you can be dead from the start.
4) Jumping from vehicles. Picture this, the green gas is hot on your trail, you are speeding as fast as you can in your car to escape the gas. You reach the safezone and head toward a house. Now, for some reason you don't break. Instead you just jump out. In real life, you would be a mess, and a very flat one at that. In H1Z1, nothing happens. You walk away no damage taken. Again, tell me that the bleeding mechanic is for realism while you jump from a car doing 100KM/H and take no damage, never mind survive.
In truth, the idea was great, and the future of the game looked secure and promising while PlayerUnknown himself worked with the H1Z1 team, but then he left to make his own game, and since then it has all been f_ucked really!

I remember seeing screenshots of Arma 1 and thinking "Wow, this game must keep me entertained for months", but after obtaining it I quickly changed my mind and thought what a buggy piece of crap this is, me being a somewhat casual gamer back then. The game was a total disaster to me and made me think "How could they even call this a game?" The best part were the voice commands. Move. To. That. Building. At.. SIX O'CLOCK! Not to mention the game ran like crap. (Only arma players know what crap means.)
(This was obviously ~6 years ago, so I was a bit younger then aswell)
Well, I had a friend in xFire who I shared a similar fate with,  but for some reason we decided to try it out together anyway. What we did was the sample Seize the area -mission that you can automatically create from the editor. Suddenly the game wasn't so bad after all. Everything that it lacked in the usual things you have in FPS games it gained back in gameplay and the complexity of the game. Suddenly the trademark buggyness and clumsyness of the engine (which is still present) was a feature instead of a problem. We played it for about 60 hours straight after that, downloading mods, missions and whatnot.
Then came Arma 2. Being a moneyless kid I was, I couldn't buy it. So we tried different cracks, playing through hamachi LAN with the same CD-Key and whatnot, but got beaten by the anti-crack software it had built in. Now you might think that's cause of our amateurism, but really it was cause nobody played the game back then and nobody could create working cracks. Literally, there was maybe 1000 players around the world who had bought the game.
Eventually I managed to buy the game and spent countless hours on it until it was time to put it on the shelf.
And then, maybe two years later, came DayZ and probably a million more players cause of it.
Suddenly there were keygens, cracks.. - whatever you needed to bypass the protection. Also, the mainstream gamer had found out what kind of possibilites the Arma engine can provide (dayz being the example). This was something the game developers deserved for putting so much effort to the series.
And now, cause of this success, Arma 3 is here. It's basically Arma 1 and 2 with a bigger budget. I wouldn't have ever thought during my Arma 1 days that it would ever get this popular.
What Arma 3 features:
- Excellent graphics
- The most realistic military simulation there is
- Huge map
- Good modability: This has always been a strong point in the series, just check Armaholic and steam workshop and you'll find all sorts of things for your liking.
- Possibility to design scenarios with endless different ways: Want a mission where you have to sneak through enemy lines and assasinate an officer? You got it.
- Excellent co-op gameplay.
- Trademark clumsyness to a lot of things, which will become a feature once you get used to it.
But.. if you're a codfag; you need to give the game some time. It's not your usual casual FPS where everything is scripted and whatnot. And get someone to play with.

ArmA 3.. Been with you since Alpha and now Apex is coming. It's a great game, really isn't much more to say. If you want a challenging, time consuming and at the same time fun tactical shooter, this is the game for you. If you expect CoD or BF, go away, right now.
Pros:
- Great mechanics
- Huuuge detailed maps with so many towns, cities and etc
- Enjoyable vehicular combat and mechanics
- Great (but cliche) single player campaign for a first person shooter
- Fun multiplayer with unlimited gamemodes to download as mods
- Eden Editor makes it fun to set up your own missions for training/fun
- Great modding community
Cons:
- The engine should be replaced for the next title, very unoptimized with huge frame drops even on good PCs.
- The action menu needs to go, seriously.
- A bit of a pain to set up a joystick for fixed-wings/helicopters
- Rain/storms could still look better, happens you see patches of blue sky right above your head
For any tactical shooter fan out there, this is a must have. But try to go into the game without comparing it to other FPS games. Just because it can be hard and has complex mechanics, doesn't mean the game sucks

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

ARMA 3 is a very unique game. I've been playing since the beta of Operation Flashpoint (the original). I have nothing but good things to say. This game is an amazing tactical infantry simulator. It does lack in the quality of planes, as they are simulated a little more on the arcade side rather than realism; don't expect DCS style flying. Helicopters are alright, but lacking some versatility. Overall as far as air flight is concerned it’s not bad at all, the feeling of being inside a chopper and seeing your fellow soldiers mount in is great. In regards to maps, there is a HUGE land mass to play on, you can also download extra maps. Making your own missions is very easy, you can setup some great CO-OP scenarios against the NPC or other players. The game features the ability to mount mods, there is a great variety, from Exile, to Altis Life, there is allot of options outside of original ARMA and its set gameplay. Multiplayer servers are generally very full, and there are allot of different types of maps and styles to choose from. If you want a very detailed and solid purchase game then this is a great buy. Infantry styled game play is really realistic, great scopes, range of guns (especially with APEX), and you feel like an actual soldier going into battle.
The only down sides that I see are to do with the mechanics of the engine. Like I mentioned before, I would've liked better airplane mechanics and physics, same with helicopters. The engine itself isn't ultra-fluent, it's very "sim like", so don’t expect “Call of Duty” styled gameplay. The controls are detailed but once you set them up, it makes for great gaming. Lastly to any other old ARMA fans, ARMA 2 has a huge amount of assets, ARMA 3 is lacking in that department quite significantly. The futuristic take on warfare might not be to everyone’s taste (it certainly didn’t sit well with me).
Overall, I would recommend this game, it's expensive, maybe get it on sale, but well worth it.

-This is a fun game. Its good. But there are a few things to consider before purchasing.
-First Off, This game runs like♥♥♥♥♥ The Reccomnded specs are a straight up lie.
-Even if you can run this game in singleplayer with a modest PC, Your going to need a monster to play MP.
-With a AMD FX-8350 and GTX 970 the MP was unplayable, the SP worked fine however.
-Arma 3 simply doesnt like AMD Cpu's, SO if you have a AMD cpu, i would recommend you stay away and maybe try on a free weekend.
-When i upgraded to a 6700k The game went from an average of 18 fps in MP to 90fps in MP.
-Another major problem i have with this game is it is set in the futrure(Like all shooters these days).
-This means there is a significant lack of iconic weapons and vehicles.(No M4's, M1 Abrams, AWP, M-24)
-Just a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ futuristic knokoffs of them.
-Another thing this game did wrong is the maps. They Suck. Empty deserts dotted with a few trees and rocks, and the cities are just the same copy and pasted buildings. Howerven the new map included in the apex DLC seems to be a good map.
-However that brings me to my last point. This games ♥♥♥♥ing DLC.
-To get the guns that somewhat resemble the iconic arms of past games you have to buy the marksman pack. You cant even pick them off a dead body till you buy them, WTF!
-Also the chopper DLC only has 2 choppers, And you cant fly them without purchasing the DLC.
-These guns and choppers should have been in from the start or in free updates.
-The new Apex DLC map looks good and is fun to play, no more vast endless deserts. But we have to pay to get the decent maps which is BS.(Also some more iconic arms in Apex, AK, RPG, Chinese Rifles)
All in all, This game is a lot of fun, there just have been alot of bad design decsions. And Before you buy you should consider that the game may not run well on many PC's and that alot of the best content is locked behind paywalls. I really wish they had set this game in the modern day instead of the future, I think The game would be better that way.

Let me give you some background with me
I first learned of Bohemia Interactive after playing Operation Flashpoint Dragon Rising and Red River.  This was on xbox 360.  I enjoyed the game.  Then I migrated to PC as my primary gaming system.  I loved the realism and strategy in those games as a 13 year old kid.  Then I found the Flashpoint games were canned for ARMA III.  So I decided to buy it about last year.
So after 65 hours spread across a year.  (I played in Chunks ex. I would play 8 hours one weekend then come back another 2 weeks later.)  I can say I have been pretending I have been having fun with this game.  I have seen all it has to offer.  The mods, the alternate game modes and things like that.  The Mil Sims games.  It sounds like alot untill you actually realize what the average player is going to do in this game.  You are going to spawn in and either select and customize your class and go or have fixed classes.  Once you spawn in, you head to the choppers.  You get dropped off and run...For several minutes at a time.  Untill you get to a elevated position and just look for bad guys in the area.  You hear a crack in the air and shots are being fired.  You look for where they are coming from and you cant see them.  So you just shoot in their direction.  Sometimes you do see the enemy, and then they die quickly because chances are if you see them, so does the rest of your team.  Thats really all this game is.   Just rinse and repeat that and thats all the Multiplayer is.  Even the Mil Sims.  All it takes is one youtube video to find out that you mostly walk. The problem with the walking isnt that its tedious.  its BORING.  There is no danger because the scenario most likely does not have enemies dug in protecting flanks or important roads.  For all the hype this game has around it, I just cant help to think most people pretend to have fun with it.  Everyone says they are having fun but what about it is fun?  The endless walking only to die from an enemy you dont see?  The boring combat where most of the time you dont even see what you are shooting at?  The game is indeed slow paced and some people like that, I love slow paced games.  But when the slow pace is 75% getting to where your going only to have a 3 minute firefight it just isnt worth it to me.  This game has everything to be fun and it is at very rare times, but the slow pace mixed in with the Optimization that turns any computer into a toaster thats trying to run Star Citizen, it just makes for a frustrating overall experience.  I have recently purchased Squad.  I bought it because I liked the unique realism to ARMA, but I didnt want to keep playing a game that just isnt fun.  Squad takes more Aracdey traits and fuses them with Arma.  The reason I liked Squad better is because it implements the things in Arma better for the average gamer like myself.  You still have to walk alot in Squad, but there is always a chance of being spotted and engaged while running to an objective.  For me atleast I needed to stop pretending to have fun with this game and have fun elsewhere.
TL:DR
I pretended to have fun with this game.  It got boring once you realized how repititve everything is.
