I really like battle royale style games, although they do have some flaws. King of the kill on the other hand has one enormous flaw which makes it impossible for me to enjoy. They can try all they want to balance all of the guns, vehicles,etc, but the spawning system in this game is ♥♥♥♥ing atrocious and a disgrace for any game that wants to be competitive. Do you have fast internet and a SSD/fast computer to install this game? If not then by the time you reach the ground others will have already got there and looted everything, you'll probably get killed on an instant. Not only that, you spawn at a random place. Compare this to PUBG where everyone spawns onto a plane, gives everyone appropriate loading time, and then let's you pick where to land. After I saw that, I checked if king of the kill fixed the god awful spawning, saw they didn't so I bought PUBG and uninstalled this garbage.
If it wasn't for the atrocious spawning would I recommend this? No, last time I played the hit registration was also luke warm garbage. I have 1000 hours in CSGO. I have probably 100 in overwatch. My aim is pretty decent, but in this game you can be aiming right at the enemy, standing still, and miss every single shot while you get killed. If the enemy is lagging might as well just quit the game, you won't hit them. Imagine running around for 20 minutes finding guns just to be killed by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t like that.
That's the general issue with these battle royale games, there's a ton of time just running around. In PUBG, most of my deaths feel fair. In this game, very little feel free. I play with around 70 ping on both. I could just be bad, but this is why I don't recommend it. I had this since it was known as just h1z1, so I have more hours than what it says.

This game always amazes me , how not to develope a game. I mean it does have a few pros, but most of the time it just the worst multiplayer game out there.
Let's start things at the begining. You queue up to play a game. Finally, there's enough people to start the match. The match starts. Now this part just blew my mind.... At the start of the match people are NOT equally start! It really depends on your computer. If you play on a toaster, good luck getting gear. By the time you land, there are tons of people who are loaded in and landed already before you. I mean is it really that hard to develope a system like other games did that wait for everybody to equally load in? Other thing is the hitreg. It's a mess...I lost count on how much time i did 99 damage. Shotty does 10 damage to the head (Yes with helmet, but seriously?? 10dmg? close range?)
Then there's the wobbly movement. While in a fight you can just A-D-A-D, crouch x 10, jump a few times and get away easily.
So, there's this new thing where you can just join in. Shoot people. Have fun (?). Try out weapons,settings etc etc. But, oh boy.... Once again. If your pc isn't fast enough you're going to respawn bleeding, sometimes without helmet.( Simple solution would be to not remove the respawn shield while you are not touching anything) Other than that. The place is small, chaotic, messy, which is okay. Item spawns could be less. Able to choose your "loadout" would be fun. ( Im not into this SMG-SHOTTY-RNG thing).
The game is a mess. DM is kinda fun, but most of the times reminds you how bad the mechanics are.
Don't waste your money on this game. If a friend of yours said to buy it, delete him/her from your friendlist (jk).

This game always amazes me , how not to develope a game. I mean it does have a few pros, but most of the time it just the worst multiplayer game out there.
Let's start things at the begining. You queue up to play a game. Finally, there's enough people to start the match. The match starts. Now this part just blew my mind.... At the start of the match people are NOT equally start! It really depends on your computer. If you play on a toaster, good luck getting gear. I mean is it really that hard to develope a system like other games did that wait for everybody to equally load in? Other thing is the hitreg. So, there's this new thing where you can just join in. Shoot people. Have fun (?). Try out weapons,settings etc etc. But, oh boy.... Once again. Let me give you some background with me
I first learned of Bohemia Interactive after playing Operation Flashpoint Dragon Rising and Red River.  This was on xbox 360.  I enjoyed the game.  Then I migrated to PC as my primary gaming system.  I loved the realism and strategy in those games as a 13 year old kid.  Then I found the Flashpoint games were canned for ARMA III.  So I decided to buy it about last year.
So after 65 hours spread across a year.  (I played in Chunks ex. I would play 8 hours one weekend then come back another 2 weeks later.)  I can say I have been pretending I have been having fun with this game.  I have seen all it has to offer.  The mods, the alternate game modes and things like that.  The Mil Sims games.  It sounds like alot untill you actually realize what the average player is going to do in this game.  You are going to spawn in and either select and customize your class and go or have fixed classes.  Once you spawn in, you head to the choppers.  You get dropped off and run...For several minutes at a time.  Untill you get to a elevated position and just look for bad guys in the area.  You hear a crack in the air and shots are being fired.  You look for where they are coming from and you cant see them.  So you just shoot in their direction.  Sometimes you do see the enemy, and then they die quickly because chances are if you see them, so does the rest of your team.  Thats really all this game is.   Just rinse and repeat that and thats all the Multiplayer is.  Even the Mil Sims.  All it takes is one youtube video to find out that you mostly walk. The problem with the walking isnt that its tedious.  its BORING.  There is no danger because the scenario most likely does not have enemies dug in protecting flanks or important roads.  For all the hype this game has around it, I just cant help to think most people pretend to have fun with it.  Everyone says they are having fun but what about it is fun?  The endless walking only to die from an enemy you dont see?  The boring combat where most of the time you dont even see what you are shooting at?  The game is indeed slow paced and some people like that, I love slow paced games.  But when the slow pace is 75% getting to where your going only to have a 3 minute firefight it just isnt worth it to me.  This game has everything to be fun and it is at very rare times, but the slow pace mixed in with the Optimization that turns any computer into a toaster thats trying to run Star Citizen, it just makes for a frustrating overall experience.  I have recently purchased Squad.  I bought it because I liked the unique realism to ARMA, but I didnt want to keep playing a game that just isnt fun.  Squad takes more Aracdey traits and fuses them with Arma.  The reason I liked Squad better is because it implements the things in Arma better for the average gamer like myself.  You still have to walk alot in Squad, but there is always a chance of being spotted and engaged while running to an objective.  For me atleast I needed to stop pretending to have fun with this game and have fun elsewhere.
TL:DR
I pretended to have fun with this game.  It got boring once you realized how repititve everything is.

I picked up Saints RowL The Third when I was looking for something to fill the void the lack of a PC release of GTA V caused. It seemed like it would be a fun GTA-clone. After 50+ hours of gameplay, I now could hardly care less about more Grand Theft Auto - I want more of the Saints!
If you've played a Grand Theft Auto game since GTA III, you'll find SR3 to be similar in a lot of ways. It is a huge open-world sandbox game. There are missions to complete which advance the storyline. There are cars to steal, cops to evade and stores to buy from (or rob). In that sense, it's a very similar game. Unlike GTA games, you can fully customize your character in SR3 - complete with full voice acting - you aren't stuck playing a character the developers created for you. Some of the missions and gameplay elements are completely over the top - one mission series had you trying to find and capture a Hulk-like clone of one of your homies, while a mini-game has you running and gunning your way through an obstacle course run by a homicidal Hello Kitty knock-off.
In most ways, I found SR3 to be better than any of the GTA games I've played. There are two ares where it falls short. The first is in the mission length - there are only about 20 or so storyline missions. There are a number of side missions and mini-games, but overall, it felt really short (like I said, it was still good for 50+ hours though). Another area where the game falls short of it's GTA bretheren is in the music. You have a number of radio stations to pick from, but there were only one or two that had music on them I could stand. It seemed like a lot of indie music - stuff they could get for lower royalties or for free. Mostly I played with the music off.
I liked SR3 so much that I rushed out and bought SR4 as soon as I finished this one. I didn't want to leave the world they'd created yet. Maybe even more telling is that I actually finished SR3, which nearly never happens these days. The gameplay may be a tad on the easy side, but after failing to finish GTA4's finale mission after dozens of attempts, I found that leaning towards being easy may be the more fun way to go. Off to play SR2 now... I love this world.

Arma 3 is a realistic military tactical shooter; if you are accustomed COD style run and gun then beware of massive amounts of frustration. Arma 3 features hands down the most accurate depiction of military warfare: from the insane detail to weapons, to the intricate depiction of vehicles, and even the movement and formation of military units. Coming from a gamer who has enjoyed countless hours of gameplay (albeit easy and unrealistic) in games like COD and BF, this was a welcome change into my gaming lineup. The wealth of options available to play like the mode 'scenario" where you can set different standards and choose your environment and setup to mimic your warfare dreams. The campaign, although lacking on a developed story, is pretty cut clean and to the point about a nation under attack while you are a fighting force trying to recapture it is different and also leaning towards simulation/realistic (don't expect COD style explosions or cutscenes). The game has it's mod support which can enhance the multiplayer aspect and also comes with different training methods to get you acclimated to the controls. Graphics are pretty demanding but I am running on Very High with an i5-4690K/GTX970 setup and hitting 60fps most of the time so take that as a reference. The content available is staggering and I will definitely continue to pour more hours into this game exploring the multiplayer aspect, the mods, and finishing up the campaign.

One of my good friends bought me this game as an early birthday present and I by far am having loads of fun by playing it. This game is beautiful and a joy to play. However there seems to be some major FPS drops on my current setup, which is higher than average. On ultra settings (in multiplayer) I get around 25-45 FPS, however when I hop into single player I average around 60 FPS on ultra settings, this has lead me to believe that this FPS drop is server side and cut the game a lot of slack due to that. However even on 30 FPS i am still able to play this game fine and have a blast with it! In my first day of playing I joined an RP server and went around town and was robbed and kidnapped in my first hour of playing. Now I must admit that while this may seem like a terrifying experience, I was laughing the entire time. There are an abundance of servers and different game modes to choose from so don't expect to get bored anytime soon! I mentioned single player earlier, and in my personal opinion this is probably the weakest part of the game, at least for me. It's very realistic and offers good gameplay but I often find myself getting very bored easily with the single player and can never have as much fun as I do with multiplayer. Overall this game is very fun and enjoyable, however with a few server optimization patches I feel that this could be one of the best military simulation shooters of all time!

This game is about two teams fighting against each other, (Red v.s. Blue) for control of the badlands. You play as one of the nine classes, each with their own customisable weapons, cosmetics, and taunts. You can play casual and just pick the maps and gamemodes you want, and quickly get in a game, try your luck in (the dead) competetive mode, or browse through custom servers. (Usually involving server plug-in's and custom files to download)
Pros:
FREE
Custom Gamemodes
Customisable Loadouts
Works on most computers very well
Recieves Updates and Balances
Steam Workshop Items
Neutral:
Micspamers, Squeakers, Screamers, Ragers, Etc.
Requires Premium Account for Cosmetics and Bigger Inventory
Bad:

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Over the top mayhem. This third-person action shooter is obviously a Grand Theft Auto (GTA) knock off. Whereas GTA games are notoriously difficult, this game (with the exception of a few missions) is an enjoyable, frustration free romp.
You play as the leader of the Saints, a criminal street game that in prior releases has managed to rise to celebrity status despite their brutal beginnings ... which continue into the present.
Mow down countless pedestrians with vehicles you've jacked from the citizenry. Engage in a myriad of extra-legal activities as you gain experience and level up your abilities ... eventually obtaining the equivalent of "god mode" and endless ammo.
Despite being a homocidal, ruthless killing machine, your character comes off as likable, tounge-in-check gang banger. You direct your avatar in a city-spanning mission to return the Saints to the former status and avenge the death of the prior leader.
If I had to choose between playing GTA IV and this, I'd pick Saints Row. If I'm going to a play a morally ambiguous (oh, who am I kidding, my SR3 character had no redeeming qualities save some wicked fashion sense), then I'd rather play through the comedic, hijinks of Saints Row, because at the end of the day, who doesn't want to run naked through the city.

Got: 800+ hrs in H1Z1 kotk and have played since very early beta. (and 100+ hr in PUBG)
First of I would say I played 90% of the time with friends and very much like this game and also pubg. As the two big BR games (at the moment) is kotk and pubg I will compare them. If you like BR games and have the time/money to play both games I would recommend to buy them both (get h1z1 on sale). If you dont have/want to I will describe the different play styles and leave it up to you too decided what is pros and cons.
H1Z1:
Fast past (You run faster then in pubg, get quicker in cars, easier to spot players, you can jump over stuff, faster reload, have the potential to have long battles, really funny car chases)
Arcade style
Stealth is not so imported in this game.
Close combat is kinda RNG with some few bugs that makes it even more RNG.
Few weapons
Random spawns but when you learn to control the parachute you can fly almost anywhere. The key here is timing (be the first to hit the ground for the sweet loot)
Daybreak is slow to fix bugs
PUBG:
Slower past then in h1z1 (Getting into cars can be a source for frustration, medium run speed, setting up an ambush is a variable strategy)
Stealth is king (If your in a town and someone spots u first then ur dead 9/10 times, u can pron in an open corn field/high grass and snipe people without beeing spotted. )
Many weapons and add ons to custimize your set up to your own personal playstyle.
You jump out of a airplane and can release your parachute when needed making basically the whole map available as a spawn
Development seems to go fast
TL:DR
H1Z1:  Casual fast past acarde shooter, alot of fun with friends.
PUBG: Stealth style medium past, alot of fun with friends and single player

Saints Row: The Third is a good game.  It is however a very different game than the previous installment in the franchise, which can make those looking for more of the material from Saints Row II disappointed by the experience The Third offers.
The key difference is one of tone.  The Third eschews the previous games reliance on black humor and a contrast between the brutality of the events on screen and the upbeat and matter of fact reactions of the characters.  Instead it re-imagines the Saints as pop icons, with their criminal acts inflated to such ludicrous proportions that they lose any sense of weight.
The diverse enemy factions with their separate, well developed leaders are replaced here by three equally colorful but frustratingly bland enemy factions with underwhelming development for the antagonist figures.
The game shines most when treated as nothing but a pure sandbox, when the story is ignored in favor of wandering the streets amusing yourself with the massive selection of toys the developers have provided.  However attempting to play through the story will quickly lead you to a succession of mandatory mini-games, most of them of little interest.  You accomplish little of any dramatic weight in the story missions, instead wandering through a parade of celebrity cameos and random asides that add little to the story.
There is fun to be had here, but it's all fluff.  Which should be kept in mind when considering my recommendation.

Over the past week or so, I got hooked on Saints Row 3. I have played it a little before I upgraded my PC quite a bit. I used to get a terrible frame rate (15-10 FPS) and wasn't into the game a bit. After upgrading my PC, I was able to maintain a steady 30-40 FPS on medium settings. I was hooked after I found that this game was amazing with a good frame rate. I first started going along my business, booting up cheats and getting as high of notority and fighting and fighting because it was fun to me. I eventually decided to start up the story mode again because I kinda left off of it ever since my computer had issues. I started getting more and more into it over the past week or so and finally finished the story today. I realized how much fun I had playing this game. The story was AMAZING, and I love how it had alternate endings (no spoilers for you!) and I just loved the story because it had memorable characters and very fun missions to play weather it be an assassination mission or just a protect your homie mission, I always seemed to have fun with it (except the ones where you are in a heli and protecting someone because I found it so much harder than the other missions). People seem to compare this game to GTA, which I can understand. I have played both games and to be honest I like Saints Row a tad bit better, because I felt that Saints Row was a lot more memorable and had a TON more customization options (outside of modding in GTA) with zombie modes, co-op and much much more. That's what I was going to talk about next; customization. This game is FULL of customization. Once you first start up the game, you will realize that you get your option to customize your character. That's normal, right? NO, not for this game. This game featured so many options that you could spend nearly a half an hour customizing your character with so many options to choose from. They also implemented the whole face construction feature where you could totally re-map your face or do what ever the hell you wanted with it. They also gave you the option to have a body builder sort of thing, where you could center your entire body around muscle, skinny, or fat. In the end, none of your customization choices mattered, weather you were a burly man, NOTHING changed your fate or how well you did in the game. They also gave you a set of choices for your character voice which I thought was amazing to put into a game. These customization options really did remind me of my childhood favourite game; Tony Hawk's skateboarding games. Especially in Tony Hawk's Underground 2 for the PS2. They had a lot of the same features they did in THUG2 that were implemented in SR3. I am definately looking at getting SR4 sometime soon (probably torrent *I STILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPERS*) I have never seen a game that made me laugh so hard at some points, and just overall had such an addictive gameplay (other than TF2). I have to give this game a 10/10. PLEASE BUY THIS GAME. Do it for the vine.

At first I raised an eyebrow..steal cars, gang fights, run over people...what! As an older player, I tend to have certain scruples and this game went against everything I would do in a game, deliberatley anyway. That said, I can tell you that I have had more damn outright FUN then any other game I have ever played. The storyline sucks you right in, and all the way through it is just outright addictive. Some of the antics that happen in game, especially when playing coop with a friend will leave you hurting from laughing! You can't take anything that happens in this game seriously..if it can go wrong...it will, with hilarious results. One of the best character creation generators I have seen, I wish other games would allow you to create a character like this game does. Wonderful animations, and facial expressions...and a rare game that you will get attached to your character.
The voice acting is top notch, and believable. Every character has a distinct personality. The world (or city) this game takes place in is spectacular, you can get lost in it, some of the best modeling I have seen. I did see some soft textures and wish this game had a hi-res texture pack, but visually awesome non the less. If you want pure fun and just forget the rules, this is the game you want. Caution, can be addictive...you will not get bored, tons of stuff to do and lots of laughing to be had.

This game is great. The mechanics, weapons, modes, are all awesome. My biggest issue is the optimization, which, depending on your personal preference, may render it unplayable. I'm running an AMD FX-8350 along with a GTX 970 with 4 GB of VRAM, and I can barely hold 30 frames in the multiplayer, even on low settings. For the most part it will run at about 25 FPS. In the single player I can usually get around 45 FPS or so, but not much more.
It really seems like they did not optimize the game what-so-ever. Personally, I don't mind the occassional frame drop, but it is certainly annoying seeing as how realistic the game is. My CPU and GPU should be more than enough to have this game completely maxed out at 60 FPS with no drops. Unfortunately though, they really didn't do anything with the game's optimization.
I still think it's fun, but if frame drops or a low frame rate bother you, I'd stay very far away. I imagine even on super high end hardware it would still have considerable issues.

Even though it might not be the best optimised game in the world, with modding possibilities gameplay is endless. If you don't even know how to code there are easy-ish to use modules so you can make something cool for you and your friends to mess around with. The game looks amazing and with almost no limitation on scale you can experiance some epic battles.
A lot of people give it hate for not running well but most don't realise the amount of detail in the game. Such as dynamic weather, volumetric coulds, advanced ballistics like if you get shot in the helmet it will help but getting shot in the face where the helmet doesn't cover then you're going to die. I also want to add that performance varies per server especially if you're playing on a server with mods or if the server has 100 players on it like King of the HIll. How many other games do you know of that can support 100 players on a server with as much detail as Arma 3 and not just visual detail with other detail I mentioned before like advanced ballistics and dynamic environment.
Just remember if you're getting Arma 3 to play on a modded life server or a popular 100 player server it might not run well because it's not the base game, it's custom content made by the community.

Gameplay:9/10
The gameplay is pretty much AWESOME. You must learn the recoil pattern and the aiming tricks which will be hard but after some hard work invested in this game you are going to love it. It has minor bugs but newer players will never ever notice and there is not variety of weapons, but that is not that big of a problem.

I sadly have to admit that the community of this game is not the best community in the world. There will be times that you will die and you will hear the enemy screaming in voice chat "YOU SUCK KID EZ PEZ GONNA FAP WITH THIS REPLAY'' and things like that. There are a lot of veteran players, a fact that makes the game really hard for the new players and that is the biggest problem of the game due to a lot of people getting bored of dying from VPP (Veteran Pro Players). I think that PUBG is superior to H1Z1 only because it has so many new players and therefore it is not hard to play and master some games. Yet there are a lot of friendly people in ''FIVES'' gamemode that will be really friendly and they will usually teach you some tricks of the game (most of these players will be VPP).
FPS-related stuff:10/10
I have to say that in this thing H1Z1 is BY FAR the best game to play if you have to choose between this and PUBG. H1Z1 is greatly optimized so you are going to easily run this in a low to average PC (6gb ram is the only necessary). Devs update it all the time and you are going to run this on your PC a lot better than PUBG. Only if you have a REAL BEAST pc I would recommend PUBG but is is still a waste of money and really overrated. In H1Z1 you are hardly ever gonna face FPS-drops.

Even though it might not be the best optimised game in the world, with modding possibilities gameplay is endless. If you don't even know how to code there are easy-ish to use modules so you can make something cool for you and your friends to mess around with. The game looks amazing and with almost no limitation on scale you can experiance some epic battles.
A lot of people give it hate for not running well but most don't realise the amount of detail in the game. Such as dynamic weather, volumetric coulds, advanced ballistics like if you get shot in the helmet it will help but getting shot in the face where the helmet doesn't cover then you're going to die. I also want to add that performance varies per server especially if you're playing on a server with mods or if the server has 100 players on it like King of the HIll. How many other games do you know of that can support 100 players on a server with as much detail as Arma 3 and not just visual detail with other detail I mentioned before like advanced ballistics and dynamic environment.
Just remember if you're getting Arma 3 to play on a modded life server or a popular 100 player server it might not run well because it's not the base game, it's custom content made by the community.

I remember when I first gave this game a go. You were thrown into a bank heist and I was like, "man a shooter? This is lame." I remember seeing images thinking this was a GTA knockoff. Either way, I was dead wrong on both accounts.
While it does resemble GTA, the story is anything but. Yeah you're a gansta. But you're waging a one man/woman war against some serious over-the-top craziness. Anything goes, from cyberspace to game shows to super powers. It is glorious! Heck, the second mission has you diving out of an airplane, shooting mooks as you swim through the air through an astounding amount of cargo and cars.
The game looks quite nice, as it's not that old. There's some great city views, and if I were to draw a cityscape, I'd probably use this game as a model.
I like that there's an Adult Swim radio station in the game. Nothing like listening to Venture Bros or Aquateen Hunger Force. And when that gets old, I switch to classical to listen to the William Tell Overture. Pretty awesome.
The homies you get are pretty cool. From the reluctant Pierce, to the aggressive Shaundi, the thoughtful Oleg, and the hackeriffic Kinzie. They're all great fun.
By far the best way to experience this game is with a buddy. It is a BLAST! Why bust some skulls by yourself when you can bring in another Saints leader for twice the firepower, the ability to talk to each other, and res each other indefinitely? It's awesome knowing you've got someone watching your back for that inevitable ambush. And watching the story together is great.
Overall this game is much cooler than I thought possible. This gets a rare, rockin' 10/10 from me.

What I like:
It is much more realistic than most other fps. You really have to think and move carefully before you take action.
The missions are also very nice and rather difficult. You cannot casually play this game without getting killed all the time.
Hitting a person is not as easy as in other games. You have got to aim carefully.
The graphics are also very good. It all seems very realistic.
What I don't like:
The ennemy AI seems to be working all right. Shame that you own team seems to consist of total morons who can't hit a barn and seem to expose themselves all the time.
What I absolutely hate about this game:
The user interface is the worst I have ever encountered. It is very complicated and it more or less completely spoils the fun. The user interface is fighting you all the way. It is totally counter-intuïtive. Nothing works as you would expect and in the middle of a fight you have more trouble using the interface than killing the enemy.
They couldn't have done a worse job if they intended to make the worst interface in the world.
It sucks big time, all the time and is spoiling the game.
Conclusion:
With a better AI (friends) and a far less complicated user interface, this could be one of the best fps ever.
But with this interface, it kind of sucks.

As someone who plays all multiplayer games with high ping, this game was absolutely destroyed in a recent update. When they added the region select menu they added a new feature the refuses to let you connect if you have too high of ping. A lot of people might not have noticed this because they're usually under 100 ping and would have never seen this appear for them but for me it was rather obvious. I start up the game, see the region select menu, select my region, and notice their wonderful message that says my ping is too high for me to connect and to try a different region. Unsurprisingly, all of the other regions have even higher pings and are, of course, unavailable. This leaves me in a situation where I'm unable to connect to any region because of my internet connection, my internet provider being the only one available in my area and therefore my only option. So thanks to the developers adding this, the game is now 100% unplayable for me (and I'm sure others) and my money is wasted.
Summary: The game won't let you past the first screen if you have higher than probably around 150 ms ping

This game ruined my life...
It started out as just a fun little casual relationship, y'know, just "oh i'll go on a multiplayer server and go play for a bit" sort of typical gamer-game relationship.
I saw there were no women wondering around... I wanted to fix it, y'know, quick fix, something to do, some options for people...
That was three years ago. now I can't even go to the ♥♥♥♥ing shop without wondering how I would bloody model it and put it into this godforsaken game! it has latched onto my life like a zombie baby and is sucking all of the energy clean out of me, I can't sit and have a good play session without noticing a bug in something and trying to fix it. I now instintively open max and model when I turn the PC on, and everything I model makes its way into the game somehow, I'm in a group of modders and I swear they are a cult worshipping the Arma franchise, I can't stop myself, it's literally an addiction... I need help.
Okay on the more serious side... this game is ♥♥♥♥ING AWESOME... if, IF you are that strange masochistic type of person who loves near simulation levels of combat realism and marching across huge maps.
I'm talking PURELY from the standpoint of an Arma 'purist' if you will, not a DayZ convert, not a lifer.
Okay so the biggest pro of this game by far is the modding capability and the community, as a member of the modding community I can say just how much you can customize this game and make it your own breed of wicked software.
every major aspect of the game can be changed and it's one of the biggest and best points of this game I can truly sing the praises of.
You can add new islands, new characters and character assets, new weapons, new vehicles, new missions, new game modes, new interface aspects, you can add true to life elements such as radio comms, and ballistics. All through addon content, trust me, if you're like me and you are a sucker for variety the storage space taken up by the mods is about 4 times as much as the actual game does.
The support Bohemia Interactive have for the modding community is fantastic, by far one of the most supportive developers of modders I know, providing a variety of tools and support to help you make addons, in fact in this most recent instalment they even take direct inspiration for extensions of the game from modders themselves, from interface elements like stamina indicators and Virtual Arsenal to actual designs of assets, such as the new ENVG in the APEX expansion.
The Arma modding community is bustling with friendly helpful people ready to help you get a leg up if you're struggling. and that's hosted by Bohemia interactive themselves, not a third party.
The DLC BI makes is very much an extra platform for mod makers as much as it is extra content for players, and they've made it so that these core engine features in the game are available to everyone, not just owners of the DLC, making it a much more fair and universal system.
Other pros:
The freedom you have within the game, it's not on rails and in corridors, it's a vast open environment, open world if you wanna call it that. if you wanna go halfway across the HUGE map to hit a target at the perfect angle you are free to do so.
If you wanna kill one guy with a helicopter, and there's a helicopter available, then hot damn you can do that.
if you wanna nuke the damn place, download a nuke mod/script and live out your sadistic fantasies of pressing that red button.
♥♥♥♥ i've found myself, before today, just putting a truck down in the editor and going for a drive around the island to kill some time rather than people, you can do that too, y'know, be a pacifist for the day.
You wanna roll in first person? done
you wanna roll in third person? done
you wanna look around with your head and not your entire body? done.
you wanna play as a guy with pink face paint? mod it, and done!
wanna attach a machine gun to a rabbit? with some jigging in the editor, consider it done!
Zeus lets you rationalise your god complex: and that is exactly why I love zeus game mode. someone in the server is♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off and i'm zeus they can see to it that they'll have a nice lightning bolt of 'shut the ♥♥♥♥ up'
you can place down cars, planes, entire hordes of enemy troops for four guys to fight, and laugh meniacally as you watch them squeal.
With recent updates, the visuals are now so much nicer, and things run a little smoother overall.
APEX itself is a pro, like seriously, just for Tanoa, just buy it already.
Cons:
Multiplayer sometimes isn't fantastic, since the advent of DayZ and Arma Life, 9 year olds have found another game to disgrace the presence of, not fun, not saying i dislike those platforms, just the kids who ruin the good experience for the rest of us, especially when our hard work in the modding community is used and abused without permission.
The game's performance isn't fantastic, BUT, BUT hear me out here, you can do A LOT about that the sheer number of options available to you ensure that in some degree you can get a good framerate. The sheer complexity of the engine means it needs quite a lot of CPU power, so bear that in mind. I've put my PC specs down at the bottom and I get fairly okay framerates on ultra high settings, you by no means need a £1000 PC for this game.
It has a few quirky bugs like the AI with Xray vision and dying if you're lying prone on a rock, i find the latter happens rarely these days.
It loads like a dead snail, it's my biggest gripe with the game, is how long it takes to load I HIGHLY recommend you install it to an SSD, it's much faster.
You will LITERALLY not see the light of day if you get into modding this thing, it takes away your life.
When you love this game like I do, you put its faults aside and just damn play it.

ARMA 3 is an open-world, tactical shooter video game developed by Czech studio Bohemia Interactive. ARMA 3 takes place on the Aegean islands of Altis (formerly Lemnos) and Stratis of Greece, in the Mediterranean Sea. The islands feature photo-realistic terrain and water environments. Altis is the largest official terrain in the Arma series with ground area covering approximately 270 km2. The smaller island, Stratis, expands over an area of 20 km2. The islands also feature over 50 villages with buildings that are both penetrable and destructible.
I knew what to expect when going into Arma III from previous experiences, yet I was still amazed by the amount of features the game have. Needless to say, patience is a necessary thing if you wish to enjoy the wonders of ARMA III. You must spend more time than you might expect tidying the menu settings to get the game to run at a decent frame rate in online sessions. I haven't lost intrest in the game after 1000+ hours. I have actually gained interest in the game, since you always have something to do.
· I would rate it a solid 10/10.

I came into this game without any prior experience to the previous titles, so for me going in with a fresh set of eyes I had no idea what to really expect other than through my experience with GTA.  I certainly played this game with the expectations that it will play like one and for the most part it offered enough twists and turns to differentiate itself from the competition.
If you played other current gen open world crime games you'll feel right at home with the controls and gameplay.  Everything from the item wheels, taking cars on the street, buying up property, and going from Point A to Point B objectives.
While this game pushes itself to further distance itself from the others of its genre through humorous story and character interactions, parts of the game will feel well-worn and something you've already threaded.  The only difference is you got orbital strike weapons and a gun that shoots sharks to deal with large groups of gangs to quickly do an objective, as opposed to having to mop up with standard firearms.
The story is really the high point of this game, characters are all well acted and some using some famous actors and actresses.  A stable of great characters with rich back-story round out the game, though at times you'll feel that the antagonists could use more details on theirs.
Overall, the game offers a decent challenge but if you're a master at sandbox crime games, you'll easily mow through the content even in higher difficulty.  What will really be the deciding factor to games like these is the replayability, with loads of side challenges and mini objectives it will add a few more hours to the core content.  The dlcs themselves are a mixed bag on the other-hand, going from mediocre with forgettable characters to an engaging one which really adds to the Saints Row universe.  I recommend only getting The Trouble with Clones and Genkibowl VII and skipping all the rest.
Your mileage will vary of course, but I think you'll certainly have your money's worth with this purchase.  You may not spend over 300+ hours like I did with mindlessly just trying to survive through max notoriety on both gangs and police or just replaying missions (not included with the game, you'll need a mod unfortunately to have mission replay) but it's more than holds it own against bigger studios with loftier budgets.

Runs below 30FPS even on when set to normal/low settings. AMD 8350, 16gb DDR3 RAM, Samsung SSD, EVGA 960GT video card. Tiny sections like the VR training can go up to 60fps but do the prologue training scenario it dips hard, even on lower settings. Depends where you are, some areas make it way worse. This game is not much more than Arma 2
All in all this is just an iteration ahead of Arma 2. Most of what you want gameplay-wise can be had in Arma 2. The improvements are all miniscule. The interface is a tiny bit more straight-forward. Controls are still crap all around, especially for driving. Many many other games do driving with keyboard and mouse better. Anyhow Arma 2 suffers from odd controls too.
Also wtf with people taking 1 whole second to register a shot. The prologue firefight and in VR training both you shoot someone, the bullet contacts, count it 1 second 1 mississippi.....and then the guy drops. This goes for leggers, arm shots, chest shots, and head shots. He is standing there, bullet hits....still standing there....and then his neck curves and he drops to the ground. It's like playing against someone in the Arctic over the internet. And that is singleplayer.
Summary
Arma 3 left a sour taste in my mouth. I read many complaints about optimization and they are true. I ignored them to my detriment. This game won't run even on an above-decent rig that can play anything else just fine. Not only does Arma 3 run slow it looks like a 10 year old game when you do get it to reach 30fps. I'd suggest waiting until the whole pack and all DLC go on sale under $20.

THIS IS MY OPINION. SORRY IF YOU DON'T AGREE.
ALSO PUBG HAS FIXED ALOT OF THINGS I'VE STATED.
REVIEW WAS POSTED JUNE 21st.
If you're stuck between PUBG and KOTK let me just break it down for you.
KOTK PROS -
•	Fast paced
•	Better audio all the way around (in my case at least)
•	Will run much better on most low end computers, don’t try to buy PUBG if you don’t have at least a decent computer
•	Nice art style
•	Consistent updates
•	Simple
•	Very entertaining with friends
•	Spawns are completely random
•	Good time-to-kill ratio with headshots (as in feels correct when shooting, I feel like I'm doing damage)
•	Car mechanics work fluidly in this game
•	Great skins
•	Ranking system is great
KOTK CONS –
•	Hit or miss when it comes to hit registering (better hope you’re lucky)
•	Shotgun is kind of broken and in an awkward slightly OP stage
•	A few very minor bugs
•	A 1 in every 500 chance you run into a hacker of some sorts, most are killable but some are top notch
•	Game ends in a few set areas so it gets old after a while but a new update will fix that
•	Not many different variants of guns (new one coming soon)
Overall I love KOTK and I personally prefer it, but I’ll still put it to you straight on PUBG.
PUBG PROS - VERY CONSISTENT UPDATES
•	Very realistic looking graphics and weapons
•	Weapons can have attachments
•	Huge map
•	Hiding is pretty good (especially in wheat fields) which may be a con for you
•	Map helps you find your way easily (very noob friendly)
•	Ability to choose where you land to a degree
•	Many different map settings
•	Weather occurs
•	Character movement is absolutely dope in my opinion
•	There’s boats
•	More weapons
PUBG CONS –
•	Misleading weapon mechanics and time to kill
•	Cars are clunky and all around just do not work well
•	The ability to choose spawns makes players spawn in a very linear line which isn’t my favorite honestly (and no you cant reach almost any point when you drop out, you can go pretty far though)
•       100 (from what I've had in games at least) people spawn compared to 174 in H1Z1 which just makes H1Z1 more actioned packed
•	Sounds are terrible, and I mean terrible, if you’re like me and rely on sound a lot in games this game will upset you highly as in you can't normally tell where shots are coming from if you hear them (I have Razer Kracken Chroma's 7.1 in perfect working order and audio settings are perfect, that being said gunshots and things of that nature are very hard to pinpoint which i don't like)
•	Kick and bullet drop on weapons seems to be not as polished in my opinion then KOTK
•	You have nothing to really play for, there are ranks (stats wise) but H1Z1 has a way of making you feel more rewarded with placements (yes you get points at a end of a game in PUBG so you can get your 6 cent skin)
On the bright side of things, I do believe PUBG has a way higher ceiling then KOTK so it could easily prove me wrong.
So there you have it. I was trying my best to not be biased but overall KOTK is my game. Don’t get me wrong, they are both good games and have their own futures. Should be great to watch them grow. Hope this helped. Later.

The often cited, for obvious reasons, comparison between Saints Row and GTA don't really do this game justice. Short if open-world, third-person, gang/crime game there is little else that can be said is the same so that's as far as I'll compare them.
The best part about this game is that it knows what it is. It knows it isn't gritty or realistic and it panders to that crazy over-the-topness that you know you occasionally want from a game. While there are of course many elements that are "normal" (escort missions, forced vehicle "sections", etc) the tight game play and bright, colorful world and enemy design makes them enjoyable. Besides as soon as you're done you can go play in traffic or drive around with a tiger in the passengers seat as much as you want (both actual mini-games).
The game really does a pretty good job of pacing. You start out feeling pretty weak, avoiding conflict and fleeing from bigger fights, but by the end you are running into a military compound because you have an extra case of rockets laying around. It also does a good job of avoiding the trap of over stimulating the player with too much too soon and I really never felt like it was dragging or tired.
Of course there are issues (you can break the money system using an age old method) but at the end of the day this game is just plain FUN, like games should be. I wholeheartedly recommend buying this game although the best method is probably to wait for the Complete Package to go on sale.

Imagine if games had a setting for "whimsy." This slider, alongside the usual contrast and brightness indicators, would decide how much charm, humor, and unexpected chaos were added to the gaming experience of your choice. Saints Row The Third is what would happen if you were playing Grand Theft Auto and this setting glitched at 200%.
There's a remarkable amount of charm and whimsy alongside the nigh-inevitable sociopathic elements of this sandbox shooter. Sure there's the wacky fun that comes from taking a rocket launcher to a helicopter, or of laying waste to a cityscape knowing that your death will only result in medical bills across town. That's part and parcel of the sandbox genre. What SR3 adds to the mix, however, is a self-awareness and a perpetual bias towards fun.
There's this pervasive understanding that a genuine and unexpected belly-laugh elevates the gaming experience, and SR3 goes out of its way to provide those genuine moments while somehow never feeling like they're trying too hard. Sometimes it's a little moment between characters. Sometimes it's a huge moment that can only happen in gaming. Sometimes it's intentionally putting the character in a  ridiculous situation and then having everyone else in the game play it completely straight. Every single time, though, I found myself appreciating the efforts and tossing off a quick "Bravo" to the developers.
By the time you're halfway through the game, you'll start worrying they'll run out of ground to cover, but don't worry - the whimsy just keeps on coming. More laudable is that the fun never overshadows the actual gameplay. Yes, sometimes it's hard to get the right shot off while you're nearly in tears from laughter, but there are other times of real, genuine, difficulty that remind you that while they're well aware that you're playing a game, the gameplay itself has to hold up.
Saints Row The Third was one of my favorite experiences of this generation of games. It's a game I thoroughly enjoyed the entire way through, and I have to thank my brother for recommending it so strongly to me. Yes, it's immature, violent, and occasionally childish, but it finds a way to be all of these things while making them seem charming, whimsical, and even occasionally literary. It's like Eddie Izzard in video game form, and it works so hard to make every single moment of gameplay feel entirely focused on entertaining you.

I have to disclose that I have a very strong nostalgic connection to this game which might make me bias. I distinctly remember that the “Orange Box” was my go to game in high school. I still think getting Half Life 2, Team Fortress 2 and Portal, all on one disc made for one of the greatest deals in gaming history! I played the living hell out of Team Fortress 2, it was one of the first online multiplayer games I ever played and was in many ways the gateway to an obsession with multiplayer gaming. I think this game proves that graphics are by no means everything. Almost all Valve games are getting on the older side at this point but somehow the dated graphics never seem to get in the way of the overall gaming experience. Perhaps this is because the gameplay and balancing is so spot on that one simple overlooks smaller and more superficial details like graphics. I think what really makes this game shine is how well thought out all the classes/characters are and how each seems to have their own important role to play as a member of the team and have their own unique identity. I still love to go back and watch the iconic and hilarious videos Valve put out to market the game. They really showed off the personality of each character and beautifully combined humor and over the top violence. Team Fortress 2 is probably one of the best free to play games out there. I can’t think of any reason this game shouldn’t be in everyone’s Stream Library.

It's been almost 3 years since the games release, and only NOW am I playing it! The first reason being that I had a massive backlog, and the second was that it was completely unplayable on my rig (no, not that type of unplayable, fix far below!).
I've played so many GTA's from the very first top down, to London and III to Vice City, you name them all, I've played them (except for V, still to come to PC!), yet honestly Saints Row just can't be compared (even though some people like to do it all the time). Sure, it's an open world. Sure there are cops, you can kill them, and get chased, just like with gangs. Sure there are linear and non-linear missions with cutscenes, but what other sandbox out there doesn't have some or all of that already?
What makes Saints Row unique is that it is FUN! There's nothing serious, it's completely HILARIOUS and when I mean fun, I mean hitting people upside the head with a pink♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shooting fish guts at your foes and watching sharks somehow defy all laws of what is possible (didn't get the DLC? SHAME ON YOU!), facegrinding people into the floor etc etc. And that is where Saints Row stands out; It's humor is unheard of in almost 90% of all the games I've ever played, it's fun to play, the missions don't feel repetitive, there's tons of customizations, hell, the cars alone and the ability to customize them totally bring back the good old days of Need For Speed: Underground, and let's not mention all the gun customizations that ACTUALLY change the look of your weapon (not just add +x damage!).
Take your favorite picks from all the games you've played and you're pretty much gonna end up with a perfect and well polished game, and aside from the early hassle with getting the game to work (and poor optimization on some machines) that is exactly what Saints Row: The Third is; a perfect game. My only woe is that the game, after playing GTA IV, is so short! :(
For those of you who were getting the damn CTD straight on the menu or loading up a new campaign, try the following, it was the only thing out of all the fixes out there that worked for me;
Reinstall the DirectX that comes with the game, inside the game folder, and run vcredist_x86.exe (found in the root of the games directory) and repair your previous install. After that, set the compatability on the game_launcher.exe, SaintsRowTheThird.exe and SaintsRowTheThird_DX11.exe to Windows Vista (Service Pack 2) and tick the "Run this program as an administrator" box.

Saints Row: The Third is an a definite fun experience but lacks in several areas. For the good the game offers a fun experience where you can drive around the city and cause absolute mayhem and do some pretty cool tricks. There's large amounts of customization for your character and vehicles you may consider pimping out as well. The city itself isn't particularly awe-inspiring large but it's good enough for the game itself. The bad things in the game though where a particular annoyance. I experienced many graphical problems and performance issues even though I have a pretty good rig that can even run the latest Battlefield maxed without issue. You can tell this game is a console port by the way the textures are horrifyingly bad. The textures would've been acceptable in 2006 but not 2011 when it came out. The story is also fairly short and doesn't provide anything really that great but still fun nonetheless.
Although there's many bad things there's also good to be had. It's a great game if you get it for a good value and I'd also take note that none of the DLC that accompany this game are worth it even if you do get it for a great deal. Just buy the base game and you'll get the entire experience.

I have to disclose that I have a very strong nostalgic connection to this game which might make me bias. I distinctly remember that the “Orange Box” was my go to game in high school. I still think getting Half Life 2, Team Fortress 2 and Portal, all on one disc made for one of the greatest deals in gaming history! I played the living hell out of Team Fortress 2, it was one of the first online multiplayer games I ever played and was in many ways the gateway to an obsession with multiplayer gaming. I think this game proves that graphics are by no means everything. Almost all Valve games are getting on the older side at this point but somehow the dated graphics never seem to get in the way of the overall gaming experience. Perhaps this is because the gameplay and balancing is so spot on that one simple overlooks smaller and more superficial details like graphics. I think what really makes this game shine is how well thought out all the classes/characters are and how each seems to have their own important role to play as a member of the team and have their own unique identity. I still love to go back and watch the iconic and hilarious videos Valve put out to market the game. They really showed off the personality of each character and beautifully combined humor and over the top violence. Team Fortress 2 is probably one of the best free to play games out there. I can’t think of any reason this game shouldn’t be in everyone’s Stream Library.

While I'm not a fan of comparing games, it goes without saying that one of the biggest questions about the Saints Row franchise revolves around its resemblance with the Grand Theft Auto series. Is it better? Is it much different from GTA? While the first is a question I don't want to involve in a review, I can confidently assert that Saints Row is in its own league.
Saints Row is a free roaming co-operative third person shooter packed with cheap humor and gang violence. However, that does not necessarily make this a bad game. I would actually say Saints Row III has very much succeeded in making cheap humor great and gang violence entertaining as far as video games go.
The setting of SRIII takes place on an island where a consortium of three large gangs are in charge of the city, and you as player have to topple these gangs in order to make your gang (the Saints) dominating. Whereas the GTA series does this through accepting certain missions from one gang against the other, the power of SRIII lies in its characters and scripted storyline as well as the complete individuality of the side missions. The fun is doubled when you bring along your friend over Internet/LAN co-op gameplay and you both develop your character traits such as combat skills, your looks, and your personal stack of vehicles (which conveniently respawn in the garage regardless of how you maul and destroy them, pretty handy).
This all works out pretty well, though not flawless. Besides an unconvincing world (which makes immersion very hard), SRIII has a couple of nasty bugs that can ruin your savegame so I recommend not writing your progress to a single slot the entire time. This should not be a buzzkill for the fun though, not when the gameplay is so fluent and the theme accompanied by proper fitting music. I would personally rate this game as one of the better games in its genre, much like what I did with Deus Ex: Human Revolution and Hitman. Luckily, Saints Row III is on sale during vacations quite often, the perfect opportunity to lock yourself up in your room and play through this game.

I think that TF2 is a fantastic game. It has been around from years ago and has remained brilliant and will likely stay that way in the near future. However, I do have some minor complaints. My first complaint is Competitive, when it was released all Valve did was take the Beta and release it. Because only a small amount of people play competitive, Valve doesn't get notified of this as much as they should, so if the community could've given Competitive a bit more attention Valve might be able to fix it in the incoming Pyro update. My second complaint is the tutorials, it's no question that the tutorials are outdated, and they will be for a while. This however makes it extremely hard for new players to learn, with most of them flocking towards CTF game modes, in which most of the maps only allow a few places for classes to set up. With 2fort for example, snipers can only go on the balcony and sometimes below it, while Engineer can only setup in the Intel room. Which promotes new players to stay in one spot when they could branch out and find imaginative spots to chill. In the long run, Valve needs to update the training guide by actually doing one for each class. But don't take this the wrong way, these are my only flaws with this game (besides the bribery of their darn hats) and generally it's one of the best/only war themed hat simulators and will remain that until Overwatch gets hats and taunts.

I have to disclose that I have a very strong nostalgic connection to this game which might make me bias. I distinctly remember that the “Orange Box” was my go to game in high school. I still think getting Half Life 2, Team Fortress 2 and Portal, all on one disc made for one of the greatest deals in gaming history! I played the living hell out of Team Fortress 2, it was one of the first online multiplayer games I ever played and was in many ways the gateway to an obsession with multiplayer gaming. I think this game proves that graphics are by no means everything. Almost all Valve games are getting on the older side at this point but somehow the dated graphics never seem to get in the way of the overall gaming experience. Perhaps this is because the gameplay and balancing is so spot on that one simple overlooks smaller and more superficial details like graphics. I think what really makes this game shine is how well thought out all the classes/characters are and how each seems to have their own important role to play as a member of the team and have their own unique identity. I still love to go back and watch the iconic and hilarious videos Valve put out to market the game. They really showed off the personality of each character and beautifully combined humor and over the top violence. Team Fortress 2 is probably one of the best free to play games out there. I can’t think of any reason this game shouldn’t be in everyone’s Stream Library.

I think that TF2 is a fantastic game. It has been around from years ago and has remained brilliant and will likely stay that way in the near future. However, I do have some minor complaints. My first complaint is Competitive, when it was released all Valve did was take the Beta and release it. Because only a small amount of people play competitive, Valve doesn't get notified of this as much as they should, so if the community could've given Competitive a bit more attention Valve might be able to fix it in the incoming Pyro update. My second complaint is the tutorials, it's no question that the tutorials are outdated, and they will be for a while. This however makes it extremely hard for new players to learn, with most of them flocking towards CTF game modes, in which most of the maps only allow a few places for classes to set up. With 2fort for example, snipers can only go on the balcony and sometimes below it, while Engineer can only setup in the Intel room. Which promotes new players to stay in one spot when they could branch out and find imaginative spots to chill. In the long run, Valve needs to update the training guide by actually doing one for each class. But don't take this the wrong way, these are my only flaws with this game (besides the bribery of their darn hats) and generally it's one of the best/only war themed hat simulators and will remain that until Overwatch gets hats and taunts.

Well, I feel like this is the last game before the whole Saints Row serie started failing down.
One of the main reasons I'm a huuuuge fan of Saints Row The Third especially is because the game is set in a serious universe with serious peoples, serious events, serious subjects and so on. Even the Saints are serious sometimes. Thing is, they do their serious stuff using not-so serious methods like flying a tank, creating a zombie apocalypse, becoming the enemy leader through plastic surgery, becoming a super hero through drinking energy drinks, cloning their dead (?) friend and much more.
Saints Row IV and V are both equally as good, but.. It's different. Having super powers and all that stuff removes the "Serious" tone from the world and gives you a world that's crazy insane with peoples doing crazy insane stuff at the place of a serious world with peoples doing crazy insane stuff.
Knowing that Saints Row V was supposed to be a DLC for Saints row IV which was itself supposed to be a DLC for Saints Row The Third.. I can understand why they're less serious, because all DLCs for Saints Row III are just completely crazy. But the fact they're full game means they're not DLCs, thus they're "Crazy insane" factor makes me dissapointed.
All in all, I think Saints Row The Third is the best of all five. The fourth and fifth are equally great, but not as much as the third. A must play.

With the recent update the game has not been improved by much. Daybreak have stated that they have fixed the pattern on the shotgun to make it more consistant, as well as the damage to relay on it further. None of these are true as you can still survive a shotgun shot to the head from point blank range.
Things that have improved this season:
The new AR-15 recoil is definetly an improvement, but they have given it 0 recoil which means that now anyone cant 2 tap. Especially when there is barely any bullet drop, this then allows new commers to spam the gun and get to straight shots, there is no skill gap.
The colors of the game have finally gotten brighter and better, last season the colors were depressing and harder to spot somebody.
Current Issues:
Dsync and lag within the servers. The servers of the game are horrible. I have constantly been shot behind a wall while taking cover. This makes close range fights even worse, as you will shoot someone at the same distance with a shotgun yet either one of you will be victorious.
Kills not counting;
On two seperate occasions, the kills towards my teammate did not count. He got 2 kills in early game (This was in fives) we stay till the end and a car rushes us. He gains another 2 kills, then when he dies, on the side where kills shows it says "1 kill". Then when our last teammate fell in fives and we lost the game, his end kills were 4. The recent was in duos. We rushed a cop car got 2 kills, we continued to another area, and got i got 2 kills this time. While we were looting we got shot in the back and my friend killed someone rushing him. I was low at the time healing. The other guy then rushes us and i die. This should leave me at 2 kills and my friend at 4 (He killed the guy that killed me). But in the end he got 3 kills.
Long range fights dont exist: People constantly cod rush (Including myself), because it is the only way to get certain kills. If you are in a long range fight with cars, then you will shoot him 3 times, then he runs only to never see him again. The game starts with 150 players and by the time the gas starts spreading there is only 75 players left. If you spend your time chasing people, by the time you kill them, there will be 20 players remaining. In the end you will end up with a game of 5-8 kills if you are extremely aggresive at the end. Point being that most of the fighting happens during early game, mid game to late game if you engage in a fight you will 75% of the time get pinched by someone from the back.
I will not compare this to PUBG, as I have not played it. I do recommend the game, however you will get mad from playing it. Although if you are thinking about playing it, you should play it now while there are still players on it. The numbers are decreasing because daybreak isnt doing much to fix the current issues.

After 500+ hours, the thing is still as clunky as all get out. Also at a certain point you are going to have to buy the Apex DLC, if you get nothing else.
But I have to say, I've probably spent more time in Arma 3 than I have in any other FPS - in terms of sheer playing time, not actual time because a lot of that was still spent fixing the thing. When it does work, once in a blue moon, it works WELL, and the fact that every single experience can be tailor fit to you and your friend's needs is the reason why.
Other FPS's have this flaw of being forced to play in the way the devs wanted you too, like CoD's invisible walls or constantly spawning enemies. Despite Arma's very obvious clunky nature, this is completley absent. There truly is no limitation to how you can complete an objective, and no shortage of ways the method you chose can go wrong. You are never invincible, but you are ALWAYS in control.
It takes effort and a lot of love to get this thing to work in the way you want it too, but you'll not find any other game that's like it, and once you'll get it to work there's literally a thousand games you can play.

As someone new to the series, this title absolutely amazed me with its intro scene and tutorial mission, where you participate in a good old bank heist.
Storytelling aspects is absolutely wonderful, with non-linear mission routes where you can pick the missions that interest you, or just ignore the missions for the time being and go shoot stuff in the streets.
Activities in The Third is very interesting, with unconventional objectives such as getting hurt as much as possible in 'Insurance Fraud', and crazy Japanese reality shows where the mascots dressed as hotdog buns try to kill you.
SRTT also has tons of self-referential humor and tons of parodies, and a lot of immature humor which I enjoyed throughout the game.
Mechanics-wise, much of the gameplay runs smoothly on my subpar system, and even then the graphics looks extremely gorgeous.
Vehicular controls are extremely well done in this game, and I'm surprised at how much fun I had simply driving around town drifting around corners and escaping the cops.
The inauguration station (character creator) is perhaps one of the most detailed one ever, allowing you to go right into the details such as 'Outer (eye)brow height' and 'Middle lip width'. Along with the wide array of hairstyles available, I'm almost convinced that you can model your character as ANYONE, from Lara Croft in Tomb Raider, to Agent 47 in Hitman, heck, you can even play as Gabe, blowing♥♥♥♥♥♥up in Steelport.
Overall this is a spectacular title, but if you did not already play SR 2, you might be a little lost at first, as some of the main characters were in the SR/ SR2.
If you're looking for pure, insane fun, definitely get this game.

Saints Row: The Third starts off with The Saints enjoying their lives as celebrities after the city takeover of Stillwater in Saints Row 2. Things spiral out of control when they attempt to rob a bank owned by a rival criminal organization known as The Syndicate. After being captured and then escaping your new enemy, you find yourself without funds or allies in a new city; Steelport.
The story is primarily focused on revenge against The Syndicate, as well as the takeover of a new city. As well, a new enemy emerges about 60% of the way through the story as the government attempts to quell the gang violence overtaking the city. Everything is taken to the extreme in the story; anytime something needs to be accomplished just leave it to the Saints to do it in the more gloriously over-the-top way possible! It’s a lot of fun and I found it hard to get bored doing any of the story missions.
Gameplay follows the same suit. While on the surface it looks and handles like any other open-world car stealing game, the options given to you really keep things awesome and interesting. The gunplay is lots of fun and the variety of options and upgrades really helps; from explosive bullets to calling in an airstrike, your arsenal should keep you well entertained. Driving is given the same treatment; the cars all handle very well and all have a nice arcade-y feel to them.
The thing I liked the most about the game is you could tell every decision was made in the pursuit of fun. If the option was to make more logical sense or to do what would be more fun to play, the game always sides with fun. Many, if not all of you, likely have this game from a bundle and I strongly suggest giving it a try!

I Have over 1100 hours on record with this game since Early Access.
The game has become much more user friendly since coming out, if you want a casual to all the way hardcore MILSIM experience, look no further.
Pro's: Huge Scale
Gorgeous visuals
Large selection of weapons
Realistic Ballistics, physics, damage implementation for various calibers, realistic Flight model including but not limited too advanced flight model implementation such as stalls, vortex ring state, damaged instrument panels and etc.
Welcoming community
Insane amount of free mods and maps (Including weapons, textures, sounds for weapons such as DragonFyre sound mod and etc..)
Tutorials that actually teach you how to play and how to not only react to contact and ambushes but also teaches you how to team play as part of a larger assault element and also combined arms (Ever wanted to be in the big boy army and participate in a large scale attack? look no further).
Good single Player Campaign.
Con's
Can still have a steep learning curve, mission making takes practice, more advanced missions scripting requires a decent concept of game script writing
Very very un-optimized for current Gen CPU's. Single thread performance only, can be resource intensive, recommend a i7 CPU for decent game play, takes a beast of a rig to run with everything maxed out in multiplayer (FPS in multiplayer is based off server side FPS and NOT client side aka your PC FPS, hence even powerful pc's can get stutter in large scale multiplayer games).
Can get pretty big in size if you subscribe to a large number of mods
Some mods can interfere with others.
TL:DR Since coming out Arma 3 has become much easier to learn and grasp with new and improved tutorials and scenarios, amazing mod support and close knit community help overcome and issues with this game such as optimization issues and map creation tools. If you do get this game, highly recommend finding a MILSIM unit and or group of players to help guide you in starting out in this game.
My Rig Specs for playing this game (At 1920x1080 with 2x FXAA and view distance of 2500 meters)
i7 3770k Over clocked too 4.1 Ghz
16GB DDR3 10600 RAM
EvGA GTX 970 Superclocked (OC 100mhz GPU, 500Mhz Memory)
Samsung 840 Pro SSD
Windows 10 64bit
